body.translated_text: <s>Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha</s> (Compendium of the Reality of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s)
CHAPTER 1
<s>VAJRADHĀTU-MAHĀ-MAṆḌALA-VIDHI-VISTARA-MAṆḌALA</s> I.1

Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, endowed with the diverse and distinguished knowledge of the adamantine empowerment-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having obtained the consecration of the sovereignty of the <s>Dharma</s> over the three realms through the jewel-crown of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the great lord of yogins of the omniscience of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the fulfiller of all wishes of the entire remainder-less realm of beings through the accomplishment of universal activity attained by the equality of all mudrās of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the greatly compassionate <s>Vairocana</s>, eternally established in the pledge of the three times, the <s>Tathāgata</s> who is the <s>vajra</s> of all body, speech, and mind — dwelt in the palace of <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, the king of the gods, praised and extolled by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s as their abode, adorned with great jewel-gems, hung with varied-colored bells, with banners, garlands, fly-whisks, necklaces, and half-necklaces fluttering in the wind and beautified by the moon — together with ninety-seven <s>koṭi</s>s of <s>bodhisattva</s>s, namely: the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, <s>Vajramuṣṭi</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, <s>Sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartin</s>, <s>Gaganagañja</s>, and <s>Sarvamārabalapramardin</s> — headed by these, ninety-seven <s>koṭi</s>s of <s>bodhisattva</s>s; and <s>Tathāgata</s>s as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. Just as a sesame pod appears completely filled, so did <s>Jambudvīpa</s> appear. And from each and every body of those immeasurable <s>Tathāgata</s>s, immeasurable and incalculable <s>Buddha</s>-fields were seen, and in those <s>Buddha</s>-fields they were teaching this very <s>dharma</s>-method.

body.text: tamekasmin samaye bhagavān sarvatathāgata-vajrādhiṣṭhānasamayajñānavividhaviśeṣasamanvāgataḥ, sarvatathāgataratnamukuṭatraidhātukadharmarājyābhiṣekaprāptaḥ, sarvatathāgatasarvajñānamahāyogīśvaraḥ, sarvatathāgatasarvamudrāsamatādhigataviśvakāryakaraṇatāśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātusarvāśāparipūrakaḥ, mahākṛpo vairocanaḥ śāśvatastryadhvasamayavyavasthitaḥ sarvakāyavākcittavajrastathāgataḥ, sarvatathāgatādhyuṣitapraśastastavite mahāmaṇiratnapratyupte vicitravarṇaghaṇṭāvasaktamārutoddhatapaṭṭasrakcāmarahārārdhahāracandropaśobhite akaniṣṭhadevarājasya bhavane vijahāra / navanavatibhirbodhisattvakoṭibhiḥ sārdhaṃ, tadyathā vajrapāṇinā ca bodhisattvena, avalokiteśvareṇa ca bodhisattvena, ākāśagarbheṇa ca, vajramuṣṭinā ca, mañjuśriyā ca, sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartinā ca, gaganagañjena ca sarvamārabalapramardinā ca, evaṃpramukhairnavanavatibhirbodhisattvakoṭibhiḥ; gaṅgānadīvālukāsamākhyātaiśca tathāgataiḥ, tadyathāpi nāma tilabimbamiva paripūrṇaṃ jambūdvīpe saṃdṛśyate / taiścāprameyaistathāgatairekaikasmācca tathāgatakāyādaprameyāsaṃkhyeyāni buddhakṣetrāṇi saṃdṛśyante, teṣu ca buddhakṣetreṣu imameva dharmanayaṃ deśayanti sma /

atha bhagavān mahāvairocanaḥ sarvākāśadhātusadāvasthitakāyavākcittavajraḥ sarvatathāgatasamavasaraṇatayā sarvavajradhātvavabodhanajñānasattvaḥ sarvākāśadhātuparamāṇurajo vajrādhiṣṭhānasambhavajñānagarbhaḥ sarvatathāgatānantatayā mahavajrajñānābhiṣekaratnaḥ sarvākāśaspharaṇatathatājñānābhisambodhyabhisambodhibhūtaḥ sarvatathāgatātmabhāvaśuddhitayāsvabhāvaśuddhasarvadharmaḥ sarvākāśacaryāgryaḥ sarvatathāgatāmoghājñākāritayā sarvāsamānuttaraviśvakarmā / sarvatathāgatamahābodhidṛḍhasattvaḥ sarvatathāgatakarṣaṇasamayaḥ sarvatathāgatānurāgaṇajñāneśvaraḥ sarvatathāgatasādhukāraḥ sarvatathāgatamahābhiṣekaratnaḥ sarvatathāgatasūryaprabhāmaṇḍalaḥ sarvatathāgatacintārājamaṇiratnaketuḥ sarvatathāgatamahāhāsaḥ sarvatathāgatamahāśuddhadharmaḥ sarvatathāgataprajñājñānaḥ sarvatathāgatacakraḥ sarvatathāgatamahāvīryasudṛḍhakavacaḥ sarvatathāgatarakṣaparipālanavajrayakṣaḥ sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajrabandhamudrājñānaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Mahāvairocana</s>, the <s>vajra</s> of body, speech, and mind eternally abiding throughout the entire space-realm, the knowledge-being of the awakening of the entire <s>vajra</s>-realm through the assembly of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the womb of knowledge born from the <s>vajra</s>-empowerment of the atoms of the entire space-realm, the jewel of the great <s>vajra</s>-knowledge-consecration through the infinity of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the one who has perfectly awakened to the <s>tathatā</s>-knowledge pervading all space, pure in the nature of all <s>dharma</s>s through the purity of the self-nature of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, foremost in the conduct throughout all space, the universal worker of unsurpassed and unequaled actions through the infallible command of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — the firm being of the great awakening of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the pledge of attracting all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the lord of the knowledge of delighting all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the applause of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the jewel of the great consecration of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the orb of the sun's rays of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the jewel-banner of the wish-fulfilling gem of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the great laughter of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the great pure <s>dharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the wisdom-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the wheel of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the great firmly heroic armor of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the <s>vajra</s>-<s>yakṣa</s> of the protection and guardianship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the knowledge of the <s>vajra</s>-binding-<s>mudrā</s> of the body, speech, and mind of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s —
Eulogy of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>

children.translated_text: <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the infallible, <s>Māra</s>, the leader of joy,
<s>Khagarbha</s> (Sky-womb), of great splendor, <s>Ratnaketu</s> (Jewel-banner), the great-smiling one. (1)
<s>Avalokita</s>-<s>Maheśa</s> (the Great Lord who Gazes), and <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the lord of all <s>maṇḍala</s>s,
the Speechless, the Universal Worker, the Heroic, the Wrathful, the Firm-grasper. (2)

children.text: vajro 'ṅ kuśaḥ śarastuṣṭiḥ ratnaḥ sūryo dhvajaḥ smitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vajra</s>, Hook, Arrow, Delight, Jewel, Sun, Banner, Smile,

children.text: padmaḥ kośaḥ sucakro vāk karma varma ravayo grahaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: Lotus, Sheath, Good-wheel, Speech, Action, Armor, Rays, Grasp. (3)
Without beginning or end, Peaceful, Fierce, Wrathful, the Greatly Patient,
<s>Yakṣa</s>, Divine-demon, Steadfast, Son of the Sun, Son of the Sun, the Great All-pervading. (4)
Lord of <s>Umā</s>, Lord of creatures, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, Victorious, the Great Sage,
World-protector, Sky, Earth, the Three Worlds, the Three Realms. (5)
Great Element, Good-purpose-for-beings, All, <s>Śarva</s>, Grandfather,
<s>Saṃsāra</s>, <s>Nirvṛti</s> (Cessation), Eternal, Right-conduct, the Great-great. (6)
Conqueror of the Three Worlds, <s>Śambhu</s>, Lord of <s>Śambhu</s>, the Bountiful Giver. (7)

body.translated_text: <s>Buddha</s>, Pure, Great Vehicle, Three-existence, Eternal, the Slayer,

children.translated_text: Lord of <s>Vajra</s>, Foremost of Good Stages, Knowledge, the Method of <s>Pāramitā</s>s,
Liberation, <s>Bodhisattva</s>, Conduct, All-<s>Tathāgata</s>. (8)
<s>Buddha</s>-purpose, <s>Buddha</s>-heart, All-awakening, Unsurpassed,
<s>Vairocana</s>, Victor, Protector, Self-arisen, <s>Dhāraṇī</s>, Mindfulness. (9)
Great Being, Great <s>Mudrā</s>, <s>Samādhi</s>, Doer of <s>Buddha</s>-activity,
Having the nature of all <s>Buddha</s>s, True, Being, Eternal Awakener of Purpose. (10)
Great Pillar, Great Time (<s>Mahākāla</s>), Great Passion, Great Bliss,
Great Transgressor, Greatest of the Great, Foremost of All, Lord of Worlds. (11)

body.text: bhagavān mahābodhicittaḥ samantabhadro mahābodhisattvaḥ sarvatathāgatahṛdayeṣu vijahāra / atha sarvatathāgatairidaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ tadyathā tilabimbamiva paripūrṇama //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s>, the great awakening-mind, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, dwelt in the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Then all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s filled this <s>Buddha</s>-field just like a sesame pod.

body.text: atha khalu sarvatathāgatā mahāsamājamāpadya, yena sarvārthasiddhirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇastenopajagmuḥ / upetya bodhisattvasya sāṃbhogikaiḥ kāyairdarśanandatvaivamāhuḥ- "kathaṃ kulaputrānuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim abhisaṃbhotsyase, yastvaṃ sarvatathāgatatattvānabhijñatayā sarvaduḥkarāṇyutsahasī-?"ti /
body.translated_text: Then indeed all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having assembled in the great assembly, approached the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> (Accomplisher of All Purposes) who was seated at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). Having approached, showing themselves to the <s>bodhisattva</s> in their enjoyment-bodies (<s>sāṃbhogika kāya</s>s), they spoke thus: 'How, O son of good family, will you attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), you who endure all austerities through ignorance of the reality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s?'

body.text: atha sarvārthasiddhirbodhisattvo mahāsatvassarvatathāgatacoditaḥsamānastata āsphānasamādhito vyutthāya, sarvatathāgatān praṇipatyāhū yaivamāha- "bhagavantastathāgatā ājñāpayata kathaṃ pratipadyāmi kīdṛśaṃ tat tattvam" iti / evamukte sarvatathāgatāstaṃ bodhisattvamekakaṇṭhenaivamāhuḥ- "pratipadyasva kulaputra svacittapratyavekṣaṇasamādhānena prakṛtisiddhena rucijaptena mantreṇa" iti oṃ cittaprativedhaṃ karomi /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>, having been urged by all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, rising from the <s>samādhi</s> of contact, bowed to all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s and spoke thus: '<s>Bhagavān</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s>s, command me! How should I proceed? What is that reality?' Thus addressed, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s spoke to that <s>bodhisattva</s> with one voice: 'Proceed, O son of good family, through the <s>samādhi</s> of self-mind examination, with the naturally accomplished <s>mantra</s> recited with delight: OṂ — I accomplish the penetration of mind!'

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ sarvatathāgatānevamāha- "ājñātaṃ me bhagavantastathāgatāḥ svahṛdi candramaṇḍalākāraṃ paśyāmi" / sarvatathāgatāḥ procuḥ- "prakṛtiprabhāsvaramidaṃ kulaputra cittaṃ, tadyathā parikarṣyate tat tathaiva bhavati / tadyathāpi nāma śvetavastre rāgarañjanam" iti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> spoke thus to all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s: 'It is understood, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s>s — I see in my own heart a moon-disc.' All the <s>Tathāgata</s>s declared: 'This mind, O son of good family, is luminous by nature. Just as it is refined, so it becomes — just as dye [colors] a white cloth.'

body.text: atha sarvatathāgatāḥ prakṛtiprabhāsvaracittajñānasya sphītīkaraṇahetoḥ punarapi tasmai bodhisattvāya oṃ bodhicittamutpādayāmi ityanena prakṛtisiddhena mantreṇa bodhicittamutpāditavantaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purpose of expanding the knowledge of the naturally luminous mind, again generated the awakening-mind (<s>bodhicitta</s>) in that <s>bodhisattva</s> with this naturally accomplished <s>mantra</s>: 'OṂ — I generate the <s>bodhicitta</s>!'

body.text: atha bodhisattvaḥ punarapi sarvatathāgatājñayā bodhicittamutpādyaivamāha- "yat taccandramaṇḍalākāraṃ taccandramaṇḍalameva paśyāmi" / sarvatathāgatā āhuḥ- "sarvatathāgatahṛdayante samantabhadraścittotpādaḥ sāmīcībhūtaḥ, tatsādhu pratipadyatām, sarvatathāgatasamantabhadracittotpādasya dṛḍhīkaraṇahetoḥ svahṛdi candramaṇḍale vajrabimbaṃ cintayānena mantreṇa oṃ tiṣṭha vajra /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s>, having again generated the <s>bodhicitta</s> by the command of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke thus: 'That which was in the form of a moon-disc — I now see it as a moon-disc itself.' All the <s>Tathāgata</s>s said: 'In the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the arising of the mind has become fitting. Therefore, practice well! For the purpose of making firm the arising of the mind of <s>Samantabhadra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, contemplate a <s>vajra</s>-image upon the moon-disc in your own heart, with this <s>mantra</s>: OṂ — Remain, O <s>Vajra</s>!'

body.text: bodhisattva āha- "paśyāmi bhagavantastathāgatāścandramaṇḍale vajram" / sarvatathāgatā āhuḥ- "dṛḍhīkurvidaṃ sarvatathāgatasamantabhadracittavajramanena mantreṇa oṃ vajrātmako 'ham //
body.translated_text: The <s>bodhisattva</s> said: 'I see, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s>s — a <s>vajra</s> upon the moon-disc.' All the <s>Tathāgata</s>s said: 'Make firm this mind-<s>vajra</s> of <s>Samantabhadra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, with this <s>mantra</s>: OṂ — I am of <s>vajra</s>-nature!'

body.text: atha yāvantaḥ sarvākāśadhātusamavasaraṇāḥ sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajradhātavaḥ, te sarve sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānena tasmin sattvavajre praviṣṭāḥ / tataḥ sarvatathāgataiḥ sa bhagavān sarvārthasiddhirmahābodhisattvo vajradhāturvajradhāturiti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, however many <s>vajra</s>-realms of the body, speech, and mind of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s there were assembled throughout the entire space-realm — all of them, through the empowerment of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, entered into that being-<s>vajra</s> (<s>sattvavajra</s>). Then by all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>, was consecrated with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration as '<s>Vajradhātu</s>! <s>Vajradhātu</s>!'

body.text: atha vajradhāturmahābodhisattvastān sarvatathāgatānevamāha "paśyāmi bhagavantastathāgatāḥ sarvatathāgatakāyamātmānam" / sarvatathāgatāḥ prāhuḥ- "tena hi mahāsattva sattvavajraṃ sarvākāravaropetaṃ buddhabimbamātmānaṃ bhāvayānena prakṛtisiddhena mantreṇa rucitaḥ parijapya oṃ yathā sarvatathāgatāstathāham" //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajradhātu</s> spoke thus to all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s: 'I see, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s>s — myself as the body of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.' All the <s>Tathāgata</s>s declared: 'Therefore, O great being, cultivate yourself as a <s>Buddha</s>-image endowed with all excellent marks, [contemplating] the being-<s>vajra</s>, with this naturally accomplished <s>mantra</s>, having recited it with delight: OṂ — Just as all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s are, so am I!'

body.text: athaivamukte vajradhāturmahābodhisattvastathāgatamātmānamabhisambudhya, tān sarvatathāgatān praṇipatyāhū yaivamāha "adhitiṣṭhata māṃ bhagavantastathāgatā imāmabhisaṃbodhiṃ dṛḍhīkuruta ceti" / athaivamukte sarvatathāgatā vajradhātostathāgatasya tasmin sattvavajre praviṣṭā iti //
body.translated_text: Then, when this was said, the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajradhātu</s>, having awakened to himself as a <s>Tathāgata</s>, bowed to all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s and spoke thus: 'Empower me, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s>s! Make firm this awakening!' Then, when this was said, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s entered into that being-<s>vajra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vajradhātu</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavān vajradhātustathāgatastasmin eva kṣaṇe sarvatathāgatasamatājñānābhisaṃbuddha sarvatathāgatavajrasamatājñānamudrāguhyasamayapraviṣṭaḥ sarvatathāgatadharmasamatājñānādhigamasvabhāvaśuddhaḥ sarvatathāgatasarvasamatāprakṛtiprabhāsvarajñānākarabhūtastathāgato 'rhān samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ saṃvṛtta iti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vajradhātu</s>, at that very moment, having awakened to the equality-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having entered the secret pledge of the <s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-equality-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, pure in self-nature through the realization of the <s>dharma</s>-equality-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having become the source of the naturally luminous knowledge of the complete equality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — became a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One.

body.text: atha sarvatathāgatāḥ punarapi tataḥ sarvatathāgatasattvavajrān niḥsṛtyākāśagarbhamahāmaṇiratnābhiṣekeṇābhiṣicyāvalokiteśvaradharmajñānamutpādya sarvatathāgataviśvakarmatāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena sumerugirimūrdhā yena ca vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ, upasaṃkramya vajradhātuntathāgataṃ sarvatathāgatatve 'dhiṣṭhya, sarvatathāgatasiṃhāsane sarvatomukhaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsuriti //
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having again emerged from the being-<s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having consecrated [him] with the great jewel-gem consecration of <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, having generated the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, having established [him] in the universal activity of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, proceeded to the summit of Mount <s>Sumeru</s> and to the pinnacle-hall of the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-gem peak. Having approached, they empowered the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vajradhātu</s> in the state of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and seated [him] facing all directions upon the lion-throne of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

body.text: Emanation of the 37 deities from samadhi
body.translated_text: Emanation of the 37 deities from <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: atha khalu akṣobhyastathāgato ratnasaṃbhavaśca tathāgato lokeśvararājaśca tathāgato amoghasiddhiśca tathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatatvaṃ svayamātmanyadhiṣṭhāya, bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya sarvasamatāsuprativedhatvāt sarvadiksamatāmabhyālambya, catasṛṣu dikṣu niṣaṇṇāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Lokeśvararāja</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amoghasiddhi</s>, having empowered in themselves the state of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and having taken hold of the equality in all directions due to the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>'s thorough penetration of complete equality, were seated in the four directions.
I.1.6 <s>Vajrasattva</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgataḥ acirābhisaṃbuddhaḥ sarvatathāgatasamantabhadrahṛdayasarvatathāgatākāśasaṃbhavamahāmaṇiratnābhiṣekābhiṣiktaḥ sarvatathāgatāvalokiteśvaradharmajñānaparamapāramitāprāptaḥ sarvatathāgataviśvakarmatāmoghāpratihataśāsanaḥ paripūrṇakāryaḥ paripūrṇamanorathaḥ sarvatathāgatatvaṃ svayamātmanyadhiṣṭhāya, sarvatathāgatasamantabhadramahābodhisattvasamayasambhavasattvādhiṣṭhānavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatamahāyānābhisamayaṃ nāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayāna niścacāra vajrasattva //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, recently fully awakened, consecrated with the great jewel-gem consecration born from the space of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s through the heart of <s>Samantabhadra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having attained the supreme <s>pāramitā</s> of the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, whose teaching of universal activity of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s is infallible and unobstructed, whose purpose is fulfilled, whose wishes are fulfilled — having empowered in himself the state of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the empowerment of the being born from the pledge of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' and from his own heart there emerged this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' — <s>Vajrasattva</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavāṃ samantabhadraścandramaṇḍalāni bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, sarvasattvānāṃ mahābodhicittāni saṃśodhya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ sarvapārśveṣvavasthitāḥ / atha tebhyaścandramaṇḍalebhyaḥ sarvatathāgatajñānavajrāṇi viniḥsṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya hṛdaye praviṣṭāni / samantabhadratvācca sudṛḍhatvācca vajrasattvasamādheḥ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānena caikadhanaḥ sakalākāśadhātusamavasaraṇapramāṇo raśmimālo pañcamūrdhā sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajramayovajravigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, sarvathāgatahṛdayān niṣkramya pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajrād vajrākārā raśmayo vicitravarṇarūpāḥ sarvalokadhātvābhāsanaspharaṇā viniścaritāḥ / tebhyaśca vajraraśmimukhebhyaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, sakaladharmadhātusamavasaraṇeṣu sarvākāśadhātuparyavasāneṣu sarvalokadhātuprasarameghasamudreṣu sarvatathāgatasamatājñānābhijñāsvabhisaṃbodhāt, sarvatathāgatamahābodhicittotpādanasamantabhadravividhacaryāniṣpādanasarva- tathāgatakulārāgaṇamahābodhimaṇḍopasaṃkramaṇasarvamāradharṣaṇasarva- tathāgatasamatāmahābodhyabhisaṃbudhyanadharmacakrapravartanaṃ yāvad aśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātuparitrāṇasarvahitasukhasarvatathāgatajñānābhijñottamasiddhiniṣpādanādīni sarvatathāgatavikurvitāni sandarśya, samantabhadratvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghanaḥ samantabhadramahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Samantabhadra</s>, having become moon-discs and emerged, purified the great <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening-mind) of all beings, and stationed himself on all sides of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Then from those moon-discs, wisdom-<s>vajra</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s emerged and entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>. And because of the universally good nature (<s>samantabhadratva</s>) and because of the extreme firmness of the <s>vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, and through the empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, a single solid [form], equal in measure to the assembly of the entire space-realm, with a garland of rays, five-headed, made of the <s>vajra</s> of the body, speech, and mind of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having a <s>vajra</s>-body, manifested and, having emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, was established in [<s>Vairocana</s>'s] hand. Then from that <s>vajra</s>, <s>vajra</s>-shaped rays of various colors and forms, illuminating and pervading all world-realms, issued forth. And from those <s>vajra</s>-ray-tips, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and in the assemblies throughout the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, at the ends of all space-realms, in the ocean-clouds of the expanse of all world-realms — having fully awakened to the wisdom of the equality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s through <s>abhijñā</s> (direct knowledge), having displayed all the miraculous activities of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — the generation of the great <s>bodhicitta</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the accomplishment of the various practices of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the approach to the great <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening) of the lineages of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the subjugation of all <s>Māra</s>s, the full awakening to the great <s>bodhi</s> of the equality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the turning of the <s>dharmacakra</s>, up to the accomplishment of the supreme attainment of the wisdom and <s>abhijñā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for the protection, benefit, and happiness of the entire limitless and inexhaustible realm of beings — and then, because of the universally good nature and because of the extreme firmness of the <s>vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, having become a single solid body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Samantabhadra</s>, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, he uttered this inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>):

children.translated_text: Ah! I am <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the firm-being (<s>dṛḍhasattva</s>) of the Self-Existent Ones (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>),
for, because of my firmness, though bodiless, I have attained the state of having a being-body (<s>sattvakāya</s>)!

body.text: atha samantabhadramahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ purataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then the body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Samantabhadra</s>, having descended from the heart of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and having stationed himself before all <s>Tathāgata</s>s resting on a moon-disc, sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatajñānasamayavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgataśīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanadharmacakrapravartanasattvārthamahopāyabalavīryamahājñānasamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātuparitrāṇasarvādhipatyasarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārtha yāvat sarvatathāgatasamatājñānābhijñānuttaramahāyānābhisamayottamasiddhyavāptiphalahetostatsarvatathāgatasiddhivajraṃ tasmai samantabhadrāya mahābodhisattvāya sarvatathāgatacakravartitve sarvabuddhakāyaratnamukuṭapaṭṭābhiṣekeṇābhiṣicya pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajrapāṇirvajrapāṇiriti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the wisdom-pledge (<s>jñānasamaya</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' for the purpose of experiencing the sovereign mastery, all happiness and mental satisfaction of the turning of the <s>dharmacakra</s> of the morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and liberation-knowledge-and-vision of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the great skillful means of benefit for beings, the strength, vigor, and pledge of great wisdom, the protection of the entire limitless and inexhaustible realm of beings — up to the attainment of the supreme accomplishment of the unsurpassed <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization through the wisdom and <s>abhijñā</s> of the equality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — consecrated that great <s>Bodhisattva Samantabhadra</s> as the universal sovereign (<s>cakravartin</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the consecration of the jewel-crown-diadem of the body of all <s>Buddha</s>s, and bestowed upon him with both hands that <s>vajra</s> of accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Thereupon he was consecrated by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration [proclaiming] '<s>Vajrapāṇi</s>! <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>!'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo vāmavajragarvollālanatayā tadavajraṃ svahṛdyutkarṣaṇayogena dhārayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi</s>, with the pride of tossing the <s>vajra</s> in his left [hand], holding that <s>vajra</s> by drawing it up to his own heart, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This is that unsurpassed <s>vajra</s> of accomplishment of all <s>Buddha</s>s!

children.text: ahaṃ mama kare dattaṃ vajraṃ vajre pratiṣṭhitam // iti //
children.translated_text: It has been given to me, in my hand — the <s>vajra</s> established in the <s>vajra</s>!

body.translated_text: I.1.7 <s>Vajrarāja</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapyamogharājamahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavasattvādhiṣṭhānavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyadaṃ sarvatathāgatākarṣaṇasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrarāja //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the empowerment of beings born from the pledge of the great <s>Bodhisattva Amogharāja</s>,' this essence of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the pledge of attracting all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrarāja</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajrapāṇi sarvatathāgatamahāṅkuśāni bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghano vajrāṅku śamahāvigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajrāṅku śamahāvigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, sarvatathāgatakarṣaṇādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, svamogharājatvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghanaḥ amogharājamahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having become great hooks (<s>mahāṅkuśa</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and emerged, entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, and having become a single solid great <s>vajra</s>-hook form, manifested and was established in the hand of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then from that great <s>vajra</s>-hook form, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and having performed the miraculous activities of all <s>Buddha</s>s — the attracting of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest — because of his infallible sovereignty (<s>amogharājatva</s>) and because of the extreme firmness of the <s>vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, having become a single solid body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Amogharāja</s>, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, he uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am the infallible sovereign (<s>Amogharāja</s>), the hook born of <s>vajra</s> (<s>vajrasaṃbhava</s>),
by which the all-pervading <s>Buddha</s>s are attracted along with [their] accomplishments!

body.text: atha so 'mogharājamahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ dakṣiṇacandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Amogharāja</s>, having descended from the heart of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and having stationed himself on the moon-disc to the right of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatākarṣaṇasamayavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatākarṣaṇasamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātusarvākarṣaṇasarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvat sarvatathāgatasamājādhiṣṭhānottamasiddhyarthaṃ tadvajrāṅkuśaṃ tasmai amogharājāya mahābodhisattvāya tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajrākarṣo vajrākarṣa iti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the pledge of attracting all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' for the purpose of experiencing the attraction of all beings in the entire limitless and inexhaustible realm, all happiness and mental satisfaction, up to the supreme accomplishment of the empowerment of the assembly of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-hook upon that great <s>Bodhisattva Amogharāja</s> in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration [proclaiming] '<s>Vajrākarṣa</s>! <s>Vajrākarṣa</s>!'
Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajrākarṣa</s>, attracting all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with that <s>vajra</s>-hook, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This is that unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-wisdom of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the supreme attraction for the accomplishment of the aims of all <s>Buddha</s>s!

body.translated_text: I.1.8 <s>Vajrarāga</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi māramahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavasattvādhiṣṭhānavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatānurāgaṇasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrarāga //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the empowerment of beings born from the pledge of the great <s>Bodhisattva Māra</s>,' this essence of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the pledge of enamoring all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrarāga</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvatathāgatakusumāyudhāni bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghano mahāvajravāṇavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajravāṇavigrahātsarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, sarvatathāgatānurāgaṇādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, sumāraṇatvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghano māramahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become flower-weapons (<s>kusumāyudha</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and emerged, entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, and having become a single solid great <s>vajra</s>-arrow form, manifested and was established in [his] hand. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-arrow form, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and having performed the miraculous activities of all <s>Buddha</s>s — the enamoring of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest — because of the excellence of conquest (<s>sumāraṇatva</s>) and because of the extreme firmness of the <s>vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, having become a single solid body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Māra</s>, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, he uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am naturally pure, the passion (<s>anurāga</s>) of the Self-Existent Ones,
for those who are dispassionate are disciplined through passion, for the purpose of purification!

body.text: atha sa māramahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya sarvatathāgatānāṃ vāmacandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Māra</s>, having descended from the heart of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and having stationed himself on the moon-disc to the left of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatānurāgaṇādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatamāraṇavajrasamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣatvadhātvanurāgaṇarsāsukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvat sarvatathāgatamārakarmottamasiddhyavāptiphalahetostadvajravāṇaṃ tasmai mārāya mahābodhisattvāya tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajradhanurvajradhanuriti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the empowerment of enamoring all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' for the purpose of experiencing the <s>vajra</s>-pledge of conquering all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the enamoring, passion, happiness, and mental satisfaction of the entire limitless and inexhaustible realm of beings, up to the attainment of the supreme accomplishment of the conquest-activity of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-arrow upon that great <s>Bodhisattva Māra</s> in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration [proclaiming] '<s>Vajradhanus</s>! <s>Vajradhanus</s>!'

body.text: atha vajradhanurbodhisattvo mahāsattvastena vajravāṇena sarvatathāgatān mārayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajradhanus</s>, conquering all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with that <s>vajra</s>-arrow, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This is that unstained passion-wisdom (<s>rāgajñāna</s>) of all <s>Buddha</s>s,

children.text: hatvā virāgaṃ rāgeṇa sarvasaukhyaṃ dadanti hi //
children.translated_text: having slain dispassion with passion, they bestow all happiness!

body.translated_text: I.1.9 <s>Vajrasādhu</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi prāmodyarājamahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavasattvādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatapramodasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrasādhu //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the empowerment of beings born from the pledge of the great <s>Bodhisattva Prāmodyarāja</s> (King of Joy),' this essence of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the pledge of the delight of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrasādhu</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sādhukārāṇi bhūtvā, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghano bhūtvā, vajratuṣṭivigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajratuṣṭivigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ tathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, sarvatathāgatasādhukārādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, suprāmodyatvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāc caikaghanaḥ prāmodyarājamahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become exclamations of 'well done!' (<s>sādhukāra</s>) and entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, having become a single solid [form], a <s>vajra</s>-satisfaction body manifested and was established in the hand of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-satisfaction body, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and having performed the miraculous activities of all <s>Buddha</s>s — the exclamations of 'well done!' to all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest — because of the excellence of joy (<s>suprāmodyatva</s>) and because of the extreme firmness of the <s>vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, having become a single solid body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Prāmodyarāja</s>, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, he uttered this inspired utterance:

children.text: aho hi sādhukāro 'haṃ sarvaḥ sarvavidāṃ varaḥ /
children.translated_text: Ah! I am the exclamation of 'well done!' — the most excellent of all, of all the omniscient ones,
for I surely generate satisfaction in those who have abandoned conceptualization!

body.text: atha sa prāmodyarājamahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ pṛṣṭhataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Prāmodyarāja</s>, having descended from the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s> and having stationed himself on the moon-disc behind all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatasaṃtoṣaṇavajrannāma samādhiṃ saṃpādya, sarvatathāgatānuttaraprāmodyajñānasamayaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātusarvasattvasantoṣaṇamahāsukhasaumanasyānubhavanārtha yāvat sarvatathāgatānuttaraharṣarasottamasiddhiprāptiphalahetostadvajratuṣṭiṃ tasmai prāmodyarājāya mahābodhisattvāya tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajraharṣo vajraharṣa iti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of satisfying all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' for the purpose of experiencing the wisdom-pledge of the unsurpassed joy of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the satisfaction of all beings in the entire limitless and inexhaustible realm, great happiness and mental satisfaction, up to the attainment of the supreme accomplishment of the unsurpassed delight-essence of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-satisfaction upon that great <s>Bodhisattva Prāmodyarāja</s> in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration [proclaiming] '<s>Vajraharṣa</s>! <s>Vajraharṣa</s>!'

body.text: atha vajraharṣo bodhisattvastena vajratuṣṭinā sarvatathāgatān sādhukāraiḥ praharṣayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajraharṣa</s>, delighting all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with that <s>vajra</s>-satisfaction through exclamations of 'well done!,' uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This is that which sets in motion the exclamation of 'well done!' of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the divine <s>vajra</s> that produces all satisfaction and increases joy!

body.translated_text: Great <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening-mind), the pledge of attracting all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the wisdom of enamoring all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and great satisfaction — these are the great pledge-beings (<s>mahāsamayasattva</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
I.1.10 <s>Vajraratna</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapyākāśagarbhamahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavaratnādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajraratnaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the empowerment of the jewel born from the pledge of the great <s>Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha</s>,' this essence of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the pledge of the consecration of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajraratna</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sarvākāśasamatājñānasuprativedhatvād, vajrasattvasamādheḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvākāśarasamayo bhūtvā viniḥsṛtās, taiḥ sarvaiḥ sarvākāśaraśmibhiḥ sarvalokadhātavo 'vabhāsitāḥ, sarvākāśadhātusamāḥ saṃvṛtā abhūvan / atha sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānena sarvo 'sākāśadhāturbhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭāḥ / suparibhāvitatvācca vajrasattvasamādheḥ sarvākāśadhātugarbhamayaḥ sarvalokadhātusamavasaraṇapramāṇo mahāvajraratnavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tasmād vajraratnavigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahāḥ prādurbhūya, sarvatathāgatābhiṣekādīni sarvatathāgatarddhivikurvitāni sarvalokadhātuṣu kṛtvā, sarvākāśadhātugarbhasusaṃbhavatvādvajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghanaḥ ākāśagarbhamahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, because of the thorough penetration of the knowledge of the equality of all space (<s>sarvākāśasamatājñāna</s>) from the <s>Vajrasattva</s> concentration, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become rays filling all space, emerged. By all those rays filling all space, all world-realms were illuminated and became enveloped, equal to the entire space-element. Then, by the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the entire space-element entered the heart of the <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>. And because the <s>Vajrasattva</s> concentration was thoroughly cultivated, a great <s>vajra</s>-jewel body, composed of the womb of the entire space-element, equal in measure to the convergence of all world-realms, manifested and was established in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s hand. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-jewel body, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms of all world-realms manifested, and having performed all <s>Tathāgata</s> miraculous displays such as the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest in all world-realms, because of the excellent arising from the womb of the entire space-element and because of the firm stability of the <s>Vajrasattva</s> concentration, they became a single solid body — the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> body of the Womb of Space (<s>Ākāśagarbha</s>) — and, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, uttered this inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>):

children.translated_text: Oh! I am indeed the self-consecration, the supreme <s>vajra</s>-jewel,
whereby even the unattached <s>Jina</s>s are known as lords of the three realms!

body.text: atha sa ākāśagarbhamahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ purataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that great <s>Bodhisattva</s> body of the Womb of Space descended from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s heart, and having stationed himself on a moon-disk before all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatamaṇiratnavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatābhiprāyaparipūrṇasamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātusarvārthapariprāptisarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvat sarvatathāgatārthasaṃpaduttamasiddhiprāptyai taṃ vajramaṇiṃ tasmai ākāśagarbhāya mahābodhisattvāya vajraratnacakravartitve vajraratnāṅkurābhiṣekeṇābhiṣicya pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajragarbho vajragarbha iti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the concentration called the <s>Vajra</s> of the Jewel-gem of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s (<s>Sarvatathāgatamaṇiratnavajra</s>), for the purpose of experiencing all happiness and well-being through the complete attainment of all aims of the entire sentient realm as the complete fulfillment of the vow of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, up to the attainment of the supreme accomplishment of the perfection of the purpose of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — consecrated that <s>vajra</s>-jewel with the consecration of the <s>vajra</s>-jewel sprout (<s>vajraratnāṅkurābhiṣeka</s>) in the sovereignty of the <s>vajra</s>-jewel <s>cakravartin</s> and bestowed it upon that great <s>Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha</s> with both hands. Thereupon, by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, he was consecrated with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration as '<s>Vajragarbha</s>, <s>Vajragarbha</s>!'

body.text: atha vajragarbho mahābodhisattvastaṃ vajramaṇiṃ svābhiṣekasthāne sthāpayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajragarbha</s>, placing that <s>vajra</s>-jewel at the site of his own consecration, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This is the consecration of all <s>Buddha</s>s for the sentient realm,
given to me in my hand — a jewel joined to the jewel!

body.translated_text: I.1.11 <s>Vajrateja</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi mahātejamahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavaratnādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyadaṃ sarvatathāgataraśmisamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrateja //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the concentration called the <s>Vajra</s> of the Jewel-Empowerment Arising from the Vow of the Great Radiance Great <s>Bodhisattva</s> (<s>Mahātejamahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavaratnādhiṣṭhānavajra</s>), this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called the Vow of the Radiance of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth from his own heart — <s>Vajrateja</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ mahāsūryamaṇḍalāni bhūtvā, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghano vajrasūryavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajrasūryamaṇḍalātsarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ tathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, sarvatathāgataraśmipramuñcanādīni sarvatathāgatarddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, sumahātejastvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghano mahātejamahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having become great sun-disks, entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s> and manifested as a single solid <s>vajra</s>-sun body, which was established in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s hand. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-sun-disk, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms of all world-realms emerged, and having performed all <s>Tathāgata</s> miraculous displays such as the releasing of the rays of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest, because of the great radiance and firm stability of the <s>Vajrasattva</s> concentration, they became a single solid body — the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> body of Great Radiance — and, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

body.text:
aho hyanupamaṃ tejaḥ sattvadhātvavabhāsanaṃ /
yacchodhayati śuddhānāṃ buddhānāmapi tāyināṃ /
body.translated_text:
Oh! The incomparable radiance that illuminates the sentient realm,
which purifies even the purified <s>Buddha</s>s, the Protectors!

body.text: atha sa vimalatejamahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ dakṣiṇacandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that great <s>Bodhisattva</s> body of Stainless Radiance descended from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s heart, and having stationed himself on a moon-disk to the right of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgataprabhāmaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgataraśmisamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātvanupamatejaḥsarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvatsarvatathāgatasvayaṃprabhāvāptyuttamasiddhaye tadvajrasūryaṃ tasmai mahātejase mahābodhisattvāya tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajraprabho vajraprabha iti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the concentration called the <s>Vajra</s> of the Empowerment of the Light-Halo of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s (<s>Sarvatathāgataprabhāmaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānavajra</s>), for the purpose of experiencing all happiness and well-being through the incomparable radiance of the entire sentient realm as the vow of the radiance of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, up to the supreme accomplishment of attaining the self-luminosity of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-sun upon that great <s>Bodhisattva</s> of Great Radiance (<s>Mahāteja</s>) in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon, by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, he was consecrated with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration as '<s>Vajraprabha</s>, <s>Vajraprabha</s>!'
Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajraprabha</s>, illuminating all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with that <s>vajra</s>-sun, uttered this inspired utterance:

This is that which destroys the darkness of ignorance of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
its splendor exceeding that of suns equal in number to atoms!
I.1.12 <s>Vajraketu</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi ratnaketumahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavaratnādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatāśāparipūraṇasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajraketu //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the concentration called the <s>Vajra</s> of the Jewel-Empowerment Arising from the Vow of the Jewel-Banner Great <s>Bodhisattva</s> (<s>Ratnaketumahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavaratnādhiṣṭhānavajra</s>), this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called the Vow of the Fulfillment of All <s>Tathāgata</s> Wishes issued forth from his own heart — <s>Vajraketu</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharo vicitravarṇarūpālaṅkārasaṃsthānāḥ patākā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghano vajradhvajavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajradhvajavigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniścaritvā, sarvatathāgataratnadhvajocchrepaṇādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, mahāratnaketutvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sadṛḍhatvāccaikaghano ratnaketumahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become banners of variegated colors, forms, and ornamental configurations, emerged, entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, and manifested as a single solid <s>vajra</s>-banner body, which was established in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s hand. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-banner body, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms of all world-realms issued forth, and having performed all <s>Buddha</s>'s miraculous displays such as the raising of the jewel-banners of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest, because of being the great jewel-banner and because of the firm stability of the <s>Vajrasattva</s> concentration, they became a single solid body — the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> body of Jewel-Banner (<s>Ratnaketu</s>) — and, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Oh! I am indeed the incomparable banner of all accomplishments,
which fulfills all purposes for those whose every wish is complete!

body.text: atha sa ratnaketurmahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ vāmacandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that great <s>Bodhisattva</s> body of Jewel-Banner descended from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s heart, and having stationed himself on a moon-disk to the left of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatocchrayādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatacintārājamaṇidhvajocchrepaṇasamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātusarvāśāparipūrisarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvat sarvatathāgatamahārthottamasiddhiprāptiphalahetoḥ tadvajradhvajaṃ tasmai ratnaketave mahābodhisattvāya tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajrayaṣṭirvajrayaṣṭiriti vajranāmabhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the concentration called the <s>Vajra</s> of the Empowerment of the Exaltation of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s (<s>Sarvatathāgatocchrayādhiṣṭhānavajra</s>), for the purpose of the complete fulfillment of all wishes of the entire sentient realm as the vow of raising the wish-fulfilling jewel-banner of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purpose of experiencing all happiness and well-being, up to the attainment of the supreme accomplishment of the great purpose of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s as its cause and fruit — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-banner upon that great <s>Bodhisattva</s> Jewel-Banner (<s>Ratnaketu</s>) in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon, by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, he was consecrated with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration as '<s>Vajrayaṣṭi</s>, <s>Vajrayaṣṭi</s>!'
Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrayaṣṭi</s>, engaging all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) with that <s>vajra</s>-banner, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This is the fulfillment of all wishes of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
called the wish-fulfilling jewel-banner — the method of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>)!

body.translated_text: I.1.13 <s>Vajrahāsa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi nityaprītipramuditendriyamahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavaratnādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgataprītisamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrahāsa //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the concentration called the <s>Vajra</s> of the Jewel-Empowerment Arising from the Vow of the Ever-Joyful with Delighted Faculties Great <s>Bodhisattva</s> (<s>Nityaprītipramuditendriyamahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavaratnādhiṣṭhānavajra</s>), this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called the Vow of Joy of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth from his own heart — <s>Vajrahāsa</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvatathāgatasmitāni bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghano vajrasmitavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, prāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajrasmitavigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahāḥ sarvatathāgatādbhūtādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, nityaprītipramuditendriyatvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghano nityaprītipramuditendriyamahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become the smiles of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, emerged, entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, and manifested as a single solid <s>vajra</s>-smile body, which was established in his hand. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-smile body, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms of all world-realms performed all <s>Buddha</s>'s miraculous displays such as the marvels of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest, and because of being ever joyful with delighted faculties and because of the firm stability of the <s>Vajrasattva</s> concentration, they became a single solid body — the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> body of Ever-Joyful with Delighted Faculties — and, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Oh! I am the great laughter, the great marvel of all supreme ones,
which they always employ, perfectly concentrated, for the <s>Buddha</s>'s purpose!

body.text: atha sa nityaprītipramuditendriyamahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ pṛṣṭhataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that great <s>Bodhisattva</s> body of Ever-Joyful with Delighted Faculties descended from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s heart, and having stationed himself on a moon-disk behind all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatādbhutādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatādbhutotpādasamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātusarvendriyānuttarasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvat sarvatathāgatendriyapariśodhanajñānābhijñāvāptiphalahetostadvajrasmitaṃ tasmai nityaprītipramuditendriyāya mahābodhisattvāya tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajraprītirvajraprītiriti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the concentration called the <s>Vajra</s> of the Empowerment of the Marvel of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s (<s>Sarvatathāgatādbhutādhiṣṭhānavajra</s>), for the purpose of experiencing supreme happiness and well-being of all faculties of the entire sentient realm as the vow of producing the marvel of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, up to the attainment of the <s>abhijñā</s> knowledge of purifying the faculties of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s as its cause and fruit — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-smile upon that great <s>Bodhisattva</s> of Ever-Joyful with Delighted Faculties in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon, by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, he was consecrated with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration as '<s>Vajraprīti</s>, <s>Vajraprīti</s>!'

body.text: atha vajraprītirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ tena vajrasmitena sarvatathāgatān praharṣayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraprīti</s>, delighting all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with that <s>vajra</s>-smile, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This is that which displays the arising of the marvel of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the great joy-producing knowledge unknown to the teachers of other schools!

body.translated_text: The great consecration (<s>mahābhiṣeka</s>), the <s>vyāma</s>-radiance-halo, the purpose of [benefiting] great beings, and the great joy — these are the great consecration-beings of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
I.1.14 <s>Vajradharma</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapyavalokiteśvaramahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavadharmādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgadharmasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajradharma //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the concentration called the <s>Vajra</s> of the <s>Dharma</s>-Empowerment Arising from the Vow of the Great <s>Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara</s> (<s>Avalokiteśvaramahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavadharmādhiṣṭhānavajra</s>), this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called the Vow of the <s>Dharma</s> of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth from his own heart — <s>Vajradharma</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ svabhāvaśuddhadharmasamatājñānasuprativedhatvāt vajrasattvasamādheḥ saddharmaraśmayo bhūtvā viniścaritaḥ, taiḥ saddharmaraśmibhiḥ sarvalokadhātavo 'vabhāsitāḥ, dharmadhātumayāḥ saṃvṛtā abhūvan / sa ca sakalo dharmadhāturbhagavato varocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghanaḥ sarvākāśadhātusamavasaraṇapramāṇo mahāpadmavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tasmād vajrapadmavigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, sarvatathāgatasamādhijñānābhijñādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni sarvalokadhātuṣu kṛtvā, svavalokanaisvaryatvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghanaḥ avalokiteśvaramahābodhisattvakāyaḥsaṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, because of the thorough penetration of the knowledge of the equality of the inherently pure <s>Dharma</s> through the <s>Vajrasattva</s> concentration, having become rays of the True <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Saddharma</s>), issued forth. By those rays of the True <s>Dharma</s>, all world-realms were illuminated and became enveloped, made of the <s>Dharma</s>-element (<s>dharmadhātu</s>). And that entire <s>Dharma</s>-element entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s> and manifested as a single solid great lotus body, equal in measure to the convergence of all space-elements, which was established in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s hand. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-lotus body, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms of all world-realms issued forth, and having performed all <s>Buddha</s>'s miraculous displays such as the <s>samādhi</s> knowledge, <s>abhijñā</s>, and the rest of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in all world-realms, because of the sovereignty of self-observation and because of the firm stability of the <s>Vajrasattva</s> concentration, they became a single solid body — the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> body of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> — and, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Oh! I am indeed the ultimate reality, primordially pure, self-existent,
whereby the purification of <s>dharma</s>s, which are like [opening] lotuses, is realized!

body.text: atha so 'valokiteśvaramahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ purataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that body of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, having become situated on a moon-disc before all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought the command.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatasamādhijñānasamayavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgataviśodhanasamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvātmapariśuddhisarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvat sarvatathāgatadharmajñānābhijñāvāptiphalahetostadvajrapadmaṃ tasma avalokiteśvarāya mahābodhisattvāya saddharmacakravartitve sarvatathāgatadharmakāyābhiṣekeṇābhiṣicya, pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatarvajranetro vajranetra iti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Sarvatathāgatasamādhijñānasamayavajra</s>' (Vajra of the Pledge of the Knowledge of the Concentration of All Tathāgatas), for the purpose of the purification pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purification of the self of all beings without remainder and without exception, for the experience of all happiness and mental delight, and up to the purpose of obtaining the fruit of the <s>dharma</s>-knowledge and direct knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — having consecrated that <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, with the consecration of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for the sovereignty of turning the wheel of the true <s>Dharma</s>, bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-lotus upon him with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration as '<s>Vajranetra</s>, <s>Vajranetra</s>.'

body.text: atha vajranetro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ tadvajrapadmaṃ patravikāsanatayā rāgaviśuddhinirlepasvabhāvāvalokanatathāvalokayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajranetra</s>, observing that <s>vajra</s>-lotus through the opening of its petals, seeing the nature of the purity of passion (<s>rāga</s>) as unstained, uttered this inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>):

children.translated_text: 'This is the realization of the truth of passion (<s>rāgatattva</s>) of all <s>Buddha</s>s;

children.text: ahaṃ mama kare dattaṃ dharma dharme pratiṣṭhitam // iti //
children.translated_text: given to me in my hand, the <s>Dharma</s> established in the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.translated_text: I.1.15 <s>Vajratīkṣṇa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi mañjuśrīmahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavadharmādhiṣṭhānavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyadaṃ sarvatathāgatamahāprajñājñānasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajratīkṣṇa //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Mañjuśrīmahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavadharmādhiṣṭhānavajra</s>' (Vajra of the Empowerment of the Dharma Arising from the Pledge of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī), this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called '<s>Sarvatathāgatamahāprajñājñānasamaya</s>' (Pledge of the Great Wisdom-Knowledge of All Tathāgatas) issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajratīkṣṇa</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ prajñāśastrāṇi bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikadhano vajrakośavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajrakośavigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniścaritvā, sarvatathāgataprajñājñānādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, sumañjuśriyatvāt vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghano mañjuśrīmahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this had issued forth, from the hearts of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very Blessed One <s>Vajradhara</s>, having become weapons of wisdom (<s>prajñāśastra</s>), issued forth, entered the heart of the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, appeared as a solid <s>vajra</s>-sheath form, and was established in the hand of the Blessed One. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-sheath form, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of dust of all world-realms issued forth, performed all the miraculous transformations of all <s>Buddha</s>s such as the wisdom-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and because of being <s>Sumañjuśrī</s> (supremely gentle and glorious), because of the extreme firmness of the <s>Vajrasattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, becoming a solid body of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, stationed in the heart of the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: 'Ah! I am remembered as <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> (Sweet Voice) of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
since from formless wisdom, the quality of voice (<s>ghoṣatva</s>) is obtained.'

body.text: atha sa mañjuśrīmahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ dakṣiṇacandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that body of <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One, having become situated on the right moon-disc of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought the command.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgataprajñājñānavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatakleśacchedanasamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātusarvaduḥkhacchedanasarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvat sarvatathāgataghoṣānugaprajñāpārirpūryuttamasiddhyarthaṃ tasmai mañjuśriye mahābodhisattvāya tadvajrakośaṃ tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajrabuddhirvajrabuddhiriti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ // atha sa vajrabuddhirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ tena vajrakośena sarvatathāgatān praharannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Sarvatathāgataprajñājñānavajra</s>' (Vajra of the Wisdom-Knowledge of All Tathāgatas), for the pledge of cutting through the afflictions of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the cutting through of all suffering of all sentient realms without remainder and without exception, for the experience of all happiness and mental delight, and up to the purpose of the supreme accomplishment of the complete fulfillment of the wisdom that accords with the voice of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-sheath upon that <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration as '<s>Vajrabuddhi</s>, <s>Vajrabuddhi</s>.' Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajrabuddhi</s>, striking all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s with that <s>vajra</s>-sheath, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: 'This is the method of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the cutter of all enemies, the supreme remover of all evil.'

body.translated_text: I.1.16 <s>Vajrahetu</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sahacittotpāditadharmacakrapravartimahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavadharmādhiṣṭhānavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatacakrasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrahetu //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the 'Vajra of the Empowerment of the <s>Dharma</s> Arising from the Pledge of the Great <s>Bodhisattva</s> who Turns the <s>Dharmacakra</s> Simultaneously with the Arising of the Mind,' this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called '<s>Sarvatathāgatacakrasamaya</s>' (Pledge of the Wheel of All Tathāgatas) issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrahetu</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharo vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalādīni sarvatathāgatamaṇḍalāni bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghano vajracakravigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajracakravigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ tathāgatavigrahā viniścaritvā, sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartanādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni sarvalokadhātuṣu kṛtvā, sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartanatvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghanaḥ sahacittotpāditadharmacakrapravartimahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this had issued forth, from the hearts of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very Blessed One <s>Vajradhara</s>, having become all the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s such as the great <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>vajradhātu</s>, issued forth, entered the heart of the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, appeared as a solid <s>vajra</s>-wheel form, and was established in the hand of the Blessed One. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-wheel form, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of dust of all world-realms issued forth, performed all the miraculous transformations of all <s>Buddha</s>s in all world-realms, including the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> simultaneously with the arising of the mind, and because of the turning of the <s>Dharmacakra</s> simultaneously with the arising of the mind, because of the extreme firmness of the <s>Vajrasattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, becoming a solid body of the great <s>bodhisattva</s> who turns the <s>Dharmacakra</s> simultaneously with the arising of the mind, stationed in the heart of the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: 'Ah! I am the <s>vajra</s>-wheel of those whose <s>dharma</s> is the foremost <s>vajra</s>,
for by the mere arising of the mind, the <s>Dharmacakra</s> is turned.'

body.text: atha sa sahacittotpāditadharmacakrapravartimahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ vāmacandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that body of the great <s>bodhisattva</s> who turns the <s>Dharmacakra</s> simultaneously with the arising of the mind, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One, having become situated on the left moon-disc of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought the command.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatacakravajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatamahāmaṇḍalasamayaṃ śeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātupraveśāvaivartikacakrasarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvat sarvatathāgatasaddharmacakrapravartanottamasiddhinimittaṃ tadvajracakraṃ tasmai sahacittotpāditadharmacakrapravartine mahābodhisattvāya tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajramaṇḍo vajramaṇḍa iti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Sarvatathāgatacakravajra</s>' (Vajra of the Wheel of All Tathāgatas), for the pledge of the great <s>maṇḍala</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the entry of all sentient realms without remainder and without exception, for the irreversible wheel, for the experience of all happiness and mental delight, and up to the purpose of the supreme accomplishment of the turning of the true <s>Dharmacakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-wheel upon that great <s>bodhisattva</s> who turns the <s>Dharmacakra</s> simultaneously with the arising of the mind, in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration as '<s>Vajramaṇḍa</s>, <s>Vajramaṇḍa</s>.'

body.text: atha vajramaṇḍo bodhisattvo sahāsattvastena vajracakreṇa sarvatathāgatānavaivartikatve pratiṣṭhāpayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajramaṇḍa</s>, establishing all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s in irreversibility with that <s>vajra</s>-wheel, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: 'This of all <s>Buddha</s>s is the purifier of all <s>dharma</s>s;
the irreversible wheel is known as the seat of enlightenment (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>).'

body.translated_text: I.1.17 <s>Vajrabhāṣa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavānavācamahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavadharmādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatajāpasamayaṃ nāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrabhāṣa //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the 'Vajra of the Empowerment of the <s>Dharma</s> Arising from the Pledge of the Great <s>Bodhisattva</s> of Speech (<s>Avāca</s>),' this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called '<s>Sarvatathāgatajāpasamaya</s>' (Pledge of the Recitation of All Tathāgatas) issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrabhāṣa</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ sarvatathāgatadharmākṣarāṇi bhūtvā viniḥ sṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikadhano vajrajāpavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajrajāpavigrahātsarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, sarvatathāgatadharmatādini sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā svavācatvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghanaḥ avācamahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this had issued forth, from the hearts of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very Blessed One <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having become all the <s>dharma</s>-syllables of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, issued forth, entered the heart of the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, appeared as a solid <s>vajra</s>-recitation form, and was established in the hand of the Blessed One. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-recitation form, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of dust of all world-realms issued forth, performed all the miraculous transformations of all <s>Buddha</s>s including the <s>dharmatā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and because of being his own speech, because of the extreme firmness of the <s>Vajrasattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, becoming a solid body of the great <s>bodhisattva</s> of Speech (<s>Avāca</s>), stationed in the heart of the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: 'Ah! I am remembered as the secret intentional speech (<s>sandhābhāṣa</s>) of the Self-Arisen Ones,
who teach the true <s>Dharma</s> free from the elaboration of words.'

body.text: atha sa avācamahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ pṛṣṭhataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then that body of the great <s>bodhisattva</s> of Speech (<s>Avāca</s>), having descended from the heart of the Blessed One, having become situated on the moon-disc behind all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought the command.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgataguhyavāgvajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatavāgjñānasamayaṃ aśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātuvāksiddhisarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvatsarvatathāgatavāgguhyatāprāptyuttamasiddhaye tadvajrajāpaṃ tasmai avācāya mahābodhisattvāya tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajravāco vajravāca iti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Sarvatathāgataguhyavāgvajra</s>' (Vajra of the Secret Speech of All Tathāgatas), for the pledge of the speech-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the accomplishment of speech for all sentient realms without remainder and without exception, for the experience of all happiness and mental delight, and up to the supreme accomplishment of obtaining the secret of the speech of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-recitation upon that great <s>bodhisattva</s> of Speech (<s>Avāca</s>) in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration as '<s>Vajravāc</s>, <s>Vajravāc</s>.'

body.text: atha vajravāco bodhisattvo mahāsattvastena vajrajāpena sarvatathāgatān saṃllāpayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajravāc</s>, engaging all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s in conversation with that <s>vajra</s>-recitation, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: 'This is the <s>vajra</s>-recitation proclaimed by all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the swift accomplisher of all the <s>mantra</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.'

body.translated_text: The knowledge of <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharmatā</s>, the wisdom-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the knowledge of turning the great wheel, and the knowledge of the cessation of the verbal elaboration of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — these are the great knowledge-beings (<s>jñānasattva</s>s) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
I.1.18 <s>Vajrakarma</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgataviśvakarmamahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavakarmādhiṣṭhānavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, idaṃ sarvatathāgatakarmasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrakarma //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the 'Vajra of the Empowerment of the Action Arising from the Pledge of the Great <s>Bodhisattva</s> of All-Encompassing Action (<s>Viśvakarma</s>) of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called '<s>Sarvatathāgatakarmasamaya</s>' (Pledge of the Action of All Tathāgatas) issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrakarma</s>!
