body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sarvakarmasamatājñānasuprativedhatvāt vajrasattvasamādheḥ sa eva bhagavan vajradharaḥ sarvatathāgatakarmasamayo bhūtvā viniḥsṛtaḥ, taiśca sarvatathāgatakarmaraśmibhiḥ sarvalokadhātavo bhāsitāḥ, sarvatathāgatakarmadhātumayāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ, sa sakalaḥ sarvatathāgatakarmadhāturbhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghanaḥ sarvākāśadhātusamavasaraṇapramāṇastataḥ sarvatathāgatakarmadhātutaḥ karmavajravigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tataḥ karmavajravigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvatathāgatakarmādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, sarvatathāgatānantakarmatvādvajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghanaḥ sarvatathāgataviśvakarmamahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this had issued forth, from the hearts of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, because of the thorough penetration of the knowledge of the equality of all actions, from the <s>Vajrasattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, that very Blessed One <s>Vajradhara</s>, having become the pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s> actions, issued forth, and by those rays of action of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, all world-realms were illuminated and became pervaded by the action-realm of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. That entire action-realm of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having entered the heart of the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, becoming solid, of a measure encompassing the entirety of the space-realm — then from that action-realm of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, an action-<s>vajra</s> form appeared and was established in the hand of the Blessed One. Then from that action-<s>vajra</s> form, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of dust of all world-realms issued forth, performed in all world-realms all the miraculous transformations of all <s>Buddha</s>s including the actions of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and because of the infinite actions of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, because of the extreme firmness of the <s>Vajrasattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, becoming a solid body of the great <s>bodhisattva</s> of All-Encompassing Action (<s>Viśvakarma</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, stationed in the heart of the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: 'Ah! Great am I, the unfailing action of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
for without effort, the <s>vajra</s> action turns for the benefit of <s>Buddha</s>s.'

body.text: atha sa sarvatathāgataviśvakarmamahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ purataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that body of the great <s>bodhisattva</s> of All-Encompassing Action (<s>Viśvakarma</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having descended from the heart of the Blessed One, having become situated on the moon-disc before all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought the command.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatāmoghavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatapūjāpravartanādyaprameyāmoghasarvakarmavidhivistarasamayaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātusarvakarmasiddhisarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvat sarvatathāgatavajrakarmatājñānābhijñottamasiddhiphalahetostatkarmavajraṃ tasmai sarvatathāgataviśvakarmaṇe mahābodhisattvāya sarvakarmacakravartitve sarvatathāgatavajrābhiṣekeṇābhiṣicya, pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajraviśvo vajraviśva iti vajramahābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Sarvatathāgatāmoghavajra</s>' (Unfailing Vajra of All Tathāgatas), for the pledge of the detailed exposition of the immeasurable unfailing procedures of all actions beginning with the offering of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the accomplishment of all actions for all sentient realms without remainder and without exception, for the experience of all happiness and mental delight, and up to the purpose of the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the knowledge and direct knowledge of the <s>vajra</s>-action-nature of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — having consecrated that great <s>bodhisattva</s> of All-Encompassing Action (<s>Viśvakarma</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-consecration of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for the sovereignty of turning all actions, bestowed that action-<s>vajra</s> upon him with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the great <s>vajra</s>-consecration as '<s>Vajraviśva</s>, <s>Vajraviśva</s>.'

body.text: atha vajraviśvo bodhisattvo mahāsatvastadvajraṃ svahṛdi sthāpya, sarvatathāgatakarmatāyānniyojayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajraviśva</s>, having placed that <s>vajra</s> in his own heart, engaging [all beings] in the action-nature of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: 'This of all <s>Buddha</s>s is the supreme performer of all-encompassing action;

children.text: ahaṃ mama kare dattaṃ viśve viśvaṃ niyojitam // iti //
children.translated_text: I have given into my hand — the entire universe has been yoked to all! Thus.

body.translated_text: I.1.19 <s>Vajrarakṣa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān duryodhanavīryamahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavakarmādhiṣṭhānavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatarakṣāsamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrarakṣa //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the empowerment of beings born from the pledge of the great <s>Bodhisattva Duryodhanavīrya</s> (Invincible Valor),' this essence of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the pledge of the protection of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrarakṣa</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajrapāṇirdṛḍhakavacāni bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghano mahāvajrakavacavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavataḥ pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajrakavacavigrahātsarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, sarvatathāgatarakṣāvidhivistarakarmādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, duryodhanavīryatvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghano duryodhanavīryamahābodhisattvavigrahaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having become firm armor (<s>dṛḍhakavaca</s>) and emerged, entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, and having become a single solid great <s>vajra</s>-armor form, manifested and was established in the hand of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-armor form, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and having performed the miraculous activities of all <s>Buddha</s>s — the elaboration of the rites of protection of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest — because of his invincible valor (<s>duryodhanavīryatva</s>) and because of the extreme firmness of the <s>vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, having become a single solid body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Duryodhanavīrya</s>, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, he uttered this inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>):

children.translated_text: Ah! I am the armor made of valor, exceedingly firm, of those who are firm in nature,
for, because of [my] firmness, I am supreme in making <s>vajra</s>-bodies for the bodiless!

body.text: atha sa duryodhanavīryamahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ dakṣiṇacandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūttvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Duryodhanavīrya</s>, having descended from the heart of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and having stationed himself on the moon-disc to the right of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatadṛḍhavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatavīryapāramitāsamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātuparitrāṇasarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvatsarvatathāgatavajrakāyaprāptyuttamasiddhihetostadvajravarma tasmai duryodhanavīryāya mahābodhisattvāya pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajramitro vajramitra iti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the firm <s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' for the purpose of experiencing the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor) pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the protection of the entire limitless and inexhaustible realm of beings, all happiness and mental satisfaction, up to the attainment of the supreme accomplishment of obtaining the <s>vajra</s>-body of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-armor upon that great <s>Bodhisattva Duryodhanavīrya</s> with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration [proclaiming] '<s>Vajramitra</s>! <s>Vajramitra</s>!'

body.text: atha vajramitro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ tena vajravarmeṇa sarvatathāgatān kavacayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramitra</s>, armoring all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with that <s>vajra</s>-armor, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This is that supreme armor of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>-<s>kavaca</s>) of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the great protection of firm valor, proclaimed as great friendship (<s>mahāmitra</s>)! Thus.

body.translated_text: I.1.20 <s>Vajrayakṣa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvamārapramārdemahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavakarmādhiṣṭhānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatopāyasamayaṃ nāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrayakṣa //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the empowerment of beings born from the pledge of the great <s>Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin</s> (Crusher of All <s>Māra</s>s),' this essence of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the pledge of skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrayakṣa</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharo mahādaṃṣṭrāyudhāni bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghano vajradaṃṣṭrāvigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajradaṃṣṭrāvigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniścaritvā, sarvatathāgataraudravinayādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, sarvamārasupramarditvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghanaḥ sarvamārapramardimahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become great fang-weapons (<s>mahādaṃṣṭrāyudha</s>) and emerged, entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, and having become a single solid <s>vajra</s>-fang form, manifested and was established in [his] hand. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-fang form, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and having performed the miraculous activities of all <s>Buddha</s>s — the wrathful discipline (<s>raudravinaya</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest — because of completely crushing all <s>Māra</s>s and because of the extreme firmness of the <s>vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, having become a single solid body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin</s>, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, he uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am the great skillful means (<s>mahopāya</s>) of the <s>Buddha</s>s who are compassionate in nature,
for, though peaceful, for the sake of beings they even assume wrathful form!

body.text: atha sa sarvamārapramardimahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ vāmacandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then that body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin</s>, having descended from the heart of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and having stationed himself on the moon-disc to the left of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatapracaṇḍavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgataduṣṭavinayasamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣatvadhātvabhayasarvasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvatsarvatathāgatamahopāyajñānābhijñāvāptyuttamasiddhiphalahetostadvajradaṃṣṭrāyudhaṃ tasmai sarvamārapramardine mahābodhisattvāya tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajracaṇḍo vajracaṇḍa iti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the fierce <s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' for the purpose of experiencing the pledge of disciplining the wicked of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, fearlessness for the entire limitless and inexhaustible realm of beings, all happiness and mental satisfaction, up to the attainment of the supreme accomplishment of the great skillful-means wisdom and <s>abhijñā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-fang weapon upon that great <s>Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin</s> in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration [proclaiming] '<s>Vajracaṇḍa</s>! <s>Vajracaṇḍa</s>!'

body.text: atha vajracaṇḍo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastadvajradaṃṣṭrāyudhaṃ svamukhe pratiṣṭhāpya, sarvatathāgatān bhīṣayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajracaṇḍa</s>, placing that <s>vajra</s>-fang weapon in his own mouth, terrifying all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This is that supreme tamer of all the wicked of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the sharp <s>vajra</s>-fang weapon — the skillful means of those compassionate in nature! Thus.

body.translated_text: I.1.21 <s>Vajrasandhi</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatamuṣṭimahābodhisattvasamayasaṃbhavakarmādhiṣṭhānavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyadaṃ sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajrabandhasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrasandhi //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the empowerment of beings born from the pledge of the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the Fist of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' this essence of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the pledge of the <s>vajra</s>-bond of body, speech, and mind of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrasandhi</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvatathāgatasarvamudrābandhā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭvaikaghano vajrabandhavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, pāṇau pratiṣṭhitaḥ / atha tato vajrabandhavigrahāt sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniścaritvā, sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvatathāgatamudrājñānādīni sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni kṛtvā, sarvatathāgatamahāmuṣṭisubandhatvād vajrasattvasamādheḥ sudṛḍhatvāccaikaghanaḥ sarvatathāgatamuṣṭimahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become the bonds of all <s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and emerged, entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, and having become a single solid <s>vajra</s>-bond form, manifested and was established in [his] hand. Then from that <s>vajra</s>-bond form, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and having performed the miraculous activities of all <s>Buddha</s>s — the <s>mudrā</s>-wisdom of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest — in all world-realms, because of the firmness of the great fist bond of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and because of the extreme firmness of the <s>vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, having become a single solid body of the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the Fist of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, he uttered this inspired utterance:

children.text: aho hi sudṛḍho bandhaḥ samayo 'haṃ dṛḍhātmanāṃ /
children.translated_text: Ah! I am the exceedingly firm bond — the pledge of those firm in nature,
for, for the accomplishment of all wishes, [I am] the binding even of the liberated!

body.text: atha sarvatathāgatamuṣṭimahābodhisattvakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ pṛṣṭhataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then the body of the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the Fist of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having descended from the heart of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and having stationed himself on the moon-disc behind all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatasamayavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya, sarvatathāgatamudrābandhasamayamaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātusarvatathāgatadevatāsānnidhyakalpanāt sarvasiddhisukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvatsarvatathāgatasarvajñānamudrādhipatyottamasiddhiphalahetostadvajrabandhaṃ tasmai sarvatathāgatamuṣṭaye mahābodhisattvāya tathaiva pāṇibhyāmanuprādāt / tataḥ sarvatathāgatairvajramuṣṭirvajramuṣṭiriti vajranāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣiktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the pledge-<s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' for the purpose of experiencing all accomplishments, happiness, and mental satisfaction through the approximation of the presence of the deities of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the <s>mudrā</s>-bond pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for the entire limitless and inexhaustible realm of beings, up to the attainment of the supreme accomplishment of the sovereignty of the omniscience-<s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — bestowed that <s>vajra</s>-bond upon that great <s>Bodhisattva</s> of the Fist of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s in the same manner with both hands. Thereupon he was consecrated by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration [proclaiming] '<s>Vajramuṣṭi</s>! <s>Vajramuṣṭi</s>!'

body.text: atha sa vajramuṣṭirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ tena vajrabandhena sarvatathāgatān bandhayannidamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi</s>, binding all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with that <s>vajra</s>-bond, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This is that greatly firm <s>mudrā</s>-bond of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
the inviolable pledge for the swift accomplishment of all <s>Buddha</s>s! Thus.

body.text: sarvatathāgatapūjāvidhivistarakarma, mahāvīryadṛḍhakavacaḥ, sarvatathāgatamahopāyaḥ, sarvamudrājñānaṃ ceti / sarvatathāgatamahākarmasattvāḥ //
body.translated_text: The elaboration of the rites of worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the greatly valorous firm armor, the great skillful means of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and the omniscience of all <s>mudrā</s>s — these are the great activity-beings (<s>mahākarmasattva</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
I.1.22 <s>Sattvavajrī</s>

body.text: atha khalvakṣobhyastathāgato bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya sarvatathāgatajñānāni niṣpādya, sarvatathāgatajñānamudraṇārthaṃ vajrāpāramitāsamayobhdavavajrādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgatavajrasamayāṃ nāma sarvatathāgatamudrāṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra sattvavajri //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Akṣobhya Tathāgata</s>, having accomplished the wisdoms of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of sealing with the wisdom of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the <s>vajrapāramitā</s>' and this <s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the <s>vajra</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Sattvavajrī</s>!

body.text:
athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyo vajraraśmayo viniścaritāḥ /
tebhyaśca vajraraśmibhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā bhūtvā, sarvatathāgatavajrapāramitājñānānyāmudrya, punarapyekaghanaḥ sarvalokadhātusamavasaraṇapramāṇo mahāvajravigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavatovairocanasya purataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, idamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>vajra</s>-rays issued forth. And from those <s>vajra</s>-rays, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms, sealed the <s>vajrapāramitā</s>-wisdoms of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and having again become a single solid great <s>vajra</s>-form equal in measure to the assembly of all world-realms, manifested and, having stationed himself before <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s> resting on a moon-disc, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am the firm being-<s>vajra</s> (<s>sattvavajra</s>) of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
for, because of [my] firmness, though bodiless, I have attained the state of having a <s>vajra</s>-body! Thus.

body.translated_text: I.1.23 <s>Ratnavajrī</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān ratnasaṃbhavastathāgataḥ bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya sarvatathāgatajñānamudraṇārthaṃ ratnapāramitāsamayasaṃbhavavajrādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ vajraratnasamayāṃ nāma svamudrāṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra ratnavajri //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of sealing with the wisdom of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the <s>ratnapāramitā</s> (jewel-perfection)' and this <s>mudrā</s> of his own called 'the <s>vajra</s>-jewel pledge' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Ratnavajrī</s>!

body.text: athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyo ratnaraśmayo viniścaritāḥ / tebhyo ratnaraśmibhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā bhūtvā, sarvatathāgatajñānānyāmudrya, punarapyekaghanaḥ sarvalokadhātusamavasaraṇapramāṇo mahāvajraratnavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya dakṣiṇapārśve candramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, idamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, jewel-rays issued forth. From those jewel-rays, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms, sealed the wisdoms of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and having again become a single solid great <s>vajra</s>-jewel form equal in measure to the assembly of all world-realms, manifested and, having stationed himself to the right of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s> resting on a moon-disc, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am regarded as the jewel-<s>vajra</s> (<s>ratnavajra</s>) of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
for I am the firm mode of consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) of all <s>mudrā</s>s! Thus.

body.translated_text: I.1.24 <s>Dharmavajrī</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān lokeśvararājastathāgato bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya sarvatathāgatajñānamudraṇārthaṃ dharmapāramitāsamayodbhavavajrādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ dharmasamayāṃ nāma svamudrāṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra dharma vajri //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Lokeśvararāja Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of sealing with the wisdom of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the <s>dharmapāramitā</s> (dharma-perfection)' and this <s>mudrā</s> of his own called 'the <s>dharma</s>-pledge' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Dharmavajrī</s>!

body.text: athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ padmaraśmayo viniścaritāḥ / tebhyaḥ padmaraśmibhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā bhūtvā, sarvatathāgatajñānānyāmudrya, punarapyekaghanaḥ sarvalokadhātusamavasaraṇapramāṇo mahāvajrapadmavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya pṛṣṭhataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, as soon as this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, lotus-rays issued forth. From those lotus-rays, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms, sealed the wisdoms of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and having again become a single solid great <s>vajra</s>-lotus form equal in measure to the assembly of all world-realms, manifested and, having stationed himself behind <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s> resting on a moon-disc, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.text: aho hi sarvabuddhānāṃ dharmavajraṃ ahaṃ śuci /
children.translated_text: Ah! I am the pure <s>dharma</s>-<s>vajra</s> (<s>dharmavajra</s>) of all <s>Buddha</s>s,

children.text: yatsvabhāvaviśuddhyā vai rāgo 'pi hi sunirmalaḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: for, by the purity of [its] own nature (<s>svabhāvaviśuddhi</s>), even passion (<s>rāga</s>) is indeed perfectly pure! Thus.

body.translated_text: I.1.25 <s>Karmavajrī</s>

body.text: atha bhagavānamoghasiddhistathāgato bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya sarvatathāgatajñānamudraṇārthaṃ karmapāramitāsaṃbhavavajrādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgatakarmasamayāṃ nāma svamudrāṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra karmavajri //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of sealing with the wisdom of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the <s>karmapāramitā</s> (activity-perfection)' and this <s>mudrā</s> of his own called 'the pledge of the activity of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth from his own heart: <s>Karmavajrī</s>!

body.text: athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sarvakarmaśmayo viniścaritāḥ / tebhyaśca sarvatathāgatakarmaraśmimabhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā bhūtvā, sarvatathāgatajñānānyamudrya, punarapyekaghanaḥ sarvalokadhātusamavasaraṇapramāṇaḥ sarvatomukho mahākarmavajravigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya vāmapārśve candramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, idamudānamudānayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, all activity-rays issued forth. And from those activity-rays of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms, having sealed all the wisdoms of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again becoming a single solid [form], equal in measure to the assembly of all world-realms, facing all directions, a great activity-<s>vajra</s> body manifested and, having stationed himself on a moon-disc to the left of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am indeed the great activity-<s>vajra</s> of all <s>Buddha</s>s, abundant,
for being one alone, I am the doer of good deeds for the entire realm of beings!

body.text: sarvatathāgatajñānasamayā, mahābhiṣekā, vajradharmatā, sarvapūjā ceti / sarvatathāgatapāramitāḥ //
body.translated_text: The wisdom-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the great consecration, the <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>-nature, and the complete offering — these are the <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
I.1.26 <s>Vajralāsyā</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanaḥ punarapi sarvatathāgataratipūjāsamayasaṃbhavavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgatakulamahādevīṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajralāsye //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the offering of delight of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' caused this great goddess of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajralāsye</s>!

body.text: athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyo vajramudrā viniḥsṛtāḥ / tebhyo vajramudrāmukhabhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā bhūtvā, punarapyekaghanā mahādevī vajrasattvasadṛśātmabhāvā vicitravarṇarūpaliṅgeryāpathā sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣitā sarvatathāgatakulasaṃgrahabhūtā vajrasattvadayitā saṃbhūya, bhagavato 'kṣobhyamaṇḍalavāmapārśve candramaṇḍalāśritā bhūtvā, idamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>vajra</s>-seals (<s>mudrā</s>) issued forth. From those <s>vajra</s>-seal-tips, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms, then becoming a single solid great goddess, similar in form to <s>Vajrasattva</s>, of various colors, forms, marks, and deportments, adorned with all ornaments, being the embodiment of the gathering of all <s>Tathāgata</s> families, the beloved of <s>Vajrasattva</s>, having stationed herself on a moon-disc to the left of <s>Bhagavān Akṣobhya</s>'s <s>maṇḍala</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.text: aho na sadṛśī me 'sti pūjā hyanyā svayaṃbhuvāṃ /
children.translated_text: Ah! There is no offering comparable to me among the Self-Existent Ones,
for through offerings of desire and delight, all offerings proceed!

body.translated_text: I.1.27 <s>Vajramālā</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgataratnamālābhiṣekasamayodbhavavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya māṃ sarvatathāgatakulamahādevīṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajramāle /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the jewel-garland consecration of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' caused this great goddess of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajramāle</s>!

body.text: athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyo mahāratnamudrā viniḥsṛtāḥ / tābhyo mahāratnamudrābhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā bhūtvā, ekaghanāṃ vajramālāṃ mahādevīṃ tathaiva saṃbhūya, bhagavato ratnasaṃbhavamaṇḍalavāmapārśve pūrṇacandramaṇḍalāśritā bhūtvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, great jewel-seals issued forth. From those great jewel-seals, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms, became a single solid <s>Vajramālā</s> great goddess in the same manner, and having stationed herself on a full moon-disc to the left of <s>Bhagavān Ratnasaṃbhava</s>'s <s>maṇḍala</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am indeed the incomparable one, celebrated as the jewel-offering,
whereby, being duly worshipped, they rule the supreme sovereignty of the three realms!

body.translated_text: I.1.28 <s>Vajragītā</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatasaṃgītisamayasaṃbhavavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgatakulamahādevīṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajragīte //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the chanting (<s>saṃgīti</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' caused this great goddess of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajragīte</s>!

body.text: athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdaye 'bhyaḥ sarvatathāgatadharmamudrā viniścaritāḥ / tābhyaśca sarvatathāgatadharmamudrābhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā bhūtvā, punarapyekaghanāṃ vajragītāṃ mahādevīṃ saṃbhūya, bhagavato lokeśvararājamaṇḍalavāmapārśve candramaṇḍalāśritā bhūtvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>dharma</s>-seals of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth. From those <s>dharma</s>-seals of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms, then became a single solid <s>Vajragītā</s> great goddess, and having stationed herself on a moon-disc to the left of <s>Bhagavān Lokeśvararāja</s>'s <s>maṇḍala</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am indeed the offering consisting of chanting for all the Omniscient Ones,
for they satisfy with offerings even those who are like echoes!

body.translated_text: I.1.29 <s>Vajranṛtyā</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatanṛtyapūjāsamayodbhavavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgatakulamahādevīṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajranṛtye /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the dance-offering of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' caused this great goddess of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajranṛtye</s>!

body.text: athāsmina viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sarvatathāgatanṛtyapūjāvidhivistarā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtāḥ / tebhyaśca sarvatathāgatasarvanṛttapūjāvidhivistarebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā bhūtvā, punarapyekaghanāṃ vajranṛttamahādevīṃ saṃbhūya, bhagavato amoghasiddhestathāgatasya maṇḍalavāmapārśve pūrṇacandramaṇḍalāśritā bhūtvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the extensive rites of the dance-offering of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s manifested and issued forth. From those extensive rites of the complete dance-offering of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms, then became a single solid <s>Vajranṛtta</s> great goddess, and having stationed herself on a full moon-disc to the left of <s>Bhagavān Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata</s>'s <s>maṇḍala</s>, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am indeed the exalted offering of all who perform the purpose of all offerings,
for through the rite of <s>vajra</s>-dance, the offering to the <s>Buddha</s>s is accomplished!

body.translated_text: The pledge of the unsurpassed happiness and satisfaction of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the garland of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the song (<s>gāthā</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and the performer of the unsurpassed offering-activity of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — these are the secret offerings of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
I.1.30 <s>Vajradhūpa</s>

body.text: atha punarapi bhagavān akṣobhyastathāgato bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya pūjāpratipūjārtha sarvatathāgatapralhādanasamayodbhavavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgatagaṇikāṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajradhūpe //
body.translated_text: Then again, <s>Bhagavān Akṣobhya Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of the offering and counter-offering to <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of gladdening all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' caused this courtesan (<s>gaṇikā</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajradhūpe</s>!

body.text: athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ anekavidhā dhūpapūjāmeghavyūhāḥ sarvavajradhātuspharaṇā bhūtvā viniścaritāḥ / tebhyaśca dhūpapūjāmeghasamudrebhyaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, punarapyekaghano vajradhūpadevatākāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya koṇe vāmapārśve candramaṇḍalāśritā bhūtvedamudānamudānayati sma /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become various incense-offering cloud-arrays pervading all <s>vajra</s>-elements, issued forth. And from those incense-offering cloud-oceans, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and then becoming a single solid <s>Vajradhūpa</s> deity-body, having stationed herself on a moon-disc at the left corner of <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! This is indeed a great offering, gladdening and auspicious,
for through the yoga of entering into beings, awakening is swiftly attained!

body.translated_text: I.1.31 <s>Vajrapuṣpa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān ratnasaṃbhavastathāgato bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya pūjāpratipūjārtha ratnābharaṇapūjāsamayasaṃbhavavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgatapratīhārīṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrapuṣpe //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of the offering and counter-offering to <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the jewel-ornament offering of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' caused this attendant (<s>pratīhārī</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrapuṣpe</s>!

body.text: athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvapuṣpapūjāvyūhāḥ sarvākāśadhātuspharaṇā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtāstebhyaśca sarvapuṣpapūjāvyūhebhyaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, punarapyekaghano vajrapuṣpadevatākāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya vāmakoṇe candramaṇḍalāśritā bhūtvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become flower-offering arrays pervading all space-elements, issued forth. And from those flower-offering arrays, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and then becoming a single solid <s>Vajrapuṣpa</s> deity-body, having stationed herself on a moon-disc at the left corner of <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am indeed the flower-offering, the creator of all ornaments,
for by worshipping the <s>Tathāgata</s> jewel-nature, it is swiftly attained!

body.translated_text: I.1.32 <s>Vajrāloka</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān lokeśvararājastathāgato bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya pūjāpratipūjārtha sarvatathāgatālokapūjāsamayodbhavavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgatadūtīṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrāloke /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Lokeśvararāja Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of the offering and counter-offering to <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the light-offering of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' caused this messenger (<s>dūtī</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrāloke</s>!

body.text: athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvālokapūjāvyūhāḥ sakaladharmadhātuspharaṇā bhūtvā viniścaritāḥ / tebhyaśca sarvālokapūjāvyūhebhyaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, punarapyekaghano vajrālokadevatākāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya vāmakoṇe candramaṇḍalāśritā bhūtvā, idamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become light-offering arrays pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, issued forth. And from those light-offering arrays, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and then becoming a single solid <s>Vajrāloka</s> deity-body, having stationed herself on a moon-disc at the left corner of <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.text: aho hyahaṃ mahodārā pūjā dīpamayī śubhā /
children.translated_text: Ah! I am indeed a most exalted offering, consisting of lamps, auspicious,
for being radiant, one swiftly obtains the vision of all <s>Buddha</s>s!

body.translated_text: I.1.33 <s>Vajragandha</s>

body.text: atha bhagavānamoghasiddhistathāgato bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya pūjāpratipūjārthaṃ sarvatathāgatagandhapajāsamayasaṃbhavavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ sarvatathāgataceṭīṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajragandhe //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of the offering and counter-offering to <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of the perfume-offering of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' caused this maid-servant (<s>ceṭī</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajragandhe</s>!

body.text: athāsyāṃ viniḥsṛtamātrāyāṃ sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvagandhapūjāvyūhāḥ sarvalokadhātuspharaṇā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtāḥ / tebhyaśca gandhapūjāvyūhebhyaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥ samāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya punarapyekaghano vajragandhadevatākāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya vāmakoṇe candramaṇḍalāśritā bhatvedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become perfume-offering arrays pervading all world-realms, issued forth. And from those perfume-offering arrays, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and then becoming a single solid <s>Vajragandha</s> deity-body, having stationed herself on a moon-disc at the left corner of <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am the divine, delightful offering consisting of perfume,

children.text: yattathāgatagandho vai sarvakāye dadāti hi // iti //
children.translated_text: for it bestows the fragrance of the <s>Tathāgata</s> upon the entire body!

body.translated_text: The wisdom-entry of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the accumulation of factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the <s>dharma</s>-light of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and the fragrance of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and liberation-knowledge-and-vision — these are the commission-bearers of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
I.1.34 <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgataḥ punarapi sarvatathāgatasamayāṃ kuśamahāsattvasamayasaṃbhavasattvavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyeyaṃ sarvatathāgatasarvamudrāgaṇapatiṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrāṃkuśa //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of beings born from the pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-pledge-hook great beings,' caused this lord of all <s>mudrā</s>-hosts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātra sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvatathāgatasarvamudrāgaṇā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtaḥ / tebhyaśca sarvatathāgatamudrāgaṇebhyaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, punarapyekaghano vajrāṅkuśamahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya vajradvāramadhye candramaṇḍalāśrito bhatvā, sarvatathāgatasamayānākarṣayanna, idamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become all <s>mudrā</s>-hosts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, issued forth. And from those <s>mudrā</s>-hosts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and then becoming a single solid body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa</s>, having stationed himself on a moon-disc at the <s>vajra</s>-gate in the middle of <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion, attracting all the pledges (<s>samaya</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am indeed the firm great attractor of all <s>Buddha</s>s,

children.text: yanmayā hi samākṛṣṭā bhajante sarvamaṇḍalam // iti //
children.translated_text: for those attracted by me resort to every <s>maṇḍala</s>!

body.translated_text: I.1.35 <s>Vajrapāśa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatasamayapraveśamahāsattvasamayasaṃbhavasattvavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadya maṃ sarvatathāgatamudrāpraveśapratīhāraṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrapāśa //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of beings born from the pledge of the great being of pledge-entry of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' caused this gateway-guard (<s>pratīhāra</s>) of <s>mudrā</s>-entry of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrapāśa</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvatathāgatasamayapraveśamudrāgaṇā bhūtvā viniścaritaḥ / tebhyaśca sarvatathāgatasamayapraveśamudrāgaṇebhyaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, punarapyekaghano vajrapāśamahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya ratnadvāramadhye candramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā sarvatathāgatāṃ praveśayann, idamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become <s>mudrā</s>-hosts of the pledge-entry of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, issued forth. And from those <s>mudrā</s>-hosts of the pledge-entry of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s>-forms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms emerged, and then becoming a single solid body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāśa</s>, having stationed himself on a moon-disc at the jewel-gate in the middle of <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion, causing all <s>Tathāgata</s>s to enter, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am indeed the firm <s>vajra</s>-noose of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
for even those who have entered into all atoms are made to enter again by me!

body.translated_text: I.1.36 <s>Vajrasphoṭa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatasamayasphoṭamahāsattvasamayodbhavasattvavajrannāmasamādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ sarvatathāgatasamayabandhannāma sarvatathāgatadūtaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrasphoṭa //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the <s>Vajra</s> of the Being Born from the Vow of the Great Being who Bursts Open the Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s (<s>Sarvatathāgatasamayasphoṭamahāsattvasamayodbhavasattvavajra</s>), this messenger of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called the Binding of the Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth from his own heart — <s>Vajrasphoṭa</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvatathāgatasamayabandhamudrāgaṇā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtastebhyaśca sarvatathāgatasamayabandhasarvamudrāgaṇebhyaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, ekaghano vajrasphoṭamahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya dharmadvāramadhye candramaṇḍalāśrito bhatvā, sarvatathāgatāna bandhayanna, idamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become the assemblies of the pledge-binding <s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, emerged. And from all those assemblies of the pledge-binding <s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms of all world-realms issued forth, became a single solid body — the great <s>Bodhisattva</s> body of <s>Vajrasphoṭa</s> — and having stationed himself on a moon-disk in the middle of the <s>Dharma</s>-gate of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-crest palace, binding all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Oh! I am indeed the firm <s>vajra</s>-burst of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
whereby for those freed from all bonds, binding is desired for the sake of beings!

body.translated_text: I.1.37 <s>Vajrāveśa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatāveśamahāsattvasamayasaṃbhavasattvavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ sarvatathāgatasarvamudrāceṭaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrāveśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the <s>Vajra</s> of the Being Born from the Vow of the Great Being of the Possession of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s (<s>Sarvatathāgatāveśamahāsattvasamayasaṃbhavasattvavajra</s>), this servant of all <s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth from his own heart — <s>Vajrāveśa</s>!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvatathāgatasarvamudrāgaṇā bhūtvā viniścaritaḥ / tebhyaśca sarvatathāgatasarvamudrāgaṇebhyaḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥ samāstathāgatavigrahā viniḥsṛtya, ekaghano vajrāveśamahābodhisattvavigrahaḥ prādurbhūya, bhagavato vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya karmadvāramadhye candramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, sarvatathāgatānāveśayanna, idamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become the assemblies of all <s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, issued forth. And from all those assemblies of all <s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s> forms equal in number to the atoms of all world-realms issued forth, became a single solid body — the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrāveśa</s> — and having stationed himself on a moon-disk in the middle of the Karma-gate of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-crest palace, possessing all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Oh! I am indeed the firm <s>vajra</s>-possession of all <s>Buddha</s>s,

children.text: yatsarvapatayo bhūtvā ceṭā api bhavanti hi // iti //
children.translated_text: whereby even those who have become lords of all become servants indeed!

body.text: savatathāgatasamākarṣaṇaṃ, praveśo, bandhaḥ, vaśīkaraṇaṃ ceti / sarvatathāgatājñākarāḥ //
body.translated_text: The attracting of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the entry, the binding, and the subjugation — these are the command-executors of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatāsamājādhiṣṭhānāya vajrācchaṭikāsaṃjñāmakārṣīt / idaṃ sarvatathāgatasamājādhiṣṭhānahṛdayamabhāṣata vajrasamāja //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the empowerment of the assembly of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, made the signal of the <s>vajra</s> finger-snap and spoke this heart of the empowerment of the assembly of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — <s>Vajrasamāja</s>!

body.text: atha tena kṣapālavamuhūrtena sarvatathāgatācchaṭikāsaṃjñāsaṃcoditāḥ sarvalokadhātuprasarameghasamudreṣu sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāstathāgatāḥ sabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalāḥ samājamāpadya, yena bhagavān vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgāro yena ca bhagavān vairocanastenopajagmurupetya oṃ sarvatathāgatapādavandanāṅkaromi // ityenena prakṛtisiddhena mantreṇa rucijaptena sarvatathāgatapādavandanāṃ kṛtvedamudānamudānayāmāsuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, in that very instant, all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — equal in number to the atoms of all world-realms, aroused by the signal of the finger-snap of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, in the cloud-oceans pervading all world-realms — together with their <s>Bodhisattva</s> retinue <s>maṇḍala</s>s, having arrived at the assembly, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-crest palace and the <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, and with this naturally accomplished <s>mantra</s> spoken with splendor — 'Oṃ, I perform homage at the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' — having performed the homage at the feet of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, they uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Oh! The worship of the <s>Bodhisattva Samantabhadra</s>,
whereby a <s>Tathāgata</s> shines in the midst of the wheel of <s>Tathāgata</s>s!

body.text: athedamuktvā te daśadiksarvalokadhātusannipatitāḥ sarvatathāgatāḥ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānena bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye sabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalāḥ praviṣṭāḥ / tebhyaśca sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ svāni svāni bodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalāni viniḥsṛtya bhagavato vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya sarvapārśveṣu maṇḍalībhūtvā samāpadyāvasthitā idamudānamudānayāmāsuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, having said this, all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s who had assembled from the world-realms of the ten directions, by the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s> together with their <s>Bodhisattva</s> retinue <s>maṇḍala</s>s. And from the hearts of all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, their respective <s>Bodhisattva</s> retinue <s>maṇḍala</s>s emerged and stationed themselves in <s>maṇḍala</s> formation on all sides of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-crest palace, and having arrived at the assembly, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Oh! The great magnanimity of all <s>Buddha</s>s, beginningless,
whereby <s>Buddha</s>s equal in number to all atoms have indeed become one!

body.translated_text: Hymn of 108 Names of <s>Mahāvajradhara</s>

body.text: atha bhagavantaḥ sarvatathāgatāḥ punarapi samājamāgamyāsya vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalasyādhiṣṭhānāyāśeṣānavaśeṣasya ca sattvadhātoḥ paritrāṇasarvahitasukhāvāptyai yāvatsarvatathāgatasamatājñānābhijñābhisaṃbodhyuttamasiddhaye bhagavantaṃ sarvatathāgatādhipatiṃ svavajrasattvamanādinidhanaṃ mahāvajradharamanena nāmāṣṭaśatenādhyeṣitavantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having again arrived at the assembly, for the empowerment of this great <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> and for the rescue, benefit, happiness, and attainment of the entire limitless and inexhaustible sentient realm, up to the supreme accomplishment of awakening to the <s>abhijñā</s>-knowledge of the equality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — entreated the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the sovereign of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, their own <s>Vajrasattva</s>, beginningless and endless, <s>Mahāvajradhara</s>, with this hymn of one hundred and eight names:

children.translated_text: <s>Vajrasattva</s>, great being, <s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,
<s>Samantabhadra</s>, first of the <s>vajra</s>, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, homage to you! (1)
<s>Vajrarāja</s>, foremost of the well-awakened, <s>Tathāgata</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-hook,
<s>Amogharāja</s>, foremost of the <s>vajra</s>, <s>Vajrākarṣa</s>, homage to you! (2)
<s>Vajrarāga</s>, of great bliss, <s>Vajravāṇa</s>, subjugator,
bearer of passion, great <s>vajra</s>, <s>Vajracāpa</s>, homage to you! (3)
<s>Vajrasādhu</s>, foremost of excellent beings, <s>Vajratuṣṭi</s>, of great delight,
king of joy, foremost of the <s>vajra</s>, <s>Vajraharṣa</s>, homage to you! (4)
<s>Vajraratna</s>, excellent <s>vajra</s>-purpose, <s>Vajrākāśa</s>, great jewel,
<s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, <s>vajra</s>-rich, <s>Vajragarbha</s>, homage to you! (5)
<s>Vajrateja</s>, of great flame, <s>Vajrasūrya</s>, light of the <s>Jina</s>s,
<s>Vajraraśmi</s>, of great radiance, <s>Vajraprabha</s>, homage to you! (6)
<s>Vajraketu</s>, excellent being-purpose, <s>Vajradhvaja</s>, great satisfier,
<s>Ratnaketu</s>, great <s>vajra</s>, <s>Vajrayaṣṭi</s>, homage to you! (7)
<s>Vajrahāsa</s>, great laughter, <s>Vajrasmita</s>, great marvel,
Joy and delight, foremost of the <s>vajra</s>, <s>Vajraprīti</s>, homage to you! (8)
<s>Vajradharma</s>, excellent truth-purpose, <s>Vajrapadma</s>, excellent purifier,
<s>Lokeśvara</s>, excellent <s>vajra</s>-eye, <s>Vajranetra</s>, homage to you! (9)
<s>Vajratīkṣṇa</s>, of the great vehicle, <s>Vajrakośa</s>, great weapon,
<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, of <s>vajra</s>-profundity, <s>Vajrabuddha</s>, homage to you! (10)
<s>Vajrahetu</s>, great wheel-ornament, <s>Vajracakra</s>, great method,
well-turning, <s>vajra</s>-arisen, <s>Vajramaṇḍa</s>, homage to you! (11)
<s>Vajrabhāṣa</s>, foremost of excellent <s>vidyā</s>s, <s>Vajrajāpa</s>, excellent giver of <s>siddhi</s>,
beyond speech, foremost of <s>vajra</s>-accomplishment, <s>Vajravāca</s>, homage to you! (12)
<s>Vajrakarma</s>, excellent <s>vajra</s>-command, <s>Karmavajra</s>, excellent all-pervading,
<s>Vajrāmogha</s>, of great magnanimity, <s>Vajraviśva</s>, homage to you! (13)
<s>Vajrarakṣa</s>, of great firmness, <s>Vajravarma</s>, greatly solid,
invincible, foremost of excellent valor, <s>Vajravīrya</s>, homage to you! (14)
<s>Vajrayakṣa</s>, of great skillful means, <s>Vajradaṃṣṭra</s>, of great terror,
crusher of burdens, fierce <s>vajra</s>, <s>Vajracaṇḍa</s>, homage to you! (15)
<s>Vajrasandhi</s>, well-present, <s>Vajrabandha</s>, liberator,
foremost pledge of the <s>vajra</s>-fist, <s>Vajramuṣṭi</s>, homage to you! (16)
Whoever maintains this auspicious one hundred and eight names,
that person is consecrated with all supreme consecrations beginning with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration! (17)
And whoever constantly sings this secondary [hymn] of the names
of <s>Mahāvajradhara</s> as a praise — that one too becomes equal to <s>Vajradhara</s>! (18)
Having been praised by us with this one hundred and eight names,
reveal the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization, the great method! (19)

body.text:
adhyeṣayāmastvāṃ nātha bhāṣasva paramaṃ vidhim /
sarvabuddhamahācakraṃ mahāmaṇḍalamuttamam // 20 //iti //
body.translated_text:
We entreat you, O Protector — proclaim the supreme procedure,
the great wheel of all <s>Buddha</s>s, the supreme great <s>maṇḍala</s>! (20)
Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān vajradharaḥ sarvatathāgatādhyeṣaṇavacanamupaśrutya sarvatathāgatasamayasaṃbhavavajrādhiṣṭhānannāma samādhiṃ samāpadye vajradhātunnāma mahāmaṇḍalamudājahāra /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having heard the entreating words of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the <s>Vajra</s>-Empowerment Born from the Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, brought forth the great <s>maṇḍala</s> called the <s>Vajradhātu</s>.

children.translated_text: Now I shall explain the supreme great <s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>Vajradhātu</s>, known as the <s>Vajradhātu</s>. (1)
Having seated oneself as appropriate in the center of the <s>maṇḍala</s>,
meditating upon and empowering the great being's great <s>mudrā</s>, (2)
then, having risen while remaining in the <s>mudrā</s>, one should look around in all directions,
and circumambulate with dignity, reciting <s>Vajrasattva</s>. (3)
With a new, well-fitted, well-measured, and beautiful
cord, the wise ones should outline the <s>maṇḍala</s> according to their ability. (4)
Four-cornered, with four gates, adorned with four arched gateways,
furnished with four cords, decorated with silk banners and garlands. (5)
In all the corner sections and at the junctions of the gate-projections,
studded with <s>vajra</s>-jewels — thus one should outline the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>. (6)
Entering the inner citadel, which resembles a wheel,
surrounded by <s>vajra</s>-cords and adorned with eight pillars, (7)
decorated with five <s>maṇḍala</s>s [with] moon[-discs] atop the <s>vajra</s>-pillars,
in the center of the central <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should place the <s>Buddha</s> image. (8)
On all sides of the <s>Buddha</s>, in the center of the [subsidiary] <s>maṇḍala</s>s,
the four foremost pledge[-deities] should be inscribed in due order. (9)
Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, in the four groups of <s>maṇḍala</s>s,
one should install the four <s>Buddha</s>s beginning with <s>Akṣobhya</s> — all the <s>Buddha</s>s. (10)
One should create the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Akṣobhya</s> together with <s>Vajradhara</s> and the rest;
the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s>, filled with <s>Vajragarbha</s> and the rest; (11)

body.text:
vajranetrādibhiḥ śuddhaṃ maṇḍalamamitāyuṣaḥ /
amoghasiddheḥ saṃlekhyaṃ vajraviśvādimaṇḍalam // iti // 12 //
body.translated_text:
the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Amitāyus</s>, purified by <s>Vajranetra</s> and the rest;
the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Amoghasiddhi</s>, to be drawn with <s>Vajraviśva</s> and the rest. (12)

children.translated_text: In the corner positions of the wheel, one should draw the <s>vajra</s>-goddesses;
in the corners of the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should draw the <s>Buddha</s>-offerings. (13)
In the middle of all the gates, the four door-guardians;
in the positions of the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should install the great beings. (14)

children.text: tato vai samyagāgrīntu mudrāṃ badhvā yathāvidhi /
children.translated_text: Then, having properly bound the foremost <s>mudrā</s> according to the prescribed method,

children.text: vajrācāryaḥ praviṣṭvā tu sphoṭya mudrāṃ samāviśeta // 15 //
children.translated_text: the <s>vajrācārya</s> (vajra-master), having entered, should snap [the fingers] and cause the <s>mudrā</s> to enter. (15)

body.translated_text: Initiation
Here, this is the heart of complete possession — Aḥ!

children.translated_text: Having sought instruction as appropriate, and having performed the self-empowerment and the rest,
having uttered one's own name, one should then accomplish with the <s>vajra</s>. (1)
The <s>vajrācārya</s>, having bound the <s>Sattvavajrāṅkuśī</s> (<s>vajra</s>-hook-of-beings <s>mudrā</s>), then again
making the burst of finger-snaps, should assemble all <s>Buddha</s>s. (2)
At that very instant, all <s>Buddha</s>s, accompanied by <s>Vajrasattva</s>,
with all <s>maṇḍala</s>s complete, come to the assembly in the <s>maṇḍala</s>. (3)
Then, having quickly bound the great <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Vajradhara</s>,
one should recite once the supreme one hundred and eight names. (4)
Then the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, pleased by the assembly, come firmly;
<s>Vajrasattva</s>, self-accomplished, stands as a spiritual friend. (5)

children.text: tato dvāreṣu sarveṣu karma kṛtvāṅku śādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, at all the gates, having performed the actions with the hook and the rest,
with the foremost great activity <s>mudrā</s>s, one should install the pledge[-deities]. (6)
With the foremost pledge <s>mudrā</s>s, with the <s>Sattvavajra</s> and the rest,

children.text: sādhayeta mahāsattvo jaḥ hūm vaṃ hoḥ pravartayan // 7 //
children.translated_text: the great being should accomplish, activating <s>Jaḥ Hūṃ Vaṃ Hoḥ</s>. (7)
Then all the great beings beginning with the <s>Buddha</s>s, completely,
attracted and well-entered, having been bound, go under that [master's] control. (8)

body.text:
tatastu guhyapūjābhiḥ santoṣya sa mahātmanā /
vijñayetsarvasatvārthaṃ kurudhvaṃ sarvasiddhaye // 9 // iti //
body.translated_text:
Then, having satisfied [them] with the secret offerings by that great soul,
one should announce: 'Act for the benefit of all beings, for the accomplishment of all [aims]!' (9)
Thus, in all <s>maṇḍala</s>s, this is the activity of the <s>vajrācārya</s>.
Initiation of the disciple
Now here follows the detailed procedure of the entry of the <s>vajra</s>-disciple and the rest into this great <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>Vajradhātu</s>.

body.text:
tatra prathamaṃ tāvat praveśo bhavatyaśeṣānavaśeṣasattvadhātuparitrāṇasarvahitasukhottamasiddhikāryakaraṇatayā /
atra mahāmaṇḍalapraveśe pātrāpātraparīkṣā na kāryā / tatkasmāddhetoḥ /
body.translated_text:
Therein, first of all, there is the entry, by way of performing the task of the supreme accomplishment of rescue, benefit, and happiness for the entire limitless and inexhaustible sentient realm.
In this entry into the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, examination of the worthy and unworthy vessel should not be made. For what reason?

body.text: santi bhagavantastathāgatāḥ kecit sattvā mahāpāpakāriṇaste idaṃ vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalaṃ dṛṣṭvā praviṣṭā ca sarvāpāyavigatā bhaviṣyanti /
body.translated_text: There are, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s>s, certain beings who have committed great evil deeds — upon seeing this <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s> and entering it, they will become free from all lower realms of existence.

body.text: santi ca bhagavantaḥ sattvāḥ sarvārthabhojanapānakāmaguṇagṛddhāḥ samayadviṣṭāḥ puraścaraṇādiṣvaśaktāḥ / teṣāmapyatrayathākāmakaraṇīyatayā praviṣṭānāṃ sarvāśāparipūrirbhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: And there are, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, beings who are greedy for all manner of food, drink, and sensual pleasures, who are hostile to the pledges (<s>samaya</s>), and who are incapable of preliminary practices and the rest. For them too, having entered here where they may do as they wish, the fulfillment of all wishes will come about.

body.text: santi bhagavantaḥ sattvā nṛtyagītahāsyalāsyāhāravihārapriyatayā sarvatathāgatamahāyānābhisamayadharmatānavabodhatvādanyadevakulamaṇḍalāni praviśanti, sarvāśāparipūrisaṃpadabhūteṣu niruttararatiprītiharṣasaṃbhavakareṣu sarvatathāgatakulamaṇḍaleṣu śikṣāpadabhayabhītā na praviśanti / teṣāmapāyamaṇḍalapraveśa [pathābhimukhavihārāṇāmapyeva] vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalapraveśo yujyata sarvaratiprītyuttamasiddhisukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ sarvāpāyagatipraveśābhimukhapathavinivartanāya ca /
body.translated_text: There are, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, beings who, because of their fondness for dancing, singing, laughter, play, eating, and recreation, and because of their failure to understand the <s>dharma</s>-nature of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, enter the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of other divine families, yet do not enter the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s> families — which are the fulfillment of all wishes, the source of unsurpassed delight, joy, and gladness — out of fear of the rules of training. For them too, even though they are headed toward paths leading to the entry of lower-realm <s>maṇḍala</s>s, entry into the <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s> is fitting — for the purpose of experiencing all delight, joy, supreme accomplishment, happiness, and mental satisfaction, and for the turning back from paths leading to entry into the lower realms.

body.text: santi ca punarbhagavanto dhārmikāḥ sattvāḥ sarvatathāgataśīlasamādhiprajñottamasiddhyupāyairbuddhabodhiṃ prārthayanto dhyānavimokṣādibhirbhūmibhiryantaḥ kliśyante / teṣāmatraiva vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalapraveśamātreṇaiva sarvatathāgatatvamapi na durlabham, kimaṅgā punaranyā siddhiriti //
body.translated_text: And furthermore, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, there are pious beings who, seeking <s>Buddha</s>-awakening through the methods of the supreme accomplishment of morality, concentration, and wisdom of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, struggle through the stages of <s>dhyāna</s>s, liberations, and the rest. For them, by the mere entry into this <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s> alone, even the state of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s is not difficult to obtain — how much more so any other accomplishment!

body.text: tatrādita eva tāvat sarvatathāgatapraṇāmacatuṣṭayaṃ kārayet / tadyathā /
body.translated_text: Therein, first of all, one should have the fourfold homage to all <s>Tathāgata</s>s performed. Namely:

body.text: sarvaśarīreṇa vajrāñjaliprasāritena praṇamedanena mantreṇa / oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānāyātmānanniryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajrasattvādhitiṣṭhasva māṃ //
body.translated_text: With the entire body, one should bow with the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s> (palms joined) extended, with this <s>mantra</s>: OṂ — For the worship and service of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I surrender myself. <s>Vajrasattva</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, empower me!

body.text: tathaiva sthito vajrāñjaliṃ hṛdi kṛtvā lalāṭena praṇamedanena mantreṇa oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjābhiṣekāyātmānanniryātayāmi savatathāgatavajraratnābhiṣiñca mām //
body.translated_text: Standing in the same way, placing the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s> at the heart, one should bow with the forehead, with this <s>mantra</s>: OṂ — For the consecration of the worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I surrender myself. <s>Vajraratna</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, consecrate me!

body.text: tatastathaivotthāya vajrāṃjalibandhena śirasā mukhena praṇamedanena mantreṇa oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāpravartanāyātmānaṃ niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajradharma pravartaya mām //
body.translated_text: Then, rising in the same way, with the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s> mudrā, one should bow with the head and face, with this <s>mantra</s>: OṂ — For the turning of the worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I surrender myself. <s>Vajradharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, set me in motion!

body.text: tatastathaiva sthito vajrāṃjaliṃ śiraso 'vatārya hṛdi kṛtvā murdhnā praṇamedanena mantreṇa oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjākarmaṇe ātmānanniryātayāmi sarvatathātavajrakarma kuru mām //
body.translated_text: Then, standing in the same way, lowering the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s> from the head and placing it at the heart, one should bow with the crown of the head, with this <s>mantra</s>: OṂ — For the activity of the worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I surrender myself. <s>Vajrakarma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, employ me!

body.text: tato raktavastrottarīyo raktapaṭṭakāvacchāditamukhaḥ sattvavajrimudrāṃ bandhayedanena hṛdayena samayastvam //
body.translated_text: Then, wearing a red cloth as an upper garment, with the face covered by a red band, one should form the <s>sattvavajrī</s> <s>mudrā</s> with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: 'You are the pledge (<s>samaya</s>)!'

body.text: tato madhyāṅgulidvayena mālāṃ granthyā praveśayedanena hṛdayena samaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then, with the two middle fingers, one should insert the garland through the knot, with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: 'Pledge HŪṂ!'

body.text: tataḥ praveśyaivaṃ vadet / "adya tvaṃ sarvatathāgatakule praviṣṭaḥ / tadahaṃ te vajrajñānamutpādayiṣyāmi, yena jñānena tva sarvatathāgatasiddhirapi prāpsyasi, kimutānyāḥ siddhīḥ / na ca tvayādṛṣṭamahāmaṇḍalasya vaktavyaṃ, mā te samayo vyathed" iti / tataḥ svayaṃ vajrācāryaḥ sattvavajramudrāmeva mūrdhvāmukhīṃ badhvā vajraśiṣyasya mūrdhni sthāsyaivaṃ vadet / "ayaṃ te samayavajro mūrdhānaṃ sphalayed, yadi tvaṃ kasyacid brūyāt /"
body.translated_text: Then, having been led in, one should say thus: 'Today you have entered the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therefore I shall generate the <s>vajra</s>-knowledge in you, by which knowledge you will attain even the accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — how much more so other accomplishments! But you must not speak of this great <s>maṇḍala</s> to one who has not seen it, lest your pledge be violated.' Then the <s>vajra</s>-master himself, forming the <s>sattvavajra</s> <s>mudrā</s> face-upward, should place it on the crown of the <s>vajra</s>-disciple's head and say thus: 'This pledge-<s>vajra</s> would split your head, should you tell anyone.'

body.text: tatastayaiva samayamudrayā udakaṃ śapathahṛdayena sakṛt parijñāpya, tasya śiṣyāya pāyayediti //
body.translated_text: Then, with that very pledge-<s>mudrā</s>, having consecrated water once with the oath heart[-<s>mantra</s>], one should give it to that disciple to drink.
Here is the oath heart[-<s>mantra</s>]:

children.translated_text: <s>Vajrasattva</s> himself today is established in your heart.

children.text: nirbhidya tatkṣaṇaṃ yāyād yadi brūyādimaṃ nayam //
children.translated_text: He would pierce through and depart in that very instant, should you divulge this teaching.

body.translated_text: <s>Vajra</s>-water! ṬHAḤ!

body.text: tataḥ śiṣyāya brūyāt / "adya prabhṛtyahante vajrapāṇiryatte 'haṃ brūyāmidaṃ kuru tatkartavyaṃ, na ca tvayāhamavamantavyo, mā te viṣamāparihāreṇa kālakriyāṃ kṛtvā narapatanaṃ syād" iti uktvā, vaktavyaṃ brūhi, "sarvatathāgatā adhitiṣṭhanto vajrasattvo me āviśatu" /
body.translated_text: Then one should say to the disciple: 'From today onwards, I am your <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>. Whatever I tell you — "do this" — that must be done. And you must not disregard me, lest through an irremediable transgression, having died, you fall into hell.' Having said this, one should say: 'Speak! "May all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, empowering [me], cause <s>Vajrasattva</s> to enter me!"'
Then the <s>vajra</s>-master, with haste, forming the <s>sattvavajrī</s> <s>mudrā</s>, should utter this:

body.text:
ayaṃ tatsamayo vajraṃ vajrasattvamiti smṛtam /
āveśayatu te 'dyaiva vajrajñānamanuttaram /
vajrāveśa aḥ /
body.translated_text:
This is the pledge — the <s>vajra</s>, known as <s>Vajrasattva</s>.
May it cause the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-knowledge to enter you this very day!
<s>Vajra</s>-entry! AḤ!

body.text: tataḥ krodhamuṣṭiṃ badhvā sattvavajrimudrāṃ sphoṭayet, mahāyānābhisamayaṃ ca vajravācā rucitoccārayediti /
body.translated_text: Then, forming the wrathful fist, one should snap the <s>sattvavajrī</s> <s>mudrā</s>, and utter the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization with <s>vajra</s>-speech, recited with delight.

body.text: tataḥ samāviśatyāviṣṭamātrasya divyaṃ jñānamutpadyate / tena jñānena paracittābhyavabudhyati / sarvakāryāṇi cātītānāgatavartamānāni jānāti / hṛdayaṃ cāsya dṛḍhībhavati sarvatathāgataśāsane / sarvaduḥkhāni ca [saṃpra]ṇaśyanti / sarvabhayavigataśca bhavati / avadhyaḥ sarvasattveṣu / sarvatathāgatāścādhitiṣṭhanti / sarvasiddhayaścāsyābhimukhībhavanti / apūrvāṇi cāsyākāraṇaharṣaratiprītikarāṇi sukhānyutpadyante / taiḥ sukhaiḥ keṣāñcitsamādhayo niṣpadyante, keṣāñcida dhāraṇyaḥ, keṣāñcita sarvāśāparipūrayo, yāvat, keṣāñcitsarvatathāgatatvamapi niṣpadyata iti /
body.translated_text: Then, as [<s>Vajrasattva</s>] enters — at the very moment of entry, divine knowledge arises. By that knowledge, one comprehends the minds of others. One knows all affairs — past, future, and present. And one's heart becomes firm in the teaching of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. And all sufferings are destroyed. And one becomes free from all fear. One becomes invulnerable among all beings. And all <s>Tathāgata</s>s empower one. And all accomplishments become present before one. And unprecedented happinesses arise that produce causeless gladness, delight, and joy. Through those happinesses, for some, <s>samādhi</s>s are accomplished; for some, <s>dhāraṇī</s>s; for some, the fulfillment of all wishes; and even, for some, the state of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s is accomplished.

body.text: tatastāṃ mudrāṃ badhvā svahṛdi mokṣayedanena hṛdayena
body.translated_text: Then, forming that <s>mudrā</s>, one should release it at one's own heart, with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]:

body.text: tiṣṭha vajra dṛḍho me bhava, śāśvato me bhava, hṛdayaṃ me 'dhitiṣṭha, sarvasiddhiñca me prayaccha, hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ //
body.translated_text: Remain, O <s>Vajra</s>! Be firm for me! Be eternal for me! Empower my heart! And grant me all accomplishments! HŪṂ HA HA HA HA HOḤ!

body.text: tatastāṃ mālāṃ mahāmaṇḍale kṣepayedanena hṛdayena pratīccha vajra hoḥ // tato yatra patati so 'sya sidhyati / tatastāṃ mālāṃ gṛhya tasyaidha śirasi bandhayedanena hadayena oṃ pratigṛṇhatvamimaṃ satvaṃ mahābalaḥ // tayā bandhayā tena mahāsattvena pratīcchito bhavati, śīghraṃ cāsya sidhyati /
body.translated_text: Then one should cast that garland into the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: 'Accept, O <s>Vajra</s>! HOḤ!' Wherever it falls — that [deity] becomes his accomplishment. Then, taking that garland, one should bind it on the head of that [disciple], with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: 'OṂ — May the greatly powerful one accept this being!' By that binding, he is accepted by that great being, and accomplishment quickly comes to him.

body.text: tatastathāviṣṭasyaiva mukhabandhaṃ muṃcedanena hṛdayena oṃ vajrasattvaḥ svayante 'dya cakṣūddhāṭanatatparaḥ uddhāṭayati sarvākṣo vajracakṣu ranuttaram // he vajra paśya //
body.translated_text: Then, while still thus possessed, one should remove the face-covering, with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: 'OṂ — <s>Vajrasattva</s> himself today, intent on opening the eyes, opens all the eyes — the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-eye! HE VAJRA — See!'

body.text: tato mahāmaṇḍalaṃ yathānupūrvato darśayet / mahāmaṇḍale ca dṛṣṭamātre sarvatathāgatairadhiṣṭhyate, vajrasattvaścāsya hṛdaye tiṣṭhati / nānādyatīvaraśmimaṇḍaladarśanādīni prātīhāryavikurvitāni paśyati / sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhitatvāt / kadācit bhagavān mahāvajradharaḥ svarūpeṇa darśanaṃ dadāti, tathāgato vati / tataḥ prabhṛti sarvārthāḥ sarvamano 'bhirucitakāryāṇi sarvasiddhira, yāvad, vajradharatvamapi tathāgatatvaṃ veti /
body.translated_text: Then one should show the great <s>maṇḍala</s> in proper sequence. And at the very moment of seeing the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one is empowered by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and <s>Vajrasattva</s> remains in one's heart. One sees various miraculous displays such as the vision of supreme radiant ray-mandalas and the rest — because of being empowered by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Sometimes the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the great <s>Vajradhara</s>, grants a vision in his own form, as a <s>Tathāgata</s>. From that time onwards, all aims, all activities desired by the mind, all accomplishments — and even the state of <s>Vajradhara</s>, the state of <s>Tathāgata</s> — [are attained].

body.text: tato mahāmaṇḍalaṃ darśayitvā vajrādhiṣṭhitakalaśād gandhodakenābhiṣiṃcedanena hṛdayena vajrābhiṣiñca //
body.translated_text: Then, having shown the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should consecrate [the disciple] with scented water from the <s>vajra</s>-empowered vase, with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: '<s>Vajra</s>-consecrate!'

body.text: tatastvekatamāṃ mudrāṃ mālāṃ vadhvā svacinhaṃ pāṇau pratiṣṭhāpyaivaṃ vadet /
body.translated_text: Then, binding one of the <s>mudrā</s>-garlands and placing one's own emblem in [the disciple's] hand, one should say thus:

children.translated_text: Today you are consecrated by the <s>Buddha</s>s with the <s>vajra</s>-consecration.
This is your state of all <s>Buddha</s>s — take the <s>vajra</s> for perfect accomplishment!

body.text: oṃ vajrādhipati tvāmabhiṣiṃcāmi tiṣṭha vajra samayastvam //
body.translated_text: OṂ — O <s>Vajra</s>-lord, I consecrate you. Remain, O <s>Vajra</s> — you are the pledge!

body.text: tato vajranāmābhiṣekeṇa abhiṣiṃcedanena hṛdayena / oṃ vajrasattva tvāmabhiṣiṃcāmi vajranāmābhiṣekataḥ he vajra nāma // yasya yannāma kuryāttasya he- śabdaḥ prayoktavya iti //
body.translated_text: Then one should consecrate with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration, with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: 'OṂ — <s>Vajrasattva</s>, I consecrate you with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration. HE <s>VAJRA</s> NĀMA!' Whatever name one gives, for that the syllable 'HE' should be used.
The detailed procedure for entry into all <s>maṇḍala</s>s.

body.text: tato brūyāt, "kinte 'bhirucirarthotpattisiddhijñānaṃ vā, ṛddhisiddhiniṣpattijñānaṃ vā, vidyādharasiddhiniṣpattijñānaṃ vā, yāvat, sarvatathāgatottamasiddhiniṣpattijñānaṃ ve" ti / tato yasya yadabhirucitaṃ tata tasyocceyam //
body.translated_text: Then one should say: 'What is your preference — the knowledge of the accomplishment of worldly aims, or the knowledge of the accomplishment of magical powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>-<s>siddhi</s>), or the knowledge of the accomplishment of the <s>vidyādhara</s> (spell-holder) attainment, or even the knowledge of the accomplishment of the supreme attainment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s?' Then, whatever is desired by whichever [disciple], that should be proclaimed for them.
Then one should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge for the accomplishment of worldly aims.
One should contemplate a <s>vajra</s>-image placed in a treasure-repository, in the heart.
