Contemplating thus, one sees the treasures situated in the earth. (1)

children.translated_text: Having drawn a <s>vajra</s>-image, one should contemplate it in the sky.
Wherever it falls and one sees [it], one should declare the treasure to be there. (2)

children.text: vajrabimbaṃ tu jivhāyāṃ bhāvayed buddhimān naraḥ /
children.translated_text: A wise person should contemplate a <s>vajra</s>-image on the tongue.
By one's own speech, one utters in the ultimate sense: 'Here it is!' (3)

body.text:
vajrabimbamayaṃ sarvaṃ bhāvayaṃ kāyamātmanaḥ /
samāviṣṭaḥ patedyatra nidhintatra vinirdiśed // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Contemplating one's entire body as made of <s>vajra</s>-image,
one who is possessed should fall wherever [guided] — there one should declare the treasure. (4)
Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
<s>Vajra</s>-treasure!
<s>Ratna</s> (Jewel)-treasure!
<s>Dharma</s>-treasure!
<s>Karma</s> (Action)-treasure!
Then one should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge for the accomplishment of <s>vajra</s> magical powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>-<s>siddhi</s>).

children.translated_text: When the <s>vajra</s>-entry has arisen, [contemplating] water as made of <s>vajra</s>-image,
contemplating [thus], one quickly becomes accomplished and walks upon the surface of water. (1)
Likewise, having generated the entry, whatever form one's own self [takes],
contemplating [thus], that very [form] becomes even a <s>Buddha</s>-form by itself. (2)
Likewise, [contemplating] oneself as possessed, 'I am space,'
contemplating [thus], for as long as one wishes, one proceeds to invisibility. (3)

body.text:
vajrāviṣṭaḥ svayaṃ bhatvā vajro 'hamiti bhāvayan /
yāvadāruhate sthānantāvadākāśago bhaved // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Having become possessed by <s>vajra</s> oneself, contemplating 'I am a <s>vajra</s>,'
for as long as one ascends to a [given] place, one becomes a sky-goer. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
<s>Vajra</s>-water!

body.translated_text: <s>Vajra</s>-form!
<s>Vajra</s>-space!
<s>Vajra</s>-great!
Then one should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge for the accomplishment of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>vidyādhara</s> attainment.

children.translated_text: Having drawn a moon-disc, one should ascend upward in homage.
Radiating a <s>vajra</s> in the hand, one becomes a <s>vajra</s>-<s>vidyādhara</s>. (1)
Having mounted a moon-disc, one should radiate a <s>vajra</s>-jewel.
For as long as the pure-souled one wishes, one rises up in an instant. (2)
Having mounted a moon-disc, with a <s>vajra</s>-lotus placed in the hand,

children.text: bhāvayan vajranetraṃ tu dadyād vidyādhṛtāṃ padam // 3 //
children.translated_text: contemplating a <s>vajra</s>-eye, one attains the state of a <s>vidyādhara</s>. (3)

body.text:
candramaṇḍalamadhyasthaḥ karmavajrāṃ tu bhāvayet /
vajraviśvadharācchīghraṃ sarvaividyādharo bhaveda // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Standing in the center of a moon-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should contemplate a <s>karma</s>-<s>vajra</s>.
Quickly becoming a <s>vajra</s>-universal-bearer, one becomes a complete <s>vidyādhara</s>. (4)

children.translated_text: Now the heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
<s>Vajradhara</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>Ratnadhara</s>!
<s>Padmadhara</s>!
<s>Karmadhara</s>!
Then one should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge for the accomplishment of the supreme attainment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

children.translated_text: Having entered the <s>samādhi</s> of all <s>vajra</s>s and pervading the space-realms,
for as long as the <s>vajra</s>-natured one wishes, one rises up in an instant. (1)
Contemplating the supreme ones in the <s>samādhi</s> of complete purity,
one quickly attains the five <s>abhijñā</s>s (supernatural knowledges), O accomplisher of knowledge! (2)
Pervading all space as being made of <s>Vajrasattva</s>,
one of firm mindfulness quickly becomes <s>Vajradhara</s> himself. (3)

body.text:
buddhabimbamayaṃ sarvamadhimucya khadhātuṣu /
sarvabuddhasamādhiṣu buddhatvāya bhaviṣyati // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Resolving all [things] as being made of <s>Buddha</s>-image in the space-realms,
in the <s>samādhi</s>s of all <s>Buddha</s>s, one will [attain] <s>Buddha</s>hood. (4)

children.translated_text: Now the heart[-<s>mantra</s>s] here:
<s>Vajra</s> <s>Vajra</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>Śuddha</s> (Pure) <s>Śuddha</s>!
<s>Sattva</s> (Being) <s>Sattva</s>!
<s>Buddha</s> <s>Buddha</s>!
The accomplishments of all <s>siddhi</s>-knowledges.
Now, when one becomes capable of holding secrets —
For that one, first of all, there should be the oath heart[-<s>mantra</s>]:

children.text: oṃ vajrasattvaḥ svayaṃ te 'dya hṛdayaṃ samavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajrasattva</s> himself today is established in your heart.
He would pierce through and depart in that very instant, should this teaching be [revealed].

body.text: tata evaṃ vaden "na tvayedaṃ śapathahṛdayamatikramitavyam; mā te viṣamāparihāreṇākālamaraṇaṃ syād, anenaiva kāyena narakapatanam" /
body.translated_text: Then one should say thus: 'You must not transgress this oath-heart[-<s>mantra</s>]; lest by the irremediable danger, untimely death befall you, and with this very body you fall into hell.'
Then one should teach the knowledge of the secret <s>mudrā</s>s.

children.translated_text: 'Having generated <s>vajra</s>-possession (<s>vajrāveśa</s>), one should give the <s>tāla</s> (clap) with concentration;
with the subtle <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s> palms, one could bring even a mountain under control.' (1)

body.translated_text: <s>Vajratālamudrā</s> (Vajra-Clap Seal).

children.translated_text: 'Having applied the method of <s>vajra</s>-possession, one should strike with <s>vajra</s>-bond palms;
through the application of the subtle clap, one would enter even into a mountain.' (2)
'Likewise, by the method of possession, with the <s>vajra</s>-bond extended,
through the snapping of the fingertips, one would shatter a hundred families in an instant.' (3)

body.translated_text:
'Through the yoga of the method of subtle possession, with all fingers concentrated,
released from the <s>vajra</s>-bond, it is the supreme remover of all suffering.' (4)
Now there is the secret practice (<s>guhyasādhana</s>) of these:

body.text:
bhagena praviśet kāyaṃ striyāyāḥ puruṣasya vā /
praviṣṭvā manasā sarvaṃ tasya kāryaṃ samaṃ sphared // iti /
body.translated_text:
'Through the <s>bhaga</s> (secret organ), one should enter the body of a woman or a man;
having entered, one should mentally spread equally throughout all the activities of that one.'

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the clap-heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>vajra vaśa</s> (vajra, subjugate!)

body.translated_text: <s>vajra viśa</s> (vajra, enter!)
<s>vajra hana</s> (vajra, strike!)
<s>vajra hara</s> (vajra, seize!)

body.text: tato hṛdayaṃ dattvā svakuladevatācaturmudrājñānaṃ śikṣayet / anena vidhinā vaktavyam / "na kasyacit tvayānyasyaiṣāṃ mudrāṇāmakovidasya ekatarāpi mudrā darśayitavyā / tatkasya he toḥ / tathā hi te satvā adṛṣṭamahāmaṇḍalāḥ santo mudrābandhaṃ prayojayanti tadā teṣānna tathā siddhirbhaviṣyati / tataste vicikitsā prāptā viṣamāparihāreṇa śīghrameva kālaṃ kṛtvāvīcīmahānarake patantaḥ / tava cāpāyagamanaṃ syād" iti //
body.translated_text: Then, having given the heart[-<s>mantra</s>], one should teach the knowledge of the four <s>mudrā</s>s of one's own family deity. By this procedure one should say: 'You must not show even a single one of these <s>mudrā</s>s to anyone else who is unskilled [in them]. For what reason? For those beings who, not having seen the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, employ the <s>mudrā</s>-bonds — for them, <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) will not occur in that way. Then those, having fallen into doubt, through the irremediable danger, will quickly die and fall into the great <s>Avīci</s> hell. And for you too, there would be a going to the lower realms.'
Now there is the knowledge of the great <s>mudrā</s> for accomplishing all <s>Tathāgata</s>-beings:

children.translated_text: 'Beginning from the knowledge of the mind, one should visualize the <s>vajra</s>-sun;
visualizing oneself as a <s>Buddha</s>-image, setting in motion the <s>vajradhātu</s>.' (1)

body.text:
anyā siddhimātrastu jñānamāyurbalaṃ varṣaḥ /
prāpnoti sarvagāmitvaṃ buddhatvamapi na durlabham // 2 // iti //
body.translated_text:
'As for other accomplishments: knowledge, longevity, strength, and splendor;
one obtains the ability to go everywhere — even <s>Buddha</s>hood is not difficult [to attain].' (2)
The <s>mudrā</s> of the complete awakening of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Now there is the great <s>mudrā</s>-bond for accomplishing <s>Vajrasattva</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Having raised the <s>vajra</s> with pride, bearing the <s>vajra</s>-pride,
through the <s>vajra</s>s of body, speech, and mind, one would oneself become <s>Vajrasattva</s>.' (1)

body.text:
anyā sarvagāmī sarvakāmapatiḥ sukhī /
ṛddhyāyurbalarūpāgryo vajrasattvasamo bhaved // iti // 2 //
body.translated_text:
'Otherwise, one becomes an all-goer, a lord of all desires, happy;
foremost in miraculous powers, longevity, strength, and beauty — one would become equal to <s>Vajrasattva</s>.' (2)

children.translated_text: 'Through the <s>vajra</s>s of body, speech, and mind, following the painting,
one should accomplish the great beings endowed with their emblems and <s>mudrā</s>s.' (3)
'Now herein, the practice of all <s>kalpa</s>s (ritual manuals) and the accomplishment itself,
and the great deeds of the accomplished — I shall teach in due order.' (4)

body.text:
pratyahaṃ prāgyathākālaṃ svādhiṣṭhānādikantathā /
kṛtvā tu sādhayetsarvaṃ tataḥ paścād yathāsukham // 5 // iti //
body.translated_text:
'Every day, at the proper time, from the self-empowerment and so forth,
having performed [the preliminaries], one should accomplish everything; then afterwards, at one's ease.' (5)
Therein, this is the detailed procedure for the practice of the great <s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Having generated <s>vajra</s>-possession, [forming] the great <s>mudrā</s> according to the proper method,

children.text: badhvā tu paratastaṃ tu mahāsattvaṃ prabhāvayet // 1 //
children.translated_text: having bound [it], one should then manifest that great being.' (1)

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā jñānasattvaṃ tu svaśarīre prabhāvayet /
children.translated_text: 'Having seen that, one should manifest the knowledge-being (<s>jñānasattva</s>) in one's own body;

children.text: ākṛṣya praveśya badhvā vaśīkṛtvā ca sādhayet //
children.translated_text: having attracted, having caused to enter, having bound, and having subjugated — one should accomplish.'

body.text: tatraiṣāṃ hṛdayāni bhavanti / vajrasattva aḥ // vajrāveśahṛdayam //
body.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s: '<s>vajrasattva aḥ</s>' — the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] of <s>vajra</s>-possession.
'<s>vajrasattva dṛśya</s>' — the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] of recollection of the great being.
'<s>jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ</s>' — the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] of attracting, entering, binding, and subjugating the great being.

children.translated_text: 'When "You are the pledge" (<s>samayastvam</s>) is spoken, the moon should enter from behind;
there one should visualize oneself as the being, saying "You are the pledge, I [am you]."' (1)

children.text: yasya sattvasya yā mudrā tāmātmānantu bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>mudrā</s> belongs to whatever being, one should visualize oneself as that;
one should accomplish through <s>vajra</s>-recitation the accomplishment of all <s>mudrā</s>s.' (2)

body.text:
"jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ" bruvan kāye sarvabuddhān praveśayet /
manasā sādhuyogena sādhanaṃ tvaparam mahad // iti // 3 //
body.translated_text:
'Saying "<s>jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ</s>," one should cause all <s>Buddha</s>s to enter into the body;
through the yoga of proper mental concentration — this is another great accomplishment.' (3)

children.translated_text: 'Now I shall teach the action of these — the supreme <s>vajra</s>-action:"
one accomplished through recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> would swiftly attain <s>Buddha</s>hood.' (4)
'One accomplished in the <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajra</s> (<s>vajra</s> of beings) would become the lord of all <s>mudrā</s>s;

children.text: sattvavajra yāntu mudrāyāṃ sarvaratnādhipaḥ sa tu // 5 //
children.translated_text: in the <s>mudrā</s> of the <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajra</s>, that one becomes the lord of all jewels.' (5)

children.text: siddhastu dharmavajra yā vai buddhadharmadharo bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'One accomplished in the <s>dharma</s>-<s>vajra</s> <s>mudrā</s> would become a bearer of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>;
in the <s>mudrā</s> of the <s>karma</s>-<s>vajra</s>, one would become a performer of <s>vajra</s>-action.' (6)
'<s>Vajrasattva</s> is accomplished through binding with the being-<s>mudrā</s> (<s>sattvamudrā</s>);
one should attract the <s>vajra</s>-holders through the application of <s>vajra</s>-attraction.' (7)
'The great <s>mudrā</s> of <s>vajra</s>-passion (<s>vajrarāga</s>) would cause even the <s>Buddha</s>s to feel passion;
one should delight all <s>Buddha</s>s through the application of <s>vajra</s>-accomplishment.' (8)
'One should give <s>Buddha</s>-consecrations — likewise the method of the jewel-<s>mudrā</s>;
one would swiftly become <s>vajra</s>-radiance through the application of <s>vajra</s>-radiance.' (9)
'Having served the <s>vajra</s>-banner bearer, one would become a fulfiller of all directions;
having applied the method of <s>vajra</s>-laughter, one would laugh equally with all <s>Buddha</s>s.' (10)
'One would become a bearer of <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s> through the application of <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>;
foremost in wisdom among all <s>Buddha</s>s through the application of <s>Vajratīkṣṇa</s>.' (11)
'Having served the <s>vajra</s>-wheel bearer, one would turn the <s>Dharmacakra</s>;
one obtains the accomplishment of <s>Buddha</s>-speech through the application of <s>Vajrabhāṣa</s>.' (12)
'Swiftly [one attains] the state of <s>vajra</s>-action through the foremost practice of <s>vajra</s>-action;
having bound on the <s>vajra</s>-armor, one would obtain <s>vajra</s>-body-hood.' (13)

children.text: vajrayakṣaṃ tu vai sādhya vajrayakṣasamo bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'Having accomplished <s>Vajrayakṣa</s>, one would become equal to <s>Vajrayakṣa</s>;
accomplished in all <s>mudrā</s>s through the binding of the <s>vajra</s>-fist.' (14)

children.text: vajralāsyāṃ tu vai sādhya mahāvajraratiṃ labhet /
children.translated_text: 'Having accomplished <s>Vajralāsyā</s>, one would obtain the great <s>vajra</s>-delight;
through the binding of <s>Vajramālā</s>, one bestows the consecration of all <s>Buddha</s>s.' (15)
'One should apply <s>Vajragītā</s> through the application of <s>vajra</s>-song;

children.text: vajranṛtyāṃ tu saṃyojya sarvabuddhaiḥ sa pūjyate // 16 //
children.translated_text: having applied <s>Vajranṛtyā</s>, one is worshipped by all <s>Buddha</s>s.' (16)
'One would gladden the entire world through the application of <s>Vajradhūpā</s>;

children.text: vajrapuṣpāṃ tu saṃyojya vaśīkuryājjagat sa tu // 17 //
children.translated_text: having applied <s>Vajrapuṣpā</s>, one would bring the world under control.' (17)
'The great <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Vajrāloka</s> bestows the eye, offering worship;
one would become a remover of all suffering through the application of <s>Vajragandha</s>.' (18)
'Through the attraction of <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s>, one becomes the supreme attractor of all;
one would become the causer of all entry through the application of <s>Vajrapāśa</s>.' (19)

body.text:
vajrasphoṭantu saṃyojya sarvabandhakṣayo bhaved /
vajrāveśavidhiṃ yojya sarvāveśaprasādhaka // 20 // iti //
body.translated_text:
'Having applied <s>Vajrasphoṭa</s>, the destruction of all bonds would occur;
having applied the method of <s>vajra</s>-possession, one becomes the accomplisher of all possession.' (20)
Now there is the knowledge of the pledge-<s>mudrā</s> (<s>samayamudrā</s>) of the <s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text: 'Having firmly bound the <s>añjali</s> (palms joined), with all fingers interlocked,
this is declared the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s>, the <s>vajra</s>-bond, because of firm binding.' (1)
'All pledge-<s>mudrā</s>s arise from the <s>vajra</s>-bond;
I shall teach the binding of those — the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-bond.' (2)
'Having made firm the <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajra</s>, with the middle fingers raised like sprouts,
by the contraction of the inner middle [fingers], the second [<s>mudrā</s>] is described by the <s>Buddha</s>.' (3)
'The middle finger and thumb form the jewel; the lotus is the contraction of the middle [fingers];
the fifth, the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, is likewise with the tips curved.' (4)
'Now, from here I shall teach, of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family,

children.text: samayagrāhikā mudrā bandhaṃ siddhiṃ ca karma ca // 5 //
children.translated_text: the pledge-receiving <s>mudrā</s>, its binding, accomplishment, and action.' (5)
'In the moon formed by the two palms, without the middle fingers,
by the joining of the tips of the little fingers — the <s>vajra</s>, with the <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajra</s> [<s>mudrā</s>].' (6)
'By the joining of the tips of the hook-like [index fingers], the one that grants approbation;
this is the group of accomplishment-<s>mudrā</s>s for the fourfold <s>Vajrasattva</s>.' (7)
'The jewel-<s>vajra</s> [<s>mudrā</s>] is by joining the tips of the thumbs and index fingers;
that same [<s>mudrā</s>] with the middle, ring, and little fingers fully extended.' (8)
'The banner (<s>patākā</s>) is accompanied by the ring and little fingers together;
that same [<s>mudrā</s>] stationed at the place of laughter, reversed.' (9)
'With extended thumbs held steady, the index fingers curved;

children.text: sā eva varjakośā tu madhyamā mukhasandhitā // 10 //
children.translated_text: that same as the <s>vajra</s>-sheath, with the middle [fingers] joined at the tips.' (10)
'That same with the ring and little fingers together is designated the wheel;
with the thumbs bound and released, raised with extended tips.' (11)
'By the joining of the tips of the little fingers and thumbs, the <s>karma</s>-<s>vajra</s>;

children.text: sā eva tu samāgryā vai hṛdisthā suprasāritā // 12 //
children.translated_text: that same with the tips together, at the heart, fully extended.' (12)
'With curved tips like fangs, the little fingers released from the joint;
the thumbs between the little fingers, pressed with curved tips.' (13)
'At the heart, with thumbs together, the fully extended garland;
with the tips of the fingers raised mouth-like, at the crown of one dancing, joined.' (14)
'The <s>vajra</s>-bond with downward offering, one's own <s>añjali</s> offering upward;
with thumbs pressed together, the fully extended anointing.' (15)

body.text:
ekatarjanīsaṃkocā dvyaṅaguṣṭhagranthibandhitā /
aṅaguṣṭhāgra yakaṭā bandhā vajraṭamuṣṭyagrasandhitā // iti // 16 //
body.translated_text:
'With one index finger contracted, bound with a knot of two thumbs;
with the tips of the thumbs hook-shaped, bound and joined at the tip of the <s>vajra</s>-fist.' (16)

children.translated_text: 'Now I shall teach the practice of these — the supreme <s>vajra</s>-practice:
with one's own <s>mudrā</s> at the heart, in the <s>samādhi</s> of the <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajra</s>.' (17)
'Now I shall teach the action of these — the supreme <s>vajra</s>-action:
through the assembly [<s>mudrā</s>s] in the <s>mudrā</s>s of the <s>vajradhātu</s> and the rest, the <s>Tathāgata</s>s' (18)
'will empower the <s>maṇḍala</s>-<s>ācārya</s> and disciples at that very moment;
when the <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajra</s> [<s>mudrā</s>] is bound, one becomes like <s>Vajradhara</s>.' (19)
'When the <s>vajra</s>-hook [<s>mudrā</s>] is merely bound, one summons all <s>Buddha</s>s;
through the application of the <s>vajra</s> of passion, one causes even the <s>Buddha</s>s to feel passion.' (20)

body.translated_text: '[Through the <s>vajra</s>-approbation bond, one obtains the delight of the <s>Buddha</s>s' gift.]
Through <s>vajra</s>-delight, one is praised by all the Victorious Ones with approbation.' (21)

children.translated_text: 'When the jewel-<s>vajra</s> [<s>mudrā</s>] is bound, one is consecrated by the <s>Buddha</s>s;
having bound the <s>vajra</s>-sun [<s>mudrā</s>], one would become like the radiance of the <s>Buddha</s>.' (22)

children.text: vajraketudharo bhūtvā sarvāśāḥ sa tu pūrayet /
children.translated_text: 'Having become a <s>vajra</s>-banner bearer, one would fulfill all directions;
through the application of <s>vajra</s>-laughter, one would laugh equally with all <s>Buddha</s>s.' (23)
'Having established the <s>dharma</s>-<s>vajra</s> [<s>mudrā</s>], one becomes like <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>;

children.text: vajrakośāṃ tu saṃgṛhya sarvakleśāṃ cchinatti saḥ // 24 //
children.translated_text: having grasped the <s>vajra</s>-sheath [<s>mudrā</s>], one cuts through all afflictions.' (24)
'Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-wheel [<s>mudrā</s>], one becomes the lord of the <s>maṇḍala</s>;
through the application of <s>Vajrabhāṣa</s>, the supreme accomplishment of <s>vajra</s>-speech.' (25)
'Having joined the <s>karma</s>-<s>vajra</s> [<s>mudrā</s>], one becomes equal to <s>vajra</s>-action;
having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-armor [<s>mudrā</s>], the body becomes made of <s>vajra</s>.' (26)
'With the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>vajra</s>-fang tips, one shatters the wicked <s>Māra</s>s;
having firmly bound the <s>vajra</s>-fist, one brings all <s>mudrā</s>s under control.' (27)

children.text: lāsyayā ratayo divyāḥ mālayā bhūṣaṇāni ca /
children.translated_text: 'Through <s>Lāsyā</s>, divine pleasures; through <s>Mālā</s>, ornaments;

children.text: gītayā sphuṭavāco nityaṃ pūjāṃ labhati nṛtyayā // 28 //
children.translated_text: through <s>Gītā</s>, clear speech; through <s>Nṛtyā</s>, one always receives worship.' (28)
'Through <s>Dhūpā</s>, one gladdens the world; through <s>Puṣpā</s>, one is adorned with beauty;
through <s>Dīpā</s>, purification of the world; through <s>Gandhā</s>, divine fragrance.' (29)

body.text:
vajrāṅakuśaḥ samākarṣed vajrapāśā praveśayet /
vajrasphoṭā tu bandhayād vajraghaṇṭā samāviśed // 30 // iti //
body.translated_text:
'<s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s> attracts; <s>Vajrapāśā</s> causes entry;
<s>Vajrasphoṭā</s> binds; <s>Vajraghaṇṭā</s> causes possession.' (30)
Now there are the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>vajra</s>-knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>s makes the <s>vajradhātu</s> firm;
from here onward I shall teach the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s according to the proper method.' (1)
'When "You are the pledge" (<s>samayastvam</s>) is spoken, one becomes the lord of all <s>mudrā</s>s;
when "Come here" (<s>anyasva</s>) is spoken, one assuredly attracts the <s>Buddha</s>s.' (2)

children.text: "aho sukha" iti prokte buddhānapi sa rāgayet /
children.translated_text: 'When "Ah, bliss!" (<s>aho sukha</s>) is spoken, one causes even the <s>Buddha</s>s to feel passion;

children.text: "sādhu sādhv" iti vai proktvā sādhukāraiḥ sa toṣayet // 3 //
children.translated_text: having said "Excellent, excellent!" (<s>sādhu sādhu</s>), one delights them with approbation.' (3)
'When "[You are of] great [nature]" (<s>sumahattvam</s>) is spoken, the consecration of all <s>Buddha</s>s;
When '<s>rūpodyota</s>' (radiance of form) is uttered, the splendor of <s>dharma</s> will arise. // 4 //

children.text: "arthaprāptira" iti prokte sarvāśāḥ pūrayet sa tu /
children.translated_text: When '<s>arthaprāpti</s>' (attainment of purpose) is uttered, one would fulfill all wishes.

children.text: "ha ha hūṃ he- "[ti prokte samabuddhahāsaṃ prāpnu] yāt // 5 //
children.translated_text: When 'ha ha hūṃ he' is uttered, one would attain the laughter equal to the <s>Buddha</s>s'. // 5 //
When '<s>sarvakāri</s>' (all-accomplishing) is uttered, one would purify even the undoable.
When '<s>duḥkhaccheda</s>' (cutting of suffering) is uttered, one cuts off all suffering. // 6 //

body.translated_text: When '<s>buddhabodhi</s>' (Buddha-awakening) is uttered, one becomes the lord of the <s>maṇḍala</s>.
When '<s>pratiśabda</s>' (echo) is uttered, one converses together with the <s>Buddha</s>s. // 7 //

children.translated_text: When '<s>śubhasiddha</s>' (auspicious accomplishment) is uttered, mastery over all arises.
When '<s>nirbhaya</s>' (fearless) is uttered, one becomes fearless from that very instant. // 8 //

children.text: "śatru bhakṣa" iti prokte sarvaśatrun sa bhakṣayet /
children.translated_text: When '<s>śatrubhakṣa</s>' (devourer of enemies) is uttered, one would devour all enemies.
When '<s>sarvasiddhi</s>' (all accomplishments) is uttered, all accomplishments will arise. // 9 //
'<s>Mahārati</s>' [bestows]
divine delight; '<s>rūpaśobhā</s>' likewise [bestows beauty of form];
'<s>Śrotrasaukhya</s>' bestows aural pleasure; '<s>sarvapūjā</s>' [bestows] supreme worship. // 10 //
'<s>Prahlādini</s>' [bestows] mental happiness; '<s>phalāgamī</s>' [bestows] the attainment of fruit;
'<s>Sutejāgri</s>' [bestows] great splendor; '<s>sugandhāṅgi</s>' [bestows] fragrance. // 11 //

body.text:
"ayāhi jaḥ" samākarṣā "ahi hūṃ hūṃ" praveśikā /
"hesphoṭa vaṃ" mahābandhā "ghaṇṭā aḥ aḥ" pracālite- // ti // 12 //
body.translated_text: 'Ayāhi jaḥ' is the attracting [<s>mudrā</s>]; 'ahi hūṃ hūṃ' is the entering [<s>mudrā</s>]; 'hesphoṭa vaṃ' is the great binding [<s>mudrā</s>]; 'ghaṇṭā aḥ aḥ' is the shaking [<s>mudrā</s>]. Thus. // 12 //

body.text:
athāsāṃ dharmamudrā [sādhanaṃ pra] vakṣyate śubham /
jivhāyāṃ bhāvayed vajrāṃ sarvakarmāṇi kurvate // ti // 13 //
body.translated_text: Now the auspicious method of accomplishing the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s of these will be taught: one should visualize a <s>vajra</s> on the tongue — it performs all activities. Thus. // 13 //
Now the binding of the <s>karma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s is as follows:

children.translated_text: Having firmly bound the <s>vajra</s>-fist, one should, with concentration, divide it in two.
The non-dual <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s> should be formed; then the bindings will be taught. // 1 //
The left <s>vajra</s>-finger should be grasped, raised by the right —
this <s>mudrā</s> is called '<s>bodhāgrī</s>' (point of awakening), the bestower of the awakening of the <s>Buddha</s>s. // 2 //

children.text: akṣobhyasya bhūmisparśā ratne tu varadā tathā /
children.translated_text: For <s>Akṣobhya</s>, it is the earth-touching [<s>mudrā</s>]; for <s>Ratna</s> (Jewel), likewise the boon-granting;
for <s>Amitāyus</s>, the meditation-gesture; for <s>Amogha</s>, the fearlessness-bestowing. // 3 //
Hereafter I shall teach the <s>karma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s in brief,
the activators of the <s>vajra</s>-activities of <s>Vajrasattva</s> and the other beings. // 4 //
The prideful lifting up by both [hands], positioned with the hook-grasp;
by the union of arrow and bell, the 'well done!' [<s>mudrā</s>] stationed at the heart. // 5 //
For consecration, a double <s>vajra</s>; at the heart, the display of the sun;
the arm-staff placed to the left; and likewise reversed at the mouth. // 6 //
The right and left spread open, [then] the sword-striking to the left at the heart;
the fire-wheel whirled, the double <s>vajra</s> risen from the mouth. // 7 //
The <s>vajra</s>-dance released with whirling, stationed on the cheek-<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>;
the armor [<s>mudrā</s>] with the tips of the little-finger-fangs, pressed by both fists. // 8 //
By the application of <s>vajra</s>-pride, with salutations shaking the mind,
the garland-binding emitted from the mouth, caused to dance by the <s>vajra</s>-dance. // 9 //
By the application of the <s>vajra</s>-fist, one should offer incense and the rest likewise.
For the worship of all <s>Buddha</s>s, the offering-<s>mudrā</s>s are prescribed. // 10 //

body.text:
tarjanyaṅkuśabandhena kaniṣṭhāyā mahāṅkuśī /
bāhugranthikaṭāgryābhyāṃ pṛṣṭhayośca nipīḍitā // iti // 11 //
body.translated_text: By the binding of the index-finger hook, with the little finger the great hook; pressed by the arm-knots and the tips of the hips, and at the backs. Thus. // 11 //

body.text:
athāsāṃ sādhanaṃ vakṣye vajrakarmakṛtā samam /
sarvavajramayaṃ vajraṃ hṛdaye paribhāvayed // iti // 12 //
body.translated_text: Now I shall teach the accomplishment of these, together with the <s>vajra</s>-activities performed: one should meditate in the heart on the <s>vajra</s> that is entirely made of <s>vajra</s>. Thus. // 12 //

children.translated_text: Now the manifold <s>vajra</s>-activities of these <s>karma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s —
when the wisdom-fist is bound, one should enter into <s>Buddha</s>-wisdom. // 13 //
When the <s>Akṣobhya</s> [<s>mudrā</s>] is bound, the mind becomes imperturbable.
With the <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, one becomes the benefactor of others. // 14 //
With the <s>Saddharmacakra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, one sets the <s>dharmacakra</s> in motion.
With the fearlessness-gesture, one quickly becomes the bestower of freedom from disease to all beings. // 15 //
Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-pride, one attains the bliss of <s>Vajrasattva</s>.
With the <s>vajra</s>-hook, one would instantly attract all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. // 16 //
With the <s>vajra</s>-arrows, one would enamor even one's own <s>vajra</s>-consort.

children.text: vajratuṣṭyā jināḥ sarve sādhukārān dadanti hi // 17 //
children.translated_text: With the <s>vajra</s>-satisfaction, all the <s>Jina</s>s indeed give exclamations of 'well done!' // 17 //
Having bound the great <s>vajra</s>-jewel, one is consecrated by the Teachers.
Having established the <s>vajra</s>-sun, one becomes equal to the <s>vajra</s>-sun. // 18 //
Having raised the <s>vajra</s>-banner, one rains down a shower of jewels.

children.text: vajrasmitāṃ samādhāya hased buddhaiḥ samaṃ laghu // 19 //
children.translated_text: Having established the <s>vajra</s>-smile, one laughs together with the <s>Buddha</s>s swiftly. // 19 //
Having established the <s>vajra</s>-blossom, one beholds the <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>.
Having firmly bound the <s>vajra</s>-sheath, one cuts off all suffering. // 20 //
Having established the <s>vajra</s>-wheel, one sets the <s>dharmacakra</s> in motion.
All the word of the <s>Buddha</s> is accomplished through <s>vajra</s>-recitation. // 21 //
Through the <s>vajra</s>-dance offering, even a <s>Buddha</s> would become subject [to one's power]
Having bound the <s>vajra</s>-armor, one would attain the essence of <s>vajra</s>. // 22 //
Having established the <s>vajra</s>-fang, one would shatter even <s>vajra</s>-nature.
With the <s>vajra</s>-fist, one would seize all — the accomplishment of all <s>mudrā</s>s is obtained. // 23 //
With the <s>vajra</s>-play, one bestows delight; with the <s>vajra</s>-garland, excellent beauty.
With the <s>vajra</s>-song, you are sweetly sung; with the <s>vajra</s>-dance, one subjugates. // 24 //
With the incense[-offering], mental delight; with the flower[-offering], ornaments.
The lamp-offering [bestows] great radiance; the <s>vajra</s>-perfume, fragrance. // 25 //

body.text:
vajrāṅkuśyā samākarṣed vajra āśā praveśayet /
bandhayed vajranigaḍā vajraghaṇṭā tu cālayed // iti // 26 //
body.translated_text: With the <s>vajra</s>-hook, one attracts; with the <s>vajra</s>-noose, one causes entry; with the <s>vajra</s>-chain, one binds; with the <s>vajra</s>-bell, one shakes. Thus. // 26 //

body.text: atha sarvamudrāṇāṃ sāmānyā bandhavidhivistaro bhavati / tatrādita eva vajrabandhāṅgulīṃ tālaṃ kṛtvā hṛdaye, idaṃ hṛdayamuccārayet vajrabandha traṭ // tataḥ sarvamudrābandhāḥ svakāyavākcittavajreṣu vaśībhavanti //
body.translated_text: Now the common elaboration of the binding procedure for all <s>mudrā</s>s is as follows. Therein, first making the <s>vajra</s>-binding finger-clap at the heart, one should pronounce this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: '<s>vajrabandha traṭ</s>!' Thereupon all <s>mudrā</s>-bindings come under the power of one's own body, speech, and mind-<s>vajra</s>s.

body.text: tato vajrāveśasamayamudrāṃ badhvā, idaṃ hṛdayamuccārayet aḥ // tataḥ samāviṣṭā mitratvenopatiṣṭhanti //
body.translated_text: Then, having bound the <s>vajra</s>-entry pledge-<s>mudrā</s>, one should pronounce this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: 'aḥ!' Thereupon [the deities], having entered, attend as friends.

body.text: tato mudrāsamayamahāsattvānanusmṛtyedaṃ hṛdayamudāharet mahāsamayasattvo 'ham // anena sarvamudrāḥ siddhyantīti / sarvamudrāvidhivistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, recollecting the <s>mudrā</s>-pledge great beings, one should pronounce this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: '<s>mahāsamayasattvo 'ham</s>' (I am the great pledge-being). By this, all <s>mudrā</s>s are accomplished. This is the elaboration of the procedure for all <s>mudrā</s>s.

body.text: atha sāmānyaḥ sādhanavidhivistaro bhavati / tatrādita eva svamudrāṃ badhvā svamudrāsatvamātmānaṃ bhāvayedanena hṛdayena samayo 'ham //
body.translated_text: Now the common elaboration of the accomplishment procedure is as follows. Therein, first binding one's own <s>mudrā</s>, one should visualize oneself as one's own <s>mudrā</s>-being with this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: '<s>samayo 'ham</s>' (I am the pledge).

body.text: tataḥ svamudrāsattvamātmānaṃ bhāvya tenādhiṣṭhāyedanena mantreṇa samayasattvādhitiṣṭhasva mām / tataḥ sādhayediti / sādhanāvidhivistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, having visualized oneself as one's own <s>mudrā</s>-being, one should empower [oneself] with this <s>mantra</s>: '<s>samayasattvādhitiṣṭhasva mām</s>' (O pledge-being, empower me!). Then one should accomplish. This is the elaboration of the accomplishment procedure.

body.text: atha siddhividhivistaro bhavati / tatrādita eva arthasiddhimicchatā tena hṛdayena arthasiddhi // anena siddhā mudrā mahārthotpattin karoti //
body.translated_text: Now the elaboration of the accomplishment-rites is as follows. Therein, first, one who desires the accomplishment of a purpose [should recite] this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: '<s>arthasiddhi</s>' (accomplishment of purpose). By this, the accomplished <s>mudrā</s> produces the arising of great purpose.

body.text: atha vajrasiddhimicchedanena hṛdayena vajrasiddhi // anena yathābhirucitavajrasiddho bhavati //
body.translated_text: Now, one who desires <s>vajra</s>-accomplishment [should recite] this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: '<s>vajrasiddhi</s>' (vajra-accomplishment). By this, one becomes accomplished in <s>vajra</s>-attainment as desired.

body.text:
atha vidyādharasiddhimicchedanena hṛdayena vajravidyādhara // anena yathābhirucitavidyādharasiddhiḥ / athottamasiddhimicchet svamudrāhṛdayeneti /
siddhividhivistaraḥ //
body.translated_text: Now, one who desires the accomplishment of becoming a <s>vidyādhara</s> (knowledge-holder) [should recite] this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: '<s>vajravidyādhara</s>' (vajra knowledge-holder). By this, one attains the <s>vidyādhara</s>-accomplishment as desired. Now, one who desires the supreme accomplishment should [recite] one's own <s>mudrā</s>-heart[-<s>mantra</s>]. This is the elaboration of the accomplishment-rites.

body.text:
atha sarvamudrāṇāṃ sāmānyaḥ svakāyavākcittavajreṣu vajrīkaraṇavidhivistaro bhavati /
yadā mudrādhiṣṭhānaṃ śithilībhavati, svayaṃ vā muktukāmo bhavati, tato 'nena hṛdayena dṛḍhīkartavyā /
oṃ vajra sattvasamayamanupālaya,
vajrasattvatvenopatiṣṭha,
dṛḍho me bhava, sutoṣyo me bhavānurakto me bhava,
supoṣyo me bhava, sarvasiddhiñca me prayaccha,

children.text: sarvakarmasu ca me cittaśreyaḥ kuru hūṃ
children.translated_text: Be well-nourished for me! Grant me all accomplishments! And in all activities, make my mind auspicious! Hūṃ!

children.text: ha ha ha ha hoḥ bhagavan sarvatathāgatavajra mā me muṃca,
children.translated_text: Ha ha ha ha hoḥ! O <s>Bhagavān</s>, <s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, do not abandon me!
Become <s>vajra</s>! O great pledge-being! Āḥ!'

body.translated_text: Now the common elaboration of the procedure for making <s>vajra</s> one's own body, speech, and mind-<s>vajra</s>s of all <s>mudrā</s>s is as follows. When the <s>mudrā</s>-empowerment becomes slack, or when one wishes to release [the <s>mudrā</s>], then one should make it firm with this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: 'Oṃ! <s>Vajrasattva</s>, guard the pledge! Attend me as <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Be firm for me! Be well-pleased with me! Be affectionate toward me!

body.text: "anenānantaryakāriṇo 'pi sarvatathāgatamokṣā api saddharmapratikṣepakā api sarvaduṣkṛtakāriṇo 'pi sarvatathāgatamudrāsādhakā varjasattvadṛḍhībhāvādihaiva janmanyāsu yathābhirucitāṃ sarvasiddhimuttamasiddhiṃ vajrasiddhiṃ vajrasattvasiddhiṃ vā yāvat tathāgatasiddhiṃ vā prāpsyantī- "tyāha bhagavāṃ sarvatathāgatavajrasattvaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatavajrasattva</s> said: 'By this, even those who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution, even those who have rejected the true <s>Dharma</s>, even those who have committed all evil deeds — all who accomplish the <s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s through the firmness of <s>Vajrasattva</s> — in this very life they will quickly attain all accomplishments as desired: the supreme accomplishment, the <s>vajra</s>-accomplishment, the <s>Vajrasattva</s>-accomplishment, or even the <s>Tathāgata</s>-accomplishment.'

body.text: atha svamudrāṇāṃ sāmānyo mokṣavidhivistaro bhavati / tatrādita eva yatoyataḥ samutpannā mudrā tān tatratatraiva muñcedanena hṛdayena vajra muḥ //
body.translated_text: Now the common elaboration of the release procedure for one's own <s>mudrā</s>s is as follows. Therein, first, wherever the <s>mudrā</s>s have arisen from, one should release them back to those very places with this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: '<s>vajra muḥ</s>!'

body.text: tato hṛdayotthitayā ratnavajrimudrayā svābhiṣekasthānasthitayābhiṣicyāgrāṅgulibhyāṃ mālāṃ veṣṭavyaṃ badhvā tathaiva kavacaṃ bandhayedanena hṛdayena oṃ ratnavajrābhiṣiñca sarvamudrā me dṛḍhīkuru varakavacena vam //
body.translated_text: Then, with the <s>Ratnavajrī</s>-<s>mudrā</s> arisen from the heart, stationed at one's own consecration-place, one should perform self-consecration, bind the garland with the tips of the forefingers, and likewise bind the armor with this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: 'Oṃ! <s>Ratnavajrī</s>, consecrate! Make all <s>mudrā</s>s firm for me with the excellent armor! Vaṃ!'

body.text: tataḥ punaḥ kavacāntaṃ mālābandhaṃ kṛtvā, samatālayā toṣayedanena hṛdayena vajra tuṣya hoḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, having again performed the garland-binding up to the armor, one should gratify with the even-clap, with this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: '<s>vajra tuṣya hoḥ</s>!'

children.text: anena vidhinā mudrā muktā baddhāśca toṣitā /
children.translated_text: By this procedure, the <s>mudrā</s>s — released, bound, and gratified —
will attain <s>vajra</s>-nature, or again [union with] <s>Vajrasattva</s>.
<s>Vajrasattva</s>, recited even once, [brings] bliss at will, with ease of self;
accomplishment is attained by recitation alone, just as by the word of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Samantabhadra</s>.

children.translated_text: In all the accomplishment-activities of <s>Vajrasattva</s> and the other beings,
even the recitation cherished here bestows accomplishment in all <s>kalpa</s>s.
By whatever preferred methods — of heart-<s>mudrā</s>s, <s>mantra</s>s, and <s>vidyā</s>s,

children.text: kalpoktaiḥ svakṛtairvāpi sādhanaṃ tvatra sarvataḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: whether taught in the <s>kalpa</s> or self-composed — accomplishment [arises] everywhere herein. Thus.

children.text: tataḥ pūjāguhyamudrāmudāharan, guhyapūjācatuṣṭayaṃ kāryam, anena vajrastutigītena gāyan /
children.translated_text: Then, displaying the secret offering-<s>mudrā</s>, the fourfold secret offering should be performed, singing with this <s>vajra</s>-praise song:
Oṃ! From the collection of <s>Vajrasattva</s>, the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-jewel!
By singing the <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>, become the performer of <s>vajra</s>-activity!

body.text: tato 'bhyantaramaṇḍale 'pyanenaiva vajrastutigītena vajranṛtyakarapuṭena gṛhya dhūpādibhiḥ pūjā kāryā / tato bāhyamaṇḍale vajradhūpādibhiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā, tāḥ pūjā svasthāneṣu sthāpayet / tataḥ "sarve yathāśaktyā pūjayantvi" ti sarvatathāgatān vijñāpya, yathecchayā dhūpādibhiḥ pūjāṃ kārayitvā, yathā praviṣṭāṃ yathā vibhavataḥ sarvarasāhāravihārādibhiḥ sarvopakaraṇarmahāmaṇḍale niryātitaiḥ santuṣyedaṃ sarvatathāgatasiddhivajravrataṃ dadyāt /
body.translated_text: Then, in the inner <s>maṇḍala</s> as well, with this very <s>vajra</s>-praise song, holding the <s>vajra</s>-dance hand-vessel, worship should be performed with incense and the rest. Then, having performed worship in the outer <s>maṇḍala</s> with <s>vajra</s>-incense and the rest, one should station those offerings in their own places. Then, having informed all <s>Tathāgata</s>s: 'May all worship according to their capacity,' and having caused worship to be performed with incense and the rest as one wishes, one should be satisfied with all the provisions — food, enjoyments, dwellings, and all requisites — offered in the great <s>maṇḍala</s> as one entered, according to one's means, and should confer this <s>vajra</s>-vow of the accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text: This is that very state of all <s>Buddha</s>hood, established in the hand of <s>Vajrasattva</s>.
You too should always uphold this firm vow of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>!

body.text:
oṃ sarvatathāgatasiddhi vajrasamaya tiṣṭha
eṣa tvā dhārayāmi vajrasatva hi hi hi hi hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ! O accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>vajra</s>-pledge, remain! I shall uphold you, O <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Hi hi hi hi hūṃ!

body.text:
tataḥ " sarveṣāṃ punarapi na kasyacid vaktavyam" iti śapathahṛdayamākhyeyaṃ /
tato yathā praviṣṭān saṃpreṣya sarvatathāgatān vijñāpayet, satvavajrimudrāṃ badhvordhvato muñced, idaṃ ca hṛdayamuccārayet /
body.translated_text: Then the oath-heart[-<s>mantra</s>] should be declared: 'This should not be told to anyone again.' Then, having sent off those who entered as before, one should inform all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, bind the <s>Sattvavajrī</s>-<s>mudrā</s> and release it upward, and pronounce this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]:

body.text: oṃ kṛto vaḥ sarvasatvārthaḥ siddhirdattā yathānugā / gacchadhvaṃ buddhaviṣayaṃ punarāgamanāya tu // vajrasattva muḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ! The purpose of all beings has been accomplished by you! Accomplishment has been granted as befitting. Go to the realm of the <s>Buddha</s>s, but for the sake of coming again! <s>Vajrasattva muḥ</s>!'

body.text: evaṃ sarvamaṇḍaleṣu kartavyaṃ / samayāgryā mudrāsu ca mokta iti //
body.translated_text: Thus it should be done in all <s>maṇḍala</s>s. The foremost of pledges should be released in the <s>mudrā</s>s. Thus.
The elaboration of the procedure of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>, from the great <s>kalpa</s>-king of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, is completed.
CHAPTER 2: <s>VAJRA-GUHYA-VAJRA-MAṆḌALA-VIDHI-VISTARA</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatasarvavajradharaṇīsamayasaṃbhavavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ / samanantarasamāpanne cātha tāvadeva sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ / sa eva bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ vajradhararūpadhāriṇyaḥ samanta jvālāgarbhā vajradhāraṇīsamayamudrā devatā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvabuddhānāṃ sarvatathāgatavajradhāraṇī jñānāni niṣpādya, sarvatathāgatasamayamudrābimbāni bhūtvā, sarvatathāgatānāṃ vajradhātumahāmaṇḍale sanniveśayogena candramaṇḍalānyāśrityedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of all <s>vajra</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' — immediately upon entering that <s>samādhi</s>, from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having become <s>dhāraṇī</s>-pledge-<s>mudrā</s> deities bearing the form of <s>Vajradhara</s>, with flames all around, with the womb of universal blazing, emerged and, in all world-realms, having accomplished the <s>vajra</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s> wisdoms of all <s>Buddha</s>s and all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having become pledge-<s>mudrā</s> images of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, stationed in the great <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>vajradhātu</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s through the yoga of arrangement, resting on moon-discs, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! The <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening-mind) indeed desires the benefit of all beings,
for the steadfast ones, out of the necessity of training, even assume a female form!

body.translated_text: Emanation of deities from <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatajñānamudrāsamayavajradhātvadhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyāttamāmabhāṣat oṃ vajradhātvīśvari hūṃ vajriṇi //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>vajradhātu</s> of the wisdom-<s>mudrā</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this, his supreme <s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ vajradhātvīśvari hūṃ vajriṇi</s>!

body.text: atha khalvakṣobhayastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajrasatvasamayajñānamudrāmaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānan nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ vajravajriṇi hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Akṣobhya Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the wisdom-<s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajrasattva</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this, his supreme <s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ vajravajriṇi hūṃ</s>!

body.text: atha ratnasaṃbhavastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajraratnasamayajñānamudrāmaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānan nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ ratnavajriṇi hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the wisdom-<s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this, his supreme <s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ ratnavajriṇi hūṃ</s>!

body.text: athāmitāyustathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajradharmasamayajñānamudrāmaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānan nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ dharmavajriṇi hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Amitāyus Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the wisdom-<s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this, his supreme <s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ dharmavajriṇi hūṃ</s>!

body.text: athāmoghasiddhistathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajrakarnasamayajñānamudrāmaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānan nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ karmavajriṇi hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the wisdom-<s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-activity-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this, his supreme <s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ karmavajriṇi hūṃ</s>!
Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> uttered the four great <s>dhāraṇī</s>-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:
<s>oṃ vajrasatvaguhyasamaye hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ guhyavajrāṅkuśi hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajraguhyarāge rāgaya hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ guhyavajrasādhvīśvari hūṃ</s>!

body.text:
samantabhadrā, tathāgatāṅka śī, ratirāgā, sādhumatī ca / vajradhāraṇyaḥ /
oṃ vajraguhyaratnasamaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text:
<s>Samantabhadrā</s>, <s>Tathāgatāṅkuśī</s>, <s>Ratirāgā</s>, and <s>Sādhumatī</s> — these are the <s>vajra</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s>s.
<s>oṃ vajraguhyaratnasamaye hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajraguhyaprabhe hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajradhvajāgraguhye hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ guhyahāsavajri hūṃ</s>!

body.text: ratnottamā, ratnolkā, dhvajāgrakeyūrā, hāsavatī ca / ratnadhāraṇyaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Ratnottamā</s>, <s>Ratnolkā</s>, <s>Dhvajāgrakeyūrā</s>, and <s>Hāsavatī</s> — these are the jewel-<s>dhāraṇī</s>s.
<s>oṃ vajradharmaguhyasamaye hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajrakośaguhye hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajraguhyamaṇḍale hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajraguhyajāpasamaye hūṃ</s>!

body.text: vajrāmbujā, ādhāraṇī, sarvacakra, sahasrāvartā ca / dharmadhāraṇyaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Vajrāmbujā</s>, <s>Ādhāraṇī</s>, <s>Sarvacakra</s>, and <s>Sahasrāvartā</s> — these are the <s>dharma</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s>s.
<s>oṃ vajraguhyakarmasamaye hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajraguhyakavace hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ guhyavajradaṃṣṭrādhāriṇi hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajraguhyamuṣṭi hūṃ</s>!

body.text: siddhottarā, sarvarakṣā, tejaḥpratyāhāriṇī, dharaṇīmudrā ca / sarvadhāraṇya iti //
body.translated_text: <s>Siddhottarā</s>, <s>Sarvarakṣā</s>, <s>Tejaḥpratyāhāriṇī</s>, and <s>Dharaṇīmudrā</s> — these are the complete <s>dhāraṇī</s>s.

children.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> again uttered the four <s>vajra</s>-secret-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:
<s>oṃ guhyasatvavajri hūṃ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>oṃ guhyaratnavajri hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ guhyadharmavajri hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ guhyakarmavajri hūṃ</s>!

children.translated_text: Those very ones — the <s>vajra</s>-<s>pāramitā</s>s and the rest — are the pledge-<s>mudrā</s>s that gather the <s>vajra</s>-secret-pledge-<s>dhāraṇī</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
They should be placed with flames, resting on moon-discs, in the great <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Vajradhātvīśvarī</s>.
Then again <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> uttered the four <s>vajra</s>-secret-offering-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:
<s>oṃ vajraguhyaratipūjāsamaye sarvapūjāṃ pravartaya hūṃ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajraguhyābhiṣekapūjāsamaye sarvapūjāṃ pravartaya hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajraguhyagītāpūjāsamaye sarvapūjāṃ pravartaya hūṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajraguhyanṛtyapūjāsamaye sarvapūjāṃ pravartaya hūṃ</s>!

body.text: tā eva vajralāsyādayaḥ sajvālāḥ svacinhā mudrāścakramaṇḍalakoṇacatuṣṭaye sthāpyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Those very ones — <s>Vajralāsyā</s> and the rest — with flames, bearing their own emblems, should be placed as <s>mudrā</s>s at the four corners of the <s>cakra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>.
Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>

body.text:
atha vajrapāṇiḥ punarapīdaṃ vajraguhyaṃ nāma mahāvajramaṇḍalamabhāṣat /
athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi vajramaṇḍalamuttamaṃ /
body.translated_text:
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> again uttered this [teaching] called the 'secret <s>vajra</s>' — the great <s>vajra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>:
Now I shall expound the supreme <s>vajra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>vajradhātu</s>, known as the '<s>vajra</s>-secret'! (1)

children.translated_text: By the method of the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should draw every <s>maṇḍala</s>;
in the centers of every <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should draw the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s. (2)

children.text: paryaṅke vajrā vajrāṃ tu vajracinteti kīrtitā // 3 // //
children.translated_text: a <s>vajra</s> in the cross-legged posture, and the <s>vajra</s> [-form], is proclaimed as <s>Vajracintā</s>. (3)

body.translated_text: A <s>caitya</s> (shrine) well-established in the cross-legged posture is known as <s>Vajradhātvīśvarī</s>;

children.translated_text: A <s>vajra</s>-jewel in the cross-legged posture is proclaimed as one's own consecration (<s>svābhiṣeka</s>);
a <s>vajra</s>-lotus in the cross-legged posture is proclaimed as the weapon (<s>āyudha</s>). (4)
An activity-<s>vajra</s> in the cross-legged posture is proclaimed as the all-<s>vajra</s> (<s>sarvavajra</s>);
they should be drawn established on lotuses, situated in halos of radiance. (5)
In the cross-legged posture, one should draw a <s>vajra</s> raised up, and likewise a double hook;
a <s>vajra</s> joined with a <s>vajra</s>, and likewise a double exclamation of 'well done!' (6)
One should make a jewel blazing in the hand, and likewise a sun-<s>mudrā</s>;
and a flaming banner-crest, with a double <s>vajra</s> at the row of teeth. (7)
In the middle of the <s>vajra</s>, one should draw a lotus, and a flaming sword;
a <s>vajra</s>-spoked <s>vajra</s>-wheel, and a tongue blazing with rays from the hand. (8)

children.text: vajraṃ tu sarvato vaktraṃ kavacaṃ vajrasaṃyutaṃ /
children.translated_text: A <s>vajra</s> with mouths in all directions, an armor joined with <s>vajra</s>;
<s>vajra</s>-fangs should likewise be drawn, and the fist-<s>mudrā</s> with both hands. (9)
The <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajra</s> and the rest should be drawn as appropriate in the <s>dhātu</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>;
emblem-<s>mudrā</s>s should be drawn in the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Vajralāsyā</s> and the rest. (10)

body.text:
bāhyātaśca yathāyogaṃ svacinhaṃtu samālikhet /
maitreyādisvacinhāni yathābhirucitaṃ likhed // 11 // iti //
body.translated_text:
And on the outside, as applicable, one should draw the respective emblems;
the emblems of <s>Maitreya</s> and the rest should be drawn as desired. (11)
Initiation into the <s>maṇḍala</s>
Now here, the extensive and various [rites] of entry and the rest into the <s>vajra</s>-secret-<s>maṇḍala</s> are [as follows]:

body.text: tatra prathamaṃ tāvadvajrācāryaḥ svayaṃ satvavajrimudrāṃ badhvā praviśet; praviśya sakṛt pradakṣiṇīkṛtya, tāṃ mudrāṃ bhagavate vajrapāṇaye niryātya, svahṛdaye yathāvanmuktvā, caturṣu dvāreṣu vajrāṅku śakarmamudrādibhiryathāvat karmāṇi kṛtvā niṣkramed, abhiniṣkramya śiṣyāṃ praveśayet vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalayogeneti / tataḥ praveśya muṣṭyācchādya siddhiguhyavajracinhaṃ datvā, vajraguhyamudrājñānaṃ śikṣayet //
body.translated_text: Therein, first the <s>vajrācārya</s> (vajra-master) himself, having formed the <s>sattvavajrī</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, should enter; having entered, having circumambulated once, having offered that <s>mudrā</s> to <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having duly released it at his own heart, having performed the appropriate rites at the four gates with the activity-<s>mudrā</s>s of <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s> and the rest, he should exit. Having exited, he should cause the disciple to enter by the method of the <s>vajradhātu</s>-great-<s>maṇḍala</s>. Then, having caused [the disciple] to enter, having covered [their eyes] with the fist, having given the emblem of the secret accomplishment-<s>vajra</s>, he should teach the <s>vajra</s>-secret-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge.
<s>Mudrā</s>
Therein, first one should teach the <s>vajra</s>-secret-body-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: In the middle of a moon-disc, [visualizing] hands, feet, palms joined, and face,
stretching forth, one should meditate on the <s>vajra</s>, and also delight the <s>vajriṇī</s> (vajra-goddess). (1)

children.text: aṅkuśaṃ bāhusaṃkocaṃ śīrṣe vajraṃ tu bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: The hook — one should meditate on the contraction of the arm, [with] a <s>vajra</s> at the head;
making a sound with the hand, one should also summon the hook-goddess. (2)
With the method of casting the arrow, stretching forth, one should strike at the heart;
one should enamor through the method of conquest, oneself becoming the desire-<s>vajrā</s>. (3)

body.text:
bāhubandhena badhnīyād hṛdayaṃ svayamātmanaḥ /
vajravarmaprayogeṇa rakṣed buddhamapi svayam // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
One should bind one's own heart with the binding of the arms;
with the application of <s>vajra</s>-armor, one should protect even the <s>Buddha</s> himself. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart [-mantras]:
<s>vajra rāgaya hoḥ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>vajrāṅkuśa jaḥ</s>!
<s>māraya māraya phaṭ</s>!
<s>bandha rakṣa haṃ</s>!
Then one should teach the <s>vajra</s>-secret-gaze-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: The <s>vajra</s>-gaze is [characterized by] eyes opened wide with passion and delight;

children.text: tayā nirīkṣatā strī tu vaśyā bhavati śāśvatī // 1 //
children.translated_text: by looking with that [gaze], a woman is brought permanently under one's power. (1)
With swiftly moving, trembling eyes, with a gaze that draws the eyelashes,
this is called the blazing-attraction [gaze]; it attracts the entire world. (2)
With furrowed brows broken in anger, with eyes contracted in wrath,
employing the wrathful gaze, one could destroy even the three worlds. (3)

body.translated_text:
With firm, unblinking eyes like stones that could crush <s>Meru</s>,
this is known as the loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) gaze — it removes fevers, seizures, and poisons. (4)

children.translated_text: Now these are their heart [-mantras]:
<s>vajradṛṣṭi maṭ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>dīptadṛṣṭyāṅkuśi jaḥ</s>!
<s>krodhadṛṣṭi hīḥ</s>!
<s>dṛḍhadṛṣṭi traṭ</s>!
Then one should teach the <s>vajra</s>-secret-speech-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.text: hoḥ hoḥ hoḥ ho iti prokte vāgvivartitayā kṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: When '<s>hoḥ hoḥ hoḥ ho</s>' is uttered, with the turning of speech, in an instant
one enamors all beings with the <s>vajra</s>-voice, clearly manifest. (1)

children.text: jjaḥ jjaḥ jjaḥ jja iti prokte krodhavācā parisphuṭāṃ /
children.translated_text: When '<s>jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ ja</s>' is uttered, with the wrathful voice, clearly manifest,
one attracts the entire world — even one like <s>Vajradhara</s>. (2)

children.text: huṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ samādhāya śabdavācā parisphuṭāṃ /
children.translated_text: Concentrating '<s>huṃ huṃ huṃ huṃ</s>' with the resounding voice, clearly manifest,
one conquers all beings — [with a voice] like the crushing of <s>Meru</s>. (3)

body.text:
haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ iti prokte sūkṣmavācā parisphuṭāṃ /
rakṣet sarvamidaṃ locamapi vajrātmakaṃ jinam // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
When '<s>haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ</s>' is uttered, with the subtle voice, clearly manifest,
one protects this entire world — even the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) whose nature is <s>vajra</s>. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart [-mantras]:
<s>vajra hoḥ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>vajra jaḥ</s>!
<s>vajra huṃ</s>!
<s>vajra haṃ</s>!
Then one should teach the <s>vajra</s>-secret-mind-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: Meditating on oneself, endowed with all excellent aspects,
as <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, one brings all <s>Buddha</s>s under one's power. (1)
Meditating on oneself, endowed with all excellent aspects,
as <s>Vajragarbha</s>, one attracts <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> himself. (2)
Meditating on oneself, endowed with all excellent aspects,
as <s>Vajranetra</s>, one conquers all <s>dharma</s>s. (3)

body.text:
sarvākāravaropetaṃ bhāvayan svayamātmanā /
vajraviśvaṃ svamātmānaṃ sarvavajraṃ sa rakṣati // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Meditating on oneself, endowed with all excellent aspects,
as <s>Vajraviśva</s>, one protects all <s>vajra</s>s. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart [-mantras]:
<s>vajrapāṇi vaśamānaya sarvabuddhān hoḥ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>vajragarbha vajrapāṇiṃ śīghramākarṣaya hūṃ jaḥ</s>!
<s>vajranetra sarvadharmān māraya hūṃ phaṭ</s>!
<s>vajraviśva rakṣa sarvavajrān haṃ</s>!
Then one should teach the <s>vajra</s>-secret-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: Placing the <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajrā</s> at one's own heart,
gazing with the <s>vajra</s>-gaze, one causes the entire world to enter. (1)
Placing the jewel-<s>vajrā</s> at one's own heart,
gazing with the blazing gaze, one brings everything under one's power. (2)
Placing the <s>dharma</s>-<s>vajrā</s> at one's own heart,

children.text: krodhadṛṣṭyā nirīkṣan vai jagatsarvaṃ sa mārayet // 3 //
children.translated_text: gazing with the wrathful gaze, one conquers the entire world. (3)

body.text:
karmavajrāṃ samādhāya hṛdaye svayamātmanaḥ /
maitrīdṛṣṭyā nirīkṣan vai rakṣetsarvamidaṃ jagad // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Placing the activity-<s>vajrā</s> at one's own heart,
gazing with the loving-kindness gaze, one protects this entire world. (4)

children.translated_text: Now these are the heart [-mantras] of those <s>vajra</s>-secret-wisdom-<s>mudrā</s>s:
<s>vajraguhyasamaya aḥ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>vajraguhyasamaya hoḥ</s>!
<s>vajraguhyasamaya huṃ</s>!
<s>vajraguhyasamaya haṃ</s>!
Then one should teach the binding of <s>vajra</s>-secret-<s>mudrā</s>s:

children.translated_text: Born from the <s>vajrāñjali</s> (vajra-salutation), they are proclaimed as the great secrets;
these great <s>mudrā</s>s — their binding will be briefly explained. (1)
With the two thumbs in cross-legged position, with curved tips of the fingertips,
with evenly [placed] middle and topmost parts — this is known as <s>Vajradhātvīśvarī</s>. (2)

children.text: sā eva madhyavajrā tu madhyābhyāṃ tu maṇīkṛtā /
children.translated_text: That very one, with a <s>vajra</s> in the middle, with the middle [fingers] made into a jewel,
and with a lotus at the tips of the ring [fingers], with outstretched hand-fingers — (3)
the foremost <s>vajra</s> with double <s>vajra</s>-tips, concealed by the two thumbs;
the exclamation-of-'well-done'-foremost-jewel, with jewel-tips blazing from the hand; (4)
the ring-finger-tip jewel — that very one reversed;
with all fingers well-extended, positioned between the thumbs. (5)
That very [mudrā] with extended finger-rings, raised from the mouth,
covered by the thumbs' vajra, positioned within, with the tips [meeting]. (6)
That [mudrā] with the two thumbs opened — then the inner vajra[-mudrā].
And again, these are the vajra-secret [mudrās], arising from the vajra-binding. (7)
And again, the dharma-secret [mudrās] with symbols generated within the cupped [hands];
with symbols positioned within the karma-secret — this is the demonstration of karma. (8)
Hereafter I shall explain the dharma-mudrās in brief.

children.text: āḥ jjaḥ hoḥ saḥ, uṃ āṃ traṃ haḥ,
children.translated_text: Āḥ Jaḥ Hoḥ Saḥ, Uṃ Āṃ Traṃ Haḥ,

children.text: hrīḥ dhaṃ bhaṃ raṃ, kaṃ haṃ huṃ vaṃ // 1 //
children.translated_text: Hrīḥ Dhaṃ Bhaṃ Raṃ, Kaṃ Haṃ Hūṃ Vaṃ. (1)
The secret mudrā, divided in two, should be arranged among the karma-mudrās;

children.text: yāvadyaḥ samayāgryo vai dvidhīkṛtya tathaiva ca // 2 //
children.translated_text: and likewise, whatever is the foremost pledge [mudrā], divided in two. (2)

body.text: athāsāṃ sādhanaṃ vakṣye samayastvam iti brūvan /
body.translated_text: Now I shall explain their accomplishment, saying 'you are the pledge.'
Having bound [the mudrā] oneself, they become accomplished — those whose nature is the bliss of desire-passion. (1)

children.text: āsāṃ tvadhikamekaṃ tu sarvakālaṃ na bandhayet /
children.translated_text: But one should not bind even one of these in excess at all times;
the discerning one should employ [them] only in secret or in a matter of great importance. (2)

body.text:
yasarvātmasitthāta hyetā dṛḍhabhāryāḥ svayaṃbhuvāṃ /
sādhakeṣu dṛḍhaṃ raktā mā tyajeyuḥ patinnijam // 3 // iti //
body.translated_text:
These are indeed the firm consorts of the self-existent ones, who are the essence of all;
firmly devoted to practitioners, they should not abandon their own lord. (3)

children.translated_text: And from the binding of all these mudrās, the following actions arise:
Having generated the vajra-possession, whether of oneself or of another,
one may bind or indeed bind again — with this heart[-mantra]:

body.translated_text: Vajra Hūṃ — Bind!
Now the releasing:

children.translated_text: From wherever all mudrās have arisen, in brief,

children.text: tatra tatra tāṃ muñcedanena hṛdayena tu //
children.translated_text: there one should release that [mudrā] — with this heart[-mantra]:

body.translated_text: Oṃ Vajra Muḥ!
Now the strengthening:

children.translated_text: Having strengthened the jewel-vajra, releasing it from the heart to the crown,
one should bind the armor with the tips — with this heart[-mantra]:

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Firm! Vajra-armor — Dhṛṭ!
Now the binding-pledge:

children.text: yathā sthāneṣu vai muktā kavacena dṛḍhīkṛtā /
children.translated_text: Having been released in their respective places and strengthened by the armor,
one should bind all with the lock — with this heart[-mantra]:

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Secret-pledge-lock — Saḥ!

children.translated_text: <s>Vajrasattva</s> recited with splendor should be employed in all maṇḍala-activities,
at this pledge[-occasion] — it is the supreme producer of all accomplishments.

body.translated_text: From the great ritual-manual of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the detailed procedure of the <s>vajra</s>-secret <s>vajra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> is completed.
CHAPTER 3: DETAILED PROCEDURE OF THE <s>VAJRA</s>-KNOWLEDGE-<s>DHARMA</s>-<s>MAṆḌALA</s>
Emanation of deities from <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatasūkṣmavajrajñānamudrāsamayamaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ sūkṣmavajrajñānasamaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the Empowerment of the <s>Maṇḍala</s> of the Pledge of the Subtle <s>Vajra</s>-Knowledge-<s>Mudrā</s> of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — Subtle-<s>vajra</s>-knowledge-pledge — Hūṃ!

body.text: atha khalvakṣobhyaḥ tathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajrasatvasūkṣmajñānasamayamaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānan nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajrasatva sūkṣmajñānasamaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Akṣobhya Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the Empowerment of the <s>Maṇḍala</s> of the Pledge of the Subtle Knowledge of <s>Vajrasattva</s> of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — <s>Vajrasattva</s>-subtle-knowledge-pledge — Hūṃ!

body.text: atha khalu ratnasaṃbhavastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajraratnasūkṣmajñānasamayamaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajraratna sūkṣmajñānasamaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the Empowerment of the <s>Maṇḍala</s> of the Pledge of the Subtle Knowledge of the <s>Vajra</s>-Jewel of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — <s>Vajraratna</s>-subtle-knowledge-pledge — Hūṃ!

body.text: atha khalvamitāyustathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajradharmasūkṣmajñānasamayamaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajradharma sūkṣmajñānasamaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Amitāyus Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the Empowerment of the <s>Maṇḍala</s> of the Pledge of the Subtle Knowledge of the <s>Vajra</s>-<s>Dharma</s> of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — <s>Vajradharma</s>-subtle-knowledge-pledge — Hūṃ!

body.text: atha khalvamoghasiddhistathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajrakarmasūkṣmajñānasamayamaṇḍalādhiṣṭhānannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajrakama sūkṣmajñānasamaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the Empowerment of the <s>Maṇḍala</s> of the Pledge of the Subtle Knowledge of the <s>Vajra</s>-Karma of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — <s>Vajrakarma</s>-subtle-knowledge-pledge — Hūṃ!

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanaḥ sarvatathāgatasūkṣmajñānavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ, samanantarasamāpanne ca bhagavatyatha tāvadeva sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sūkṣmajñānavajraraśmayo viniścaritvā, sarvalokadhātavo 'vabhāsya sarvasatvānāṃ, sarvatathāgatasūkṣmajñānavajrasamādhisamāpattīn dṛḍhī kṛtya punarapyekadhyībhūtvā, samādhijñānavajrakāyatāmadhyālambyaikaghanastathāgatajñānaḥ saṃbhūya, bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the Subtle Knowledge-<s>Vajra</s> of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s. And the very moment the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered that <s>samādhi</s>, subtle knowledge-<s>vajra</s>-rays issued forth from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and having illuminated all world-realms and all beings, having strengthened the attainment of the <s>samādhi</s> of the subtle knowledge-<s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and having again become unified, having abided in the nature of the <s>samādhi</s>-knowledge-<s>vajra</s>-body, becoming a single solid <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, it entered the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having entered from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s> knowledges, spoke this great pledge-<s>vajra</s> of the subtle knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — Subtle-<s>vajra</s>!

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyo vajrapāṇirviniḥsṛtya, sarvatathāgatasūkṣmajñānavajrabimbamātmānamadhiṣṭhāya, sarvatathāgatanāsikāgreṣu sthitvedamudānamudānayāmāsa / aho hi sarvabuddhānāṃ sūkṣmavajramahaṃ mahat / yanmahatvātsa sūkṣmo 'pi traidhātukamapi sphared // iti //
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this was spoken, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> issued forth from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and having empowered himself as the subtle knowledge-<s>vajra</s>-image of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, standing at the tip of the noses of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, uttered this inspired utterance: 'Oh! I am the great subtle <s>vajra</s> of all <s>Buddha</s>s — that which, though subtle because of its greatness, pervades even the three realms!'

body.text: athedamuktvā bhagavān vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ sarvatathāgatanāsikāgrebhyaḥ susūkṣmavajrajñānanimittaspharaṇatāya sarvatathāgatakāyebhyaḥ spharitvā, sakaladharmadhātuspharaṇatāyogena sarvākāśadhātuṃ susūkṣmavajrajñānanimittaiḥ saṃspharya, sakalākāśadhātuvispharitasarvatathāgatajñānavajrabimbamātmānamadhiṣṭhāyāvasthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Having said this, <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having pervaded from the bodies of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s from the tips of their noses by means of the radiation of the sign of the exceedingly subtle <s>vajra</s>-knowledge, and having pervaded the entire space-element with the signs of the exceedingly subtle <s>vajra</s>-knowledge through the yoga of pervading the entire <s>dharmadhātu</s>, having empowered himself as the knowledge-<s>vajra</s>-image of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s pervading the entire space-element, stood firm.

body.text: atha tasminneva kṣaṇe sarvatathāgatāḥ sarvatathāgatajñānavajramadhye vajradharmatāmadhyālambya, sarvatathāgatasūkṣmajñānavajrādhiṣṭhānannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyāvasthitāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, at that very moment, all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, abiding in the <s>vajra</s>-nature of <s>dharma</s> within the knowledge-<s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, entered and remained in the <s>samādhi</s> called the Empowerment of the Subtle Knowledge-<s>Vajra</s> of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

body.text: atha tataḥ sarvatathāgatajñānavajrātsarvatathāgatasamādhijñānahṛdayaṃ niścacāra vajranābhi tathāgata hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then from that knowledge-<s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the <s>samādhi</s>-knowledge heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth — <s>Vajranābhi</s> — <s>Tathāgata</s> — Hūṃ!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ punarapi sūkṣmajñānapraveśayogena sarvatathāgatakāyeṣu praviṣṭvā, hṛdaye vajrabimbāni bhūtvāvasthitāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged, <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having again entered the bodies of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s through the yoga of the entry of subtle knowledge, having become <s>vajra</s>-images in their hearts, stood firm.

children.text: atha tebhyaḥ sarvatathāgatasatvavajrebhya idaṃ mahājñānahṛdayacatuṣṭayaṃ niścacāra /
children.translated_text: Then from all those <s>Sattvavajra</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, this set of four great knowledge-hearts issued forth:
<s>Vajra</s>-natured!

body.translated_text: Heart-<s>vajra</s>-hook!
Abide, passion-<s>vajra</s> — enter the heart!
Oh, <s>vajra</s>-satisfaction!

The <s>Vajrasattva</s> knowledge-<s>mudrā</s>, the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the empowerment of the assembly of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of enamoring all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of great satisfaction — these are the great <s>vajra</s>-<s>samādhi</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiḥ sarvatathāgatahṛdayaḥ punarapi sūkṣmajñānapraveśayogena svahṛdayaṃ praviṣṭvā hṛdaye vajrabimbamātmānamadhiṣṭhāyāvasthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, being the heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having again entered his own heart through the yoga of the entry of subtle knowledge, having empowered himself as a <s>vajra</s>-image in the heart, stood firm.

children.translated_text: Then from that <s>vajra</s>-body, this set of four hearts issued forth:
<s>Vajra</s>-jewel-natured!

body.translated_text: Heart — <s>Vajra</s>-sun!
Abide, summit of the <s>vajra</s>-banner — Vaṃ!
Heart — <s>Vajra</s>-laughter!

body.text: sarvatathāgatavajrābhiṣekajñānamudraḥ, mahāprabhāmaṇḍalavyūhajñānamudraḥ, sarvatathāgatāśāparipūraṇajñānamudraḥ, sarvatathāgatamahāhāsajñānamudra iti / sarvatathāgataratnasamādhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-consecration of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the array of the great radiance-halo, the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the fulfillment of the wishes of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the great laughter of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — these are the jewel-<s>samādhi</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiḥ punarapi sūkṣmavajrajñānapraveśayogena svahṛdayaṃ vajrahṛdayaṃ praviṣṭvā vajrabimbamātmānamadhiṣṭhāyāvasthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having again entered his own heart — the <s>vajra</s>-heart — through the yoga of the entry of subtle <s>vajra</s>-knowledge, having empowered himself as a <s>vajra</s>-image, stood firm.

children.translated_text: Then from that <s>vajra</s>-image, this set of four hearts issued forth:
<s>Vajra</s>-lotus-natured!

body.translated_text: Heart — <s>Vajra</s>-sheath!
Abide, <s>vajra</s>-wheel — enter the heart!
<s>Vajra</s>-tongue-tip heart!

The knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the equality of all <s>dharma</s>s, the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the entry into the great wheel, and the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the verbal elaboration of the <s>Dharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — these are the <s>dharma</s>-<s>samādhi</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiḥ punarapi svahṛdayavajrahṛdayavajrāt susūkṣmajñānapraveśayogena tadvajrahṛdayaṃ praviṣṭvā, punarapi sūkṣmavajrabimbamātmānamadhiṣṭhāyāvasthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having again entered that <s>vajra</s>-heart from the <s>vajra</s> of his own heart's <s>vajra</s>-heart through the yoga of the entry of exceedingly subtle knowledge, having again empowered himself as a subtle <s>vajra</s>-image, stood firm.

children.translated_text: Then from that subtle <s>vajra</s>-image, this set of four hearts issued forth:
All-<s>vajra</s>-natured!

body.translated_text: Heart — <s>Vajra</s>-armor!
Abide, <s>Vajrayakṣa</s> — heart!
<s>Vajra</s>-fist heart!

body.text: sarvatathāgataviśvakarmajñānamudraḥ, duryodhanavīryajñānamudraḥ, sarvamāramaṇḍalavidhvaṃsanajñānamudraḥ, sarvatathāgatabandhajñānamudra iti / sarvatathāgatakarmasamādhayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the universal activity of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of invincible valor, the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the destruction of all <s>Māra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>s, and the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the binding of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — these are the karma-<s>samādhi</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ punarapi susūkṣmajñānanimittaspharaṇayogena sarvatathāgatakāyebhyo niḥkramya, vajrapāṇimahābodhisattvakāyaḥ saṃbhūya, punarapi vajrasatvādimahābodhisatvavigrahāṇi bhūtvā, svāni svāni cinhāni hṛdayeṣu pratiṣṭhāpya, vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalasanniveśayogena candramaṇḍalānyāśritya svahṛdayasamādhayaḥ samāpadyāvasthitā iti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having again emerged from the bodies of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s through the yoga of radiating exceedingly subtle knowledge-signs, having become the body of the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>, having again become the forms of the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>s beginning with <s>Vajrasattva</s>, having established their respective symbols in their hearts, and having assumed [positions on] moon-disks in the arrangement of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>, they entered their own heart-<s>samādhi</s>s and stood firm.
Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, again, for the purpose of accomplishing the <s>samādhi</s>-knowledge-<s>abhijñā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this <s>vajra</s>-subtle-knowledge-<s>maṇḍala</s>:

children.translated_text: Now I shall explain the supreme <s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>Vajradhātu</s>, known as the <s>Vajrasūkṣma</s> (Subtle <s>Vajra</s>). (1)
By the method of the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should install the great beings;
in the center of the <s>vajra</s>, one should draw the <s>Buddha</s>, and in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>s as well. (2)

body.text:
mahāsatvāḥ samālekhyāḥ svamudrāhṛdayantathā /
samādhito niṣaṇṇāstu vajrabandhakaradvayā // 3 // iti //
body.translated_text:
The great beings should be drawn with their own <s>mudrā</s>s and hearts,
seated in <s>samādhi</s>, with both hands in <s>vajra</s>-binding. (3)
<s>Mudrā</s>

body.text: athātra vajrasūkṣmadharmamaṇḍala ākarṣaṇādividhivistaro, mahāmaṇḍalayogena praveśādividhivistaraṃ jñānacinhaṃ pāṇibhyāṃ datvā, svacittaparikarmamahāmudrājñānaṃ śikṣayet /
body.translated_text: Now here, in the <s>vajra</s>-subtle-<s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, the detailed procedure of attraction and the rest, [follows] the method of the great <s>maṇḍala</s>; for the detailed procedure of entry and the rest, having given the knowledge-symbol with the hands, one should teach the self-purification great <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.text: jivhāṃ tālugatāṃ kṛtvā nāsikāgraṃ tu cintayet /
children.translated_text: Having placed the tongue against the palate, one should contemplate the tip of the nose.
From the bliss-touch of the subtle <s>vajra</s>, the mind becomes concentrated. (1)
When the sign of the bliss-touch of the subtle <s>vajra</s> arises,
one should radiate that sign — that mind pervades everywhere. (2)
By radiation at will, the mind pervades even the three realms;
then one should withdraw it back until it reaches the tip of the nose. (3)
Then, from that point on, whatever one meditates upon with perfect concentration,
all of that should be made firm — produced by <s>samādhi</s>-knowledge. (4)
Now, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Subtle <s>vajra</s>!

body.translated_text: Radiate, <s>vajra</s>!
Withdraw, <s>vajra</s>!
<s>Vajra</s> — firm — abide!

children.text: maitrī yasya satvasya saha bhūyāt mahādṛḍhā /
children.translated_text: For whichever being great firm loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) arises,
by the yoga of mind-radiation, one should radiate that among all beings. (1)
By the yoga of the radiation of loving-kindness, whatever compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>) [arises] for anyone,
one who is engaged in the welfare of all beings should radiate [it] through practice. (2)
All are luminous by nature, primordially pure, equal to space;

children.text: adharmo 'pyatha vā dharm[aḥ spha]raṃ bhāvena tuṣyati // 3 //
children.translated_text: whether non-<s>dharma</s> or <s>dharma</s>, one is satisfied by the radiant meditation. (3)

body.text:
durdurūṭasamamukhyā buddhabodhāvabhājayāḥ /
teṣāṃ saṃśodhanārthāya mahopekṣāṃ tu bhāvayed // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Those who are chiefly stubborn and resistant, who do not partake of <s>Buddha</s>-awakening —
for the purpose of purifying them, one should cultivate great equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Radiate with great loving-kindness!

body.translated_text: Radiate with great compassion!
All-pure — joy — radiate!
Awaken all beings!
Then one should teach the recollection-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:
