children.translated_text: In space or in another place, through the application of the subtle <s>vajra</s> —

children.text: utthito vā niṣaṇṇo vā vajrabimbaṃ tu bhāvayet // 1 //
children.translated_text: Whether standing or seated, one should contemplate a <s>vajra</s>-image. (1)
Likewise, in all situations, through the subtle <s>vajra</s> application,
one should contemplate the heart-<s>vajra</s> <s>bodhisattva</s>, well-concentrated. (2)
One should contemplate the great image of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> in all situations,
through the subtle <s>vajra</s> application, properly and in due sequence. (3)

body.text:
sarvākāravaropetaṃ buddhabimbaṃ tu sarvataḥ /
yathāvadanupūrveṇa bhāvayetsusamāhita // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
One should contemplate a <s>Buddha</s>-image endowed with all excellent marks, everywhere,
properly and in due sequence, well-concentrated. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Become <s>vajra</s>-face!

body.translated_text: Enter, great <s>bodhisattva</s>!
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, show your own form!
Enter through <s>Buddha</s>-recollection (<s>buddhānusmṛti</s>)!

children.translated_text: Through the subtle <s>vajra</s> application, one should contemplate by oneself —
a moon-disc as one's own self — this is the cultivation of <s>bodhicitta</s>. (1)
In the center of a moon-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should contemplate by oneself —
a <s>vajra</s>-image as one's own self — this is the cultivation of the being-<s>vajra</s> (<s>sattvavajra</s>). (2)
Employing the subtle <s>vajra</s> method, one should contemplate by oneself —
oneself as the heart of the being-<s>vajra</s> — this is the cultivation of <s>Vajrasattva</s>. (3)

body.text:
sarvākāravaropetaṃ bhāvayetsvayamātmanā /
buddha bimbaṃ svamātmānaṃ buddhabodhestu bhāvanā // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Endowed with all excellent marks, one should contemplate by oneself —
a <s>Buddha</s>-image as one's own self — this is the cultivation of <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Enter, <s>Samantabhadra</s>!

body.translated_text: Enter, being-<s>vajra</s> (<s>sattvavajra</s>)!
Enter, <s>samādhi</s>-knowledge of <s>Vajrasattva</s>!
I am a <s>Tathāgata</s>!
Then one should teach the secret <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge of the <s>dharma</s>-nature of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

children.translated_text: 'I am equal to a <s>Tathāgata</s>' — speaking once with <s>vajra</s>-speech,
through the attainment of the two faculties, one subjugates all beings. (1)
'I am equal to the great <s>vajra</s>' — speaking once with <s>vajra</s>-speech,
through the attainment of the two faculties, one certainly attracts the world. (2)
'I am equal to <s>Vajradharma</s>' — speaking once with <s>vajra</s>-speech,
through the attainment of the two faculties, one destroys the entire world. (3)

body.text:
viśvavajrasamo 'haṃ hi vajravācā sakṛdvadan /
dvayendriyasamāpattyā sarvakarma sa sādhayed // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
'I am equal to the universal <s>vajra</s>' — speaking once with <s>vajra</s>-speech,
through the attainment of the two faculties, one accomplishes all actions. (4)

children.translated_text: Then one should teach the <s>samādhi</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge of the knowledge-<s>vajra</s>-empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Through the subtle <s>vajra</s> application, one should contemplate from the center of the <s>vajra</s> —

children.text: buddhabimbaṃ svamātmānaṃ buddhatvaṃ so hyavāpnuyād // iti //
children.translated_text: a <s>Buddha</s>-image as one's own self — one would thereby attain <s>Buddha</s>hood.
Then one should teach the <s>samādhi</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge of <s>Vajrasattva</s>.
Employing the subtle <s>vajra</s> method, the hosts of <s>vajra</s>s and the rest in the heart —
contemplating [them], <s>Vajrasattva</s> and the rest bestow their own accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Then one should teach the <s>samādhi</s>-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s> families.

children.translated_text: Born from the <s>vajra</s>-binding, sixteen are proclaimed.
The supreme <s>samādhi</s>-pledge — the binding of those will be explained. (1)
Cross-legged, face-up, curled and uncurled,
and the fourth at the heart — in the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Vajrasattva</s> and the rest. (2)
At the forehead, at the head, at the back, at the shoulders, applied for laughter,
mouth-sustaining, sword at the heart, heart-blossoming, placed at the mouth, (3)

body.text:
mū(rdhan)vakṣastu vaktrasthā jyeṣṭhasthā puratastathā /
ataḥ paraṃ samāsena dharmamudrāstu śikṣayed // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
crown-and-chest, placed at the face, at the chief [position], and in front —
beyond this, one should teach the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s in brief. (4)

body.text:
dṛ kki / gra gra / ma ṭaḥ / a gra /
traṃ traṃ / aṃ aṃ / caṃ caṃ / tra ṭaḥ /
dhṛ ṭaḥ / bhṛ ṭaḥ / kra saḥ / ha haḥ /
va va / vaṃ vaṃ / pha ṭaḥ / gra saḥ //
body.translated_text:
DṚ KKI / GRA GRA / MA ṬAḤ / A GRA /
TRAṂ TRAṂ / AṂ AṂ / CAṂ CAṂ / TRA ṬAḤ /
DHṚ ṬAḤ / BHṚ ṬAḤ / KRA SAḤ / HA HAḤ /
VA VA / VAṂ VAṂ / PHA ṬAḤ / GRA SAḤ

children.translated_text: Then one should teach the foremost <s>dharma</s>-action to the practitioner of the subtle <s>vajra</s> —
the knowledge-fist, having divided the pledge in two, should be applied.

body.translated_text: From the great ritual-text (<s>mahākalparāja</s>) of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the detailed procedure of the <s>vajra</s>-knowledge-<s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> is completed.
CHAPTER 4 — <s>VAJRA-KĀRYA-KARMA-MAṆḌALA-VIDHI-VISTARA</s>

body.text: I.4 Emanation of deities from samadhi
body.translated_text: I.4 — Emanation of deities from <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatānuttarapūjāvidhivistaraspharaṇakarmasamayavajrādhiṣṭhānan nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgata vajradhātvanuttarapūjāspharaṇa samaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s>-empowerment of the pledge of pervading activity for the detailed procedure of the unsurpassed worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this supreme <s>vidyā</s>: OṂ — In the pledge of pervading the unsurpassed worship of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — HŪṂ!

body.text: atha khalvakṣobhayastathāgatāḥ sarvatathāgatavajrasatvānuttarapūjāvidhivistaraspharaṇakarmasamayavajrādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgatavajrasatvānuttarapūjāspharaṇasamaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s>-empowerment of the pledge of pervading activity for the detailed procedure of the unsurpassed worship of <s>Vajrasattva</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this supreme <s>vidyā</s>: OṂ — In the pledge of pervading the unsurpassed worship of <s>Vajrasattva</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — HŪṂ!

body.text: atha khalu ratnasaṃbhavastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajraratnānuttarapūjāvidhivistaraspharaṇakarmasamayavajrādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgatavajraratnānuttarapūjāspharaṇasamaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s>-empowerment of the pledge of pervading activity for the detailed procedure of the unsurpassed worship of <s>Vajraratna</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this supreme <s>vidyā</s>: OṂ — In the pledge of pervading the unsurpassed worship of <s>Vajraratna</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — HŪṂ!

body.text: atha khalvamitāyustathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajradharmānuttarapūjāvidhivistaraspharaṇakarmasamayavajrādhiṣṭhānanāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgatavajradharmānuttarapūjāspharaṇasamaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s>-empowerment of the pledge of pervading activity for the detailed procedure of the unsurpassed worship of <s>Vajradharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this supreme <s>vidyā</s>: OṂ — In the pledge of pervading the unsurpassed worship of <s>Vajradharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — HŪṂ!

body.text: atha khalvamoghasiddhistathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajrakarmānuttarapūjāvidhivistaraspharaṇakarmasamayavajrādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgatavajrakarmānuttarapūjāspharaṇasamaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amoghasiddhi</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s>-empowerment of the pledge of pervading activity for the detailed procedure of the unsurpassed worship of <s>Vajrakarma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this supreme <s>vidyā</s>: OṂ — In the pledge of pervading the unsurpassed worship of <s>Vajrakarma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — HŪṂ!

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanaḥ punarapi sarvatathāgatapūjāvidhivistarasakaladharmadhātuspharaṇakarmasamayavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ; samanantarasamāpanne cātha tāvadeva sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sa eva bhagavāṃ vajradharaḥ sakaladharmadhātuspharaṇāḥ sarvākāśadhātusamavasaraṇāḥ sarvavici[tra]pūjāvyūhavidhivistarameghasamudradevatā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, sarvalokadhātuprasarameghasamudrasarvatathāgataparṣanmaḍaleṣu sarvatathāgatānuttaramahābodhicittotpādanasarvatathāgatakulārāgaṇasamantabhadracaryāniṣpādanamaho bodhimaṇḍapasaṃkramamaṇasarvamāradharṣaṇasarvatathāgata[samatā]bhisaṃbhudhyanasarvatathāgatamahāmaṇḍalotpādanasakalatrilokavijayasaddharmacakrapravartanāśeṣānavaśeṣasatvadhātvarthakaraṇādini sarvabuddharddhivikurvitāni sandarśayanto 'vasthitāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the pledge of pervading activity for the detailed procedure of the worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s throughout the entire <s>dharma</s>-realm.' And immediately upon entering, from the hearts of all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, having become worship-cloud-ocean goddesses pervading the entire <s>dharma</s>-realm, converging throughout the entire space-realm, displaying the detailed arrangements of variegated worship, emerged; and standing in the assembly-<s>maṇḍala</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s throughout the cloud-oceans pervading all world-realms, they displayed all <s>Buddha</s>'s miraculous powers — the generation of the great <s>bodhicitta</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the accomplishment of the <s>Samantabhadra</s> practice of delighting all <s>Tathāgata</s> families, the approach to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), the vanquishing of all <s>Māra</s>s, the awakening to the equality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the production of the great <s>maṇḍala</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the conquest of the entire three worlds, the turning of the wheel of the True <s>Dharma</s>, and the benefiting of the entire remainder-less and inexhaustible realm of beings.

body.text: tāśca pūjāmeghasamudradevatāḥ svamudrāvyagrakarayugalāḥ sarvatathāgatān vidhivatsaṃpūjya, vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalayogena candramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvedamudānamudānayāmāsuḥ /
body.translated_text: And those worship-cloud-ocean goddesses, with their pairs of hands holding their respective <s>mudrā</s>s, having duly worshipped all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, seated on moon-discs according to the arrangement of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>, uttered this inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>):

children.translated_text: Oh! I am indeed the <s>Buddha</s>-worship, the instigator of all worship,
for all <s>Buddha</s>s bestow that which is the greatness of <s>Buddha</s>hood!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiḥ punarapi sarvatathāgatapūjādikarmavidhivistaraṃ vajrakāryannāma karmamaṇḍalamabhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, again proclaimed the detailed procedure of the activities beginning with the worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — the activity-<s>maṇḍala</s> called '<s>Vajrakārya</s>' (Vajra-Task).

children.translated_text: OṂ — In the activity-<s>vajra</s> of the pervading worship of the complete self-surrender to all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — Do, do! AḤ!
OṂ — In the foremost activity of the pervading worship of the attraction of the complete self-surrender to all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — Attract, attract! JAḤ!

body.translated_text: OṂ — In the activity-arrow of the pervading worship of the enamoring of the complete self-surrender to all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — HŪṂ HOḤ!
OṂ — In the activity-delight of the pervading worship of the applause of the complete self-surrender to all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — AḤ!

body.text: sarvatathāgatasukhasukhā, sarvatathāgatākarṣaṇī, sarvatathāgatānurāgiṇī, sarvatathāgatasaṃtoṣaṇī ceti sarvatathāgatamahāpūjāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'She of the happiness of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' 'She who attracts all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' 'She who enamors all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' and 'She who satisfies all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' — these are the great offerings of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
OṂ — Homage to the jewels of the body-consecration of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! <s>Vajra</s>-gem! OṂ!

body.text: oṃ namaḥ sarvatathāgatasūryebhyo vajratejini jvāla hrīḥ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — Homage to the suns of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! <s>Vajra</s>-radiance, blaze! HRĪḤ!
OṂ — Homage to the supreme wish-fulfilling jewel-banners that fulfill all wishes of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! Supreme <s>vajra</s>-banner! TRAṂ!
OṂ — Homage to those who produce the great joy and delight of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! <s>Vajra</s>-laughter! HAḤ!

body.text: mahādhipatinī, mahodyotā, mahāratnavarṣā, mahāprītiharṣā ceti sarvatathāgatābhiṣekapūjāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'The Great Sovereign Lady,' 'The Great Illuminator,' 'The Great Jewel-Rain,' and 'The Great Joy-Gladness' — these are the consecration-offerings of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
OṂ — With the <s>samādhi</s>s of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>-nature of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I praise! Supreme great <s>dharma</s>! HRĪḤ!
OṂ — With the displays of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I praise! Great sound-follower! DHAṂ!
OṂ — With the methods of all <s>sūtrānta</s>s including the turning of the wheel of syllables of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I praise! All <s>maṇḍala</s>s! HŪṂ!
OṂ — Singing with the <s>Buddha</s>-recitations (<s>saṃgīti</s>) of the intentional speech (<s>sandhābhāṣa</s>) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I praise! <s>Vajra</s>-speech! VAṂ!

children.translated_text: 'Great Knowledge-Song,' 'Great Sound-Follower,' 'Enterer of All <s>Maṇḍala</s>s,' and '<s>Mantra</s>-Conduct' —
these are the <s>dharma</s>-offerings of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

body.translated_text: OṂ — In the activity of the offering of pervading incense-clouds of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — Do, do!
OṂ — In the activity of the offering of pervading flower-showers of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — Scatter, scatter!
OṂ — In the activity of the offering of pervading lamp-flames of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — Bear, bear!
OṂ — In the activity of the offering of pervading perfume-oceans of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — Perform, perform!

body.text: satvavatī, mahābodhyaṅgavatī, cakṣuṣmatī, gandhavatī ceti / sarvatathāgatakarmapūjāḥ //
body.translated_text: 'She of Beings,' 'She of the Great Limbs of Awakening,' 'She of the Eyes,' and 'She of Fragrance' — these are the activity-offerings of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>
Now here, the <s>vajra</s>-task-activity-<s>maṇḍala</s> exists as the promoter of the worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s without remainder.

children.translated_text: Now I shall proclaim the supreme activity-<s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>Vajradhātu</s>, known as the <s>Vajra</s>-Task (<s>Vajrakārya</s>).
According to the method of the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should install <s>Buddha</s>-images.
According to the method of <s>Vajrasattva</s> and the rest, one should draw the ocean-goddesses.

body.translated_text: Initiation into the <s>maṇḍala</s>
Now here is the detailed procedure beginning with entry into the <s>vajra</s>-task-activity-<s>maṇḍala</s>.

body.text: tatrādita eva praveśayet vajradhātupraveśayogena / praveśyaivaṃ vadet / "sarvatathāgatapūjāsamayo 'yaṃ / tattvayā dinedine etāḥ ṣoḍaśapūjā yathāśaktitaḥ kāryā" iti //
body.translated_text: Therein, first of all, one should lead [the disciple] in according to the method of <s>Vajradhātu</s> entry. Having led [the disciple] in, one should say thus: 'This is the pledge of the worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therefore, you must perform these sixteen offerings day by day, to the best of your ability.'

body.text:
tato mukhabandhaṃ muktvā, karmamaṇḍalaṃ darśayitvā, viśvacinhaṃ pāṇibhyāṃ
dadyāt //
body.translated_text: Then, having removed the face-covering and shown the activity-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should give the universal emblem (<s>viśvacihna</s>) with both hands.

body.text: tataḥ sarvatathāgatairapi sa pūjyate, kaḥ punarvādo 'nyairiti //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, even all <s>Tathāgata</s>s worship that [disciple] — what need to speak of others?
<s>Mudrā</s>
Then one should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge for the worship of the accomplishment of the great <s>bodhicitta</s>.

children.translated_text: Through the firm generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, thinking 'I am a <s>Buddha</s>,'
worshipping oneself with jewels and the rest, one would obtain even the bliss of <s>Buddha</s>s. (1)
Through the firm generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, thinking 'I am a <s>Buddha</s>,'
worshipping oneself with garlands and other worship offerings, one is self-consecrated. (2)
Through the firm generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, thinking 'I am a <s>Buddha</s>,'
worshipping oneself with song, pleasure, and worship offerings, one should enamor [all]. (3)

body.text:
bodhicittadṛḍhotpādādbuddho 'hamiti cintayan /
nṛtyataḥ pūjayannātmā buddhairapi sa pūjyate // 4 // iti //
body.translated_text:
Through the firm generation of <s>bodhicitta</s>, thinking 'I am a <s>Buddha</s>,'
worshipping oneself while dancing, one is worshipped even by <s>Buddha</s>s. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
I am of <s>Buddha</s>-nature!

body.translated_text: I consecrate the <s>Buddha</s>!
I praise the <s>Buddha</s>!
I worship the <s>Buddha</s>!
Then one should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge of the worship of all <s>Buddha</s>s.

children.translated_text: Through the supreme applications of the <s>vajra</s> of body, speech, and mind, bowing thus,
worshipping all <s>Buddha</s>s, one would certainly become worthy of veneration. (1)
The great merit of all <s>Buddha</s>s, born from the <s>vajra</s> of body, speech, and mind —
one whose worship-nature is rejoicing would quickly attain <s>Buddha</s>hood. (2)
From the divine <s>vajra</s> of body, speech, and mind that surrenders oneself,
'I worship the perfectly awakened ones with all offerings' — thus one is worshipped. (3)

body.text:
sarva kuśalasaṃbhāraṅkāyavākcittavajrataḥ /
pariṇāmanapūjābhiḥ sarvabuddhasamo bhaved // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
'Through the <s>vajra</s>-nature of body, speech, and mind, all accumulations of merit,
through dedication-offerings, one would become equal to all <s>Buddha</s>s.' (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these [heart-mantras] are:
<s>praṇamāmi</s> (I pay homage)!

body.translated_text: <s>anumode</s> (I rejoice)!
<s>buddhapūja</s> (Buddha-offering)!
<s>pariṇāma</s> (dedication)!
Then one should teach the <s>dharma</s>-offering-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: '<s>Dharma</s>s are by nature luminous (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvara</s>), primordially pure by their own nature;
having worshipped with this <s>dharma</s>, one would obtain the pleasures of delight.' (1)
'The syllable "<s>a</s>" is to be declared as the entrance in the collection of all <s>dharma</s>s;
with this <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, one cuts through all sufferings.' (2)
'The <s>Tathāgata</s> is herein the cause of all <s>dharma</s>s;
having worshipped with the offering of the true <s>Dharmacakra</s>, one becomes a bearer of the <s>Dharma</s>.' (3)
'All <s>dharma</s>s are by nature like an echo;
having worshipped with this <s>dharma</s>-offering, one would obtain self-mastery.' (4)
Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>sarvaśuddha</s> (all-pure)!

body.translated_text: <s>samantabhadra</s> (universally good)!
<s>dharmacakra</s> (dharma-wheel)!
<s>niḥprapañca</s> (free from elaboration)!
Then one should teach the <s>samādhi</s>-offering-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: 'In the <s>vajra</s>s of body, speech, and mind, one's own atoms —
visualizing <s>vajra</s>-images, one would swiftly become a <s>vajra</s>-self.' (1)
'In the <s>vajra</s>s of body, speech, and mind, one's own atoms —
visualizing all <s>Buddha</s>s, one would quickly become the <s>Dharmakāya</s>.' (2)
'In the <s>vajra</s>s of body, speech, and mind, one's own atoms —
visualizing <s>Vajrasattva</s>s, one becomes equal to <s>Vajrasattva</s>.' (3)

body.text:
kāyavākcittavajreṣu svakīyāḥ paramāṇavaḥ /
bhāvayan buddhabimbāni saṃbuddhatvamavāpnuyād // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
'In the <s>vajra</s>s of body, speech, and mind, one's own atoms —
visualizing <s>Buddha</s>-images, one would attain perfect <s>Buddha</s>hood.' (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>vajrakāya</s> (vajra-body)!

body.translated_text: <s>dharmakāya</s> (dharma-body)!
<s>satvakāya</s> (being-body)!
<s>buddhakāya</s> (buddha-body)!
Then one should teach the secret-offering-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: 'The happiness-offering of the full embrace of all bodies, of the Self-Arisen Ones —
offering this, one would swiftly become equal to <s>Vajrasattva</s>.' (1)
'The happiness of the union of firm passion and the grasping of hair —
offering this to the <s>Buddha</s>s, one becomes equal to <s>Vajraratna</s>.' (2)
'The happiness of firm confidence, the happiness of the contact of the tongue and the supreme kiss —
offering this to the <s>Buddha</s>s, one becomes equal to <s>Vajradharma</s>.' (3)

body.text:
dvayendriyasamāpattiyogasaukhyāni sarvataḥ /
niryātayaṃstu pūjāyāṃ vajrakarmasamo bhaved // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
'The happiness of the union of the two organs, the yoga-bliss in every way —
offering this in worship, one would become equal to <s>Vajrakarma</s>.' (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s of the secret <s>mudrā</s>s:
<s>rativajra</s> (delight-vajra)!

body.translated_text: <s>rāgavajra</s> (passion-vajra)!
<s>prītivajra</s> (joy-vajra)!
<s>kāmavajra</s> (desire-vajra)!
Then one should teach the knowledge of the great <s>mudrā</s> of the offering-action of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text:
'Through the yoga at the heart, side, back, and likewise from the forehead and so forth,
at the mouth, ear, head, back, crown, seat, and hip.'
[These are the placement locations.]

body.translated_text: Then one should teach the knowledge of the pledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the offering-action of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text: 'Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-bond, through the application of the great <s>mudrā</s>,
placing [the <s>mudrā</s>] at the heart and other locations, one should worship the Victorious Ones.'

body.translated_text: Then one should teach the knowledge of the <s>dharma</s> of the offering of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

body.text:
oṃ grayaḥ yyaḥ sā /
tri raṃ haṃ naḥ /
khaṃ ṣaṃ hūṃ hi /
śa ṇa siḥ saṃ /
body.translated_text:
<s>oṃ grayaḥ yyaḥ sā</s> /
<s>tri raṃ haṃ naḥ</s> /
<s>khaṃ ṣaṃ hūṃ hi</s> /
<s>śa ṇa siḥ saṃ</s> /
'The action-<s>mudrā</s>s, in brief — the action-<s>mudrā</s> is made twofold.'
The detailed procedure of the <s>vajra</s>-action-<s>karma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> from the <s>Sarvatathāgatamahāyānābhisamaya</s>, the Great King of Ritual Manuals, is completed.

body.text: CHAPTER 5 EPILOGUE OF THE SARVA-TATHAGATA-MAHAYANABHISAMAYA NAMA MAHA-KALPA-RAJA
body.translated_text: Chapter 5: Epilogue of the <s>Sarvatathāgatamahāyānābhisamaya</s>, the Great King of Ritual Manuals.
1.5 Emanation of deities

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānena sarvatathāgatakulamutpādya, asya sarvatathāgatakulamahākalpavidhivistarasya sarvasiddhisaṃgrahārthamidaṃ sarvatathāgatamudrāhṛdayamabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi vaṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, through the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having generated the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments of the detailed procedure of the great ritual manual of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this <s>mudrā</s>-heart[-<s>mantra</s>] of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s: <s>oṃ sarvatathāgatamuṣṭi vaṃ</s>!

body.text: atha khalvakṣobhayastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānena sarvatathāgatakulamutpādyāsya sarvatathāgatakulamahākalpavidhivistarasya sarvasiddhisaṃgrahārthamimāṃ sarvatathāgatamudrāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrasatvamuṣṭi aḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Akṣobhya Tathāgata</s>, through the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having generated the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments of the detailed procedure of the great ritual manual of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this <s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s: <s>oṃ vajrasatvamuṣṭi aḥ</s>!

body.text: atha ratnasaṃbhavastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānena sarvatathāgatakulamutpādyāsya sarvatathāgatakulamahākalpavidhivistarasya sarvasiddhisaṃgrahārthamimāṃ sarvatathāgatamudrāmabhāṣat oṃ vajraratnamuṣṭi traṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata</s>, through the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having generated the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments of the detailed procedure of the great ritual manual of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this <s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s: <s>oṃ vajraratnamuṣṭi traṃ</s>!

body.text: athāmitāyustathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānena sarvatathāgatakulamutpādyāsya sarvatathāgatakulamahākalpavidhivistarasya sarvasiddhisaṃgrahārthamimāṃ sarvatathāgatamudrāmabhāṣat oṃ vajradharmamuṣṭi khaṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Amitāyus Tathāgata</s>, through the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having generated the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments of the detailed procedure of the great ritual manual of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this <s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s: <s>oṃ vajradharmamuṣṭi khaṃ</s>!

body.text: athāmoghasiddhistathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānena sarvatathāgatakulamutpādyāsya sarvatathāgatakulamahākalpavidhivistarasya sarvasiddhisaṃgrahārthamimāṃ sarvatathāgatamudrāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrakarmamuṣṭi hāṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata</s>, through the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having generated the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments of the detailed procedure of the great ritual manual of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this <s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s: <s>oṃ vajrakarmamuṣṭi hāṃ</s>!
Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ svādhiṣṭhānena bhagavato vairocanasya tathāgatasya sarvatathāgatakulamutpādyāsya sarvatathāgatakulamahākalpavidhivistarasya sarvasiddhisaṃgrahāyedaṃ vajrasiddhinnāma caturmudrāmaṇḍalamabhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, through his own empowerment, having generated the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for the Blessed One <s>Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of gathering all accomplishments of the detailed procedure of the great ritual manual of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this four-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> called '<s>Vajrasiddhi</s>' (Vajra-Accomplishment):

children.translated_text: 'Now, from here I shall teach the supreme <s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>vajradhātu</s>, known as <s>Vajrasiddhi</s>.' (1)
having first placed a <s>Buddha</s>-image, one should draw the four sets of <s>mudrā</s>s.' (2)

body.translated_text: 'Through the method of the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, the wise one should draw the threads;
'In the centers of the moon-discs, one should draw the <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s and the rest.' (3)
Initiation into the <s>maṇḍala</s>

body.text: athātra vajrasiddhimudrāmaṇḍala ākarṣaṇādividhivistaraṅkṛtvā tathaiva praveśyaivaṃ bruyāt / "na tvayā kasyacidimaṃ rahasyapaṭalamudghāṭayitavyaṃ / tatkasya hetoḥ? santi satvā durdṛṣṭayaḥ pāpakarmāṇo hīnavīryā vaikalyarahitāḥ citrakarmaṇyanabhijñāḥ; te vajradhātvādiṣu sarvatathāgatakulamaṇḍaleṣu mahatsviti kṛtvā hīnavīryatayā na praviśante / teṣāmarthāyedaṃ vajrasiddhimudrāmaṇḍalaṃ sarvatathāgatakulamaṇḍalasamayabhūtamaśeṣānavaśeṣasatvadhātuparitrāṇasarvahitasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārtha yāvat sarvatathāgatavajrottamasiddhinimittamadhiṣṭhitamiti / na tvayaiṣāṃ sarvatathāgatakulasamayamudrārahasyānāṃ na pratyabhiśraddhānīyaṃ / mā te narakatiryakpretopapattiḥ syāt, viṣamāparihāreṇa vākālamaraṇaṃ syād" ityuktvā, mukhabandhaṃ muktvā maṇḍalaṃ darśayet /
body.translated_text: Then, in this <s>Vajrasiddhi</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, having performed the detailed procedure of attraction and the rest, having caused [the disciple] to enter in the same manner, one should say thus: 'You must not reveal this secret chapter to anyone. For what reason? There are beings of wrong views, of evil actions, of inferior energy, free from defects [but] unskilled in the arts of painting. They, thinking the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in the <s>vajradhātu</s> and the rest are great, do not enter because of inferior energy. For the benefit of those, this <s>Vajrasiddhi</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, which is the pledge of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, has been empowered for the protection of all sentient realms without remainder and without exception, for the experience of all benefit, happiness, and mental delight, and up to the purpose of the supreme <s>vajra</s>-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. You must not disbelieve in these secrets of the pledge-<s>mudrā</s>s of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Lest rebirth as a hell-being, animal, or hungry ghost befall you, or lest untimely death befall you through irremediable danger.' Having said this, one should remove the face-covering and show the <s>maṇḍala</s>.
<s>Mudrā</s>
Then one should speak the pledge of the <s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.text: yāṃ yāṃ mudrāṃ tu badhnīyādya[sya ya]sya mahātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever <s>mudrā</s> one binds, of whatever great being,
one should recite the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] with its meaning and visualize that [deity] as oneself.' (1)
'Through this yoga of knowledge, they attain the accomplishment of the great beings;
all <s>mudrā</s>s of all [beings] are according to the words of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>.' (2)
Then one should speak the secret of all <s>mudrā</s>s:
'Having opened one's own sense-organ, one should grasp it with the <s>vajra</s>-fist grip;

children.text: tena mudrāṃ spṛśedyāṃ tu sā vaśaṃ yāti tatkṣaṇāt //
children.translated_text: with that, whichever <s>mudrā</s> one touches — it comes under control at that very moment.'

body.translated_text: Then one should speak the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all <s>mudrā</s>s:

children.translated_text: 'Having applied the method of the subtle <s>vajra</s>, one should bind the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s>;
through this method-yoga, one brings the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> under control.'

body.translated_text: Then one should speak the action of all <s>mudrā</s>s:

children.translated_text: 'The pleasures of song, dance, taste, food, and dwelling and the rest —
offering these to the <s>Buddha</s>s, one should bring the action-<s>mudrā</s> under control.'

body.translated_text: Then one should teach the knowledge of the secret <s>mudrā</s> that accomplishes all <s>maṇḍala</s>s:

children.translated_text: 'Having become self-arisen with an erect phallus (<s>stabdhaliṅga</s>), one should lie upon a white cloth;
having empowered the phallus as a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), [saying:] "I myself am the <s>vajradhātu</s>."' (1)
'Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-bond, with the middle [fingers] raised like sprouts,
with the tips of the little fingers at the tips — this is the pledge of the foremost pledges.' (2)
'Through the application of the subtle <s>vajra</s>, one should visualize with concentration;
the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the subtle <s>vajra</s>, leading to mastery of <s>samādhi</s>.' (3)

body.text:
vajramudrādvikaṃ badhvā gṛṇhed vajrantayordṛḍham /
kaniṣṭhāgrā nibandhena vajrakāryāgramaṇḍala // 4 // iti //
body.translated_text:
'Having bound the <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s> twofold, one should firmly grasp the <s>vajra</s> between them;
with the binding of the little-finger tips — the supreme <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>vajra</s>-action.' (4)

body.text: "tato yathāvad vajrasatvādimahāmudrābandhacatuṣṭayaṃ śikṣayitvā, yathāvad vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalavidhivistara iti, yathāvajrasiddhicaturmudrāmaṇḍalamevamakṣobhayādīni sarvamaṇḍalāni caturmudrāmaṇḍalayogena likhet / svābhiḥ svābhirmudrābhiḥ sarvasiddhayo dadantīti / evampaṭākuḍyākāśasarvasthānābhilikhitāni sarvasiddhayo dadantīti //
body.translated_text: 'Then, having duly taught the fourfold binding of the great <s>mudrā</s> beginning with <s>Vajrasattva</s>, and the detailed procedure of the great <s>vajradhātu</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> — just as the <s>Vajrasiddhi</s> four-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, so too the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of <s>Akṣobhya</s> and the rest should be drawn through the method of the four-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>. Through their own respective <s>mudrā</s>s, all accomplishments are granted. Thus, whether drawn on cloth, walls, or in space — in all locations, they grant all accomplishments.'

body.text: maṇḍalakalpanātprabhṛti keṣāṃcittasminneva maṇḍalapraveśe siddhiryathābhirucitā, keṣāṃcittata ārabhya divasena, keṣāṃcid divasacatuṣṭayet, keṣāṃcicchoḍaśāhāt, keṣāṃcitpañcānantaryakāriṇāmapi yathākāmaṃ sukhataḥ sarvakāryāṇi kurvatāṃ sarvānurāgasarvarasāhāravihārasukhānyanubhavatāṃ varṣeṇottamā siddhiriti bhagavatā nidiṣṭeti //
body.translated_text: 'From the time of the <s>maṇḍala</s>-construction onward: for some, accomplishment as desired occurs at that very <s>maṇḍala</s>-entry; for some, from that point within a day; for some, within four days; for some, within sixteen days; for some — even those who have committed the five immediate [heinous actions] — performing all tasks as they wish and at ease, experiencing all passions, all delights of taste, food, and dwelling — the supreme accomplishment [occurs] within a year.' This was taught by the Blessed One.

body.text: 1.6 Emanation of the deity from samadhi
body.translated_text: 1.6 Emanation of the deity from <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanaḥ punarapi sarvatathāgatottamasiddhisamayavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ sarvatathāgatamahāyānābhisamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra vajrasatva //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called '<s>Sarvatathāgatottamasiddhisamayavajra</s>' (Vajra of the Pledge of the Supreme Accomplishment of All Tathāgatas), caused this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called '<s>Sarvatathāgatamahāyānābhisamaya</s>' (Realization of the Great Vehicle of All Tathāgatas) to issue forth from his own heart: <s>Vajrasattva</s>!
Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ aśeṣānavaśeṣasatvadhātuparitrāṇasarvahitasukhasaumanasyānubhavanārthaṃ yāvatsarvatathāgatasarvottamasiddhaye idaṃ mahāyānābhisamayamaṇḍalamabhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, for the protection of all sentient realms without remainder and without exception, for the experience of all benefit, happiness, and mental delight, and up to the supreme accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this <s>Mahāyānābhisamaya</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Now, from here I shall teach the supreme being-<s>maṇḍala</s> (<s>sattvamaṇḍala</s>),
resembling the <s>vajradhātu</s>, known as <s>Vajrasattva</s>.' (1)

body.text:
mahāmaṇḍalayogena sutrayedbāhyamaṇḍalaṃ /
candramaṇḍalamadhye tu vajrasatvanniveśayed // 2 // iti //
body.translated_text:
'Through the method of the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should draw the threads of the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>;
in the center of the moon-disc, one should place <s>Vajrasattva</s>.' (2)
Initiation into the <s>maṇḍala</s>
Then, having duly performed the attraction, entry, and the rest, one should generate the accomplishment-knowledges of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

body.text: tatra prathamantāvadvaktavyaṃ "na tvayā kasyacidadṛṣṭasamayasyaiṣāṃ rahasyānāma[kovi]dasya vaktavyaṃ / mā te sarvāpāyopapattaye bhaveyu, rviṣamāparihāreṇākālamaraṇaṃ vā syād" iti //
body.translated_text: There, first of all, one should say: 'You must not speak to anyone who has not seen the pledge, who is unskilled, of these secrets. Lest rebirths in all lower realms befall you, or lest untimely death befall you through irremediable danger.'
Then one should teach the knowledge of the practice for the supreme accomplishment of <s>Vajrasattva</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Mounted upon a full moon-disc, embraced by the great <s>mudrā</s>,

children.text: vajrasatvaṃ svamātmānaṃ bhāvayaṃ sidhyate laghu // riti //
children.translated_text: visualizing oneself as <s>Vajrasattva</s>, one is quickly accomplished.'

body.translated_text: Then one should teach the knowledge of the secret pledge of all <s>maṇḍala</s>s:

children.translated_text: 'There is no evil in the three realms comparable to dispassion (<s>virāga</s>);
therefore, the state of being free from desire (<s>kāmavirāga</s>) should not be practiced by you again.'

body.translated_text: <s>mahāsamaya han phaṭ</s>!

body.text: tataḥ śapathahṛdayaṃ dadyādevaṃ / sarvatathāgatakulamaṇḍaleṣu vidhivistareṣu samayasaṃvarandātavyaṃ //
body.translated_text: Then one should give the oath-heart[-<s>mantra</s>] thus: 'In the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of the family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, in the detailed procedures, the pledge-restraint (<s>samayasaṃvara</s>) must be given.'

body.text: tato vajrasatvamahāmudrādibandhacatuṣṭayaṃ śikṣayet / tathaiva siddhaya iti /
body.translated_text: Then one should teach the fourfold binding of the great <s>mudrā</s> beginning with <s>Vajrasattva</s>. Likewise the accomplishments.

body.text: evaṃ paṭādiṣu sarvapratimāsu ca manīṣitavidhānena sarvasiddhayo dadanti / evaṃ yathā vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalavidhivistara iti //
body.translated_text: Thus, by the prescribed procedure in painted cloths and all images, they grant all accomplishments. Thus, as in the elaboration of the procedure of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>.
<s>Mudrā</s>

body.text: atha sarvatathāgatāḥ punarapi samāhajāmāgatya, bhagavate sarvatathāgatādhipataye mahābodhicittāya vajrasatvāya mahāvajrapāṇaye vajratuṣṭyānena hṛdayena sādhukāramadaduḥ oṃ //
body.translated_text: Then all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having again come together in assembly, gave the exclamation of 'well done!' to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the sovereign of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the great <s>bodhicitta</s>, <s>Vajrasattva</s>, the great <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, with <s>vajra</s>-satisfaction, with this heart-[<s>mantra</s>]: Oṃ!

children.text: sādhu te vajrasatvāya vajraratnāya sādhu te /
children.translated_text: Well done to you, O <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Well done to you, O <s>Vajraratna</s>!

children.text: vajradharmāya te sādhu sādhu te vajrakarmaṇe // 1 //
children.translated_text: Well done to you, O <s>Vajradharma</s>! Well done to you, O <s>Vajrakarma</s>! (1)
This <s>sūtra</s> is well spoken — the unsurpassed <s>Vajrayāna</s>,
the secret of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the compendium of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. (2)
Even the name of <s>Vajrasattva</s> is the supreme bestower of all accomplishments.
One who practices with purity indeed attains <s>Buddha</s>hood through bliss. (3)

body.text:
vajradharmaprayogeṇa sarvakāmasukhaiḥ sukhaṃ /
sādhayejjanmanīhaiva sukhamakṣayamavyayam // 4 // iti /
body.translated_text: Through the application of <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>, happiness through all desired pleasures — one should accomplish in this very life imperishable, inexhaustible bliss. (4) Thus.
The great <s>kalpa</s>-king called 'The <s>Mahāyāna</s> Realization of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' from the <s>Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha</s>, is completed.
CHAPTER 6: <s>TRILOKAVIJAYA-MAHĀ-MAṆḌALA-VIDHI-VISTARA</s>
Hymn of 108 Names of <s>Mahācakravartin</s>

body.text: atha bhagavantaḥ sarvatathāgatāḥ punaḥ samājamāgamya, bhagavantaṃ sarvatathāgatamahācakravartinamanena nāmāṣṭaśatenādhyeṣitavantaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having again come together in assembly, entreated the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the great <s>cakravartin</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, with this hymn of one hundred and eight names:

children.translated_text: O <s>Vajrasattva</s>, great <s>vajra</s>, O lord of <s>vajra</s>, excellent accomplisher!
O <s>vajra</s>-consecration, O <s>vajra</s>-radiance, O <s>vajra</s>-banner — homage to you! (1)
O <s>vajra</s> of laughter, O great <s>dharma</s>, O <s>vajra</s>-sheath, O greatly excellent one!
O foremost sovereign of all <s>maṇḍala</s>s, O one free from conceptual elaboration — homage to you! (2)
O <s>vajra</s>-activity, O great protector, O fierce <s>yakṣa</s>, O great seizer!
O <s>vajra</s>-fist, O great <s>mudrā</s>, O all-<s>mudrā</s> — homage to you! (3)
O <s>bodhicitta</s>, O great awakening, O <s>Buddha</s>, O all <s>Tathāgata</s>s!
O <s>Vajrayāna</s>, O great wisdom, O <s>Mahāyāna</s> — homage to you! (4)
O all-purpose, O one whose purpose is all reality, O great-being-purpose, O all-knower!
O omniscient, O all-doer, O all, O all-seer — homage to you! (5)
O one whose nature is <s>vajra</s>, O foremost excellent <s>vajra</s>, O <s>vajra</s>-valor, O excellent <s>vajra</s>-bearer!
O great pledge, O one whose purpose is reality, O great truth — homage to you! (6)
O <s>vajra</s>-hook, O great desire, O well-delighted, O greatly radiant one!
O <s>vajra</s>-radiance, O radiant splendor, O <s>Buddha</s>-radiance — homage to you! (7)
O foremost <s>vajra</s>-sovereign, O foremost <s>vajra</s>, O foremost of the foremost <s>vidyā</s>s, O supreme among men!
O supreme <s>vajra</s>, O foremost of the great foremost, O supreme <s>vidyā</s> — homage to you! (8)
O <s>Vajradhātu</s>, O greatly secret, O <s>vajra</s>-secret, O bearer of the well-hidden!
O subtle <s>vajra</s>, O great meditation, O <s>vajra</s>-activity — homage to you! (9)
O foremost <s>Buddha</s>, O foremost <s>Buddha</s>-<s>vajra</s>, O <s>Buddha</s>-awakening, O greatly wise one!
O <s>Buddha</s>-wisdom, O great <s>Buddha</s>, O <s>Buddha</s> of <s>Buddha</s>s — homage to you! (10)
O <s>Buddha</s>-worship, O great worship, O being-worship, O excellent worshipper!
O great skillful means, O great accomplishment, O <s>vajra</s>-accomplishment — homage to you! (11)
O great body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>Sarasvatī</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>!
O great mind of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>vajra</s>-mind — homage to you! (12)
O sovereign of the <s>Buddha</s>s, O executor of the <s>Jina</s>'s command, O friend of the <s>Buddha</s>s, O foremost of <s>Jina</s>s!
O great <s>Vairocana</s>, O all-pervading one, O teacher, O one who is both peaceful and wrathful — homage to you! (13)
O great reality of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, O limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), O great method!
O wisdom of all <s>pāramitā</s>s, O ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>) — homage to you! (14)
O <s>Samantabhadra</s>, O foremost in conduct, O <s>Māra</s>, O crusher of <s>Māra</s>!
O foremost of all, O wisdom of equality, O one who goes everywhere — homage to you! (15)
O <s>Buddha</s>-huṃkāra, O huṃkāra, O <s>vajra</s>-huṃkāra, O tamer!
O one whose body is the <s>viśvavajra</s>, O fierce <s>vajra</s>, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> — homage to you! (16)
You are to be venerated, worshipped, honored, and revered by the <s>Tathāgata</s>s,
because your mind is firm as <s>vajra</s> — you are called <s>Vajrasattva</s>. (17)

children.text: tvadadhīnā hi saṃbodhi pitā tvaṃ sarvadarśināṃ /
children.translated_text: Awakening depends upon you; you are the father of all the All-Seeing Ones.
The <s>Tathāgata</s>s have arisen and will arise, having relied upon you. (18)
By this king of praises, one should praise with great devotion.
Even one who sings and praises [thus] would become equal to <s>Vajradhara</s>. (19)

body.text:
adhyeṣayāmastvānnātha sarvabuddhavaśaṅkaraṃ /
sarvasatvārthakāryārthamutpādaya kulaṃ svakam // 20 // iti //
body.translated_text: We entreat you, O Lord, for what brings all <s>Buddha</s>s under your power — for the purpose of accomplishing the aims of all beings, manifest your own family! (20) Thus.

body.text: Subjugation of Mahesvara and his retinue
body.translated_text: Subjugation of <s>Maheśvara</s> and His Retinue

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiḥ sarvatathāgatādhipatiḥ sarvatathāgatādhyeṣaṇavacanamupaśrutya, tadvajraṃ svahṛdi pratiṣṭhāpya, tān sarvatathāgatān āhūyaivamāha / "bhāgavantaḥ sarvatathāgatā na pratipadyāmi" // sarvatathāgatā prāhuḥ / "ko hetuḥ?" // vajradharaḥ prāha / "santi bhagavantaḥ satvāḥ maheśvarā diduṣṭasa] tvā, ye yuṣmābhirapi sarvatathāgatairavineyāḥ, teṣāṃ mayā kathaṃ pratipattavyam!" //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the sovereign of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having heard the words of entreaty from all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, established that <s>vajra</s> in his own heart and, having summoned all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke thus: 'O <s>Bhagavān</s>s, all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — I do not undertake [this]!' All <s>Tathāgata</s>s said: 'What is the reason?' <s>Vajradhara</s> said: 'There are, O <s>Bhagavān</s>s, beings — great lords (<s>maheśvara</s>), extremely wicked beings — who are untameable even by you, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s. How should I deal with them?'

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgataḥ [sarvatathāga]tādhiṣṭhānena sarvatathāgatamahopāyajñānavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ / samanantarasamāpanne cātha tāvadeva sa[rvatathāga]tāḥ sakalākāśadhātuparamāṇurajaḥ samavasaraṇa[spharaṇa] tāya sumerugirimūrdhni vajramaṇiratnakūṭāgāre [punaḥ] samājamāgamya, sarvatathāgatasamatāmadhyālambhya, bhagavato vairocanasya śrīvatsahṛdaye praviṣṭāḥ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, through the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the great skillful-means wisdom of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.' And immediately upon entering, thereupon all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, with the pervasion equal to the assembly of the atoms and particles of the entire space-realm, having again come together in assembly on the summit of Mount <s>Sumeru</s> in the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion, having taken up the equality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, entered the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>-heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatahṛdayamātmānamadhiṣṭhāya sarvavajrasamatayā aśeṣānavaśeṣasatvadhātuparitrāṇasarvahitasukhottamasiddhihetoḥ sarvaduṣṭavinayāya ca, sarvatathāgatamahākaruṇopāyasamādhijñānamadhyālambhya, sarvatathāgatamahākarūṇopāyakrodhasamaya vajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ / samanantarasamāpanne cātraitasminneva kṣaṇe sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ sarvatathāgatasamayannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ niścacāra huṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, having empowered himself as the heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, with the equality of all <s>vajra</s>s, for the sake of protecting the entire limitless and inexhaustible realm of beings, for the supreme accomplishment of all benefit and happiness, and for the discipline of all the wicked — having taken up the wisdom of the <s>samādhi</s> of the great compassion and skillful means of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of the pledge of the great compassion and skillful-means wrath of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.' And immediately upon entering, at that very instant, from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth: Hūṃ!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre vajrapāṇihṛdayavajrātsa eva bhagavān vajradharaḥ samantajvālāgarbhāḥ sabhrukuṭibhrūbhaṅgotkuñcitalalāṭavikaṭadaṃṣṭrākarālamukhāḥ vajrāṅkuśakoṣapāśādivajrajvālānnipradīptapraharaṇavyagrakarāḥ anekavidhavarṇālaṅkāravicitraveṣadharāḥ vajrapāṇivigrahā viniścaritvā, sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvaduṣṭavinayaṅkṛtvā, bhagavato vairocanasya sarvato vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalayogena candramaṇḍalāśritā bhutvedamudānamudānayiṃsuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged, from the heart-<s>vajra</s> of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s> — with garlands of flames on all sides, with frowning knitted brows and curled foreheads, with terrifying mouths of fearsome fangs, with hands brandishing blazing <s>vajra</s>-weapons such as <s>vajra</s>-hooks, nooses, and the rest, wearing ornaments and varied costumes of manifold colors — <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>-forms emerged, and having performed the discipline of all the wicked in all world-realms, having stationed themselves on moon-discs on all sides of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s> through the yoga of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>, they uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! I am the disciplinary skillful means of those possessed of great skillful means,
for through the disciplinary skillful means for beings, even the stainless ones assume wrathful form! Thus.

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatāprapañcadharmatāmadhyālambhya, sarvatathāgatamahākrodhavajrasamayavajrādhiṣṭhānannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ sarvatathāgatavajra-huṅ-karannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ vidyottamamabhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, having taken up the non-elaboration <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of reality) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s>-empowerment of the great wrathful <s>vajra</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' and spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s>, the heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the <s>vajra</s>-huṃkāra of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s':

children.translated_text: Seize! Seize! Hūṃ!
Cause to seize! Hūṃ!
Bring [them]! Hoṃ! O <s>Bhagavān</s>!
<s>Vajra</s> hūṃ phaṭ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ! <s>Suṃbha</s>! <s>Nisuṃbha</s>! Hūṃ!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyo bhagavānvajrapāṇirviniḥsṛtya, sarvalokadhātuprasarameghasamudrebhyo yāvantaḥ sarvatathāgatāḥ sabodhisatvaparṣadmaṇḍalāḥ samādhiṣṭhāyākṛṣya, vajrasamayamahāmaṇḍale praveśya, samayairbadhvā, punarapyekaghano mahāvajrakrodhakāyo bhūtvā, bhagavato [vairo]canasya hṛdaye sthitvemamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged, <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s> emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s from the ocean-clouds pervading all world-realms, together with their <s>bodhisattva</s> retinue-assemblies — having empowered and attracted them, having caused them to enter the <s>vajra</s>-pledge great <s>maṇḍala</s>, having bound them with the pledges — and having again become a single solid great wrathful <s>vajra</s>-body, standing in the heart of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, he uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! The all-round goodness of the awakening-mind (<s>bodhicitta</s>) is faultless,
for through the discipline of beings, even wrath becomes delightful! Thus.

body.text: atha sa mahāvajrakrodhakāyo bhagavato hṛdayādavatīrya, sarvatathāgatānāṃ purataścandramaṇḍalāśrito bhūtvā, punarapyājñāṃ mārgayā[māsa] //
body.translated_text: Then that great wrathful <s>vajra</s>-body, having descended from the heart of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and having stationed himself on a moon-disc before all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, again sought instruction.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatasamayākarṣaṇavajrannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatasamayāṅkuśannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛ[daya]n niścacāra huṃ ṭakki jjaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the <s>vajra</s> of attracting the pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called 'the pledge-hook of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s' issued forth from his own heart: 'Hūṃ ṭakki jaḥ!'

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvalokadhātuprasarameghasamudreṣu yāvantastrailokyādhipatayo maheśvarādayaste sa[rve sa]rvalokasanniveśagaṇaparivṛtāḥ aśeṣānavaśeṣāḥ sarvatathāgatasamayavajrāṅku śenākṛṣṭāḥ samānā yena sumerugirimūrdhā [yena] ca vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārastenopasaṃkramya, bhagavato vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya sarvataḥ parivāryāvasthitā abhūvan //
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this emerged, all the lords of the three worlds — <s>Maheśvara</s> and the rest — as many as there are in the ocean-clouds pervading all world-realms, together with all their worldly host-retinues, entirely without remainder, attracted by the pledge-<s>vajra</s>-hook of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, approached the summit of Mount <s>Sumeru</s> and the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion, and stood surrounding <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion on all sides.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇistadvajraṃ svahṛdayādgṛhyollālayan sarvāvantaṃ sakalatraidhātukatrilokacakramavalokyaivamāha / "pratipadyata [mārṣā]ssarvatathāgataśāsane, mama cājñāṃ pālayata!" / atha ta evamāhuḥ / "katham pratipadyāmaḥ?" / bhagavān vajrapāṇirāha / "buddha dharmaṃ ca saṅghaṃ ca śaraṇagamanaṃ pratipattitaḥ, sarvajñajñānalābhāya pratipadyadhvaṃ mārṣā!" iti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, taking that <s>vajra</s> from his own heart and tossing it, surveying the entire triple world — the complete realm of the three worlds — spoke thus: 'Submit, O noble ones, to the teaching of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, and obey my command!' Then they spoke thus: 'How should we submit?' <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s> said: 'Take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s> — submit for the attainment of omniscient wisdom, O noble ones!'

body.text: atha yo 'smin lokadhātau sakalatrailokyādhipatirmahādevaḥ sarvatrailokyādhipatyagarvito mahākrodhatāndarśayannevamāha / "ahaṃ bho yakṣa trailokyādhipatirīśvaraḥ kartā vikartā sarvabhūteśvaro devātidevo mahādevaḥ; tatkathamahaṃ te yakṣajñāṅkariṣyāmī-?" ti //
body.translated_text: Then he who in this world-realm was the sovereign of the entire three worlds, <s>Mahādeva</s>, proud of his lordship over all three worlds, displaying great wrath, spoke thus: 'I, O <s>yakṣa</s>, am the lord of the three worlds, <s>Īśvara</s>, the creator and destroyer, the lord of all beings, the god above gods, <s>Mahādeva</s>! How then shall I follow the command of you, a <s>yakṣa</s>?'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiḥ punarapi vajramullālayannājñāpyati / "bho duṣṭasattva śīghraṃ praviśa maṇḍalaṃ, mama ca samaye tiṣṭha!" /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, again tossing the <s>vajra</s>, commanded: 'O wicked being, quickly enter the <s>maṇḍala</s> and abide in my pledge!'

body.text: atha mahādevo devo bhagavantamidamavocat / "ko 'yaṃ bhagavannīdṛśaḥ satvo yo 'yamīśvarasyaivamājñāndadāti?" /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, the god, spoke to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Who is this being, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, who gives commands to <s>Īśvara</s> himself in this manner?'

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvāvantaṃ maheśvarāditrailokyagaṇamāhūyaivamāha / "pratipadyata mārṣāstriśaraṇagamanasamayasaṃvare; māyaṃ vajrapāṇiryakṣaḥ krūraḥ krodhanaścaṇḍo mahābodhisatvaśca vo dīptena vajreṇa sakalameva traidhātukaṃ nāśayed" iti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having summoned the entire host of the three worlds headed by <s>Maheśvara</s>, spoke thus: 'Submit, O noble ones, to the pledge-discipline of taking the three refuges! Lest this <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, this cruel, wrathful, fierce <s>yakṣa</s> and great <s>bodhisattva</s>, destroy the entire triple world with his blazing <s>vajra</s>!'

body.text: atha maheśvaraḥ sakalatrailokyādhipatyatayā svajñānavaśitayā ca bhagavato vajrapāṇerbhayasandarśanārthaṃ mahācaṇḍakrodhatāṃ mahābhairavarūpatāṃ mahājvālotsṛjanatāṃ mahā[rau]drāhāsatāṃ sahagaṇaiḥ sandarśayannevamāha / "ahaṃ bhoḥ sakalatrailokyādhipastvaṃ mamājñāndadāsī-" ti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Maheśvara</s>, because of his lordship over the entire three worlds and because of the mastery of his own knowledge, for the purpose of showing fear to <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, displaying — together with his retinue — great fierce wrath, great terrifying form, the emission of great flames, and great terrible laughter, spoke thus: 'I am the sovereign of the entire three worlds — you would give me commands?'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇistadvajraṃ [sagarvam] ullālayan vihasannevamāha / "pratipadya bho kaṭapūtanamānuṣamānsāhāra citibhasmabhakṣyabhojya śayyāsanaprāvaraṇa mamājñā[mpālaya]!" / atha maheśvaro mahādevaḥ sakalaṃ trailokyaṃ mahākrodhāviṣṭamadhiṣṭhāya, evamāha / "tvamapi mamājñāṃ pālaya, samaye ca prati[padya!" i]ti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, tossing that <s>vajra</s> with pride and laughing, spoke thus: 'Submit, O wretched devourer of human flesh from charnel grounds, eater of ashes from funeral pyres, [dwelling on] bed-seats and coverings — obey my command!' Then <s>Maheśvara Mahādeva</s>, having empowered the entire three worlds, possessed by great wrath, spoke thus: 'You too should obey my command and submit to my pledge!'

body.text:
atha vajrāpāṇirmahākrodharājo bhagavantametadavocad / "ayambhagavanmahādevo devaḥ svajñānabalagarvāt maheśvaryā[dhipa]tyāt ca sarvatathāgataśāsane na praṇamati /
tatkathamasya kriyata?" iti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great wrathful king, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'This <s>Bhagavān Mahādeva</s>, the god, out of the pride of his own knowledge and power and because of his sovereignty as supreme lord, does not bow down to the teaching of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. What then should be done regarding him?'

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatahṛdayasaṃbhūtaṃ mahāvajrasa[mayaṃ] smārayati oṃ nisumbha vajra huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> recited this great <s>vajra</s>-pledge born from the heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s: <s>oṃ nisumbha vajra hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ svavajrahṛdayamudājahāra huṃ // athāsmin bhāṣitamātra sakalatraidhātukasannipatitā mahādevādayaḥ sarvatrailokyādhipatayaḥ adhomukhāḥ prapatitāḥ ārtasvaraṃ manvanto bhagavato vajrapāṇeśca śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ / sa ca mahādevo devo bhūmyāṃ prapatito niśceṣṭībhūto mṛtaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> uttered his own <s>vajra</s> heart [-mantra]: <s>hūṃ</s>! And the moment this was uttered, <s>Mahādeva</s> and all the other lords of the three worlds assembled from the entire threefold world-system fell face-downward, uttering anguished cries, and took refuge in <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>. And that <s>Mahādeva</s>, the god, having fallen to the ground, became motionless and died.

body.text: atha bhagavān jānanneva vajrapāṇimevamāha / "pratipadyasva vajrapāṇe asya sakalatrilokacakrasyābhayāya, mā pañcatvamāpādaya" / atha vajrapāṇirmahākrodharājo bhagavato vacanamupaśrutya tāṃ sarvadevādīnāhūyaivamāha / "buddhaṃ dharma saṅghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ pratipadyata, mamājñākāritāyāṃ ca, yadīṣṭaṃ vaḥ svajīvitam" iti / atha ta evamāhuḥ / "sabuddhadharmasaṅghasamudrāṃccharaṇaṃ gacchāmaḥ, tvacchāsanājñāṃ na jānīma" iti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing full well, said this to <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>: 'Act, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, for the fearlessness of this entire threefold world-cycle — do not bring about the dissolution [of all beings]!' Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great wrathful king, having heard the word of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, summoned all those gods and the rest and said thus: 'Take refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>, and in obedience to my command — if your own lives are dear to you!' Then they said thus: 'We go for refuge to the ocean of <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s> — but we do not know the instruction of your teaching.'

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgatastānāhūyaivamāha / "ayaṃ bho devo 'smākaṃ sarvatathāgatādhipatiḥ sarvatathāgatapitā sarvatathāgatājñākaraḥ sarvatathāgatajyeṣṭhaputro bhagavāṃ samantabhadro bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ sarvasatvavinayena kāryakaraṇatayā mahākrodharājyatāyāmabhiṣiktaḥ / tatkasmāddhetoḥ? / santi yuṣmadmadhye mahādevādayo duṣṭagaṇās te sarvatathāgatairapi na śakyāḥ śāntayā pāpebhyo nivārayituṃ / teṣāṃ pāpasatvānāṃ nigrahāya adhitiṣṭhitastadyusmābhirasya samaye sthātavyamityājñā" iti / ta evamāhur / "asmākaṃ bhagavannasmājjīvitavipralāyātparitrāyasva / yāmājñāndāsyati tatkariṣyamaha" iti / bhagavānāha / "haṃ bho mārṣā etameva śaraṇaṃ gacchatāyameva vaḥ paritrāsyati, nānya" iti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, having summoned them, said thus: 'O gods, this one is our lord of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the father of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the executor of the commands of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the eldest son of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — <s>Bhagavān Samantabhadra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, who has been consecrated in the sovereignty of the great wrathful king for the purpose of accomplishing the task of training all beings. For what reason? There are among you wicked hosts such as <s>Mahādeva</s> and the rest, whom even all <s>Tathāgata</s>s are unable to restrain from evil through peaceful means. He has been empowered for the subjugation of those sinful beings. Therefore by you, in his pledge, you must stand — this is the command.' They said thus: 'Protect us, <s>Bhagavān</s>, from this destruction of our lives! Whatever command he gives, that we shall do.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Yes, sirs, go to this very one for refuge — he alone will protect you, no other.'

body.text: atha te trilokasakalatraidhātukasannipatitāḥ tribhuva[napata]yo yena bhagavān vajradharastenābhimukhā ekakaṇṭhena mahārtān svarānpramuñcata evamāhuḥ / "paritrāyasva bho bhagavan paritrāyasva ato maraṇaduḥkhād" iti //
body.translated_text: Then those lords of the three worlds, assembled from the entire threefold world-system of the three realms, facing the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, with one voice, releasing cries of great anguish, said thus: 'Protect us, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, protect us from this suffering of death!'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvastāṃ devādīnāhūyaivamāha / "haṃ bho duṣṭāḥ pratipadyata mama śāsane / mā vo [dīptenā]nena vajreṇa ekajvālīkṛtya, sarvāneva bhasmīkuryām" iti / ta evamāhuḥ / "samantabhadrastvaṃ bhagavansarvatathāgatacittotpāda[ḥ śāntavinītaḥ] sarvasatvahitaiṣī sarvasatvābhayapradaḥ / tatkathaṃ bhagavannasmākannirdahiṣyatī-?" ti / atha vajrapāṇirmahākrodharajastānevamāha / "[ahaṃ bho] mārṣāḥ samantabhadro yena sarvatathāgatājñākāritvādyuṣmadvidhānāṃ duṣṭasatvajātīyānāṃ pāpacittānāṃ saṃśodhanārthāya, vināśayāmi yadi matsamaye na tiṣṭhata" iti / te prāhur "evamastvi" ti //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>, having summoned those gods and the rest, said thus: 'Yes, O wicked ones, submit to my teaching! Lest with this blazing <s>vajra</s>, having turned you all into a single flame, I reduce you all to ashes!' They said thus: 'You, <s>Bhagavān</s>, are <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the mind-generation of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, peaceful, disciplined, desiring the benefit of all beings, granting fearlessness to all beings. How then, <s>Bhagavān</s>, will you burn us?' Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great wrathful king, said to them thus: 'I, sirs, am <s>Samantabhadra</s> — whereby, because of being the executor of the commands of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purpose of purifying the sinful minds of wicked beings of your kind, I shall destroy [you] if you do not abide in my pledge.' They replied: 'So be it!'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahākrodharājo maheśvaraṃ muktvānyāndevānāśvāsyotthāpanārthamidam vajrottiṣṭhannāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayamabhāṣat vajrottiṣṭha // athāsmin bhāṣitamātre maheśvaraṃ muktvā sarve te tridhātukasannipatitāstribhuvanapatayaḥ saparivārāḥ saṃmūrcchitāḥ samānāḥ samāśvastahṛdayā abhūvan divyāni sukhānyanubhavanto vigatabhayacchabhitaromaharṣā bhagavantaṃ vajrapāṇinamavalokayantaḥ samutthitā iti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great wrathful king, having set aside <s>Maheśvara</s> and having reassured the other gods, uttered this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called '<s>vajra</s>-arise' (<s>vajrottiṣṭha</s>) for the purpose of raising them up: <s>vajrottiṣṭha</s>! And the moment this was uttered, all those lords of the three worlds assembled from the three realms, with their retinues — except <s>Maheśvara</s> — who had fainted, having regained consciousness and having their hearts reassured, experiencing divine pleasures, with their fear, trembling, and goosebumps departed, looking upon <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, stood up.

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇiṃ bodhisatvamāmantrayāmāsa / "ayaṃ mahāsatvo mahādevo devādhipatirnotthāpitaḥ, tatkimasya jīvitavipraṇāśena kṛtena?; jīvāpayainaṃ, satpuruṣo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyatī-" ti / atha vajrapāṇir "evamastv" iti kṛtvedaṃ mṛta saṃjīvanahṛdayamudājahāra vajrāyuḥ // athāsmin bhāṣitamātre mahādevo devo mṛtaḥ saṃjīvyotthātumicchati, na śakto vyutthātuṃ / tato bhagavantametadavocat / "kimahaṃ bhagavatā evaṃ śāsyāmi?" / bhagavānāha / "na tvaṃ pratipadyasvāsya mahāsatpuruṣasyājñāṅkartu / ayameva tena śāsti, nāhaṃ" / maheśvaraḥ prāha / "kinna tvaṃ bhagavaṃcchakto 'smāddṛṣṭasatvānparitrātum?" iti / bhagavānāha / "nāhamasmātsamarthaḥ paritrātuṃ" / āha / "tatkasmāddhetor" / āha / "sarvatathāgatādhipatitvāt" / āha / "nāhaṃ bhagavaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamājāne / kintu yatra hi nāma tathāgatānāmapi sarvatraidhātukādhipatīnāmanyo 'dhipatistanna jāne ko 'yam" iti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>: 'This <s>Mahāsattva Mahādeva</s>, the lord of gods, has not been raised up. What good has been accomplished by the destruction of his life? Revive him — he will become a good person.' Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, saying 'So be it,' uttered this heart [-mantra] for reviving the dead: <s>vajrāyuḥ</s>! And the moment this was uttered, <s>Mahādeva</s>, the god, having died, was revived and wished to rise — but was unable to stand up. Then he addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'Am I to be disciplined thus by the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'No — you should submit to carry out the command of this great and noble being. He is the one who teaches you, not I.' <s>Maheśvara</s> said: 'Are you, <s>Bhagavān</s>, not able to protect beings seen [to be in danger] from him?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'I am not capable of protecting from him.' He said: 'For what reason?' He said: 'Because he is the lord of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.' He said: 'I do not understand the meaning of what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said, <s>Bhagavān</s>. But that there should be another lord over the <s>Tathāgata</s>s themselves, who are lords of the entire threefold world — I do not know who this is.'

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ punarapi mahādevamāhūyaivamāha / "na pratipa[dyasi kiṃ] duṣṭasatva mamājñāṅkartum?" iti / atha mahādevo vajrasatvavacanamupaśrutya kupitaścaṇḍībhūtastathā patita eva punarapi mahāraudrarūpatāṃ darśaya[nne]vamāha / "maraṇamapyutsahāmi; na ca tavājñāṅkariṣyāmi" //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, again summoned <s>Mahādeva</s> and said thus: 'Do you not submit, wicked being, to carry out my command?' Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, having heard the words of <s>Vajrasattva</s>, became enraged and fierce and, while still lying fallen, displaying his great terrifying form, said thus: 'I am willing even to die, but I shall not carry out your command!'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvo mahākopatāṃ sandarśayansvakramatālādida[manuca]ran niścacāra oṃ pādākarṣaṇa vajra hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>, displaying his great anger, issuing forth this [mantra] while treading with his own step-stamp and dancing: <s>oṃ pādākarṣaṇa vajra hūṃ</s>!

body.text: atha bhagavataścaraṇatālātsamantajvālā garbhākṛtabhrukuṭīdaṃṣṭrākarālamahāvaktro vajrā nucaro bhagavato vajrapā] ṇeḥ purataḥ sthitvājñāṃ mārgayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then from the sole of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s foot, a <s>vajra</s>-attendant with a womb of universal flames, with furrowed brows and a great terrifying mouth with fangs, stood before <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s> and sought instruction.

body.text: atha vajrāpāṇirmaheśvarasaṃśodhananimittamevamāha oṃ pādākarṣākarṣasya sarvavajradharānucara [kaṇḍa kaṇḍa va]jra hūṃ jaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, for the purpose of purifying <s>Maheśvara</s>, said thus: <s>oṃ pādākarṣākarṣasya sarvavajradharānucara kaṇḍa kaṇḍa vajra hūṃ jaḥ</s>!

body.text: athaivamukte mahādeva umādevīsahitaḥ ūrdhvapādo nagnaḥ sarvajagadbhirupahasyamānaḥ pādākarṣaṇavajrānucareṇa bhagava[to vajrapā]ṇeḥ purataḥ pādatāle sthāpita iti /
body.translated_text: And when this was uttered, <s>Mahādeva</s>, the god, together with the goddess <s>Umā</s>, with feet upward, naked, being laughed at by all the world, was placed at the sole of <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>'s foot by the foot-dragging <s>vajra</s>-attendant.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirbodhisatvo bhagavantametadavocat / "ayaṃ bhagavan duṣṭasatvaḥ sapatnīkaḥ kiṃ karomi?" [iti] / bhagavānāha oṃ vajrākrama hoḥ // athaivamukte vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvo mahādevaṃ vāmapādākrāntaṃ kṛtvā, dakṣiṇena comā [yāḥ stanau pīḍa]yannidaṃ svahṛdayamudājahāra oṃ vajrāviśa hanaya traṃ traṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'This wicked being, <s>Bhagavān</s>, together with his consort — what should I do [with him]?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: <s>oṃ vajrākrama hoḥ</s>! And when this was uttered, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having placed <s>Mahādeva</s> under his left foot, and with his right [foot] pressing down upon <s>Umā</s>'s breasts, uttered this, his own heart [-mantra]: <s>oṃ vajrāviśa hanaya traṃ traṭ</s>!

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre mahādevaḥ samāviṣṭvā, svakarasahasreṇa mukha[saha]stramahanat / atha vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgārasya bāhyataḥ sarvatribhuvanairmahānādo muktaḥ / "ayaṃ so 'smākamadhipatiranena mahātmanā [śāsyata" iti] //
body.translated_text: And the moment this was uttered, <s>Mahādeva</s>, having been entered [by the vajra-power], struck his own thousand faces with his thousand hands. And from outside the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion, a great cry was released by all the three worlds: 'This lord of ours is being disciplined by this great being!'

body.text: atha bhagavān mahādevasyopari mahākaruṇāmutpādya, idaṃ sarvabuddhamaitrīhṛdayamabhāṣat oṃ buddha maitrī vajra rakṣa haṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having generated great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) toward <s>Mahādeva</s>, uttered this heart of the loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) of all <s>Buddha</s>s: <s>oṃ buddha maitrī vajra rakṣa haṃ</s>!

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre mahādevasya tadāveśaduḥkhamupaśāntaṃ / tacca vajrapāṇipādatalasparśamanuttarasiddhyabhiṣekasamādhivimokṣadhāraṇī jñānābhijñāvāptaye yāvat tathāgatatvāya saṃvṛtta iti / atha mahādevo bhagavatpādatalasparśātsarvatathāgatasamādhidhāraṇīvimokṣasukhānyanubhavanta mahādevakāyaṃ vajrapāṇipādamūle nipātayitvā, adhastād dvātriṃśadgaṅgānadīvālukopamalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥ samā lokadhātavo 'tikramya, bhasmacchatrā nāma lokadhātustatra bhasmeśvaranirghoṣo nāma tathāgata utpannaḥ / atha tasmānmahādevakāyādidamudānaṃ niḥ sṛtavān /
body.translated_text: And the moment this was uttered, the suffering of <s>Mahādeva</s>'s [vajra-]possession was pacified. And that touch of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>'s foot-sole resulted in the attainment of the unsurpassed accomplishment — the consecration, <s>samādhi</s>, liberation, <s>dhāraṇī</s>, wisdom, and <s>abhijñā</s> — up to <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood. Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, through the touch of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s foot-sole, experiencing the bliss of the <s>samādhi</s>, <s>dhāraṇī</s>, and liberation of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, cast down his <s>Mahādeva</s>-body at the foot of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, and having passed below through world-realms equal in number to the atoms and particles of thirty-two <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand world-realms, [he arrived at] the world-realm called <s>Bhasmacchatrā</s> (Ash-Canopy), where a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Bhasmeśvaranirghoṣa</s> (Sound of the Lord of Ashes) was born. Then from that <s>Mahādeva</s>-body, this inspired utterance issued forth:

children.translated_text: Ah! The unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-wisdom of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
having cast [one] down to the syllable-ground, they establish [one] in <s>nirvāṇa</s>!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvastānanyān nārāyaṇādān sarvatrilokādhipatīnevamāha / "praviśadhvaṃ mārṣā asminsarvatathāgatavajrasamayamahāmaṇḍale; praviṣṭvā sarvatathāgatasamayamanupālayata!" / ta evamāhuḥ / "yathā jñāpayasi tathā kurma" iti //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> addressed those other lords of the entire three worlds, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the rest, thus: 'Enter, sirs, this great <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! Having entered, maintain the pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s!' They said thus: 'As you command, so we shall do.'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvastāṃstribhuvanasanniveśānāhūyaivamāha / "pratigṛṇhata mārṣāḥ punastriśaraṇagamanaśikṣāsamayasaṃvaraṃ, mama ca samaye tiṣṭhata!" / ta evamāhuḥ "evamastviti / kintu vayaṃ tava samayam [akovidāḥ]" /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>, having summoned those inhabitants of the three worlds, said thus: 'Accept, sirs, once again the training of the threefold refuge, the pledge-vow, and abide in my pledge!' They said thus: 'So be it! But we are unfamiliar with your pledge.'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiḥ svasamayamanuprādāt / bodhicittaṃ samutpadya yathā ca kramataḥ para[m / bodhyarthāya yathābalaṃ yata]dhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> bestowed his own pledge: 'Having generated the <s>bodhicitta</s> (awakening-mind), and progressively further, strive, well-concentrated, for the purpose of awakening, according to your ability.'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ teṣāṃ devādīnāṃ, "praveśamahāsamayamudrāṃ bandhāna" iti kṛtvā, bandhayanti sma, anena [mahāsamaya]mudrāhṛdayeneti /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>, having told those gods and the rest to 'bind the entry-great-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>,' they bound it, with this great-pledge-<s>mudrā</s> heart [-mantra]:

body.text:
oṃ vajra samaya gṛhṇa bandha samayaṃ,
vajrasatva samayamanusmara sarvatathāgatasamayastvaṃ /

children.text: dṛḍhī me bhava, sthiro me bhava, [āhāryo me bhava, apratihā]ryo me bhava,
children.translated_text: <s>dṛḍhī me bhava, sthiro me bhava, āhāryo me bhava, apratihāryo me bhava</s>,
<s>sarvakarmasu ca me cittaśreyaḥ kuru</s>,
<s>ha ha ha ha hūṃ</s>!

body.translated_text:
<s>oṃ vajra samaya gṛhṇa bandha samayaṃ</s>,
<s>vajrasatva samayamanusmara sarvatathāgatasamayastvaṃ</s>,

And the moment this was uttered, [<s>Vajrapāṇi</s>], having entered [their minds] with the <s>vajra</s>-wrath <s>mudrā</s> with both hands throughout the entire assembly of inhabitants of the three worlds in the threefold world-system, having bound them, they became firm [in the pledge].
New names of all the deities

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiryathāvatpraveśayitvā, sarvamahāmaṇḍalaṃ yathānupūrveṇa deśayitvā, vajraratnābhiṣekairabhiṣicya, vajracinhāni ca karebhyo datvā, vajranāmābhiṣekairabhiṣicya, sarvatathāgatasatvārthatāyāṃ sthāpayāmāsa / atha sarvatrailokyādhipatīnāṃ karma bhavati / tadyathā, maheśvarāya krodhavajraḥ, nārāyaṇāya māyāvajraḥ, sanatkumārāya vajraghaṇṭaḥ, brahmaṇe maunavajraḥ, indrāya vajrāyudhaḥ, iti vidyārājyakā ityabhiṣiktāḥ / tato 'ntarīkṣacarāṇāṃ sarvadevādhipa[tīnāmanuprādāt /] tadyathā, amṛtakuṇḍale vajrakuṇḍaliḥ, indave vajraprabhaḥ, mahādaṇḍāgrāya vajradaṇḍaḥ, piṅgalāya vajrapiṅgalaḥ, ityevamādāya vajrakrodhā ityabhiṣiktāḥ / tata ākāśacarāṇāṃ sarvadevādhipatīnāmanuprādāt / tadyathā, madhumattāya vajraśauṇḍaḥ, madhukarāya vajramālā, jayāya vajravaśī, jayāvahāya vijayavajra, ityevamādyā gaṇapataya ityabhiṣiktāḥ / tato bhaumānāṃ sarvadevādhipatīnāmanuprādāt / tadyathā, kośapālāya vajramusalaḥ, vāyave vajrānilaḥ, agnaye vajrānalaḥ, kuberāya vajrabhairavaḥ, ityevamādayo dūtā ityabhiṣiktāḥ / tataḥ pātālādhipatīnāṃ sarvadevānāmanuprādāt / tadyathā, varāhāya vajrāṅkuśaḥ, yamāya vajrakālaḥ, pṛthvīcūlikāya vajravināyakaḥ, varuṇāya nāgavajraḥ, ityevamādyāśceṭakā ityabhiṣiktāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having duly led [them] in, having taught the entire great <s>maṇḍala</s> in due order, having consecrated [them] with the <s>vajra</s>-jewel consecrations, having given the <s>vajra</s>-symbols into their hands, having consecrated [them] with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecrations, established [them] in the service of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-beings. Then the activity for all the lords of the three worlds takes place. Namely: for <s>Maheśvara</s> — Wrathful <s>Vajra</s>; for <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — Illusion <s>Vajra</s>; for <s>Sanatkumāra</s> — <s>Vajra</s>-bell; for <s>Brahmā</s> — Silent <s>Vajra</s>; for <s>Indra</s> — <s>Vajra</s>-weapon — thus they were consecrated as '<s>Vidyā</s>-kings.' Then he bestowed [names] upon all the lords of the sky-dwelling deities. Namely: for <s>Amṛtakuṇḍali</s> — <s>Vajrakuṇḍali</s>; for <s>Indu</s> — <s>Vajraprabha</s>; for <s>Mahādaṇḍāgra</s> — <s>Vajradaṇḍa</s>; for <s>Piṅgala</s> — <s>Vajrapiṅgala</s> — thus they were consecrated as '<s>Vajra</s>-wrathful ones.' Then he bestowed [names] upon all the lords of the space-faring deities. Namely: for <s>Madhumatta</s> — <s>Vajraśauṇḍa</s>; for <s>Madhukara</s> — <s>Vajramālā</s>; for <s>Jaya</s> — <s>Vajravaśī</s>; for <s>Jayāvaha</s> — <s>Vijayavajra</s> — thus they were consecrated as '<s>Gaṇapati</s>s.' Then he bestowed [names] upon all the lords of the earth-dwelling deities. Namely: for <s>Kośapāla</s> — <s>Vajramusala</s>; for <s>Vāyu</s> — <s>Vajrānila</s>; for <s>Agni</s> — <s>Vajrānala</s>; for <s>Kubera</s> — <s>Vajrabhairava</s> — thus they were consecrated as 'messengers.' Then he bestowed [names] upon all the deities who are lords of the netherworld. Namely: for <s>Varāha</s> — <s>Vajrāṅkuśa</s>; for <s>Yama</s> — <s>Vajrakāla</s>; for <s>Pṛthvīcūlikā</s> — <s>Vajravināyaka</s>; for <s>Varuṇa</s> — <s>Nāgavajra</s> — thus they were consecrated as 'servants.'
New names of <s>Śaiva</s> goddesses
