body.text: tatastrailokyādhipatiḥ sarvadevīnāṃ vajraratnābhiṣekeṇābhiṣicya, svacinhebhyo vajrādhiṣṭhāpya, [vajra] nāmābhiṣekeṇābhiṣicya, sarvatathāgatasatvārthatāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayāmāsa / tadyathā, umāyai krodhavajrāgniḥ, rukmiṇyai [vajrasauvarṇī], ṣaṣṭhyai vajrakaumārī, brahmāṇyai vajraśāntiḥ, indrāṇyai vajramuṣṭiri, tyevamādyā vajrarājanikā ityabhiṣiktāḥ / tato 'ntarīkṣacarīṇāṃ [sarvamā]tṛṇāmanuprādāt / tadyathā, amṛtāyai vajrāmṛtā, rohiṇyai vajrakāntiḥ, daṇḍahāriṇyai daṇḍavajrāgrā, jātāhāriṇyai vajra[mekhalā], ityevamādyā vajrakrodhinya ityabhiṣiktāḥ / tataḥ khecarīṇāṃ sarvamātṝṇāmanuprādāt / tadyathā, māraṇyai vajravilayā, [aśanā]yai vajrāśanā, vasanāyai vajravasanā, ratyai vajravaśā, ityevamādyā gaṇikā ityabhiṣiktāḥ / tato bhūcarīṇāṃ sarvamātṝṇāmanuprādāt / tadyathā, śivāyai vajradūtī, vāyavyai vegavajriṇī, āgnedhryāyai vajrajvālā, kuberyai vajravikaṭā, ityevamādyā vajradūtya ityabhiṣiktāḥ / tataḥ pātālavāsinīnāṃ sarvamātṝṇāmanuprādāt / vārāhyai vajramukhī, cāmuṇḍāyai vajrakālī, cchinnanāsāyai vajrapūtanā, vāruṇyai vajramakarī, ityevamādyā vajraceṭya ityabhiṣiktāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the lord of the three worlds, having consecrated all the goddesses with the <s>vajra</s>-jewel consecration, having empowered [them] with the <s>vajra</s> upon their own symbols, having consecrated [them] with the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration, established [them] in the service of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-beings. Namely: for <s>Umā</s> — Wrathful <s>Vajra</s>-fire; for <s>Rukmiṇī</s> — <s>Vajrasauvarṇī</s>; for <s>Ṣaṣṭhī</s> — <s>Vajrakaumārī</s>; for <s>Brahmāṇī</s> — <s>Vajraśānti</s>; for <s>Indrāṇī</s> — <s>Vajramuṣṭi</s> — thus they were consecrated as '<s>Vajra</s> queens.' Then he bestowed [names] upon all the sky-dwelling mothers. Namely: for <s>Amṛtā</s> — <s>Vajrāmṛtā</s>; for <s>Rohiṇī</s> — <s>Vajrakānti</s>; for <s>Daṇḍahāriṇī</s> — <s>Daṇḍavajrāgrā</s>; for <s>Jātāhāriṇī</s> — <s>Vajramekhalā</s> — thus they were consecrated as '<s>Vajra</s>-wrathful goddesses.' Then he bestowed [names] upon all the space-faring mothers. Namely: for <s>Māraṇī</s> — <s>Vajravilayā</s>; for <s>Aśanā</s> — <s>Vajrāśanā</s>; for <s>Vasanā</s> — <s>Vajravasanā</s>; for <s>Rati</s> — <s>Vajravaśā</s> — thus they were consecrated as 'courtesans.' Then he bestowed [names] upon all the earth-dwelling mothers. Namely: for <s>Śivā</s> — <s>Vajradūtī</s>; for <s>Vāyavī</s> — <s>Vegavajriṇī</s>; for <s>Āgneyī</s> — <s>Vajrajvālā</s>; for <s>Kuberī</s> — <s>Vajravikaṭā</s> — thus they were consecrated as '<s>Vajra</s>-messengers.' Then he bestowed [names] upon all the mothers dwelling in the netherworld. For <s>Vārāhī</s> — <s>Vajramukhī</s>; for <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s> — <s>Vajrakālī</s>; for <s>Cchinnanāsā</s> — <s>Vajrapūtanā</s>; for <s>Vāruṇī</s> — <s>Vajramakarī</s> — thus they were consecrated as '<s>Vajra</s>-servants.'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ teṣāṃ sarvapraviṣṭānāmbuddhajñānāni niṣpādya, sarvamudrābandhāni śikṣayitvā, vajrasamayānyanuprādāt anena śapathahṛdayena /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>, having accomplished <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge for all those who had entered, having taught all the <s>mudrā</s>-bindings, bestowed the <s>vajra</s>-pledges with this oath heart[-<s>mantra</s>]:

children.translated_text: This <s>vajra</s>, the great <s>vajra</s>, empowered by all <s>Buddha</s>s —
if [their] pledges are transgressed, it would quickly burn to ashes the [offending] families!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Strike! Pledge! Hūṃ Phaṭ!
<s>Mudrā</s>
Then he bestowed the <s>mudrā</s> for seizing the hearts:

children.translated_text: Having bound the pair of <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s with the index fingers bound as hooks,
one should make the turning and reversing — one who contemplates the purpose of the task. (1)
You [deities] must stand before that one for the accomplishment of the task;
lest this pledge become the destruction of your lives! (2)
Having strengthened the <s>vajra</s>-binding, well-controlled with curved tips,
joining the pair of thumbs, one should press the two middle [fingers]. (3)

children.text: ayaṃ vaḥ samayo hanyād yadiṃ kaścidatikramet /
children.translated_text: This pledge of yours would strike whoever transgresses it —
the binding of the pledge-<s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>vidyādhara</s>! (4)
But the binding of the little fingers of the pair of <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s,
with the finger-tips grasped behind, turned and placed on the head — (5)
this is the binding of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>vidyādhara</s>, the pledge of the great-souled one.
Whoever looks upon the wrathful one should stand before that one thus. (6)

children.text: vajrarakṣāṃ dṛḍhāṃ badhvā vajrabandhaṃ tu pīḍayet /
children.translated_text: Having bound the firm <s>vajra</s>-protection, one should press the <s>vajra</s>-binding.
This is indeed the pledge of the earth-dwellers, the protector of all beings. (7)
Whoever, for the purpose of rescue, would bind [the mudrā] accompanied by wrath —
for the protection of that being, [the deities] must stand behind that one. (8)
Having bound the pair of <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s, pressed by the left <s>vajra</s>-tip,
having made the turning and reversing, one should snap the little finger-joint. (9)

body.text:
ya[di krodhaṃ samāviśet] prayuñcet samayohya /
tasya yuṣmābhiḥ purataḥ stheyaṃ sarvāgrasiddhaya // iti // 10 //
body.translated_text:
If one should enter the wrathful [state] and employ this pledge —
before that one you [deities] must stand, for the accomplishment of all supreme [aims]! (10)

children.translated_text: Knotted with the <s>vajra</s>-binding, firmly [joined] with the index-finger yoga,
one should cast the <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s> at the mouths of the middle [fingers] and thumbs. (11)

body.text:
parivartya lalāṭe tu sthāpya yastu samāvhayet /
tasya stheyaṃ puraḥ śaśvad yadi jīvi[taṃ sthāpayed // 12 // i]ti //
body.translated_text:
Turning and placing it on the forehead — whoever summons thus,
before that one [the deities] must stand forever, if life is to be preserved! (12)

body.text:
athāsāṃ sakalatrilokahṛdayagrahaṇasamayamudrāṇāṃ samayagrahaṇahṛdayāni bhavanti /
oṃ valitodvalita vajrākarṣaya [huṃ jjaḥ //] vajravalitamudrāyā devākarṣaṇahṛdayaṃ /
huṃ vajrāgra pīḍaya samaya huṃ // antarīkṣacarāṇaṃ //
body.translated_text:
Now, these are the pledge-seizing heart[-<s>mantra</s>s] of the pledge-<s>mudrā</s>s for seizing the hearts of all the three worlds:
Oṃ — Turning and reversing — <s>Vajra</s> attract! Hūṃ Jaḥ! — This is the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] of the <s>Vajra</s>-turning <s>mudrā</s> for attracting deities.
Hūṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-tip press! Pledge! Hūṃ! — For the sky-dwellers.

body.text:
oṃ vajramālāgra vaṃ // māladhāriṇī[nāṃ /]
oṃ vajrabandha haṃ // bhūcarāṇāṃ /
oṃ vajra pātāla bhaṃja bhaṃja huṃ phaṭ // pātālanivāsināṃ /
oṃ herūka vajra samaya sarvaduṣṭa samaya mudrā prabhaṃjaka huṃ phaṭ // sarvamātṝṇāmiti //
body.translated_text:
Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-garland-tip! Vaṃ! — For the garland-bearers.
Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-bind! Haṃ! — For the earth-dwellers.
Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-netherworld — shatter, shatter! Hūṃ Phaṭ! — For the netherworld inhabitants.
Oṃ — <s>Heruka Vajra</s> — pledge — shatterer of all hostile pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>s! Hūṃ Phaṭ! — For all the mothers.

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇirbhagavantametadavocat / "ahaṃ bhagavaṃ sarvatathāgatairduṣṭadamaka ityabhiṣiktaḥ, tatsādhvājñāpayaiṣāṃ sarvaduṣṭamaṇḍalabandhānāṃ kathaṃ pratipadyāmi" /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, have been consecrated by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s as the tamer of the hostile. Therefore, please command — how should I deal with all these hostile <s>maṇḍala</s>-bindings?'

body.text: atha bhagavānidamupaśrutya evamāha / oṃ vajra suṃbha nisuṃbha huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having heard this, spoke thus: Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s> — <s>Sumbha</s>, <s>Nisumbha</s>! Hūṃ Phaṭ!
Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>, for the rescue of all beings, spoke this heart[-<s>mantra</s>] for attracting all <s>maṇḍala</s>s:

body.text: oṃ vajra samayākarṣaya sarvamaṇḍalān vajradhara satyaṃ mātikrama huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-pledge — attract all <s>maṇḍala</s>s! <s>Vajradhara</s> — in truth — do not transgress! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

children.translated_text: The pair of <s>vajra</s>-hooks turned at the heart,
the pair of outer hooks — this is the supreme attraction of the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>s.

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre sarvamaṇḍalāni sarvataḥ sumerugirimūrdhni bādhyataḥ parivāryāvasthitāni /
body.translated_text: The moment this was spoken, all <s>maṇḍala</s>s from everywhere stood surrounding [<s>Sumeru</s>] from the outside on the summit of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇistāṃ sarvamaṇḍalasanniveśānāhūyaivamāha / "pratipadyata mārṣāḥ prāṇātipātavairamaṇyasamayasaṃgrahaṇam!" iti / atha tairbāhyamaṇḍalasamayasatvairbhagavāṃ vijñapto, "vayaṃ bhagavan mānsāhārā dṛṣṭasatvatayā ojohāreṇa jīvikāṃ kalpayāmaḥ; tadājñāpayatu bhagavān kathamasmābhirjīvitavyam" iti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having summoned all those <s>maṇḍala</s> assemblies, spoke thus: 'Accept, O sirs, the pledge of the restraint from the enmity of taking life!' Then those outer <s>maṇḍala</s> pledge-beings informed the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'We, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are flesh-eaters; we sustain our livelihood by consuming the vital essence of visible beings. Therefore, may the <s>Bhagavān</s> command — how are we to live?'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatva imaṃ duṣṭavajrakrodhamabhāṣat / oṃ duṣṭavajrakrodha hana daha paca vidhvaṃsaya vikira sarvaduṣṭasamayamudrāmaṇḍalān bhaṃja bhaṃja marda marda khāda khāda paramantrān vajra samaya huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> spoke this hostile <s>vajra</s>-wrath: Oṃ — Hostile <s>vajra</s>-wrath — strike, burn, cook, destroy, scatter! Shatter, shatter all hostile pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>s! Crush, crush! Devour, devour the rival <s>mantra</s>s! <s>Vajra</s>-pledge! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

children.translated_text: With the <s>vajra</s>-wrath fingers properly wrapped at the nail-joints,
one should join [them] tightly from the mouth — this <s>mudrā</s> destroys the hostile!

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre sarvaduṣṭamaṇḍalāni ekadhyībhūtvānekāni vidhvansitāni vikīrṇāni, samayamudrābandhāḥ sphoṭitāḥ / te ca duṣṭasamayasatvā dahyamānāḥ pacyamānā mahānto mahārauravāntāntān khān muñcanto, yena bhagavān mahāvajradharastenāñjalayo badhvaivamāhuḥ / "paritrāyasva bhagavan, yena vayaṃ prāṇān na parityajāmaḥ!" /
body.translated_text: The moment this was spoken, all the hostile <s>maṇḍala</s>s, having become unified, were destroyed and scattered in multitudes; their pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-bindings were shattered. And those hostile pledge-beings, being burned and cooked, releasing great terrible cries, joined their palms toward the <s>Bhagavān Mahāvajradhara</s> and said thus: 'Rescue us, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, so that we do not lose our lives!'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat / "ājñāpayasva bhagavan kathameṣāṃ duṣṭamaṇḍalānāṃ pratipadyāmi" / atha bhagavānidamuvāca oṃ nisuṃbha hana daha paca gṛhṇa bandha huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> again said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Command, O <s>Bhagavān</s> — how should I deal with these hostile <s>maṇḍala</s>s?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke thus: Oṃ — <s>Nisumbha</s> — strike, burn, cook, seize, bind! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatva i[maṃ] vajrakrūrakrodhamabhāṣat oṃ mahāvajrakrūrakrodha pātaya sarvaduṣṭamaṇḍalān, vināśaya sarvaduṣṭasamayān, vikira vidhvaṃ[saya spho]ṭaya bhaṃjaya sarvaduṣṭasamayamudrābandhān, gṛhṇa hana daha paca sarvaduṣṭasamayasatvān, vajra samaya huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> spoke this <s>vajra</s> fierce wrath: Oṃ — Great <s>vajra</s> fierce wrath — cast down all hostile <s>maṇḍala</s>s! Destroy all hostile pledges! Scatter, destroy, shatter, break all hostile pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-bindings! Seize, strike, burn, cook all hostile pledge-beings! <s>Vajra</s>-pledge! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre sarvaduṣṭasamayamudrāmaṇḍalāni punarapyekadhyībhūtvā mahāsāgare prapatitānīti //
body.translated_text: The moment this was spoken, all the hostile pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>s, having again become unified, fell into the great ocean.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat / "ahaṃ bhagavatā sarvaduṣṭadamanāyādhyeṣitaḥ / tadeṣāṃ ḍākinīgrahādīnāṃ sarvagrahāṇāṃ kathaṃ pratipadyāmi? /"
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> again said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I have been entreated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> for the taming of all the hostile. How then should I deal with all the spirits (<s>graha</s>) such as <s>ḍākinī</s>s and the rest?'

body.text: atha bhagavānidamavocat oṃ hana hana vajra huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke thus: Oṃ — Strike, strike! <s>Vajra</s>! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ punarapi sarvaḍākinyādiduṣṭagrahākarṣaṇahṛdayamabhāṣat oṃ vajrākarṣaya śīghraṃ sarvaduṣṭagrahān vajradharasatyena huṃ jaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> again spoke this heart[-<s>mantra</s>] for attracting all hostile spirits such as <s>ḍākinī</s>s and the rest: Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s> — attract quickly all hostile spirits! By the truth of <s>Vajradhara</s>! Hūṃ Jaḥ!

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre ḍākinyādayaḥ sarvaduṣṭagrahāḥ sumerugirimūrdhni bāhyato maṇḍalībhūtvāvasthitā iti //
body.translated_text: The moment this was spoken, the <s>ḍākinī</s>s and all the hostile spirits stood assembled in <s>maṇḍala</s> formation outside on the summit of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ tāṃ ḍākinyādīn sarvaduṣṭagrahānāhūyaivamāha / "pratipadyata mārṣāḥ prāṇātipātavairamaṇyaśikṣāsamayasaṃvare; mā vo vajreṇādīptena pradīptenaikajvālībhūtena kulāni nirdaheyam" /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>, having summoned those <s>ḍākinī</s>s and all the hostile spirits, spoke thus: 'Accept, O sirs, the pledge of the training-restraint from the enmity of taking life! Lest I burn your families with the blazing, burning <s>vajra</s> become a single flame!'

body.text: atha te ḍākinyādayaḥ sarvaduṣṭagrahā yena bhagavān tenāñjalim badhvā bhagavantaṃ vijñāpayāmāsuḥ / "vayaṃ bhagavan mānsāśinas, tadājñāpayasva kathaṃ pratipattavyam" iti /
body.translated_text: Then those <s>ḍākinī</s>s and all the hostile spirits, joining their palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, informed the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'We, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are flesh-eaters. Therefore, please command — how should we conduct ourselves?'

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇimevamāha "pratipadyasva vajrapāṇe eṣāṃ sarvānāṃ mahākaruṇāmutpādyopāyandātum" iti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke thus to <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>: 'Act, O <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> — having generated great compassion toward all of them, give [them] the skillful means!'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahākāruṇika idaṃ sarvasatvamaraṇanimittajñānamudrāhṛdayamabhāṣat oṃ vajra pratigṛhaṇa hṛdayamākarṣaya, yadyayaṃ satvo māṃsādatvena mriyate, tadasya hṛdayanniṣkramatu, samaya huṃ jjaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the greatly compassionate <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> spoke this heart[-<s>mantra</s>] of the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> for knowing the sign of death of all beings: Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s> — accept! Attract the heart! If this being will die due to flesh-eating, then let [the vital force] depart from its heart. Pledge! Hūṃ Jaḥ!
Now the binding of this <s>mudrā</s> is as follows:

children.translated_text: Having established the <s>vajra</s>-binding, [placing] the well-befriended [hands] at the heart with both arms,
with the <s>vajra</s>-finger-tips, one should draw upward at one's own armpits.

body.text: anayā mudrayā bhavadbhiḥ sarvasatvahṛdayānyapakṛṣya bhoktavyānī-" ti /
body.translated_text: 'With this <s>mudrā</s>, you [spirits] should extract the hearts of all beings [who are destined to die] and consume [them].'

body.text: atha te ḍākinyādayaḥ sarvaduṣṭagrahā huluhuluprakṣveḍitāni kṛtvā svabhavanaṃ gatā iti //
body.translated_text: Then those <s>ḍākinī</s>s and all the hostile spirits, having made cries of 'hulu, hulu!', departed to their own abodes.

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat / "ahaṃ bhagavadbhiḥ sarvatathāgataiḥ sarvaduṣṭadamaka iti kṛtvādhyiṣṭaḥ / tadājñāpayatu me bhagavān jvarādīnāṃ vyādhīnāṃ kiṅkaromi" //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'I, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, have been empowered by all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s as the subduer of all evil ones. Therefore, may the <s>Bhagavān</s> command me — what shall I do regarding fevers and other diseases?'
Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: OṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ sarvajvarādyākarṣaṇahṛdayamudājahāra oṃ vajra samayānaya sarva[duṣṭa]jvarādīnnāśayaṃ huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> uttered the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] for attracting all fevers and the rest: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>, by the pledge, bring! Destroy all evil fevers and the rest! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre jvarādayaḥ sarve sumerugirimūrdhni bāhyataḥ parivāryavasthitā abhūvan /
body.translated_text: And at the very moment this was uttered, all fevers and the rest stood surrounding [the assembly] outside, on the summit of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇistān jvarādīnāhūyaivamāha / "pratipadyata mārṣāḥ satvopaghātavairamaṇyaśikṣāgrahaṇasaṃvare!" / atha ta evamāhu / "vayaṃ bhagavan satvau [jo 'pa]hṛtya jīvikāṃ kalpayāmaḥ / tatsādhu bhagavānājñāpayatu kathaṃ pratipadyāmaha" iti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having summoned those fevers and the rest, spoke thus: 'Accept, O sirs, the discipline of the vow to refrain from harming beings!' Then they spoke thus: 'We, <s>Bhagavān</s>, make our livelihood by seizing the vitality of beings. Therefore, may the <s>Bhagavān</s> kindly command us — how should we proceed?'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatva idaṃ svakarmaviśuddhijñānamudrāhṛdayamudājahāra oṃ vajrakarma viśodhaya sarvāvaraṇāni buddhasatyena samaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> uttered this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]-<s>mudrā</s> knowledge of the purification of one's own <s>karma</s>: OṂ — <s>Vajrakarma</s>, purify! All obscurations — by the truth of the <s>Buddha</s> — pledge! HŪṂ!
And here is the <s>mudrā</s>-binding:

children.translated_text: Having firmly joined the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s>, with the two index fingers curved,
well-bound, restrained by the thumbs — it is called 'the remover of evil.'

body.text: iyaṃ mudrā yasya jvarādisarvavyādhispṛṣṭasya karmato darśayet, tadyuṣmābhirapasartavyaṃ; mā vo jīvitanāśo bhaved" iti / atha ta "evamastv" iti kṛtvā prakrāntā iti //
body.translated_text: 'This <s>mudrā</s>, when shown through [ritual] action to one afflicted by fever and all other diseases — you must depart from that one; lest your lives be destroyed!' Then they, having said 'So be it!,' departed.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ sarvatathāgatānevamāha / "ahaṃ bhagavadbhiḥ sarvāvaraṇanīvaraṇakarmāvaraṇaviśuddhihetoḥ svahṛdayebhyo viniḥsṛṣṭaḥ / tadājñāpayatu me bhagavantaḥ eṣānnarakādīnāṃ sarvāpāyānāṃ kathaṃ pratipattavyam" iti /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'I, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, have been sent forth from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for the purpose of purifying all obscurations, hindrances, and <s>karma</s>-obscurations. Therefore, may the <s>Bhagavān</s>s command me — what shall I do regarding the hells (<s>naraka</s>) and all the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>)?'
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: OṂ KṢAPAYA VAJRA SVĀHĀ!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ rauravādisarvāpāyagaticakrākarṣaṇahṛdamabhāṣat oṃ sarvāpāyakarṣaṇa viśodhana vajrasamaya huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> uttered the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] for attracting the wheel of all lower realms beginning with the <s>Raurava</s> hell: OṂ — Attract all lower realms! Purify! <s>Vajra</s>-pledge! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre rauravamahārauravādayaḥ sarvāpāyasanniveśāḥ sumerugirimurdhni bāhyataḥ parivāryāvasthitāḥ /
body.translated_text: And at the very moment this was uttered, the <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, and all other assemblages of lower realms stood surrounding [the assembly] outside, on the summit of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>.

body.text:
atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ tānapāyabhūmipatitān sarvasatvānāhūyaivamāha / "gṛhṇata mārṣāstriśaraṇagamanasaṅkaṭāt! / eṣa vayaṃ buddhaṃ dharma saṃghaṃ tvaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gacchāma" iti /
atha vajrapāṇiḥ sarvāpāyasphoṭanahṛdayamudājahāra oṃ vajrapāṇi visphoṭaya sarvāpāyabandhanāni pramokṣaya sarvāpāyagatibhya sarvasatvān sarvatathāgatavajra samaya traṭ //
body.translated_text:
Then the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having summoned all those beings who had fallen into the lower realms, spoke thus: 'Accept, O sirs, the protective discipline of going for refuge to the Three [Jewels]! Thus: we go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and to you!'
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> uttered the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] for bursting open all lower realms: OṂ — <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, burst open! Release all the bonds of the lower realms! From all lower-realm destinies, [release] all beings! <s>Vajra</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! TRAṬ!
And here is the <s>mudrā</s>-binding:

children.translated_text: Having firmly made the <s>vajra</s>-binding, joined by the two middle [fingers],
with the tips of the four outer [fingers] touching — it is called 'the burster of evil.'

body.text: atha te tryapāyagaticakrāntarasthitāḥ sarvasatvā vajrapāṇisakāśādimāṃ mudrāṃ dṛṣṭvā, sarvadurgatibhyaścyutvā, bhagavato vairocanasya pādamūle upapannāḥ / te cāpāyā mahāsamudre patitā iti /
body.translated_text: Then all those beings situated within the wheel of the three lower destinies, having seen this <s>mudrā</s> from <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having departed from all evil destinies, were reborn at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>. And those lower realms fell into the great ocean.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat / "ahaṃ bhagavannaśeṣānavaśeṣatvadhātuparitrāṇasarvahitasukhānubhavanārtha yāvatsarvatathāgatatvottamasiddhiphalāvāptihetoḥ sarvatathāgatasiddhivajraṃ datvā, sarvatathāgatairadhyiṣṭaḥ /tatsādhu ājñāpayantu me bhaga[vantaḥ] sarvatathāgatā athaiṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ kiṅkaromī-"ti /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, have been empowered by all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having been given the accomplishment-<s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purpose of protecting the entire remainder-less and inexhaustible realm of beings, for the experience of all benefit and happiness, and for the attainment of the fruit of the supreme accomplishment of the state of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therefore, may the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, kindly command me — what shall I do regarding these human beings?'

body.text: atha sarvatathāgatāḥ punaḥ samājamāgamyedamavocan oṃ vajrapāṇi mahā[maṇḍale] praveśaya, sarvān duṣṭaraudrān nivāraya, pāpebhyaḥ pramokṣaya, durdṛṣṭiparyāpannān viśodhaya nāśaya vināśaya ha ha ha ha hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having again assembled, spoke thus: OṂ — <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, lead into the great <s>maṇḍala</s>! Ward off all evil and fierce ones! Release from sins! Purify those caught in wrong views! Destroy, annihilate! HA HA HA HA HŪṂ!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiḥ sarvatathāgatājñāvacanamupaśrutya, aśeṣānavaśeṣasatvadhātuparitrāṇasarvahitasukhottamasiddhinimittaṃ yāvat sarvatathāgatajñānābhijñāvāptiphalahetoridaṃ sarvatathāgatamahāvajrasamayabhūtaṃ trilokavijayannāma mahāmaṇḍalamabhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having heard the command-words of all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, for the purpose of the supreme accomplishment of all benefit and happiness for the protection of the entire remainder-less and inexhaustible realm of beings, and for the attainment of the fruit of the <s>abhijñā</s>-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, proclaimed this great <s>maṇḍala</s> called '<s>Trailokyavijaya</s>' (Conqueror of the Three Worlds), which is the great <s>vajra</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

children.translated_text: Now I shall proclaim the supreme great <s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>Vajradhātu</s>, supreme, accomplishing all <s>siddhi</s>s, (1)
called '<s>Trailokyavijaya</s>' (Conqueror of the Three Worlds), the pledge born of <s>vajra</s>,
the promoter of <s>Buddha</s>-awakening, the destroyer of all evil ones. (2)

body.text: tatrānena mantraṇa sūtrayet oṃ vajrasamaya sūtraṃ mātikrama //
body.translated_text: Therein, with this <s>mantra</s> one should draw the thread: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-pledge — thread! Do not transgress!

children.translated_text: Four-cornered, four-doored, adorned with four gateways,
fitted with four threads, beautifully adorned with bands and garlands. (1)
At all corners of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, at the junctions of the door-projections,
with one's own mind, one should thread the outer <s>maṇḍala</s> with <s>vajra</s>-jewels. (2)
Within that, the wise one [should draw] one adorned with <s>vajra</s>-jewels,
four-cornered, four-doored, with gateways of eight pillars. (3)
At the tops of the <s>vajra</s>-pillars, adorned with five <s>maṇḍala</s>s,
one should thread the <s>maṇḍala</s> there; the thread should be filled with colors. (4)

body.text: tatrāyaṃ raṅgajāpaḥ oṃ vajracitra samaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Here is the color-application recitation: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-variegated — pledge! HŪṂ!

children.translated_text: Then, the <s>vajra</s>-master, having taken his position in the center, concentrated,
should mentally open the four <s>vajra</s>-doors.

body.text: tatrāyaṃ dvārodghāṭanamantraḥ oṃ vajrodghāṭaya samaya praveśaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Here is the door-opening <s>mantra</s>: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>, open! Pledge, let enter! HŪṂ!

children.text: sauvarṇe rājate vāpi mṛṇmaye vā sucitrite /
children.translated_text: On golden, silver, or clay [tablets], well-decorated,
on four-cornered bricks, one should install <s>Buddha</s>-images.

body.text: tatredaṃ sarvatathāgatākarṣaṇahṛdayaṃ bhavati / oṃ vajra jvālāgnipradīptākarṣaya sarvatathāgatān mahāvajra samaya hūṃ jaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here is the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] for attracting all <s>Tathāgata</s>s: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>, blazing fire, burning — attract all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! Great <s>vajra</s> — pledge! HŪṂ JAḤ!

children.translated_text: Before the <s>Buddha</s>, one should install a <s>vajra</s> in the midst of flames.
In the midst of flames, one should draw a jewel, a lotus, and a universal weapon (<s>viśvāyudha</s>).

body.translated_text: Now here are the installation heart[-<s>mantra</s>s] of these <s>vajra</s>-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>s:
HŪṂ — Being-<s>vajra</s>, flame-garland! HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — Jewel-<s>vajra</s>, flame-garland! HŪṂ TRAḤ!
OṂ — <s>Dharma</s>-<s>vajra</s>, flame-garland! HŪṂ HRĪḤ!
HŪṂ — <s>Karma</s>-<s>vajra</s>, flame-garland! HŪṂ HAḤ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, before the <s>Buddha</s> likewise,
the wise one should duly draw the <s>Vajra</s>-HŪṂ-<s>kāra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>.

body.text: tatredaṃ vajravegahṛdayaṃ bhavati oṃ vajravegākrama hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Here is the <s>vajra</s>-speed heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-speed, advance! HŪṂ!

body.text: evaṃ vajradhātvādiṣu sarvamaṇḍaleṣu sūtramākramya, sarvato gacchediti //
body.translated_text: Thus, having advanced the thread in all <s>maṇḍala</s>s starting with the <s>Vajradhātu</s>, one should proceed everywhere.
And here is the <s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: Having mentally cast the line or the <s>vajra</s>-thread,
even those who enter with intent to roam — the pledge does not [allow] that. (1)
There, in the center, one should draw the great being, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>,
of the splendor of a great blue lotus, embodying the <s>vajra</s>-HŪṂ-<s>kāra</s>. (2)
With a mouth fierce with slightly bared fangs, with a wrathful laughing face,
standing in the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> stance, with a radiance enveloped in garlands of flames. (3)
Trampled under the left foot should be <s>Maheśvara</s>,
and the right foot should be drawn resting on the breast of <s>Umā</s>. (4)

body.translated_text: Here is his heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: HŪṂ!

children.translated_text: On all his sides, one should install <s>vajra</s>-wrathful ones,
fierce with bared fangs, with radiance enveloped in garlands of flames.
Now here are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
HŪṂ!

body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajrasattva</s>-wrathful one! HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-wrathful one, attract! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: oṃ vajrakāma krodha rāgāya hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajrakāma</s>-wrathful one, to passion! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: oṃ vajratuṣṭikrodha sādhu sādhu hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-satisfaction-wrathful one, well done, well done! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, in the second supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>,
there one should draw <s>Vajrābhiṣeka</s> (Vajra-Consecration), surrounded by wrathful ones.
Now here are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
TRAḤ!

body.text: oṃ vajrabhṛkuṭi krodha hara hara huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajrabhṛkuṭi</s>-wrathful one — seize, seize! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: oṃ vajrasūrya mahājvālāmāla krodha jvālaya sarva huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-sun, great flame-garland, wrathful one — blaze all! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: oṃ vajra krodha ketu dehi huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-wrathful-banner — give! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: oṃ vajrāṭṭahāsa krodha haḥ haḥ haḥ haḥ huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-boisterous-laughter-wrathful one — HAḤ HAḤ HAḤ HAḤ! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, in the third supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>,
one should draw <s>Vajrasena</s> (Vajra-Army), surrounded by great-souled wrathful ones.
Now here are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
HRĪḤ!

body.text: oṃ vajradharma krodha vināśaya viśodhaya huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajradharma</s>-wrathful one — destroy, purify! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: oṃ vajratīkṣṇa krodha cchinda cchinda huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-sharp-wrathful one — cut, cut! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: oṃ vajrahetu krodha praviśa praveśaya maṇḍalaṃ sarvā huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-cause-wrathful one — enter, cause to enter the <s>maṇḍala</s>! All! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: oṃ vajrakrodha bhāṣa vada vada huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-wrathful one — speak, speak, speak! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, in the fourth supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>,
one should draw <s>Vajrāveśa</s> (Vajra-Entry), surrounded by hosts of <s>vajra</s>-wrathful ones.
Therein, their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
AḤ!

body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajrakarma</s>!

body.text: oṃ vajrakavaca krodha rakṣa rakṣa huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-armor-wrathful one — protect, protect! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: oṃ vajrayakṣa krodha khāda khāda huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-<s>yakṣa</s>-wrathful one — devour, devour! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: huṃ vajrakrodha muṣṭi sādhaya samaya huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: HŪṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-wrathful-fist — accomplish the pledge! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

children.translated_text: At the corners of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, properly and in due order,
according to the <s>Vajradhātu</s> method, one should draw the secret offerings.
Now here are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]-<s>mudrā</s>s of those:
OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-play-goddess, enamor! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-garland-goddess, consecrate! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.text: oṃ vajragīte gāda gāda hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-song-goddess — sing, sing! HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-dance-goddess, subjugate! HŪṂ PHAṬ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, in the supreme outer <s>maṇḍala</s>,
there at the corners one should make the four offering goddesses.
Now here are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]-<s>mudrā</s>s of those:
OṂ — In the pledge of the pervading <s>vajra</s>-incense offering — HŪṂ PHAṬ!

body.translated_text: OṂ — In the pledge of the pervading <s>vajra</s>-flower offering — HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — In the pledge of the pervading <s>vajra</s>-lamp offering — HŪṂ PHAṬ!
OṂ — In the pledge of the pervading <s>vajra</s>-perfume offering — HŪṂ PHAṬ!

children.translated_text: The hook and the rest should be made at the four door-centers,
and the outer <s>vajra</s>-families at the positions of the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>.
Now here are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]-<s>mudrā</s>s of those:

children.text: oṃ vajrāṅkuśa mahākrodhākarṣaya sarvasamayān hūṃ jjaḥ //
children.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-hook, great wrathful one — attract all pledges! HŪṂ JAḤ!

body.text: oṃ vajrapāśa mahākrodha praveśaya sarvasamayān huṃ hūṃ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-noose, great wrathful one — cause all pledges to enter! HŪṂ HŪṂ!

body.text: oṃ vajrasphoṭa mahākrodha bandha bandha sarvasamayān huṃ vaṃ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-fetter, great wrathful one — bind, bind all pledges! HŪṂ VAṂ!

body.text: oṃ vajrāveśa mahākrodhāveśaya sarvasamayān huṃ aḥ //
body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Vajra</s>-entry, great wrathful one — cause all pledges to enter! HŪṂ AḤ!
Initiation into the <s>maṇḍala</s>
Now here is the detailed procedure for entry into the <s>Trailokyavijaya</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>.

body.text: tatrādita eva tāvatsvayaṃ vajrā [cāryo va]jrakodhaterintirimudrāṃ badhvā praviśet / praviṣṭvā sarvatathāgatāṃ vijñāpayet / "ahaṃ bhagavantastathāgatāḥ krodhavaśaṃ yāsyāmi [nigrahītavyāṃ] nigrahīṣyāmi saṃgrahītavyāṃ saṃgrahīṣyāmi / tanme bhagavanta ājñāpayantu, kathaṃ pratipadyāmī"ti kṛtvā, vajrakrodhaterintirimudrāṃ sva[hṛdaye ya]thāvatsthāpya, vajrāṅkuśādibhiḥ karmāṇi kṛtvā, punaḥ sarvasamayamudrāṃ bandhayet; tataḥ sarve sānnidhyaṅkalpayanti / tato guhyapūjācatuṣṭayaṃ kṛtvā tathā dhūpādibhiśca //
body.translated_text: Therein, first of all, the <s>vajra</s>-master himself, having formed the <s>Vajrakrodhaterintiri</s> <s>mudrā</s>, should enter. Having entered, he should petition all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s: 'I, <s>Bhagavān</s>s, <s>Tathāgata</s>s, shall proceed under the control of wrath — I shall subdue those to be subdued, I shall gather those to be gathered. Therefore, may the <s>Bhagavān</s>s command me — how should I proceed?' Having done so, having duly placed the <s>Vajrakrodhaterintiri</s> <s>mudrā</s> at one's own heart, having performed the actions with the <s>vajra</s>-hook and the rest, one should again bind the pledge-<s>mudrā</s> of all; thereupon all [deities] manifest their presence. Then, having performed the fourfold secret offering, and likewise with incense and the rest —

body.text: tato vajraśiṣyāṃ praveśayedanena vidhinā svayaṃ vajrācāryo vajrakodhatirintirimudrāṃ badhvā, śiṣyāya bandhayedanena hṛdayena oṃ gṛṇha vajra samaya huṃ vaṃ //
body.translated_text: Then one should lead the <s>vajra</s>-disciple in by this procedure: the <s>vajra</s>-master himself, having formed the <s>Vajrakrodhaterintiri</s> <s>mudrā</s>, should bind it on the disciple, with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: OṂ — Accept, <s>Vajra</s> — pledge! HŪṂ VAṂ!

body.text: tato nīlavastrāntarīyanīloṣṇīṣāvabandhaśirāḥ, nīlaraktakena mukhaṃ badhvā, praveśayedanena mantreṇa oṃ vajra samayaṃ praviśāmi // tataḥ praveśya vajrāveśasamayamudrayāsyāveśamutpādayedanena hṛdayena vajrāveśa aḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, [the disciple] having donned a blue inner garment, with head bound with a blue turban, having covered the face with a blue-red [cloth], one should cause [the disciple] to enter with this <s>mantra</s>: <s>oṃ vajra samayaṃ praviśāmi</s> (Oṃ, I enter the vajra pledge)! Then, having caused [the disciple] to enter, one should generate possession through the pledge-<s>mudrā</s> of <s>vajra</s>-possession with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: <s>vajrāveśa aḥ</s>!

body.text: tataḥ samāviśati / tenāveśena sarvatathāgatairadhiṣṭhyate / sarvaṃ cātītānāgatapratyutpannannimiṣādeva jānāti / avadhyaśca bhavati sarvasatvebhyaḥ, adhṛṣyaḥ / huṃkāreṇa ca sarvasatvanigrahānugrahasamarthībhavati / vajrapāṇiścāsya nityaṃ sarvakāryāṇi sādhayatīti //
body.translated_text: Then [the disciple] becomes possessed. Through that possession, one is empowered by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. And one knows everything — past, future, and present — in the blink of an eye. And one becomes invulnerable to all beings, inviolable. And through the syllable <s>hūṃ</s>, one becomes capable of subduing and favoring all beings. And <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> constantly accomplishes all [that one's] tasks.

body.text: tataḥ śapathahṛdayaṃ dadyāt / tato yathāvat mukhabandhaṃ muktvā, mahāmaṇḍalaṃ darśayet / maṇḍale dṛṣṭamātre tu sarvapāpairvimucyate, sakalatrilokavijayasamartho bhavati / huṃkāreṇa ca mahādevādisarvadevākarṣaṇapraveśanabandhanavaśīkaraṇapātanakṣamo bhavati / sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānācca vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ satatānuddhaḥ svakīyāḥ siddhīrdadāti //
body.translated_text: Then one should give the oath-heart[-<s>mantra</s>]. Then, having duly removed the face-covering, one should show the great <s>maṇḍala</s>. At the mere sight of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, one is freed from all sins and becomes capable of conquering all three worlds. And through the syllable <s>hūṃ</s>, one becomes capable of attracting, entering, binding, subjugating, and casting down all gods beginning with <s>Mahādeva</s>. And through the empowerment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, constantly being invoked, grants his own accomplishments.

body.text: tato 'sya vajrābhiṣekeṇābhiṣicya, tīkṣṇasvavajracinhaṃ yathāvat pāṇibhyāṃ dātavyamanena mantreṇa oṃ vajrapāṇi vajrakarmakaro bhava //
body.translated_text: Then, having consecrated that one with the <s>vajra</s>-consecration, one should duly give the sharp <s>vajra</s>-emblem of one's own [family] with both hands, with this <s>mantra</s>: <s>oṃ vajrapāṇi vajrakarmakaro bhava</s> (Oṃ, Vajrapāṇi, become a performer of vajra-action)!

body.text: tato vajranāmābhiṣekandadyādanena mantreṇa / oṃ vajrakrodha tvāmabhiṣiṃcāmi vajranāmābhiṣekataḥ hevajra nāma // tato yasya yannāma kuryāt tasya heśabdaḥ prayoktavya iti //
body.translated_text: Then one should give the <s>vajra</s>-name consecration with this <s>mantra</s>: <s>oṃ vajrakrodha tvāmabhiṣiṃcāmi vajranāmābhiṣekataḥ hevajra nāma</s> (Oṃ, Vajra-wrath, I consecrate you with the vajra-name consecration — your name is He-vajra)! Then, for whatever [disciple] whatever name one would give, the syllable 'he' should be prefixed.
Then one should generate the knowledges:

children.translated_text: 'Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-image at the heart, radiating with a mass of flames,
through the attainment of <s>vajra</s>-wrath, one would cause the entire world to be possessed.' (1)

children.text: vajraratnaṃ lalāṭe tu samālikhya tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: 'Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-jewel at the forehead, likewise,
through the attainment of <s>vajra</s>-wrath, one would bring all beings under control.' (2)
'Having placed the <s>vajra</s>-lotus at the throat, radiating with a garland of flames,
through the attainment of <s>vajra</s>-wrath, one would destroy all beings.' (3)
'Having established the <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajra</s> at the crown, radiating with a mass of flames,
through the attainment of <s>vajra</s>-wrath, one would protect this entire world.' (4)
Now, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s of these knowledge-<s>mudrā</s>s:
<s>huṃ satva vajra krodhāviśa aḥ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>ho ratna vajrakrodha traḥ</s>!
<s>huṃ dharma vajrakrodha phaṭ</s>!
<s>haṃ karma vajrakrodha rakṣa</s>!
<s>Mudrā</s>
Then one should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge for attracting gods and the rest:

children.translated_text: 'Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-hook on the palm, designated by the syllable <s>hūṃ</s>,
one should move the finger wrathfully — the supreme attraction of gods.' (1)
'Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-hook in the middle of the sole of one's own foot,
trampling with the phallus, with that very [mudrā] one would assuredly attract the gods.' (2)
'Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-hook on one's own erect penis,
moving [it], one would attract all women beginning with <s>Umā</s>.' (3)
'Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-hook on the anus and the navel likewise,
trampling with that whichever god — that is the supreme attraction of that one.' (4)
Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>oṃ vajra krodhāgrākarṣaya huṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajra kramāṅkuśakrodhākarṣaya huṃ phaṭ</s>!
<s>oṃ vajra krodhadaṇḍāgrākarṣaya huṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: oṃ vajrakrodhāsanāgacchākarṣayāmi te vajra samayamanusmara huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajrakrodhāsanāgacchākarṣayāmi te vajra samayamanusmara huṃ phaṭ</s>!
Then one should teach the fourfold <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: 'Standing in the warrior's stance (<s>pratyālīḍha</s>), through the application of <s>vajra</s>-possession,
in an instant, by the mere [syllable] <s>hūṃ</s>, one would cause the entire world to be possessed.' (1)
'With the <s>vajra</s>-voice, one should properly utter [the mantra] accompanied by the four <s>hūṃ</s>-syllables —
the heart of all <s>Buddha</s>s — one would assuredly bring everything [under control].' (2)
'Through the attainment of <s>vajra</s>-wrath, with the gaze of the foremost <s>vajra</s>-wrath,
one could slay the entire world through the yoga of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>hūṃ</s>-syllable.' (3)

body.text:
manasā varmayetkāyamātmanastu parasya vā /
mahākavacayogena rakṣetsarvamidaṃ jagad // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
'With the mind, one should armor the body — of oneself or of another;
through the yoga of the great armor, one would protect this entire world.' (4)

children.translated_text: Now, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:

children.text: oṃ vajra krodha kāyāveśaya huṃ aḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajra krodha kāyāveśaya huṃ aḥ</s>!

body.text: oṃ vajra vidyottama mahākrodhānaya ho bhagavan vajra huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajra vidyottama mahākrodhānaya ho bhagavan vajra huṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: oṃ vajra krodha dṛṣṭi hana daha paca vināśaya huṅkāreṇa pātaya vajra samaya huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajra krodha dṛṣṭi hana daha paca vināśaya huṅkāreṇa pātaya vajra samaya huṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: oṃ manodṛḍha vajra kavaca krodha rakṣa huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ manodṛḍha vajra kavaca krodha rakṣa huṃ phaṭ</s>!
Then one should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge for sealing all beings:

children.translated_text: 'Through the attainment of <s>vajra</s>-wrath, whomever one embraces,
through the recitation of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>hūṃ</s>-syllable, that one becomes sealed.' (1)

children.text: saṃlapanmahatā vācā ṭṭakki hūṃ phaṭ sakṛdvadet /
children.translated_text: 'Conversing with the great voice, uttering "<s>ṭṭakki hūṃ phaṭ</s>" once,

children.text: yasya kruddhaḥ sa dīptena vajreṇābhihato bhavet // 2 //
children.translated_text: against whomever one is wrathful, that one is struck by the blazing <s>vajra</s>.' (2)
'One should gaze with the <s>vajra</s>-gaze, in the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>vajra</s>-wrath —

children.text: yasya yasya tu satvasya so so maraṇamāpnuyāt // 3 //
children.translated_text: whatever being, that very one would meet death.' (3)

body.text:
manasā mārayāmīti vajraṃ hṛdi tu bhāvayet /
huṃkāreṇaiva sarveṣāṃ mudrayatyabhitaḥ svayam // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
'Mentally [thinking] "I shall slay," one should visualize the <s>vajra</s> at the heart;
by the <s>hūṃ</s>-syllable alone, one seals all [beings] on every side, by oneself.' (4)

body.text:
yasya satvasya yenaiva manasā mudrayatyasau /
ābhirmudrābhirabhyartha sarvakarmāṇi sādhayed // iti // 5 //
body.translated_text:
'Whatever being, with whatever mind, one seals —
with these <s>mudrā</s>s, having been entreated, one should accomplish all actions.' (5)

children.translated_text: Now, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>ṭakki aḥ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>ṭakki jjaḥ</s>!
<s>ṭakki huṃ</s>!
<s>ṭakki haṃ</s>!

body.text: ekaikayā tu mudrayā caturṣu karmasu catvāri mudrāhṛdayāni prayuñcediti //
body.translated_text: With each single <s>mudrā</s>, one should employ four <s>mudrā</s>-heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s in the four actions.
Then one should teach the knowledge of the secret wrath-<s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Having embraced [the consort] with all limbs, one should apply the <s>hūṃ</s>-syllable to that one;
through the union of the two organs, that one's life would perish.' (1)
'Kissing, grasping the lip with the teeth, through the yoga of the <s>hūṃ</s>-syllable,
through the union of the two organs, the face of that one would fall off.' (2)
'Whoever would apply the <s>hūṃ</s>-syllable while experiencing bliss,
through the union of the two organs, that one would experience suffering.' (3)

body.text:
huṃkāraṃ yaḥ prayuñjīta sarvāṅgena tu pīḍayan /
dvaye[ndriyasa]māpattyā tasya sarvatanuḥ pated // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
'Whoever would apply the <s>hūṃ</s>-syllable while pressing with all limbs,
through the union of the two organs, the entire body of that one would fall.' (4)

children.translated_text: Now, herein these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>huṃ aḥ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>huṃ jjaḥ</s>!
<s>huṃ hoḥ</s>!
<s>huṃ haṃ</s>!
Then one should teach the knowledge of the <s>Trilokavijaya</s> (Conqueror of the Three Worlds) great <s>maṇḍala</s> pledge-truth-<s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Through the application of the <s>vajradhātu</s>, one should be mindful of the <s>Buddha</s>;
whoever is [dedicated] to the benefit of beings, that one would attain <s>Buddha</s>hood.' (1)
'Having drawn <s>Maheśvara</s> and <s>Umā</s> on the ground and likewise trampled [upon them],
following the painting, one should establish the being-<s>mudrā</s>.' (2)
'By merely binding this [<s>mudrā</s>], one becomes the conqueror of the three worlds;
one swiftly becomes an accomplished <s>vidyādhara</s>, like the <s>vajra</s>-<s>hūṃ</s>-syllable.' (3)
'Standing in the midst of a flame-<s>maṇḍala</s>, following the painting,
through the <s>vajra</s>s of body, speech, and mind, one should bind the being-<s>mudrā</s>s.' (4)

body.text:
athāsāṃ karma vakṣyāmi vajrakarmamanuttaraṃ /
buddhānusmṛtisaṃsiddhaḥ śīghraṃ buddhatvamāpnuyād // iti // 5 //
body.translated_text:
'Now I shall teach the action of these — the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-action:
one accomplished through recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> would swiftly attain <s>Buddha</s>hood.' (5)

children.translated_text: 'Having bound the <s>Trilokavijaya</s> [<s>mudrā</s>], one becomes the conqueror of the three worlds;
having <s>vajra</s>-life, an all-goer, like the <s>vajra</s>-<s>hūṃ</s>-syllable.' (6)
'Through <s>vajra</s>-consecration, sovereignty — worldly lordship and the excellent <s>Dharma</s>-queen;
the great wrath of the action-<s>vajra</s>, one becomes a performer of <s>vajra</s>-action.' (7)
'Through the being-wrath, great fortitude; through the wrath-hook, summoning;
through wrath-passion, one enamors; through approbation-wrath, one grants satisfaction.' (8)
'Through <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>, one destroys everything; through sun-wrath, great radiance;
through banner-wrath, one seizes riches; through great laughter, one slays.' (9)
'Through <s>dharma</s>-wrath, one seizes <s>dharma</s>s; through the wrath-<s>vajra</s>, one cuts;
through cause-wrath, one removes sufferings; through wrath-speech, one seizes speech.' (10)

body.text:
karmakrodhā sukarmāṇi kuryād rakṣāṃ tu rakṣayā /
krodhayakṣā ripuṃ khādet krodhamuṣṭistu siddhidā // iti // 11 //
body.translated_text:
'Through action-wrath, good actions; one should make protection through the protector;
through <s>Yakṣa</s>-wrath, one devours enemies; through the wrath-fist, accomplishment is granted.' (11)
Now there is the binding of the <s>vajra</s>-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Arising from the double-<s>vajra</s>, the foremost pledges are proclaimed;
I shall teach the binding of those — the unsurpassed wrath-binding.' (1)
'Having established the arm-<s>vajra</s>, with the little-finger hooks bound,
the one named <s>Trilokavijaya</s> — with the two index fingers threatening.' (2)

body.text:
tathaivāgryā mukhāsaṃgānmaṇistu pravikuñcitā /
samotthamadhyapadmā tu madhyāgryadvayavarjite // ti // 3 //
body.translated_text:
'Likewise, with the tips joined at the tips, the jewel is curved;
with the middle [fingers] raised evenly as the lotus, without the tips of the two middle [fingers].' (3)

children.translated_text: 'The <s>vajra</s> of the two index fingers, with the right one curved as a hook;
that very one with the grasped <s>hūṃ</s>-syllable, and likewise the approbation [<s>mudrā</s>].' (4)
'With the two tips established as <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>, at the heart the foremost sun-<s>maṇḍala</s>;
with arms extended, at the crown, the index-finger-tip laughter.' (5)
'With the index-finger nails joined, the sheath-fist on the right;
with the evenly raised middle-tip wheel, issued forth from the mouth.' (6)

body.text:
tarjanīmadhyavajrā ca grīvā veṣṭitatarjanī /
agryādhikamahādaṃṣṭrā grastāgrā vajrā muṣṭine- //ti // 7 //
body.translated_text:
'The <s>vajra</s> of the index and middle [fingers], the neck with index finger wound around;
the supreme great fang, with grasped tips — the <s>vajra</s>-fist.' (7)

children.translated_text: 'The <s>mudrā</s>s of the joints of <s>Vajralāsyā</s> and the rest — those very ones with the <s>hūṃ</s>-syllable;

children.text: dharmamudrāstu tā eva huṃkāraiḥ sahitāḥ punaḥ // 8 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s are those very ones again, accompanied by <s>hūṃ</s>-syllables.' (8)

body.translated_text: Now there are the <s>vajra</s>-pledge-<s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>hūṃ</s>-syllable is from the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>vajra</s>; the <s>traḥ</s>-syllable from <s>Vajragarbha</s>;
the <s>hrīḥ</s>-syllable of <s>Vajrasena</s>; the <s>aḥ</s>-syllable of <s>Vajraviśva</s>.'

body.text: ataḥ paraṃ dharmamudrāḥ samāsata evaṃ bhavanti /
body.translated_text: From here onward, the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s are briefly thus:

body.text: huṃ heḥ trāṃ taṃ, hi hīḥ deḥ haḥ, dhik khīḥ hūṃ graṃ, kṛ vaṃ dṛ aḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>huṃ heḥ trāṃ taṃ, hi hīḥ deḥ haḥ, dhik khīḥ hūṃ graṃ, kṛ vaṃ dṛ aḥ</s> /
'The <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s are well-accomplished, of the host of <s>vajra</s>-wrath [deities].'
Then there are the <s>vajra</s>-pledge-action-<s>mudrā</s>s:

children.translated_text: 'Having made the wrath-fist twofold, through the yoga of <s>vajra</s>-pride and the rest,
the action-<s>mudrā</s>s are briefly known in the great <s>vajra</s>-family.' (1)
'Whatever <s>mudrā</s>, whatever side of the action,

children.text: tatra tatra tu vai veṣṭya tāṃ tāṃ mudrāṃ prayojayet // 2 //
children.translated_text: there in each case one should wrap and apply that respective <s>mudrā</s>.' (2)

body.translated_text: Procedure for all <s>mudrā</s>s.
Now herein there is the common <s>mudrā</s>-binding of the <s>Trilokavijaya</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>Trilokavijaya</s> <s>mudrā</s>, of the foremost <s>vajra</s>-pledge,
of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>hūṃ</s>-syllable <s>mantra</s>, grants all accomplishments instantly.' (1)
'With the little-finger-tip hooks one should bind, with two <s>vajra</s>s above and below;
this is the pledge-hook <s>mudrā</s> — it attracts everything instantly.' (2)
'Among all supreme <s>vidyā</s>s, <s>Trilokavijaya</s> is known;
she is the slayer of all, and likewise the performer of all actions.' (3)
'Having properly joined the tips of the two <s>vajra</s>-fingers, well-concentrated,
one would raise up all the dead — known as "<s>vajra</s>, arise!"' (4)
'Having properly bound the tips of the two <s>vajra</s>-fingers with the <s>vajra</s>-bond,
reversing and placing at the crown — it increases life and health.' (5)
the index finger firmly contracted, reversed — the foot-dragging [<s>mudrā</s>].' (6)

body.translated_text: 'Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-bond, with the thumbs inserted,

children.translated_text: 'Having bound the <s>Trilokavijaya</s> [<s>mudrā</s>], whichever image one tramples
with the left foot — that being is accomplished within a month or half.' (7)
'Having bound the <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s> twofold, one should strike [the two mudrās] against each other;

children.text: yasya vai rātvakāyaṃ tu samāviṣṭastu tāḍayet // 8 //
children.translated_text: whoever is a night-body (vampire), having been possessed, one should strike.' (8)

children.text: vajramudrādvikaṃ badhvā kavacaṃ svaṃ parasya vā /
children.translated_text: 'Having bound the <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s> twofold, as armor for oneself or another,

children.text: granthanan tarjanībhyāṃ tu rakṣā bhavatī śāśvatī // 9 //
children.translated_text: knotting with the index fingers — protection becomes eternal.' (9)
'Having made the <s>vajra</s>-bond at the palm, one should cover [the enemy] with a wrathful mind;
pressing firmly with the thumb-<s>vajra</s>, the great <s>vajra</s>-family is accomplished.' (10)
'Having made firm the <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajra</s>, with the two thumbs grasping the middle [fingers];
the little finger from the <s>vajra</s>-mouth, the sharp [<s>mudrā</s>] that is the pledge-grasping. // 11 //
Having bound the dual <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, with curved tips fastened,
making a rolling and unrolling [motion] — the supreme attraction of gods. // 12 //
Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-bond, with curved tips well-fastened,
joining the pair of thumbs, pressing in the middle — [the mudrā] of those in mid-air. // 13 //
The middle of the little fingers, within the dual <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>,
grasped by the foremost fingers from behind, reversed — [the mudrā] of those who move in space. // 14 //
Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-protection, one should press the <s>vajra</s>-bond —
this is the pledge of the terrestrial beings, the all-accomplishing, inviolable one. // 15 //
Having bound the dual <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, pressed by the tips of the left <s>vajra</s>[-finger],
snapped with the last fingers — this is the attractor from the netherworld. // 16 //
The pair of index fingers firmly knotted by the <s>vajra</s>-bond,
the <s>vajra</s> of the middle finger and thumb — the destroyer of wicked <s>mudrā</s>s. // 17 //
Having bound the non-dual <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, placing it at the heart with concentration,
one should press the wrathful fist — the destroyer of outer <s>maṇḍala</s>s. // 18 //
Grasping the left <s>vajra</s>-finger with the curved tip of the right,
snapping with great wrath, one could topple even Mount <s>Sumeru</s>. // 19 //
Grasping the left <s>vajra</s>-finger with the tip of the right index-hook,
attracting with great wrath, one brings all planetary spirits under power. // 20 //
Establishing the <s>vajra</s>-bond firmly at the heart with both arms,

children.text: vajrāgryābhyāṃ svakukṣau tu kuśaṃstu hṛdayaṃ hṛdi // 21 //
children.translated_text: with the <s>vajra</s>-tips at one's own belly, the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] as a tuft at the heart. // 21 //
With the mouths of the two foremost fingers, one should press with wrathful mind,
at the base of the pair of thumbs — the supreme attractor of fevers. // 22 //
Having made firm the <s>vajrāñjali</s> (vajra-salutation), with both index fingers curved,
with well-joined thumbs fastened — the remover of sins. // 23 //
Having bound the pair of foremost fingers from within the dual <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>,
one should instantly cast [them] upward — the supreme raiser of the fallen. // 24 //
Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-bond, with the mouth of the middle [fingers] joined,
by the contact of the mouths of the four last [fingers], one instantly bursts open sin. // 25 //

body.translated_text: Now the <s>mudrā</s>-binding for the accomplishment of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s is as follows:

children.translated_text: First stringing the <s>maṇḍala</s> with the cord, by means of grasping the <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>,

children.text: sūtraṃ tu dhārayetpaścāt yathāvat sūtraṇaṃ smṛtaṃ // 1 //
children.translated_text: one should then hold the cord — the proper stringing is thus remembered. // 1 //
With the well-joined tips of the dual <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>,
having made all the colors, one should invoke with blazing gaze. // 2 //

body.text:
dvivajrāgryāṅgulī samyak sandhāyottānato dṛḍhaṃ /
vivārayeta saṃkruddho dvāroddhāṭanamuttamam // iti // 3 //
body.translated_text: Properly joining the tips of both <s>vajra</s>-fingers, firmly upturned, one should open with great wrath — the supreme door-opening [<s>mudrā</s>]. Thus. // 3 //

children.translated_text: Now the accomplishment of all <s>mudrā</s>s of the entire <s>vajra</s>-family is as follows:
Assuming the <s>pratyālīḍha</s> (warrior) stance, uttering with wrathful voice,

children.text: krodhadṛṣṭyā tu saṃkruddhaḥ sarvakarmāṇi sādhayed // iti //
children.translated_text: with wrathful gaze and great anger, one should accomplish all activities. Thus.

body.translated_text: The elaboration of the procedure of the <s>Trilokavijaya</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>, from the great <s>kalpa</s>-king of the <s>vajra</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, is completed.

body.text:
CHAPTER 7 KRODHA-GUHYA-MUDRA-MANDALA-VIDHI-VISTARA
Emanation of deities form samadhi
body.translated_text:
CHAPTER 7: <s>KRODHA-GUHYA-MUDRĀ-MAṆḌALA-VIDHI-VISTARA</s>
Emanation of Deities from <s>Samādhi</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi vajradhāraṇīsamayasaṃbhavavajrādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ sarvavajriṇi vajramāte ānaya sarva vajrasatyena hūṃ jjaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>vajra</s> born from the pledge of <s>vajra</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s>,' spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: 'Oṃ! O all <s>vajriṇī</s>s, O <s>vajra</s>-mother, bring [them] all! By the truth of <s>vajra</s>! Hūṃ jaḥ!'

body.text: athāsyāṃ bhāṣitamātrāyāṃ vajrapāṇihṛdayātsa eva bhagavān vajrāpāṇiḥ vajrapāṇisadṛśasarvātmabhāvāḥ samantajvālāgarbhā vajrakrodhasamayamudrā devatā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvatathāgatārthān niṣpādya, bhagavato vajrasatvasya guhyabhāryatāpracchādanārtha kāyavākcittavajramudrābimbāni bhūtvā, bhagavato vairocanasya trilokavijayamahāmaṇḍalayogena candramaṇḍalāśritā bhūtvedamudānamudānayiṃsuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, the moment this was spoken, from the heart-<s>vajra</s> of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s> — self-forms resembling <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, with garlands of flames on all sides — having become wrathful <s>vajra</s>-pledge-<s>mudrā</s> deities and emerged, having accomplished the purposes of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s in all world-realms, and having become body, speech, and mind <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s> images for the purpose of concealing the secret consort-nature of <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>, stationed themselves on moon-discs through the yoga of the <s>Trilokavijaya</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, and uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Ah! The unsurpassed secret wisdom of all <s>Buddha</s>s,
for the sake of the bliss of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, they even assume consort-form! Thus.

body.translated_text: Hīḥ!
Delineation of the <s>Maṇḍala</s>
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having again spoken the [text] called 'the <s>vajra</s>-pledge secret of the <s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> of his own family pledge,'

children.translated_text: Now I shall fully explain the supreme <s>vajra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>Vajradhātu</s>, known as the 'wrathful secret.' // 1 //
By the method of the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should string the entire <s>maṇḍala</s>.
In the positions of the five <s>maṇḍala</s>s, one should install the secret <s>mudrā</s>s. // 2 //
In the center of this <s>vajra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should install the <s>Buddha</s>-image.
One who is wise should draw the wrathful pledges of the <s>Buddha</s> properly. // 3 //
Having emerged with <s>vajra</s>-speed to the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>,

children.text: tatra madhye likhet tiryak śūlavajraṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ // 4 //
children.translated_text: in the center there, one should draw a trident-<s>vajra</s> (<s>śūlavajra</s>) established crosswise. // 4 //
In the midst of the flames, one should draw in proper sequence

children.text: vajraṃ vajrāṅkuśaṃ caiva vāṇaṃ tuṣṭistathaiva ca // 5 //
children.translated_text: a <s>vajra</s>, a <s>vajra</s>-hook, an arrow, and satisfaction likewise. // 5 //
Having entered with <s>vajra</s>-speed the second supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>,
one should draw the <s>vajra</s>-jewel, established in the center of the wheel. // 6 //
In the center [draw] the <s>vajra</s>-frown (<s>vajrabhṛkuṭi</s>), the <s>vajra</s>-sun, and likewise the banner,
and the row of teeth — one should draw these <s>vajra</s>s on the sides. // 7 //
Having entered with <s>vajra</s>-speed the third supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>,
one should draw the divine <s>vajra</s>-lotus, established in the center of the lotus. // 8 //
In the midst of the flames one should draw a lotus, a sword, and likewise a wheel,

children.text: vajrajivhāṃ yathāvat tu tasyāḥ pārśveṣu sa[rveṣu // 9 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>vajra</s>-tongue properly, on all sides of that. // 9 //
Having entered with <s>vajra</s>-speed the fourth supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>,
on a crossed <s>vajra</s> one should draw a <s>vajra</s> surrounded by greatly radiant <s>vajra</s>s. // 10 //
On all its sides, with splendor bristling with all flames,
one should draw a <s>viśvavajra</s>, an excellent armor, a <s>vajra</s>-fang, and a fist. // 11 //
In the corners of the outer positions, one should draw properly.
Hereafter I shall teach the <s>mudrā</s>-<s>vidyā</s>s in brief. // 12 //

body.translated_text: Siḥ!
Oṃ! <s>vajrakrodhasamaye</s> siḥ!
Oṃ! <s>vajraroṣāṅkuśī</s>, bring all! Siḥ!

body.text: oṃ vajraroṣe kāmavajriṇi vaśaṃ me ānaya hi siḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ! <s>vajraroṣe</s>! O <s>kāmavajriṇī</s>, bring [them] under my power! Siḥ!
Oṃ! <s>vajratuṣṭikrodhe</s>, satisfy all! Siḥ!
<s>Vajra</s>-siṃkāra-<s>maṇḍala</s>.
Jiḥ!
Oṃ! <s>vajrabhṛkuṭikrodhe</s>, seize all purposes! Jiḥ!

body.text: oṃ vajrajvālāmālaprabhe mahākrodhā[gni jvālaya sarva viroṣe jiḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ! <s>vajrajvālāmālaprabhe</s>, great wrathful one, blaze with fire and burn all, O <s>viroṣe</s>! Jiḥ!

body.text: oṃ vajra]dhvajāgrakeyūramahākrodhe dehi me sarvaṃ jiḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ! <s>vajradhvajāgrakeyūramahākrodhe</s>, give me all! Jiḥ!
Oṃ! <s>vajrāṭṭahāsanī</s>, laugh with the great burst of terrifying laughter — slay! Jiḥ!
<s>Vajra</s>-jiṃkāra-<s>maṇḍala</s>.
Diḥ!

body.text: oṃ vajraśuddhakrodhe hana māraya duṣṭān diḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ! <s>vajraśuddhakrodhe</s>, strike and slay the wicked! Diḥ!
Oṃ! <s>vajratīkṣṇakrodhe</s>, cut all with the <s>vajra</s>-sheath! Diḥ!

body.text: oṃ [vajrahetumahā krodhe praveśa cakra praveśaya sarvān] diḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ! <s>vajrahetumahākrodhe</s>, enter — cause the wheel to enter all! Diḥ!

body.text: oṃ vajrajivhe mahākrodhabhāṣe vācaṃ muñca diḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ! <s>vajrajivhe mahākrodhabhāṣe</s>, release speech! Diḥ!
<s>Vajra</s>-diṃkāra-<s>maṇḍala</s>.
Nhiḥ!

body.text: oṃ sarva mukhe [karmavajriṇi mahākrodhe kuru sarvān nhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ! <s>sarvamukhe karmavajriṇī mahākrodhe</s>, accomplish all! Nhiḥ!

body.text: oṃ vajra] kavacakrodhe rakṣa māṃ nhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ! <s>vajrakavacakrodhe</s>, protect me! Nhiḥ!

body.text: oṃ vajracaṇḍakrodhe mahāyakṣiṇi vajradaṃṣṭrākarālabhīṣaṇi bhīṣā[paya nhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ! <s>vajracaṇḍakrodhe mahāyakṣiṇī vajradaṃṣṭrākarālabhīṣaṇī</s>, terrify! Nhiḥ!
Oṃ! <s>vajrakrodhe muṣṭibandha</s>! Nhiḥ!
<s>Vajra</s>-nhiṃkāra-<s>maṇḍala</s>.

children.translated_text: Then in the corner <s>maṇḍala</s>s, the <s>vidyā</s>-heart[-mantra]s of the secret <s>vajra</s>-dance offering are:
<s>vajra</s> hūṃ rkhne!

body.translated_text: <s>vajra</s> hūṃ ghūṃ!
<s>vajra</s> hūṃ rte!
<s>vajra</s> hūṃ steṃ!

children.translated_text: In the outer corners, the heart[-mantra]s of the musical offering are:
<s>vajra</s> tī te!

body.translated_text: <s>vajra</s> ṭaṃ ṭaḥ!
<s>vajra</s> dhā dhū!
<s>vajra</s> dhau dhaḥ!

children.translated_text: The offering-heart[-mantra]s of the door-guardians are:
<s>vajra</s> jaḥ jjaḥ!

body.translated_text: <s>vajra</s> hūṃ hūṃ!
<s>vajra</s> vaṃ vaṃ!
<s>vajra</s> aḥ aḥ!
Initiation into the <s>Maṇḍala</s>

body.text: athāsmin vajrakulaguhyamaṇḍale praveśavidhivistaro bhavati / tatrādita eva tāvat trilokavijayamahāmaṇḍalapraveśavidhinā praviśya, vajraguhyavajrakulasamayamudrāpratimudropamudrājñānamudrābhiḥ vajradharapūjārtha nṛtyopahāraḥ kartavya iti /
body.translated_text: Now the elaboration of the procedure for entry into this <s>vajra</s>-family secret <s>maṇḍala</s> is as follows. Therein, first one should enter by the procedure of entry into the <s>Trilokavijaya</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>, and the offering of dance should be performed for the purpose of worshipping <s>Vajradhara</s> with the pledge-<s>mudrā</s>, counter-<s>mudrā</s>, sub-<s>mudrā</s>, and wisdom-<s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-secret <s>vajra</s>-family pledge.

body.text: tatredaṃ nṛtyapratinṛtyopanṛtyajñānanṛtyopahāramudrājñānaṃ bhavati / [tatrādita eva vajradhātusaṃgrahahṛdayaṃ vajragītena gāyan sarvatathāgatānāṃ stotropahāraṅkṛtvā, vajrācāryeṇa satvavajrimudrā sphoṭayitavyā, tato yathā pra[viṣṭa]mudrābhiḥ samāviśanti /
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge of the offering of dance, counter-dance, sub-dance, and wisdom-dance. Therein, first, singing with the <s>vajra</s>-song the heart[-mantra] of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> collection, having made the offering of praise to all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the <s>vajrācārya</s> should snap the <s>Sattvavajrī</s>-<s>mudrā</s>. Then, through the <s>mudrā</s>s [appropriate to] how one entered, [the deities] enter.

children.translated_text: By the application of <s>vajra</s>-dance, the pair of wrathful <s>vajra</s>-fingers —
one should bind the <s>vajra</s>-huṃkāra-<s>mudrā</s> at the heart. // 1 //
Then, by the procedure of dance, with the wrathful <s>vajra</s>-hook,
attracting all <s>Buddha</s>s, one should hurl the <s>vajra</s>-arrow. // 2 //
By hurling the <s>vajra</s>-arrow, one should accomplish with <s>vajra</s>-satisfaction.
Having released the <s>mudrā</s> according to the rite, one should bind with the clap. // 3 //
By this offering procedure, one should satisfy <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>.

children.text: tuṣṭaḥ sat sarvakāryāṇi sādhayed rucitaḥ kṣaṇāt // 4 //
children.translated_text: When satisfied, he accomplishes all tasks instantly, with pleasure. // 4 //
Therein, these are the dance heart[-mantra]s:
<s>siddhya vajra</s>! (Accomplish, O <s>vajra</s>!)

body.translated_text: <s>ānaya vajra</s>! (Bring, O <s>vajra</s>!)
<s>rāgaya vajra</s>! (Enamor, O <s>vajra</s>!)
<s>sādhu vajra</s>! (Well done, O <s>vajra</s>!)
Then the counter-dance offering should be performed:

children.text: tathaiva nṛtyan vāmāṃ tu gṛhya dakṣiṇamuṣṭinā /
children.translated_text: Dancing in the same manner, grasping the left with the right fist,

children.text: parivartya lalāṭo tu niveśyāgryā mukhena tu // 1 //
children.translated_text: reversing at the forehead, placing with the tip of the mouth — // 1 //
dancing in the same manner, reversing the sun, one should invoke.
Having cast up the <s>vajra</s>-banner, one should laugh with the <s>vajra</s>-terrifying-laughter. // 2 //
By this offering procedure, [one tames] kings and all humans,
and through mastery, great splendor, generosity, and hope, one should satisfy [them]. // 3 //
Therein, these are the counter-<s>mudrā</s> heart[-mantra]s:
<s>āhi vajra</s>! (Approach, O <s>vajra</s>!)

body.translated_text: <s>jvālaya vajra</s>! (Blaze, O <s>vajra</s>!)
<s>dehi vajra</s>! (Give, O <s>vajra</s>!)
<s>hasa hasa vajra</s>! (Laugh, laugh, O <s>vajra</s>!)

children.translated_text: Dancing in the same manner, having released, with evenly cupped hands joined,
placing the foremost fingers at the heart, with salutations shaking the mind. // 1 //

children.text: tathaiva nṛtyaṃ chinded vai vajrakośena nāśakān /
children.translated_text: Dancing in the same manner, one should cut the destroyers with the <s>vajra</s>-sheath,
and whirl the wheel-<s>maṇḍala</s> with the rotation of a fire-wheel. // 2 //

children.text: gāyan vai vajravācā tu pūjayed vajrapāṇinaṃ /
children.translated_text: Singing with the <s>vajra</s>-voice, one should worship <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>.
By this offering procedure, all becomes eternal. // 3 //

body.translated_text: Therein, these are the sub-<s>mudrā</s> heart[-mantra]s:
<s>kāmaya vajra</s>! (Desire, O <s>vajra</s>!)
<s>cchindaya vajra</s>! (Cut, O <s>vajra</s>!)
<s>bhrāmaya vajra</s>! (Whirl, O <s>vajra</s>!)
<s>brūhi vajra</s>! (Speak, O <s>vajra</s>!)

children.translated_text: The wrathful <s>vajra</s>-fingers properly, with mouths turned upward and joined,
reversed at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>, the index finger stationed at the mouth. // 1 //
By the application of <s>vajra</s>-activity, the foremost <s>maṇḍala</s> of all tasks,
displaying by the procedure of dance, one should pacify at the heart. // 2 //
By the same dance procedure, one should bind the <s>vajra</s>-protection,
establishing the <s>vajra</s>-fangs, one should press with the <s>vajra</s>-fist. // 3 //

body.text:
anena pūjāvidhinā sarvakarmakṣamo bhavet /
kṛtvā caturvidhāṃ pūjāṃ mudrāṃ muñced yathāvidhir // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text: By this offering procedure, one becomes capable of all activities. Having performed the fourfold offering, one should release the <s>mudrā</s> according to the rite. Thus. // 4 //

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart[-mantra]s:
<s>nṛtya vajra</s>! (Dance, O <s>vajra</s>!)

body.translated_text: <s>rakṣa vajra</s>! (Protect, O <s>vajra</s>!)
<s>khāda vajra</s>! (Devour, O <s>vajra</s>!)
<s>bandha vajra</s>! (Bind, O <s>vajra</s>!)
Then one should learn the wrathful secret <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.text: vajraṃ gṛhya tu pāṇibhyāṃ sphoṭayet kruddhamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Taking the <s>vajra</s> in both hands, one should snap [it] with wrathful mind —

children.text: yasya nāmnā tu hṛdayaṃ sphuṭet tasya janasya hi // 1 //
children.translated_text: the heart of that person in whose name [it is snapped] would burst open. // 1 //

children.text: adhoṣṭhaṃ daśanairgṛhya yasya nāmnā tu pīḍayet /
children.translated_text: Biting the lower lip with the teeth, pressing in the name of whomever,
that person's head would quickly burst open, should they transgress the command. // 2 //
With the great wrathful <s>vajra</s>-gaze, one should close the eyes;

children.text: nirīkṣat yasya nāmnā tu sphuṭet etasya cākṣiṇī // 3 //
children.translated_text: looking at whomever by name, that one's eyes will burst open. (3)

body.text:
vajrakrodhasamāpattyā hṛdayaṃ svayamātmanā /
pīḍayed vajrabandhena tasya cittaṃ parisphuṭed // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Through the wrathful <s>vajra</s>-<s>samāpatti</s>, one's own heart
one should squeeze with the <s>vajra</s>-binding — that one's mind will burst apart. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart [-mantras]:
<s>huṃ vajrasphoṭa ṭhaḥ</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>huṃ mukhavajra ṭhaḥ</s>!
<s>huṃ vajranetra ṭhaḥ</s>!
<s>huṃ manovajra ṭhaḥ</s>!

body.text: tato mahāvajrakulaguhyamudrājñānaṃ śikṣayet / tatra prathamaṃ tāvanmahāmudrābandho bhavati /
body.translated_text: Then one should teach the great <s>vajra</s>-family secret-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge. Therein, first there is the binding of the great <s>mudrā</s>s:

children.translated_text: With the hook-binding of the little fingers, one should arrange the wrathful <s>vajra</s>s;
on the back of the left trident — this is known as <s>Trailokyavijayā</s>. (1)

body.text:
suprasāritavāmāgryā tathaivottānavārijā /
parivartya tathā caiva vāmavajrā pratiṣṭhite // ti // 2 //
body.translated_text:
With well-extended left foremost [finger], and likewise with the back of the left [hand] raised,
and having likewise reversed — [this is] established with the left <s>vajra</s>. (2)

children.translated_text: Having made the <s>vajra</s>-binding at the base, one should cover with an angry mind;
tightly, with the thumb-<s>vajra</s> — this is known as <s>Krodhaterintirī</s>. (3)
With curved-tip hooks and with the index-finger-mouth <s>vajriṇī</s>;
the exclamation-of-'well-done' with the foremost [fingers], and the foremost <s>vajra</s> placed at the mouth. (4)
At the heart, resembling the sun; with the foremost [fingers] joined, placed at the crown;

children.text: parivartya smitasthā tu samāgryā kuḍmalā tathā // 5 //
children.translated_text: having reversed, placed with a smile; and with the foremost [fingers] joined in a bud. (5)
With the two [hands in] sword-fist grip, the foremost [fingers] as wheel — the binding;
with the foremost [fingers] joined, raised from the mouth, the index finger extended. (6)

body.text:
tarjanī gale bandhā tu tābhyāṃ daṃṣṭrā mukhasthitā /
gāḍhamuṣṭinibandhāśca mahāmudrāḥ prakalpitā // 7 // iti //
body.translated_text:
The index finger bound at the throat; by those two, fangs placed at the mouth;
and with tightly bound fists — the great <s>mudrā</s>s are thus arranged. (7)
Now the binding of the <s>vajra</s>-family secret-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>s is [as follows]:

children.translated_text: Born from the secret fist, they are proclaimed as the foremost pledges;
their binding I shall explain — the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-binding. (1)

children.text: hṛdisthā valitā pārśve vāṇākarṣā tu vāmataḥ /
children.translated_text: Placed at the heart, rotated to the side; the arrow-attraction to the left;
and raised from the heart, the frown — having indeed reversed. (2)
Resembling the sun-disc, with arms extended at the crown;
having reversed, placed with a smile, well-positioned at the center of the face. (3)
With the appearance of striking with the tip of the sheath; showing the casting of the wheel;
and raised from the mouth, with the body-foremost disc at the crown. (4)
At the shoulders, at the heart, at the sides — the <s>vajra</s>-protection posture;
and through the positioning of the fangs, tightly squeezed with the fist. (5)

body.text:
bāhyamaṇḍalamudrāstu bandheccihnānusārataḥ /
samayā vajrabandhena tathāsyā vajramuṣṭinā // 6 // iti //
body.translated_text:
The outer <s>maṇḍala</s> <s>mudrā</s>s should be bound following the emblems;
the pledge [mudrās], with the <s>vajra</s>-binding and also with the <s>vajra</s>-fist. (6)

body.text:
atha vajrakulaguhyadharmamudrā bhavanti /
pha ṭṭaḥ / śa ṭṭaḥ / ma ṭṭaḥ / sa ṭṭaḥ /
ra ṭṭaḥ / ta ṭṭaḥ / ghṛ ṭṭaḥ / ha ṭṭaḥ /
pa ṭṭaḥ / tra ṭṭaḥ / ka ṭṭaḥ / dha ṭṭaḥ /
ku ṭṭaḥ / ri ṭṭaḥ / kha ṭṭaḥ / va ṭṭaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Now the <s>vajra</s>-family secret-<s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s are:
<s>pha ṭṭaḥ / śa ṭṭaḥ / ma ṭṭaḥ / sa ṭṭaḥ /
ra ṭṭaḥ / ta ṭṭaḥ / ghṛ ṭṭaḥ / ha ṭṭaḥ /
pa ṭṭaḥ / tra ṭṭaḥ / ka ṭṭaḥ / dha ṭṭaḥ /
ku ṭṭaḥ / ri ṭṭaḥ / kha ṭṭaḥ / va ṭṭaḥ</s>!

children.translated_text: Now the binding of the <s>vajra</s>-family secret-activity-<s>mudrā</s>s is [as follows]:
The activity-<s>mudrā</s>s are, in brief, the <s>vajra</s>-fist divided in two;

children.text: yathā sthāneṣu saṃstheyā krodhaduṣṭyā suroṣavān // iti //
children.translated_text: they should be placed in their respective positions, very wrathful, with the wrathful gaze.

body.translated_text: From the <s>Sarvatathāgatavajrasamaya</s> (Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s), the great ritual king — the extensive rite of the wrathful-secret-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> is completed.
CHAPTER 8 — EXTENSIVE RITE OF THE <s>VAJRA</s>-FAMILY-<s>DHARMA</s>-KNOWLEDGE-PLEDGE-<s>MAṆḌALA</s>
Emanation of deities from <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatavajrakulasamādhijñānamudrādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ savidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgatasūkṣmavajrakrodha hūṃ phaṭ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom-<s>mudrā</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-family of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this supreme <s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ sarvatathāgatasūkṣmavajrakrodha hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahākrodharājā trilokavijayasūkṣmavajravidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sūkṣmavajrakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great wrathful king, uttered this supreme <s>Trailokyavijaya</s> subtle-<s>vajra</s> <s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ sūkṣmavajrakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajragarbho [bodhi]satva imaṃ trilokavijayasūkṣmavajravidyottamabhāṣat oṃ sūkṣmavajraratnākrama hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajragarbha</s> uttered this supreme <s>Trailokyavijaya</s> subtle-<s>vajra</s> <s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ sūkṣmavajraratnākrama hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajranetro bodhisatva imaṃ trilokavijayasūkṣmavajravidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sūkṣmavajrapadmakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajranetra</s> uttered this supreme <s>Trailokyavijaya</s> subtle-<s>vajra</s> <s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ sūkṣmavajrapadmakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajraviśvo bodhisatva imaṃ trilokavijayasūkṣmavajravidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sūkṣmavajrakarmakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajraviśva</s> uttered this supreme <s>Trailokyavijaya</s> subtle-<s>vajra</s> <s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ sūkṣmavajrakarmakrodhākrama hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ punarapi svakulamutsādya, vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalayogena sanniveśyaitāni svahṛdayānyabhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>, having again brought forth his own family and arranged them by the method of the <s>vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>, uttered these heart [-mantras] of his own:

body.text: oṃ vajrasatva sūkṣmajñāna krodha hūṃ phaṭ // 1 //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajrasatva sūkṣmajñāna krodha hūṃ phaṭ</s>! (1)
<s>oṃ sūkṣmavajrāṅkuśākarṣaya mahākrodha hūṃ phaṭ</s>! (2)
<s>oṃ vajrasūkṣmarāgakrodhānurāgaya tīvraṃ hūṃ phaṭ</s>! (3)
<s>oṃ sūkṣmavajratuṣṭikrodha hūṃ phaṭ</s>! (4)

body.text: oṃ sūkṣmavajrabhṛkuṭikrodha hara hara hūṃ phaṭ // 5 //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ sūkṣmavajrabhṛkuṭikrodha hara hara hūṃ phaṭ</s>! (5)

body.text: oṃ vajrasūkṣmajvālāmaṇḍalakrodha sūrya jvālaya hūṃ phaṭ // 6 //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajrasūkṣmajvālāmaṇḍalakrodha sūrya jvālaya hūṃ phaṭ</s>! (6)

body.text: oṃ sūkṣmavajradhvajāgrakrodha sarvārthān me prayaccha śīghraṃ hūṃ phaṭ // 7 //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ sūkṣmavajradhvajāgrakrodha sarvārthān me prayaccha śīghraṃ hūṃ phaṭ</s>! (7)

body.text: oṃ vajrasūkṣmahāsakrodha ha ha ha ha hūṃ phaṭ // 8 //
body.translated_text: <s>oṃ vajrasūkṣmahāsakrodha ha ha ha ha hūṃ phaṭ</s>! (8)
