body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>vajra</s> born from the <s>dharma</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: 'Oṃ <s>vajra vit</s>!'

body.text: atha vajrāpāṇiḥ punarapīdaṃ svadharmasamayamabhāṣat oṃ hana hana hu phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> again spoke his own <s>dharma</s>-pledge: 'Oṃ hana hana hūṃ phaṭ!'

body.text: atha vajragarbhaḥ svadharmasamayamabhāṣat oṃ hara hara huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajragarbha</s> spoke his own <s>dharma</s>-pledge: 'Oṃ hara hara hūṃ phaṭ!'

body.text: atha vajranetraḥ svadharmasamayamabhāṣat oṃ mara mara huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajranetra</s> spoke his own <s>dharma</s>-pledge: 'Oṃ mara mara hūṃ phaṭ!'

body.text: atha vajraviśvaḥ svadharmasamayamabhāṣat oṃ kuru kuru huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajraviśva</s> spoke his own <s>dharma</s>-pledge: 'Oṃ kuru kuru hūṃ phaṭ!'

body.text: atha vajravidyottamaḥ svadharmasamayamabhāṣat oṃ huṃ huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajravidyottama</s> spoke his own <s>dharma</s>-pledge: 'Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ!'

body.text: atha māyāvajra uvāca oṃ cchinda cchinda huṃ phaṭ // oṃ āviśāviśa huṃ phaṭ // oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ sva huṃ phaṭ // oṃ bhinda bhinda huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Māyāvajra</s> said: 'Oṃ cchinda cchinda hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ āviśa āviśa hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ bhinda bhinda hūṃ phaṭ!'
<s>Vidyā</s>-king [-mantras].
'Oṃ dama dama hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ māraya māraya hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ ghātaya ghātaya hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ bhaya bhaya hūṃ phaṭ!'
Wrathful ones.
'Oṃ mada mada hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ bandha bandha hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ vaśībhava hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ jaya jaya hūṃ phaṭ!'
Retinue-lords.
'Oṃ bhyo bhyo hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ ghu ghu hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ jvala jvala hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ khāda khāda hūṃ phaṭ!'
Messengers.
'Oṃ khana khana hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ mara mara hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ vibha vibha hūṃ phaṭ!'
Servants.
Delineation of the <s>Maṇḍala</s>
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> again spoke this <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>dharma</s>-pledge of all <s>vajra</s>-families:

children.translated_text: Now I shall fully explain the supreme great <s>maṇḍala</s>.
One should draw the entire <s>maṇḍala</s>, resembling the <s>Trilokacakra</s>. // 1 //
All having entered <s>samādhi</s> — <s>Buddha Vajradhara</s> and the rest —
by the method of the <s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should draw the heart-symbols.

body.translated_text: Initiation into the <s>Maṇḍala</s>

body.text: athātra [dharmasamaya]maṇḍale yathāvatkarma kṛtvā, vajradhārimudrāṃsu vajraghaṇṭāṃ [baddhaṃ badhyai]vaṃ bruyāt "na tvayā kasyacidasamayadṛṣṭasyādṛṣṭadevakulasya vaktavyam" iti uktvā, tāṃ ghaṇṭāṃ raṇāpayet evaṃ ca brūyāt, śapathahṛdayaṃ datvā /
body.translated_text: Now in this <s>dharma</s>-pledge <s>maṇḍala</s>, having performed the rites properly, having bound the <s>vajra</s>-bell in the <s>vajra</s>-bearer <s>mudrā</s>, one should say thus: 'You must not speak to anyone who has not seen the pledge, about the deity-family that has not been seen.' Having said this, one should ring that bell and speak thus, giving the oath heart[-mantra]:

children.translated_text: Just as this bell has been rung and as this sound is certain,

children.text: tathedaṃ karmavajraṃ te nāśaṃ kuryattathā dhruvaṃ // 1 //
children.translated_text: so too this activity-<s>vajra</s> of yours would certainly effect destruction — // 1 //

body.text:
vajrācāryatvagauravyaṃ vajrasrātṛṣvamitratā /
duṣṭamaitrīvirāsaśca yadi kuryādbhavān kadā // iti // 2 //
body.translated_text: if you should ever act with disrespect toward the <s>vajrācārya</s>, enmity toward <s>vajra</s>-brothers, or wicked friendliness. Thus. // 2 //
<s>Mudrā</s>

body.text: tato mukhabandhaṃ muktvā, maṇḍalaṃ darśya, dharmasamayamudrājñānaṃ śikṣayet /
body.translated_text: Then, having released the mouth-seal, having shown the <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should teach the <s>dharma</s>-pledge <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge.

body.text: Samadhis of Vidyaraja, Vajrakrodha, Gana, Duta and Ceta
body.translated_text: <s>Samādhi</s>s of <s>Vidyārāja</s>, <s>Vajrakrodha</s>, <s>Gaṇa</s>, <s>Dūta</s>, and <s>Ceṭa</s>

children.translated_text: Of <s>Buddha Vajradhara</s> and the rest, in the <s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> properly,
the meditation of the supreme <s>vajra</s>-<s>vidyā</s> is indeed the equality of all. // 1 //

body.text:
māyopamaṃ jagadidaṃ duḥkhaṃ gaṇṭhopamaṃ tathā /
nirvāṇaṃ sarvaduḥkhānāṃ vajraṃ bhediṣvanuttaram // iti // 2 //
body.translated_text: This world is like an illusion (<s>māyopama</s>); suffering is like a lump. <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s> that shatters all suffering. Thus. // 2 //
<s>Vidyā</s>-king <s>samādhi</s>s.

children.translated_text: Wrath is foremost in disciplining beings; gentleness is certainly slaying.

children.text: daṇḍāt samo na nirghāto mithyādṛṣṭirbhayaṃkaraḥ // iti //
children.translated_text: There is no punishment equal to the staff; false views are fear-making. Thus.

body.translated_text: <s>Vajra</s>-wrathful <s>samādhi</s>s.

children.translated_text: There is no fortitude equal to intoxication; there is no binding equal to the garland.

children.text: striyo hi rāgo jagadvaśaṃkaraḥ dhairyamātrā parājitā // iti //
children.translated_text: Passion for women is the subjugator of the world; fortitude alone is defeated. Thus.

body.translated_text: Retinue <s>samādhi</s>s.

children.text: prahāro nigrahāgrayo hi sparśānāṃ tu samīraṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Striking is the foremost of restraints; among touches, wind is the stirrer.

children.text: tejasāṃ hutabhug jyeṣṭhaḥ bhojanānāṃ tu lohitam // iti //
children.translated_text: Among radiances, fire is the chief; among foods, blood. Thus.

body.translated_text: Messenger <s>samādhi</s>s.

children.text: daṃṣṭrā śuddhaḥ praviṣṭastu mṛtyuḥ sarva pade sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fang is pure; having entered, death is established in every step.

children.text: bhayāttulyo na vighnāsti jalāttulyo na vai rasa // iti //
children.translated_text: There is no obstacle equal to fear; there is no taste equal to water. Thus.

body.translated_text: Servant <s>samādhi</s>s.

The elaboration of the procedure of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>dharma</s>-pledge of all <s>vajra</s>-families, from the great <s>kalpa</s>-king of the <s>vajra</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, is completed.
CHAPTER 14: <s>SARVA-VAJRA-KULA-KARMA-MAṆḌALA-VIDHI-VISTARA</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatakarmasamayodbhavavajrādhiṣṭhānannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavi[dyottamāmabhāṣat / oṃ vajra] karmapravartani samaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment of the <s>vajra</s> born from the activity-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: 'Oṃ <s>vajra karmapravartani samaye</s> hūṃ!'

body.text:
atha vajrapāṇiḥ punarapi svakarmottamamabhāṣat [oṃ vajravilāse pūjaya hūṃ //]
atha vajagarbhaḥ svakarmottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajrābhiṣeke 'bhiṣiñce hūṃ //
body.translated_text:
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> again uttered his own supreme activity [-mantra]: <s>oṃ vajravilāse pūjaya hūṃ</s>!
Then <s>Vajragarbha</s> uttered his own supreme activity [-mantra]: <s>oṃ vajrābhiṣeke 'bhiṣiñce hūṃ</s>!

body.text:
atha vajranetraḥ svakarmottamamabhāṣa[t oṃ vajragīte gāhi hūṃ //]
atha vajraviśvo bodhisatvaḥ svakarmavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajranṛtye nṛtya hūṃ //
body.translated_text:
Then <s>Vajranetra</s> uttered his own supreme activity [-mantra]: <s>oṃ vajragīte gāhi hūṃ</s>!
Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajraviśva</s> uttered his own supreme activity-<s>vidyā</s>: <s>oṃ vajranṛtye nṛtya hūṃ</s>!

body.text: atha vajravidyottama [imāṃ svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat] oṃ vajravidyottama nṛtya nṛtya vikurva vikurva huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajravidyottama</s> (the Supreme <s>Vidyā</s>) uttered this, her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajravidyottama nṛtya nṛtya vikurva vikurva hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrakrodhavajrāgni mahādevīmāṃ svakarmasama[yāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrakrodha] vajrāgne jvālaya triśūlaṃ bhinda hṛdayaṃ vajreṇa hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrakrodhavajrāgni</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Wrath-<s>Vajra</s>-Fire), the great goddess, uttered this, her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajrakrodha vajrāgne jvālaya triśūlaṃ bhinda hṛdayaṃ vajreṇa hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrahemā mahādevīmāṃ svakarmasaṃmayāmabhāṣat [oṃ vajraheme cchinda cakreṇa] vajriṇi hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrahemā</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Golden), the great goddess, uttered this, her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajraheme cchinda cakreṇa vajriṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrakaumārīmāṃ svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrakaumārī śīghramāveśaya ghaṇ[ṭāśabdena] vajrapāṇipriye vajrasamayamanusmara raṇa raṇa hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrakaumārī</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Virgin) uttered this, her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajrakaumārī śīghramāveśaya ghaṇṭāśabdena vajrapāṇipriye vajrasamayamanusmara raṇa raṇa hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajraśāntirmahādevīmāṃ svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajraśā[nta japa ja]pākṣamālayā sarvān māraya śānta dṛṣṭyā hūṃ phaṭ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajraśānti</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Peace), the great goddess, uttered this, her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajraśānta japa japākṣamālayā sarvān māraya śānta dṛṣṭyā hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajramuṣṭirmahādevīmāṃ svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajramuṣṭi [hana hana] vajreṇa bhinda bhinda pīḍaya pīḍaya sarvaduṣṭahṛdayāni oṃ suṃbha nisuṃbha hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajramuṣṭi</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Fist), the great goddess, uttered this, her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajramuṣṭi hana hana vajreṇa bhinda bhinda pīḍaya pīḍaya sarvaduṣṭahṛdayāni oṃ suṃbha nisuṃbha hūṃ phaṭ</s>!
These are the <s>vidyā</s>-queens (<s>vidyārājanikā</s>).

body.text: atha [vajrāmṛtakrodhā imāṃ svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrāmṛte sarvaduṣṭān gṛhṇa bandha hana paca vidhvaṃsaya vināśaya bhinda cchinda bhasmīkuru mūrdhantānuya [vajreṇa ye ketumamamukasya] vidhnavināyakāstān dāmaya dīptakrodhavajriṇi hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrāmṛtakrodhā</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Nectar-Wrath) uttered this, her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajrāmṛte sarvaduṣṭān gṛhṇa bandha hana paca vidhvaṃsaya vināśaya bhinda cchinda bhasmīkuru mūrdhantānuya vajreṇa ye ketumamamukasya vidhnavināyakāstān dāmaya dīptakrodhavajriṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrakāntiḥ svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrakānti mā[raya saumyarūpe pra]dīptarāgeṇa śīghraṃ sphoṭaya hṛdayaṃ vajradharasatyena mahājyotsnākarāle śītaraśmivajriṇi hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrakānti</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Beauty) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajrakānti māraya saumyarūpe pradīptarāgeṇa śīghraṃ sphoṭaya hṛdayaṃ vajradharasatyena mahājyotsnākarāle śītaraśmivajriṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajradaṇḍāgrā svakarmasa[mayāmabhāṣat] oṃ vajradaṇḍāgre ghātaya huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajradaṇḍāgrā</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Staff-Tip) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajradaṇḍāgre ghātaya hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajramekhalā mahākrodhā imāṃ svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajramekhale kha[na khana śabdena vaśīku]ru duṣṭyā māraya bhīṣaṇi hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajramekhalā</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Girdle), the great wrathful one, uttered this, her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajramekhale khana khana śabdena vaśīkuru duṣṭyā māraya bhīṣaṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!
These are the wrathful <s>vidyā</s>s (<s>krodhavidyā</s>).

body.text: athavajravilayā svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajravi[laye cchinda sina bhinda va]jriṇī mādayonmādaya piva piva hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajravilayā</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Dissolution) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajravilaye cchinda sina bhinda vajriṇī mādayonmādaya piva piva hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrāśanā svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrāśane bha[kṣaya sarvaduṣṭān vajradaśani śaktidhāri]ṇi mānuṣamāṃsāhāre nararucirāśubhapriye majjavasānulepanaviliptagātre ānaya sarvadhanadhānyahiraṇyasuva[rṇādīni saṃkrāmaya baladevarakṣi]ṇi hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrāśanā</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Devourer) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajrāśane bhakṣaya sarvaduṣṭān vajradaśani śaktidhāriṇi mānuṣamāṃsāhāre nararucirāśubhapriye majjavasānulepanaviliptagātre ānaya sarvadhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇādīni saṃkrāmaya baladevarakṣiṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajravasanā svakarmasamayamabhāṣat oṃ vajravasane ānaya sarvavastrānnapānādyu pa[karaṇāni śīghraṃ vaśīkuru enaṃ] me prayacchāviśāviśa satyaṃ kathaya vajrakośadhāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajravasanā</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Garment) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajravasane ānaya sarvavastrānnapānādyupakaraṇāni śīghraṃ vaśīkuru enaṃ me prayacchāviśāviśa satyaṃ kathaya vajrakośadhāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajravaśī svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ [vajravaśī ānaya vaśīkuru sarvastriya] sarvapuruṣān dāsīkuru ṛddhān prasādaya vyavahārebhyo 'pyuttāraya vijayakari vajrapatākādhāriṇi huṃ [phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajravaśī</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Subjugation) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajravaśī ānaya vaśīkuru sarvastriyaḥ sarvapuruṣān dāsīkuru ṛddhān prasādaya vyavahārebhyo 'pyuttāraya vijayakari vajrapatākādhāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!
These are the <s>vajra</s>-courtesans (<s>vajragaṇikā</s>).

body.text: atha vajra] dūtīmāṃ svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajradūti ānaya sarvān maṇḍalaṃ praveśayāveśaya bandhaya sarvakarmā[ṇi me kuru śīghraṃ śīghraṃ laghu laghu] trāsaya māraya rāveṇa vajrakhaṅgadhāriṇi huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajradūtī</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Messenger) uttered this, her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajradūti ānaya sarvān maṇḍalaṃ praveśayāveśaya bandhaya sarvakarmāṇi me kuru śīghraṃ śīghraṃ laghu laghu trāsaya māraya rāveṇa vajrakhaṅgadhāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vegavajriṇi svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vegavajriṇī ghu ghu] ghu ghu śabdena māraya vikira vidhvaṃsaya vajrapaṭadhāriṇi huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vegavajriṇī</s> (Swift <s>Vajra</s>-Woman) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vegavajriṇī ghu ghu ghu ghu śabdena māraya vikira vidhvaṃsaya vajrapaṭadhāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrajvālā svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrajvālaya sa]rvaṃ vajra jvālaya daha daha bhasmīkuru huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrajvālā</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Flame) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajrajvālaya sarvaṃ vajra jvālaya daha daha bhasmīkuru hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajravikaṭā svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajravikaṭe pravikaṭa[daṃṣṭrākarālabhīṣaṇa]vakte śīghraṃ gṛhṇāveśaya bhakṣaya rudhiraṃ piva mahāyakṣiṇi vajrapāśadhāriṇi huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajravikaṭā</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Terrifying) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajravikaṭe pravikaṭadaṃṣṭrākarālabhīṣaṇavakte śīghraṃ gṛhṇāveśaya bhakṣaya rudhiraṃ piva mahāyakṣiṇi vajrapāśadhāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!
These are the <s>vajra</s>-messengers (<s>vajradūtī</s>).

body.text: atha vajramu[khī vajraceṭī sva]karmasamayāmabhāṣāt oṃ vajramukhi ānaya vajradaṃṣṭri bhayānike pātālanivāsini khana khana khāhi khāhi sarva mukhe [praveśaya sphoṭa]ya marmāṇi sarvaduṣṭānāṃ vajraniśitāsidhāriṇi huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajramukhī Vajraceṭī</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Face, <s>Vajra</s>-Maid-Servant) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajramukhi ānaya vajradaṃṣṭri bhayānike pātālanivāsini khana khana khāhi khāhi sarva mukhe praveśaya sphoṭaya marmāṇi sarvaduṣṭānāṃ vajraniśitāsidhāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrakālī svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrakāli [mahāpreta]rūpiṇi mānuṣamāṃsarudhirapriye ehyehi gṛhṇa gṛhṇa bhakṣaya vajraḍākini vajraśaṅkale sarvadevagaṇamātṛbhūte hara hara [prāṇānamukasya] kapālamālālaṃṅkṛtasarvakāye kiṃ cirāyasi vajrakhaṭvāṅgadhāriṇi pretamānuṣaśarīre śīghramāveśaya praveśaya bandha[ya vaśīkuru māraya vajrarākṣasi hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ //]
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrakālī</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-<s>Kālī</s>) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajrakāli mahāpretarūpiṇi mānuṣamāṃsarudhirapriye ehyehi gṛhṇa gṛhṇa bhakṣaya vajraḍākini vajraśaṅkale sarvadevagaṇamātṛbhūte hara hara prāṇānamukasya kapālamālālaṅkṛtasarvakāye kiṃ cirāyasi vajrakhaṭvāṅgadhāriṇi pretamānuṣaśarīre śīghramāveśaya praveśaya bandhaya vaśīkuru māraya vajrarākṣasi hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrapūtanā svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat atha vajrapūtane mānuṣamāṃsavasārudhiramūtrapurīṣaśleṣmasiṃghāṇakare[to garbhakariṇya yāhi] śīghramidamasya kuru vajraśodhanikādhāriṇi sarvakarmāṇi me kuru huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapūtanā</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Demoness) uttered her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajrapūtane mānuṣamāṃsavasārudhiramūtrapurīṣaśleṣmasiṃghāṇakaretogarphakariṇya yāhi śīghramidamasya kuru vajraśodhanikādhāriṇi sarvakarmāṇi me kuru hūṃ phaṭ</s>!

body.text: atha vajramakarīmāṃ svakarmasamayāmabhāṣat [oṃ vajramakari gra]sa grasa śīghraṃ śīghraṃ praveśaya pātālaṃ bhakṣaya vajramakaradhāriṇi huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajramakarī</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-<s>Makara</s>) uttered this, her own activity-pledge: <s>oṃ vajramakari grasa grasa śīghraṃ śīghraṃ praveśaya pātālaṃ bhakṣaya vajramakaradhāriṇi hūṃ phaṭ</s>!
These are the <s>vajra</s> maid-servants (<s>vajraceṭī</s>).
Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> again uttered this activity-<s>maṇḍala</s> of the entire <s>vajra</s>-family:

children.translated_text: Now I shall expound the supreme activity-<s>maṇḍala</s>;
by the method of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should draw the entire <s>maṇḍala</s>. (1)
All the foremost parts of the <s>maṇḍala</s>s have the <s>Buddha</s> at their center;
one should arrange the great beings in sequence and in rows. (2)
In the center of that, <s>Vajravidyottama</s> himself, together with his consort;
one should worship with the secret dance-offerings of <s>Vajralāsyā</s> and the rest. (3)
Therein, the goddesses, in due order, through the <s>cakra</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> method,
should be drawn dancing with their <s>mudrā</s>s and counter-<s>mudrā</s>s. (4)

body.text:
pūjārtha buddhavajribhyāṃ vajranṛtyaprayogataḥ /
[caturaśradvāreṣu vai yathākramaṃ dhū]pādikam // iti // 5 //
body.translated_text:
For the purpose of worship, by the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>vajra</s>s, through the application of <s>vajra</s>-dance,
at the four square gates, in due order, incense and the rest. (5)

body.text:
Mudra
athātra karmamaṇḍale samākarṣaṇādikarma kṛtvā, yathāvad vajradhārikarmasamayamudrāṃ badhvaivaṃ vadet ["na tvayā kasyacidadṛṣṭadevakulasyā]jñātakarmasyedaṃ guhyakarma vaktavyaṃ, mā te samayo vyathed!" iti uktvā, vajrācāryaḥ svakarmavajradhārisamayamudrāṃ bandhayet; krodhadṛṣṭyā nirīkṣannidamuttārayet oṃ vajradhāryāveśaya praveśaya nṛtyāpaya sarvakarmasiddhiṃ prayaccha huṃ a hūṃ a la la la la vajri //
body.translated_text:
<s>Mudrā</s>
Now here, in the activity-<s>maṇḍala</s>, having performed the attraction and other rites, having duly formed the <s>vajra</s>-bearer activity-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>, one should say thus: 'You must not speak of this secret activity to anyone from an unseen deity-family whose rites are unknown — lest your pledge be broken!' Having said this, the <s>vajrācārya</s> should form his own activity-<s>vajra</s>-bearer pledge-<s>mudrā</s>; looking with the wrathful gaze, he should recite this: <s>oṃ vajradhāryāveśaya praveśaya nṛtyāpaya sarvakarmasiddhiṃ prayaccha hūṃ a hūṃ a la la la la vajri</s>!

body.text: tataḥ svayamāviśya praviśeti, mudrāpratimudrābhirnṛtyopahārapūjāṃ karoti / tataḥ prabhṛti sarvakarmāṇi kāyavāgdṛṣṭimanovajramudrābhirīpsitena karoti /
body.translated_text: Then, having oneself entered and caused to enter, one performs the dance-offering-worship with <s>mudrā</s>s and counter-<s>mudrā</s>s. From that point on, one performs all activities with the body, speech, gaze, and mind <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s as desired.
Then, having released the face-covering, one should teach the dance-offering-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: The foremost pledges of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>vajra</s>-bearers and the rest are divided in two;
the <s>Vajralāsyā</s> and other offerings are for <s>Vajravidyottama</s>. (1)
Of all those <s>vidyā</s>s, duly and in sequence,
one should worship the activity-<s>maṇḍala</s> with dance-offering-worships. (2)
Through the application of <s>vajra</s>-dance, one should bring together the great <s>mudrā</s>s;
having divided the foremost pledges in two, one should release with the counter-<s>mudrā</s>s. (3)

body.text:
ābhirnṛtyopahāreṇa pūjayaṃ sarvanāyakān /
mahāvajradharādiśca karmasiddhi bhaved dhruvam // 4 // iti //
body.translated_text:
With these dance-offerings, worshipping all the leaders,
and the great <s>Vajradhara</s> and the rest — the accomplishment of activities will certainly come about. (4)
From the <s>Sarvatathāgatavajrasamaya</s> (Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s), the great ritual king — the extensive rite of the activity-<s>maṇḍala</s> of the entire <s>vajra</s>-family is completed.

body.text: CHAPTER 15 EPILOGUE OF THE SARVA-TATHAGATA-VAJRA-SAMAYA NAMA MAHA-KALPA-RAJA
body.translated_text: CHAPTER 15 — EPILOGUE OF THE <s>SARVATATHĀGATAVAJRASAMAYA</s>, THE GREAT RITUAL KING

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiḥ sarvavajrakulān sarvasattvārthaṃ [sthitvā] yāvan sanniyojyāvaivartikabhūmau pratiṣṭhāpya, jānanneva bhagavantametadabhāṣat / "ahaṃ bhagavadbhiḥ sarvatathāgataistava guhyadhāritve 'bhiṣiktaḥ / [yadā]jñāpayasva kintat tathāgataguhyam!" iti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, having established all the <s>vajra</s>-families for the benefit of all beings, and having stabilized them on the irreversible stage (<s>avaivartikabhūmi</s>), knowing full well, addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: 'I have been consecrated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, in the office of guardian of your secrets. Command me — what is the secret of the <s>Tathāgata</s>s!'

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgataguhyavajraṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ [sarvatathāgataguhyamabhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the secret <s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this secret of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.text: yathā yathā hi vinayāḥ sarvasatvāḥ] svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: According to how beings are by nature to be trained,

children.text: tathā tathā hi satvārthaṃ kuryādrāgādibhiḥ śuciḥ //
children.translated_text: just so should the pure one act for the benefit of beings — through passion and the rest.

body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> uttered this, his own secret:

For the benefit of all beings, on account of the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching,
one may destroy all beings — and is not stained by sin.
Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajragarbha</s> uttered this, his own jewel-secret:
For the benefit of all beings, through the application of the <s>Buddha</s>-body,

body.text: harastu sarvacintāni na sa pāpena lipyate //
body.translated_text: one may take away all worries — and is not stained by sin.
Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajranetra</s> uttered this, his own <s>dharma</s>-secret:

body.text:
rāgaśuddhaḥ sukhā[samaḥ jinagocaradānataḥ /]
sahāya paradārā niṣeve sa puṇyamāpnute //
body.translated_text:
Purified through passion, equal to bliss, through bestowing the domain of the <s>Jina</s>s,
even resorting to the wives of others together — one gains merit.
Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajraviśva</s> uttered this, his own activity-secret:

children.translated_text: For the benefit of all beings, on account of the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching,

children.text: sarvakarmāṇi kurvan vaṃ sa bahupuṇyamāpnute // iti //
children.translated_text: performing all activities — one gains abundant merit.

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgato bhagavate guhyadhāri[ṇe vajra]dharāya sādhukārairabhiṣṭavet //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s> acclaimed <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, the guardian of secrets, with exclamations of 'well done!':

children.text: sādhu te vajrasatvāya vajraratnāya sādhu te /
children.translated_text: Well done to you, <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Well done to you, <s>Vajraratna</s>!

children.text: vajradharmāya te sādhu sādhu te vajrakarmaṇe //
children.translated_text: Well done to you, <s>Vajradharma</s>! Well done to you, <s>Vajrakarman</s>!
This <s>sūtra</s> is well-spoken — the unsurpassed <s>Vajrayāna</s>,
the secret of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the compendium of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>!

body.translated_text: From the <s>Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha</s> (Compendium of the Tattvas of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s), the great ritual king called the Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s is completed.

body.text:
CHAPTER 16 SAKALA-JAGAD-VINAYA-MAHA-MANDALA-VIDHI-VISTARA
Hymn of 108 names of Avalokitesvara
body.translated_text:
CHAPTER 16 — EXTENSIVE RITE OF THE GREAT <s>MAṆḌALA</s> FOR THE TRAINING OF THE ENTIRE WORLD
Hymn of 108 Names of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>

body.text: atha sarvatathāgatāḥ punaḥ samājamāgamya, [tameva vajradharaṃ] bhagavantaṃ sarvadharmeśvaramavalokiteśvaramanena nāmāṣṭaśatenādhyeṣitavantaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having again come to the assembly, requested that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, the lord of all <s>dharma</s>s, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, with these one hundred and eight names:

children.translated_text: <s>Padmasattva</s> (Lotus-Being)! <s>Mahāpadma</s> (Great Lotus)! <s>Lokeśvara</s> (World-Lord)! <s>Maheśvara</s> (Great Lord)!
<s>Avalokiteśa</s> (All-Seeing Lord)! Foremost of the Steadfast! <s>Vajradharma</s>! Homage to you! (1)
<s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of <s>Dharma</s>)! Most Pure! King of Beings! Of Great Wisdom!
Lotus-Natured! Great Lotus! Lord of Lotuses! Homage to you! (2)
Lotus-Born! Of Beautiful Lotus-Splendor! Lotus-Pure! Great Purifier!
<s>Vajrapadma</s> (<s>Vajra</s>-Lotus)! Of Beautiful Lotus-Limbs! Lotus of Lotuses! Homage to you! (3)
Great All-Pervader! Great Illuminator! Of Great Deeds! Great Exemplar!
Most Steadfast! Great Hero! Great Valiant One! Homage to you! (4)
Aspiration of Beings! <s>Mahāyāna</s>! <s>Mahāyoga</s>! Grandfather (<s>Pitāmaha</s>)!

children.text: śambhu śaṅkara śuddhārtha buddhapadma namo 'stu te // 5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s>! <s>Śaṅkara</s>! Of Pure Purpose! <s>Buddhapadma</s> (Buddha-Lotus)! Homage to you! (5)
<s>Dharma</s>-reality-purpose, true <s>Dharma</s>, pure <s>Dharma</s>, doer of good <s>Dharma</s>,
great <s>Dharma</s>, foremost of good <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Dharmacakra</s>, homage to you! (6)
<s>Buddha</s>-being, foremost of excellent beings, <s>Dharma</s>-being, excellent being-upholder,
supreme being, excellent being-knower, being of beings, homage to you! (7)
Lord of Observation (<s>Avalokiteśa</s>), foremost protector, great protector, observer,
light of the world, world's purpose, Lord of the World (<s>Lokanātha</s>), homage to you! (8)
World-syllable, great beyond syllables, foremost of syllables, syllable-like,
syllable of syllables, all-eyed, wheel-syllable, homage to you! (9)
Lotus-handed, great-handed, comforter, giver,
<s>Buddha</s>-<s>Dharma</s>, great <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Buddha</s>-natured, homage to you! (10)
<s>Buddha</s>-form, great form, <s>vajra</s>-form, knower of beautiful forms,
<s>Dharma</s>-light, foremost of excellent radiance, light of the world, homage to you! (11)
Lord of lotus-glory, foremost protector, lord of <s>Dharma</s>-glory, possessing a protector,
<s>Brahma</s>-protector, great <s>Brahma</s>, son of <s>Brahma</s>, homage to you! (12)
Lamp, foremost of lamps, fierce lamp, lamp-light, excellent illuminator,
lord of lamps, great lamp, <s>Buddha</s>-lamp, homage to you! (13)
<s>Buddha</s>-consecrated, foremost of <s>Buddha</s>s, son of <s>Buddha</s>, greatly wise,
<s>Buddha</s>-consecration, foremost of crowns, <s>Buddha</s> of <s>Buddha</s>s, homage to you! (14)
<s>Buddha</s>-eye, great eye, <s>Dharma</s>-eye, great seer,
<s>samādhi</s>-knowledge, all-in-all, <s>Vajranetra</s>, homage to you! (15)
Whoever with complete devotion cultivates or praises
this secondary [hymn] of your one hundred and eight names — would attain sovereignty over the world. (16)

body.text:
adhyeṣayāma tvāṃ vīra prakāśaya mahāmune /
svakaṃ tu kulamutpādya dharmamaṇḍalamuttamam // 17 // iti //
body.translated_text:
We entreat you, O hero — reveal, O great sage,
having produced your own family, the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>! (17)

body.text: athāryāvalokiteśvaro bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ sarvatathāgatādhyeṣaṇavacanamupaśrutya, yena bhagavāṃcchākyamunistathāgataḥ tenābhimukhaṃ sthitvā, tadvajrapadmaṃ svahṛdi pratiṣṭhāpyedamudānamudānayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, the Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, having heard the entreating words of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, stood facing the <s>Bhagavān Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, and having established that <s>vajra</s>-lotus in his own heart, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.text: aho hi paramaṃ śuddhaṃ vajrapadmamidaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: Oh! This <s>vajra</s>-lotus of mine is supremely pure!

children.text: pitāhamasya ca suto 'dhitiṣṭha kulaṃ tvidam // iti //
children.translated_text: I am its father and he the son — empower this family!

body.text: Emanation of the deities from samadhi
body.translated_text: Emanation of the deities from <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatavajradharmasamayasaṃbhavādhiṣṭhānapadmannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvatathāgatadharmasamayaṃ nāma sarvatathāgatahṛdayaṃ svahṛdayānniścacāra hrīḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the Lotus of the Empowerment Born from the <s>Vajra</s>-<s>Dharma</s>-Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, this heart of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s called the <s>Dharma</s>-Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s issued forth from his own heart — Hrīḥ!

body.text: athāsmin viniḥsṛtamātre sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyaḥ padmākārā anekavarṇarūpaliṅgeryapathā raśmayo viniḥsṛtya, sarvalokadhātuṣu rāgādīni viśuddhadharmatājñānāni saṃśodhya, punarapyāgatyāryāvalokiteśvarasya hṛdaye praviṣṭā iti //
body.translated_text: The moment this emerged from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, lotus-shaped rays of various colors, forms, marks, and modes of conduct issued forth, and having purified the knowledges of pure <s>dharma</s>-nature such as passion and the rest in all world-realms for all beings, they returned and entered the heart of the Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatadharmasamayannāma svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajrapadmottama hrīḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own called the <s>Dharma</s>-Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s: Oṃ — Supreme <s>Vajra</s>-lotus! Hrīḥ!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatva idaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajra huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

body.text: atha vajragarbho bodhisatva idaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajraratnottama traḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajragarbha</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — Supreme <s>vajra</s>-jewel! Traḥ!

body.text: atha vajranetro bodhisatva idaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajravidyottama hrīḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajranetra</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — Supreme <s>vajra</s>-<s>vidyā</s>! Hrīḥ!

body.text: atha vajraviśvo bodhisatva idaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajraviśvottama aḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajraviśva</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — Supreme <s>vajra</s>-universal! Aḥ!

body.text: atha khalvavalokiteśvaro bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ sarvarūpasaṃdarśanaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyedaṃ sarvajagadvinayasamayannāma svahṛdayamabhāṣat oṃ huṃ hrīḥ hoḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara</s>, having entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the Display of All Forms, spoke this heart[-<s>mantra</s>] of his own called the Pledge of Disciplining All the World: Oṃ Hūṃ Hrīḥ Hoḥ!

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre āryāvalokiteśvarahṛdayāt sa eva bhagavāṃ vajradharaḥ āryāvalokiteśvararūpadhāriṇaḥ padmapratiṣṭhāḥ padmamudrācinhadhārivicitravarṇarūpaveṣālaṅkārāḥ tathāgatādisarvasatvamūrtidhārā mahābodhisatvavigrahā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasatvānāṃ yathā vaineyatayā svarūpāṇi sandarśyāśeṣānavaśeṣasatvadhātuvinayaṃ kṛtvā, punarapyāgatya, vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalayogena bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya sarvataścandramaṇḍalāśritā bhūtvedamudānamudānayiṃsuḥ /
body.translated_text: The moment this was spoken, from the heart of the Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>, bearing the form of the Noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, established on lotuses, bearing lotus-<s>mudrā</s>-symbols, with variegated colors, forms, attire, and ornaments, assuming the bodily forms of all beings including <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest, becoming great <s>Bodhisattva</s> forms, emerged. And having displayed their own forms to all beings in all world-realms as appropriate to their trainability, having disciplined the entire limitless and inexhaustible sentient realm, they returned and, in the arrangement of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>, stationed themselves on all sides on moon-disks of the <s>Bhagavān Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s>, and uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Oh! The skillful means of all <s>Buddha</s>s, whose nature is compassion —

children.text: yatra hyu pāyavinayād devā api bhavanti hi //
children.translated_text: whereby through disciplining by skillful means, even the gods come into being indeed!

body.translated_text: Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>

body.text: atha bhagavānavalokiteśvaro bodhisatvo mahāsatvaḥ svakulamutpādya, sarvatathāgatebhya sarvasatvābhayārthaprāptyuttamasiddhivajradharmatājñānābhijñāvāptiphalahetorniryā[tya, sarvajaga]dvinayaṃ nāma mahāmaṇḍalamabhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara</s>, having generated his own family, having dedicated to all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for the purpose of attaining fearlessness for all beings, the supreme accomplishment of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>-nature-knowledge-<s>abhijñā</s> as its fruit and cause, spoke the great <s>maṇḍala</s> called Disciplining the World (<s>Jagadvinaya</s>):

children.translated_text: Now I shall explain the supreme great <s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>Vajradhātu</s>, designated as Disciplining the World (<s>Jagadvinaya</s>). (1)
Four-cornered, with four gates, adorned with four arched gateways,
furnished with four cords, decorated with silk banners and garlands. (2)
In all <s>maṇḍala</s> corners and at the junctions of the gate-projections,
studded with <s>vajra</s>-jewels — thus one should outline the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>. (3)
Within that, one should cast a four-cornered cord[-outline];
for the second, the gate-corners should be fashioned in lotus-shape. (4)
With the device of eight pillars, one should draw an eight-petaled lotus;
in the middle of its filaments, one should install the <s>Buddha</s>-image. (5)

body.translated_text: Here, this is the heart[-<s>mantra</s>] for installing the <s>Buddha</s>: <s>Buddha</s> Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: On all sides of the <s>Buddha</s>, one should draw in the center of the lotus —

children.text: vajraṃ ratnaṃ tathā padmaṃ viśvapadmaṃ tathaiva ca //
children.translated_text: a <s>vajra</s>, a jewel, likewise a lotus, and a universal-lotus likewise.
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Oṃ!

body.translated_text: Huḥ!
Dhīḥ!
Kṛḥ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, [entering] the <s>Jagadvinaya</s> <s>maṇḍala</s>,
there one should depict <s>Lokeśvara</s>, emanating all forms. (1)
On all his sides, by the method of <s>Vajragarbha</s> and the rest,
one should draw the great beings beginning with <s>Buddha</s>, bearing lotus-symbols. (2)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Āḥ!
Oṃ — <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>Dharma</s>! Hūṃ!

children.text: oṃ vajrapadmāṅkuśa kośadhara vajrasatva hūṃ phaṭ //
children.translated_text: Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-lotus-hook, sheath-bearer, <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Slay, slay! Bearer of lotus-flower weapons, unfailing arrow! Hoḥ!

body.text:
oṃ padmasaṃbhava padmahasta sādhu hūṃ /
vajravegena cākramya dvitīyaṃ maṇḍalantathā /
body.translated_text:
Oṃ — Lotus-born, lotus-handed — well done! Hūṃ!
Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, likewise the second <s>maṇḍala</s> —
there in the center one should draw the <s>Tathāgata</s> amidst matted locks. (1)

children.translated_text: On all his sides, by the method of <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s> and the rest,
one should draw the lotus-symbol bearers duly, in order. (2)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Hūṃ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Lotus-<s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>! Traḥ!
Oṃ — Lotus-sun — blaze! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ padmamaṇi ketudhara candra pralhādayāvalokiteśvara dehi me sarvārthān śīghraṃ samaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Lotus-jewel, banner-bearer, moon — delight, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> — give me all aims quickly! Pledge! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ padmāṭṭahāsaikadaśamukha haḥ haḥ haḥ haḥ hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Lotus-boisterous-laughter, eleven-faced! Haḥ Haḥ Haḥ Haḥ! Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, likewise the third <s>maṇḍala</s> —
one should draw the great being in <s>samādhi</s>, established on a lotus. (1)
On all his sides, duly and in order,
by the method of Lotus-Light and the rest, one should install the great beings. (2)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Dha!

body.text:
oṃ tārā
padmavalokaya māṃ samayasatva hūṃ //
body.translated_text:
Oṃ — <s>Tārā</s>!
Observe me with a lotus[-gaze], O pledge-being! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ padmakumāra padmaśaktidhara khaṅgena cchinda cchinda hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Lotus-<s>Kumāra</s>, bearer of the lotus-spear — cut, cut with the sword! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

body.text: oṃ padma nīlakaṇṭha śaṃkhacakragadāpadmapāṇi vyāghracarmanivasan kṛṣṇasarpakṛtayajñopavītājinacarmavāmaskandhottarīya nārāyaṇa[rūpadha]ra trinetra muṃcāṭṭahāsaṃ praveśaya samayān dehi me siddhimavalokiteśvara hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Lotus <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> (Blue-Throated One), bearer of conch, wheel, mace, and lotus in hand, wearing a tiger-skin, with a black serpent as sacred thread and an antelope-skin over the left shoulder, bearing the form of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, three-eyed — release the boisterous laughter! Cause the pledges to enter! Give me accomplishment, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ brahma padmasaṃbhava japa japa padmabhāṣa hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — <s>Brahma</s>, lotus-born — recite, recite! Lotus-speech! Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, likewise the fourth <s>maṇḍala</s> —
there one should draw the lotus with four faces, bearing a lotus-trident. (1)
On all his sides, by the method of <s>vajra</s>-dance and the rest,
one should draw the great beings bearing lotus-symbols, as prescribed. (2)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Trīḥ!

body.text: oṃ padmanaṭṭeśvara naṭṭa naṭṭa pūjaya sarvatathāgatān vajrakarmasamayākarṣaya praveśaya bandhayāveśaya sarvakarmasiddhiṃ me prayacchāvalokiteśvara hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Lotus-dance-lord — dance, dance! Worship all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! <s>Vajra</s>-karma-pledge — attract, cause to enter, bind, possess! Grant me the accomplishment of all activities, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ abhayaṃdadāvalokiteśvara rakṣa bandha padmakavacaṃ samaya haṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, giver of fearlessness — protect! Bind! Lotus-armor! Pledge! Haṃ!

body.text: oṃ mahāpracaṇḍa viśvarūpa vikaṭapadmadaṃṣṭrākarāla bhīṣaṇavaktra trāsaya sarvān padmayakṣa khāda khāda dhik dhik dhik dhik //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Greatly fierce, universal-formed, terrible with lotus-fangs, with a terrifying face — terrify all! Lotus-<s>yakṣa</s> — devour, devour! Dhik Dhik Dhik Dhik!

body.text: oṃ padmamuṣṭi samaya[stva] bandha hūṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Lotus-fist — your pledge — bind! Hūṃ Phaṭ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, in all the corners one should draw
the deities of lotus-play and the rest, by the method of <s>vajra</s>-play and the rest.
Therein, these are the <s>mudrā</s>s:

children.text: oṃ padmalāsye rāgaya mahādevi rāgapūjāsamaye hūṃ //
children.translated_text: Oṃ — Lotus-play-goddess — enamor! O great goddess, in the pledge of passion-worship! Hūṃ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Lotus-garland-goddess — consecrate! In the pledge of consecration-worship! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Lotus-song-goddess — sing! In the pledge of song-worship! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Lotus-dance-goddess — dance! In the pledge of setting in motion all worship! Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, in the vicinity of the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>,
one should draw the four offering goddesses of lotus-incense and the rest.
Therein, these are the offering <s>mudrā</s>s:

children.text: oṃ padmadhūpapūjāsamaye pralhādaya padmakūladayite mahāgaṇi padmarati hūṃ //
children.translated_text: Oṃ — In the pledge of lotus-incense-offering — delight! O beloved of the lotus-family, great <s>gaṇi</s> (attendant), lotus-delight! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ padmapuṣpapūjāsamaye padmavāsini mahāśriye padmakulapratīhāri sarvārthān sādhaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — In the pledge of lotus-flower-offering — O lotus-dweller, great <s>Śrī</s>, door-keeper of the lotus-family — accomplish all aims! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ padmadīpūjāsamaye padmakulasundari mahādūtyāloka saṃjanaya padmasarasvati hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — In the pledge of lotus-lamp-offering — O beauty of the lotus-family, great messenger-light — generate! Lotus-<s>Sarasvatī</s>! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ padmagandhapūjāsamaye mahāpadmakulaceṭi kuru sarvakarmāṇi me padmasiddhi hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — In the pledge of lotus-perfume-offering — O great servant of the lotus-family — perform all actions for me! Lotus-<s>siddhi</s>! Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: Then the <s>gaṇa</s>[-pati]s and all the rest, in the four lotus-gates,

children.text: samālekhyā yathāvattu teṣāṃ ca hṛdayārthata // iti //
children.translated_text: should be duly drawn — and their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s] accordingly.
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:

children.text: oṃ hayagrīva mahāpadmāṅkuśākarṣaya śīghraṃ sarvapadmakulasamayān padmāṅkuśadhara hūṃ jjaḥ //
children.translated_text: Oṃ — <s>Hayagrīva</s>, great lotus-hook — attract quickly all lotus-family pledges! O lotus-hook-bearer! Hūṃ Jaḥ!

body.text: oṃ amoghapadmapāśa krodhākarṣaya praveśaya mahāpaśupatiyamavarūṇakuberabrahmaveṣadhara padmakula samayān hūṃ hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Unfailing lotus-noose, wrathful one — attract! Cause to enter! O bearer of the guise of the great <s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> — the lotus-family pledges! Hūṃ Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ padmasphoṭa bandha sarvapadmakulasamayān śīghraṃ hūṃ vaṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Lotus-burst — bind all lotus-family pledges quickly! Hūṃ Vaṃ!

body.text: oṃ ṣaḍmukha sanatkumāraveṣadhara padmaghaṇṭayāveśaya sarvapadmakulasamayān sarvamudrāṃ bandhaya sarvasiddhayo me prayaccha padmāveśa aḥ aḥ aḥ aḥ aḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Six-faced one, bearing the guise of <s>Sanatkumāra</s> — with the lotus-bell, cause all lotus-family pledges to enter! Bind all <s>mudrā</s>s! Grant me all accomplishments! Lotus-entry! Aḥ Aḥ Aḥ Aḥ Aḥ!
Initiation into the <s>maṇḍala</s>

body.text: athātra sarvajagadvinayapadmamaṇḍalavidhivistaro bhavati / tatrādita eva padmācāryo vajrapadmasamayamudrāṃ badhvā yathāvatpraviśya, vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalayogena karma kuryādimairhṛdayaiḥ oṃ padmasphoṭādhitiṣṭha aḥ //
body.translated_text: Now here follows the detailed procedure of the World-Disciplining Lotus <s>Maṇḍala</s>. Therein, first of all, the lotus-master, having bound the <s>vajra</s>-lotus-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>, should duly enter. By the method of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should perform the action with these heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]: Oṃ — Lotus-burst — empower! Aḥ!

body.text: tatastathaivājñāmājya, tathaiva samayamudrayā svayamabhiṣicya, padmavigrahaṃ gṛhya, svapadmanāmoccārya, padmāṅkuśādibhiśca karma kṛtvā, tatastābhireva dharmamudrābhirmahāsatvāṃ sādhayet / tatastathaiva siddhiriti //
body.translated_text: Then, having likewise sought instruction, having likewise consecrated oneself with the pledge-<s>mudrā</s>, having taken the lotus-body, having uttered one's own lotus-name, and having performed the action with the lotus-hook and the rest — then, with those very <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s, one should accomplish the great beings. Then likewise comes the accomplishment.

body.text: tataḥ padmaśiṣyān praveśayet / tatrāditaḥ padmaśiṣyāya śapathahṛdayaṃ dadyāt / "padmasatvaḥ svayante 'dya iti kartavyam" /
body.translated_text: Then one should lead the lotus-disciples in. Therein, first of all, one should give the oath heart[-<s>mantra</s>] to the lotus-disciple: 'The Lotus-Being (<s>Padmasattva</s>) himself today is established in you — this must be done.'

body.text: tato [ājñāpa]yāt / "na kasyacittvayedaṃ guhyavidhivistaramākhyeyaṃ; mā te narakapatanaṃ bhavet, viṣamāparihāreṇa ca kālakriye" ti //
body.translated_text: Then one should command: 'This detailed secret procedure must not be told by you to anyone; lest you fall into hell, and through an irremediable [transgression] there be death!'

body.text: tataḥ samaya[mudrāṃ bandhaye]d anena hṛdayena oṃ vajrapadmasamayastvaṃ //
body.translated_text: Then one should bind the pledge-<s>mudrā</s> with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: OṂ — You are the <s>Vajra</s>-Lotus pledge!

body.text: tataḥ śvetavastrottarīyaḥ śvetaraktakena mukhaṃ vadhvā praveśayedanena hṛdayena oṃ padmasamaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then, wearing a white cloth as upper garment, having covered the face with a white-red [band], one should lead [the disciple] in with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: OṂ — Lotus-pledge! HŪṂ!

body.text: tato yathāvatkarma kṛtvā, padmavigrahaṃ pāṇau dātavyaṃ oṃ padmahasta vajradharmatāṃ pālaya // tena vaktavyaṃ "kīdṛśīmā vajradharmate-" ti / tato vaktavyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Then, having duly performed the actions, one should give a lotus figure into [the disciple's] hand: OṂ — Lotus-hand, guard the <s>Vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>-nature! That one should say: 'What is this <s>Vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>-nature?' Then one should say:

children.translated_text: Just as this red lotus is not stained by the faults of its origin,

children.text: bhāvayet sarvaśuddhiṃ tu tathā pāpairna lipyate //
children.translated_text: so one should cultivate total purity — thus one is not stained by sins.

body.translated_text: This is the <s>dharma</s>-nature here.
<s>Mudrā</s>
Then one should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge of the Lotus family.

children.text: padmaṃ tu hṛdaye likhye padmabhāvanayā hṛdi /
children.translated_text: One should draw a lotus at the heart; through lotus-contemplation in the heart,
one would subjugate <s>Padmaśrī</s> (Lotus-Splendor) — how much more so inferior womankind! (1)

children.text: buddhabimbaṃ lalāṭe tu likhyābhīkṣṇaṃ tu bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: One should draw a <s>Buddha</s>-image at the forehead and contemplate it constantly;
through that contemplation, one quickly obtains consecration. (2)
Having pierced [the channel at] the mouth with a <s>Buddha</s>-image, one should radiate [it] on the tongue;
the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> herself constantly abides in the mouth. (3)

body.text:
padmamuṣṇīṣamadhye tu sthāpayitvā samāhitaḥ /
bhāvayan padmamuṣṇīṣe khegāmī sa vaśannayed // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Having placed a lotus in the center of the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>, concentrated,
contemplating [it] on the lotus-<s>uṣṇīṣa</s>, one becomes a sky-goer and subjugates [all]. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Bring <s>Padmaśrī</s> (Lotus-Splendor) under control! HOḤ!

body.translated_text: Grant the lotus-consecration! VAṂ!
Lotus-<s>Sarasvatī</s>, purify! HŪṂ!
Subjugate the lotus-sky-goers! JAḤ!
These are the Lotus family <s>mudrā</s>-knowledges.

children.translated_text: On a wall, or in the sky, contemplating the supreme lotus,
by this, the supreme subjugation of all beings [is achieved]. (1)
In the sky or in another place, contemplating the supreme lotus,

children.text: yadā paśyet tadā gṛhṇed rucyānadṛśyatāṃ vrajet // 2 //
children.translated_text: when one sees [it], one should grasp [it]; with delight, one proceeds to invisibility. (2)
On a wall, or in the sky, one should establish a universal lotus;

children.text: paśyaṃ gṛṇhedyathā taṃ tu viśvarūpī tadā bhavet // 3 //
children.translated_text: seeing and grasping that, one then becomes of universal form. (3)

children.text: ākāśe vānyadeśe vā vajrapadmaṃ tu bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: In the sky or in another place, one should contemplate a <s>vajra</s>-lotus;

children.text: taṃ tu gṛhṇaṃ kṣaṇāccaiva padmavidyādharo bhavet // 4 //
children.translated_text: grasping that, in an instant one becomes a lotus-<s>vidyādhara</s>. (4)
Therein, their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
OṂ — Enter the knowledge-lotus that subjugates the entire world! AḤ!

body.translated_text: OṂ — Knowledge-lotus, remain! Make invisible! VAṂ!

children.text: oṃ samādhi viśvapadma tiṣṭha vaiśvarūpyaṃ darśaya bhagavan ḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Samādhi</s> universal lotus, remain! Show universal form, <s>Bhagavān</s>! ḌHAḤ!

children.text: oṃ samādhi vajrapadma tiṣṭhottiṣṭha śīghraṃ hrīḥ //
children.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Samādhi</s> <s>vajra</s>-lotus, remain, arise quickly! HRĪḤ!
Having drawn <s>Lokeśvara</s> in the <s>maṇḍala</s>s and everywhere,
before him one should attract with the foremost <s>Hayagrīva</s> <s>mudrā</s>. (1)
Having drawn <s>Lokeśvara</s> in the <s>maṇḍala</s>s, before him indeed,
with the <s>Amoghapāśa</s> <s>mudrā</s>, one should subjugate the world. (2)
Having drawn <s>Lokeśvara</s> in the <s>maṇḍala</s>s and everywhere,
before him one should bind with the foremost <s>Padmasphoṭa</s> <s>mudrā</s>. (3)

body.text:
lokeśvaraṃ samālikhya maṇḍalādiṣu tasya vai /
purataḥ padmaghaṇṭayā sarvāveśanamuttamam // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Having drawn <s>Lokeśvara</s> in the <s>maṇḍala</s>s, before him indeed,
with the <s>Padmaghaṇṭā</s> (Lotus-Bell), the supreme entry of all. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
OṂ — Lotus-hook, attract all great beings! HŪṂ JAḤ!

body.translated_text: OṂ — <s>Amoghapāśa</s>-wrathful one! HŪṂ HOḤ!
OṂ — <s>Padmasphoṭa</s>! VAṂ!
OṂ — <s>Padmaghaṇṭā</s>, cause all to enter! AḤ!

children.translated_text: One should contemplate oneself as a being with four lotus-faces;
then, accomplished, one becomes many-formed in an instant. (1)
Contemplating the lotus-lotus as one's own self,
established in the <s>Vajradharma</s> <s>samādhi</s>, one attains the imperishable lotus. (2)
In the center of <s>Lokeśvara</s>'s matted locks, contemplating by oneself
a <s>Buddha</s>-image as one's own self, one becomes equal to <s>Amitāyus</s>. (3)

body.text:
bhāvayan svayam[ātmanā viśva]rūpasamādhinā /
viśvarūpasamādhistho lokeśvarasamo bhavet // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Contemplating by oneself, in the <s>samādhi</s> of universal form,
established in the <s>samādhi</s> of universal form, one becomes equal to <s>Lokeśvara</s>. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Lotus-universal!

body.translated_text: <s>Dharmakāya</s>-lotus!
<s>Buddha</s>-consecration!
<s>Lokeśvara</s>!

body.text:
tato mahāmaṇḍalasarvamudrājñānaṃ śikṣayet /
tatra praveśaṃ tāvan mahāmudrājñānaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text:
Then one should teach the great <s>maṇḍala</s> all-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge.
Therein, the entry — the great <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge — is:

children.translated_text: Standing in the center of a moon-<s>maṇḍala</s>, following the drawing [instructions],
the lotus-established beings, one's own — one should contemplate for one's own self.

body.translated_text: Now here is the action of those:

children.translated_text: Having bound the great <s>Buddha</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, one becomes equal to <s>Amitāyus</s>.
Having established the <s>vajra</s>-lotus, one becomes equal to <s>Lokeśvara</s>. (1)
Having bound the <s>Buddha</s>-consecration [<s>mudrā</s>], one is consecrated by the <s>Sugata</s>s.

children.text: padmapadmā samādhiṃ tu dadyād viśvā suviśvatāṃ // 2 //
children.translated_text: Having established the <s>Padmapadmā</s> <s>samādhi</s>, she bestows [the power of] universal form. (2)
The universal form for those to be trained — the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel-consecration-giver;
the <s>Padmasattvī</s> <s>samādhi</s> — the splendor of the Lotus Wrath Goddess. (3)
<s>Vajralokeśvarī</s> — the supreme accomplishment; <s>Padmarāgiṇī</s> —
<s>Buddheśvarī</s> — <s>Buddha</s>hood; <s>Vajrapadmā</s> — the bestower of good accomplishment. (4)
<s>Kāmeśvarī</s> — the state of supreme passion; <s>Tuṣṭi</s> — goodness;
<s>Bhṛkuṭi</s> — the pacifier of wrath; <s>Padmasūryā</s> — the bestower of good radiance. (5)
<s>Padmacandrā</s> — bestows great beauty; <s>Hāsā</s> — the state of good laughter;
by <s>Tārā</s>, the supreme accomplishment; by <s>Padmakhaṅgā</s>, good fortune. (6)
<s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> — great attraction; <s>Paṇḍaravāsinī</s> — accomplishment;
<s>Padmanarteśvarī</s> — accomplishment; <s>Abhayā</s> — the bestower of fearlessness. (7)
<s>Pracaṇḍā</s> — the subduer of evil ones; <s>Padmamuṣṭi</s> — the good accomplisher;

children.text: lāsyā ratiṃ dhanaṃ mālā sarvaṃ gītā sukhaṃ nṛtyā // 8 //
children.translated_text: <s>Lāsyā</s> — delight; <s>Mālā</s> — wealth; <s>Gītā</s> — everything; <s>Nṛtyā</s> — happiness. (8)

body.text: dhūpā lhādaṃ śubhaṃ puṣpādīpā dṛṣṭiṃ gandha sugandhatāṃ // 9 //
body.translated_text: <s>Dhūpā</s> — joy; <s>Puṣpā</s> — auspiciousness; <s>Dīpā</s> — sight; <s>Gandhā</s> — sweet fragrance. (9)

children.translated_text: <s>Hayagrīvā</s> — attraction; <s>Amoghā</s> — subjugation;
<s>Padmasphoṭā</s> — the great binder; <s>Sarvāveśā</s> — the bell-goddess. (10)

body.translated_text: Then comes the Lotus family pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge.

children.translated_text: Having established the <s>vajra</s>-binding, from the joining of the thumbs and the tips,
this <s>mudrā</s> is the <s>dharma</s>-pledge, the bestower of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>. (1)
Having established the <s>vajra</s>-binding, with the middle [fingers], the tips and ring [fingers],
this is the <s>mudrā</s> of the supreme <s>Buddha</s>-<s>vidyā</s>, the bestower of <s>Buddha</s>hood. (2)
Having established the <s>vajra</s>-binding, the middle [fingers] joined with <s>vajra</s>,
this is the <s>mudrā</s> of the supreme <s>Vajra</s>-<s>vidyā</s>, the bestower of <s>vajra</s>-hood. (3)
That very one, with a gem in the middle, is the bestower of the <s>vajra</s>-jewel;
through the cupped-middle method, it is the bestower of lotus-accomplishment. (4)
Having joined the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s>, it becomes the <s>vajra</s>-action-maker.
Having established the <s>dharma</s>-<s>vajra</s>, the pledge is accomplished in an instant. (5)
The <s>vajra</s>-binding with the tips, the bestower of <s>Buddha</s>-accomplishment.
Hereafter I shall proclaim the being-<s>mudrā</s>s in particular. (6)
Having established the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s>, with the middle [fingers] evenly raised,
with the little fingers and thumbs opened — it is called 'Universal Lotus.' (7)
That very one, with cross-legged thumbs, with curved tip-body,
with the <s>vajra</s>-matted-lock middle [fingers] on the crown — it is called 'Matted-lock <s>Buddha</s>.' (8)
Having firmly made the <s>vajra</s>-binding, with the thumbs below joined,
the two index fingers contracted, raised from <s>samādhi</s>. (9)
Having established the <s>añjali</s>, with the index fingers pressed by the <s>vajra</s>,
with the thumbs opened at the mouth — this is the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Amogheśvara</s>. (10)
Having firmly made the <s>vajra</s>-binding, one should bind it face-up;
with the thumbs making a lotus — it is called 'Lotus-<s>Buddha</s>.' (11)
With the tips of the thumb-<s>vajra</s>s, a hook and a sword;
the two outer [fingers] opened, the tips of the middle and ring [fingers] cupped. (12)
Having established the <s>añjali</s>, with the thumbs curled and curved,
grasping the index finger with the index finger, one should attract with the lotus-arrow. (13)
Likewise, binding the face-up <s>añjali</s> with the 'well-done' <s>mudrā</s> —
it gives the exclamation of 'well done!' — it is called 'Good Lotus.' (14)
Having firmly made the <s>añjali</s>, with curved tips placed at the mouth,
with the little fingers opened — it is called 'Lotus-<s>Bhṛkuṭi</s>.' (15)
Having firmly made the <s>vajra</s>-binding, one should extend it at the heart;
it is renowned as 'Lotus-Sun,' a <s>maṇḍala</s> of all fingers. (16)
Having firmly made the <s>añjali</s>, with the index fingers forming a gem,
the foremost Lotus-Jewel-Banner, extended with the arms at the crown. (17)
The <s>vajra</s>-binding at the crown of the head, extended with the tips and mouth together,
with one's own mouth in boisterous laughter — it becomes 'Eleven-Faced.' (18)
Having established the <s>samādhi</s>-lotus, with the thumbs evenly raised,
this is the <s>mudrā</s> of Lotus-<s>Tārā</s>, the bestower of all accomplishments. (19)
The <s>mudrā</s> of Lotus-<s>Tārā</s>, through the foremost lotus-yoga binding;
this is the <s>mudrā</s> of Lotus-Sword, through the arrangement in the form of a sword. (20)
Cupped-tip great lotuses, and the thumb-mace;
curved-tip great conch — wheeled with the <s>vajra</s>-binding. (21)
Having firmly made the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s>, with the right [hand] wrapped in the OṂ,
with the left tip-thumb [in] recitation — all tips opened as lotuses. (22)
Having established the <s>vajra</s>-finger, left and right likewise,
dancing with playful turns, placed at the crown — the Dancing Lotus Lady. (23)
Having firmly made the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s>, armored with all tips,

children.text: parivartya tu padmena hṛdi sthāpya dṛḍhaṃkarī // 24 //
children.translated_text: turning with the lotus, placing firmly at the heart. (24)
Having firmly made the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s>, through the secret <s>yakṣa</s> application,
with the <s>añjali</s>-cup extended, placed at the mouth — Lotus-<s>Yakṣiṇī</s>. (25)
Having divided the <s>vajra</s>-fist in two, curving the middle [fingers],
placed on the backs of one's own thumbs — it is called 'Lotus-Fist.' (26)
Through the <s>Vajradhātu</s> method, risen from the <s>vajra</s>-<s>añjali</s>,
one should bind the foremost pledge of all the foremost offering goddesses. (27)
Having firmly made the <s>vajra</s>-binding, one should join the two index fingers,
joining them in front with contraction — it is called '<s>Hayagrīva</s>.' (28)
Having established the lotus-<s>añjali</s>, with the index-finger-knot binding,
this is the <s>Amoghapāśa</s> <s>mudrā</s>, a chain of index fingers and thumbs. (29)

body.text:
padmāñjaliṃ samādhāya vajrāveśaprayogataḥ /
aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ tu saṃpīḍya kaniṣṭhānāmikāntarāv // 30 // iti //
body.translated_text:
Having established the lotus-<s>añjali</s>, through the <s>vajra</s>-entry application,
pressing with the thumbs between the little fingers and ring fingers. (30)

body.text:
atha padmakuladharmamudrājñānaṃ bhavati /
hrī / grī / prī / hī / śrī / sī / dī / hīḥ /
gī / dhī / krī / vī / vi / rī / ṣṭrī / aḥ /
body.translated_text:
Now comes the Lotus family <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:
HRĪ / GRĪ / PRĪ / HĪ / ŚRĪ / SĪ / DĪ / HĪḤ /
GĪ / DHĪ / KRĪ / VĪ / VI / RĪ / ṢṬRĪ / AḤ
Having divided the lotus-fist in two, one should establish the <s>karma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s.

From the <s>dharma</s>-pledges of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, from the great ritual-text (<s>mahākalparāja</s>), the detailed procedure of the great <s>maṇḍala</s> for the discipline of the entire world is completed.

body.text:
CHAPTER 16 PADMA-GUHYA-MUDRA-MANDALA-VIDHI-VISTARA
Emanation of deities from samadhi
body.translated_text:
CHAPTER 16 — <s>PADMA-GUHYA-MUDRĀ-MAṆḌALA-VIDHI-VISTARA</s>
Emanation of deities from <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatadharmadhāraṇīsamayasaṃbhavamudrādhiṣṭhānapadmannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgatadharmasamaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the lotus of the empowerment of the <s>mudrā</s> born from the <s>dharma</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this, his own supreme <s>vidyā</s>: OṂ — In the <s>dharma</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s — HŪṂ!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ imāṃ svakulasaṃbhavāṃ vidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrasamaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> uttered this supreme <s>vidyā</s> born from his own family: OṂ — In the <s>vajra</s>-pledge — HŪṂ!

body.text: atha vajragarbho bodhisatva mahāsatva imāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ maṇiratnasamaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> uttered this, his own supreme <s>vidyā</s>: OṂ — In the jewel-gem pledge — HŪṂ!

body.text: atha vajranetro bodhisatva imāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ padmasamaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajranetra</s> uttered this, his own supreme <s>vidyā</s>: OṂ — In the lotus-pledge — HŪṂ!

body.text: atha vajraviśvo bodhisatva imāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ karmasamaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajraviśva</s> uttered this, his own supreme <s>vidyā</s>: OṂ — In the <s>karma</s>-pledge — HŪṂ!
Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the noble <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, proclaimed this, his own family-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>:

children.translated_text: resembling the <s>Vajradhātu</s>, known as the 'lotus secret.' // 1 //

body.translated_text: Now I shall proclaim the unsurpassed <s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> —

children.translated_text: By the method of the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should string the entire <s>maṇḍala</s>.

children.text: tasya madhye supadme vai vajradhātvīśvarīṃ likhet // 2 //
children.translated_text: In the center of that, on a beautiful lotus, one should draw <s>Vajradhātvīśvarī</s>. // 2 //
On all sides of that, the foremost pledges as above —
<s>Dharmavajrī</s> and the rest should be drawn, accompanied by their <s>vidyā</s>s. // 3 //
Therein, their <s>mudrā</s>s are:
'Oṃ <s>sarvatathāgata dharmeśvari</s> hūṃ!'
'Oṃ <s>dharma samaye vajrapadmini</s> hūṃ!'
'Oṃ <s>buddhābhiṣeka ratna samaye</s> hūṃ!'

body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>tārā samaye</s> hūṃ!'
'Oṃ <s>viśvamukhe</s> hūṃ!'

children.translated_text: Having emerged with <s>vajra</s>-speed to the <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Viśvarūpā</s>-chief,
in the center there one should draw a lotus, surrounded by lotuses. // 1 //
On all its sides, lotus-<s>mudrā</s>s are established.
One should draw lotus-symbols, the own <s>mudrā</s>s of those of <s>Sugata</s>-nature. // 2 //
Therein, their <s>mudrā</s>s are:
Hrīḥ!

body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>padmatathāgate</s>!'
'Oṃ <s>Samantabhadra padmavajrāṅkuśakośadhāriṇi</s> hūṃ!'

children.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>padmarati</s>!'
'Oṃ <s>padmatuṣṭi</s>!'
Having entered with <s>vajra</s>-speed the second <s>maṇḍala</s> likewise,
one should draw <s>Buddhābhiṣekā</s>, a great lotus in the midst of the topknot. // 1 //
On all its sides, in proper sequence,
one should install the foremost pledges, endowed with lotus-symbols. // 2 //
Therein, their heart[-mantra]s are:
Śrīḥ!

body.text: oṃ bhṛkuṭi taṭi vetaṭi padme hūṃ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>bhṛkuṭi taṭi vetaṭi padme</s> hūṃ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmajvāle</s> hūṃ!'
'Oṃ <s>somini padme</s> hūṃ!'

body.text:
oṃ padmahāsini
ekādaśavaktre diri diri īṭṭe vaṭṭe cale pracale kusumadhare ili praviśa siddhiṃ me prayaccha hūṃ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>padmahāsini ekādaśavaktre diri diri īṭṭe vaṭṭe cale pracale kusumadhare ili praviśa siddhiṃ me prayaccha</s> hūṃ!'

children.translated_text: Having entered with <s>vajra</s>-speed the third <s>maṇḍala</s> likewise,

children.text: tatra madhye supadme tu padmamudrāṃ niveśayet // 1 //
children.translated_text: in the center there, on a beautiful lotus, one should install the lotus-<s>mudrā</s>. // 1 //
Likewise on all sides, in proper sequence,
one should draw those endowed with lotus-symbols, established in lotus form. // 2 //
Therein, their <s>mudrā</s>s are:
Dhīḥ!

body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>tāre tuttāre</s> hūṃ!'
'Oṃ dhī hūṃ!'

body.text:
oṃ padmacakragadādhāriṇi nīlakaṇṭhe sidhya sidhya huṃ //]
oṃ paṇḍaravāsiniṃ padmasaṃbhave vada vada hūṃ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>padmacakragadādhāriṇi nīlakaṇṭhe</s> sidhya sidhya hūṃ!' 'Oṃ <s>paṇḍaravāsinī padmasaṃbhave</s> vada vada hūṃ!'

children.translated_text: Having entered with <s>vajra</s>-speed the fourth supreme <s>maṇḍala</s>,
in the center of the lotus, one should draw a lotus with a garland of flames, bristling with radiance. // 1 //
On all its sides, in proper sequence,
one should draw lotus-symbols, established in the center of the lotus. // 2 //
Therein, their <s>mudrā</s>s are:
Strīḥ!

children.text: oṃ padmanarteśvari pūjaya sarvatathāgatān naṭṭa naṭṭa hūṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>padmanarteśvari</s>, worship all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! <s>naṭṭa naṭṭa</s> hūṃ!'

children.text: oṃ abhaye padmakavacabandhe rakṣa māṃ hūṃ haṃ //
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>abhaye padmakavacabandhe</s>, protect me! Hūṃ haṃ!'

body.text: oṃ mahāpracaṇḍi padmayakṣiṇi viśvarūpadhāriṇi bhīṣāpaya sarvaduṣṭān khāda khād huṃ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>mahāpracaṇḍi padmayakṣiṇi viśvarūpadhāriṇi</s>, terrify all the wicked! <s>khāda khāda</s> hūṃ phaṭ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmamuṣṭi</s> aḥ muḥ!'

children.translated_text: Having entered with <s>vajra</s>-speed, one should draw the <s>Buddha</s>-offerings,
the <s>mudrā</s>s beginning with the lotus-hook, with lotus-symbols in brief. Thus.
Now their <s>mudrā</s>s are:
'Oṃ <s>padmaratipūje</s> hoḥ!'

body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>padmābhiṣekapūje</s> raṭ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmagītapūje</s> gīḥ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmanṛtyapūje</s> kṛṭ!'
'Oṃ <s>dhūpapadmini</s> hūṃ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmapuṣpi</s> hūṃ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmakulasundari dharmāloke</s>, worship! Hūṃ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmagandhe</s> hūṃ!'

children.translated_text: Offering goddesses.

children.text: oṃ padmāṅkuśyākarṣaya mahāpadmakulān hayagrīvasamaye huṃ jaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>padmāṅkuśī</s>, attract the great lotus families! <s>Hayagrīvasamaye</s> hūṃ jaḥ!'

body.text: oṃ amoghapāśakrodhasamaye praviśa praveśaya sarvasamayān hūṃ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>amoghapāśakrodhasamaye</s>, enter, cause all pledges to enter! Hūṃ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmaśaṅkale</s> vaṃ!'

body.text: oṃ padmaghaṇṭādhāri śīghramāveśaya samayān ṣaṇmukhi aḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>padmaghaṇṭādhāri</s>, quickly cause the pledges to enter! <s>ṣaṇmukhi</s> aḥ!'

body.text: athātra mudrāmaṇḍale ākarṣaṇādividhivistaraṃ kṛtvā, padmaśiṣyān yathāvat [praveśya,] evaṃvaden "na tvayā kasyacid vaktavyaṃ yadatra guhyaṃ, mā te narakapatanaṃ bhavet, duḥkhāni cātrajanmani-" ti /
body.translated_text: Now, in this <s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, having performed the elaboration of the procedure of attraction and the rest, having properly caused the lotus-disciples to enter, one should say thus: 'You must not speak to anyone what is secret herein — lest falling into hell befall you, and sufferings in this birth.'

body.text: tataḥ samāveśyaivaṃ vadet / "[te cakṣuḥpathe] kīdṛśo 'vabhāsaḥ? tadyathā vadati tathā siddhir" iti / "tadyadi śvetālokaṃ paśyet tasyottamasiddhijñānaṃ śikṣayet / atha pītaṃ paśyet tasyārthotpattijñānaṃ śikṣayet / atha raktaṃ paśyet tato 'nurāgaṇajñānaṃ śikṣayet / atha kṛṣṇaṃ paśyet tato 'bhicārakajñānaṃ śikṣayet / atha vicitraṃ paśyet tataḥ sarvasiddhijñānaṃ śikṣayed" iti jñātvā, yathāvanmukhabandhaṃ muktvā, yathābhājanatayā jñānānyutpādayet / mudrājñānaṃ ca śikṣayet /
body.translated_text: Then, having caused [the deity] to enter, one should say: 'What sort of radiance [appears] in your field of vision? Whatever one says, accordingly is the accomplishment.' If one sees white light, one should teach the wisdom of supreme accomplishment. If one sees yellow, one should teach the wisdom of the arising of purpose. If one sees red, one should teach the wisdom of enamoring. If one sees black, one should teach the wisdom of destructive rites. If one sees variegated [light], one should teach the wisdom of all accomplishments. Having thus determined [this], releasing the mouth-seal properly, one should generate the wisdoms according to the capacity [of the disciple], and should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge.

body.text: evaṃ vajradhātvādiṣvapi sarvamaṇḍaleṣu yathābhājanatayā mudrājñānāni śikṣayediṃyaṃ parīkṣā //
body.translated_text: Thus in all <s>maṇḍala</s>s beginning with the <s>Vajradhātu</s>, one should teach the <s>mudrā</s>-wisdoms according to capacity — this is the examination.
Four Wisdoms (<s>Jñāna</s>)
Now the wisdom of the accomplishment of the supreme attainment is as follows:

children.translated_text: Visualizing <s>Lokeśvara Mahāsattva</s> in universal form, with oneself,
meditating on the great <s>mudrā</s>, one would attain the supreme accomplishment. // 1 //
Having made firm the <s>Buddhābhiṣekā</s>-pledge, concentrated,
meditating on oneself, one attains the supreme accomplishment. // 2 //
One should visualize oneself as <s>Padmapadma Mahāsattva</s>.
Well-concentrated, one attains the supreme accomplishment. // 3 //

body.text:
amogheśvaramayīṅkarmamudrāṃ svayambhuvaḥ /
sādhayan vidhivacchīghramagryāṃ siddhimavāpnuyād // 4 // iti //
body.translated_text: Accomplishing the activity-<s>mudrā</s> of the <s>Amogheśvara</s>-form, of the Self-Existent One, according to the rite, one would quickly attain the supreme accomplishment. // 4 // Thus.

children.translated_text: Now their heart[-mantra]s are:
'Oṃ <s>padmasattvo 'haṃ sidhya</s> hoḥ!'

body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>buddhābhiṣeko 'haṃ sidhya māṃ</s>!'
'Oṃ <s>dharmasamādhir ahaṃ sidhya</s> hoḥ!'
'Oṃ <s>amogheśvaro 'haṃ sidhya māṃ</s>!'
Then the wisdom of the accomplishment of purpose is as follows:

children.translated_text: Having placed gold in the mouth, meditating on oneself,
with the great <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Viśveśvara</s>, one [piece] would become a thousand. // 1 //
Having taken a <s>tola</s> (measure) of gold, with the foremost pledge greatly firm,
meditating on oneself, one [piece] would become a thousand. // 2 //
Having placed a pearl in the mouth, meditating on oneself,
as <s>Lokeśvara</s>, one [pearl] would become a thousand. // 3 //

body.text:
sarvaratnāni saṃgṛhya pāṇibhyāṃ karmamudrayā /
bhāvayan svayamātmānameko bhūyātsahasraśa // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text: Having gathered all jewels in both hands with the activity-<s>mudrā</s>, meditating on oneself, one [jewel] would become a thousand. Thus. // 4 //

children.translated_text: Therein, their heart[-mantra]s are:
'Oṃ <s>padmahiraṇyaprada</s> hūṃ jjaḥ!'

body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>padmasuvarṇaprada</s> hūṃ jjaḥ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmamuktāprada</s> hūṃ jjaḥ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmasarvaratnaprada</s> hūṃ jjaḥ!'
Now the wisdom of enamoring is as follows:

children.translated_text: Meditating on the great <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Viśveśvara</s> with oneself,

children.text: padmaṃ gṛhya puraḥ sthāti yasya so 'syānurajyati // 1 //
children.translated_text: taking a lotus and standing before whomever — that one becomes enamored. // 1 //
Having firmly taken a red lotus, with the great pledge-<s>mudrā</s>,
meditating on oneself, one enamors all women. // 2 //
Meditating on oneself, having hidden a lotus in the appropriate manner,

children.text: nirīkṣed vajradṛṣṭyā vai sarvalokaṃ sa rāgayet // 3 //
children.translated_text: gazing with the <s>vajra</s>-gaze, one enamors the entire world. // 3 //

body.text:
karmamudrāprayogeṇa padmaṃ gṛhya yathāvidhi /
karābhyāṃ bhrāmayan tantu rāgayet sarvayoṣita // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text: By the application of the activity-<s>mudrā</s>, having taken a lotus according to the rite, whirling it with both hands indeed — one enamors all women. Thus. // 4 //

children.translated_text: Therein, their heart[-mantra]s are:
'Oṃ <s>viśveśvara mahāpadma</s> hoḥ!'

body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>samayapadma</s> hoḥ!'
'Oṃ <s>yogapadma</s> hoḥ!'
'Oṃ <s>karmapadma</s> hoḥ!'
Now the wisdom of destructive rites (<s>abhicāra</s>) is as follows:

children.translated_text: Meditating on the great <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Viśveśvara</s> with oneself,
whoever's lotus one cuts before [them] — that one's death occurs instantly. // 1 //

children.text: padmaṃ gṛhya dṛḍhaṃ samyak samayāgryā tayaiva hi /
children.translated_text: Having firmly taken a lotus properly, with the foremost pledge itself,

children.text: sphoṭayet tantu sudṛḍhaṃ yasya nāmnā sa naśyati // 2 //
children.translated_text: one should snap it firmly — that one in whose name [it is snapped] is destroyed. // 2 //

children.text: samādhimudrāṃ sandhāya padmaṃ guhya yathā tathā /
children.translated_text: Having joined the <s>samādhi</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, having hidden a lotus in the appropriate manner,

children.text: yasya nāmnā tu padmaṃ vai cchindetsa tu vinaśyati // 3 //
children.translated_text: whoever's lotus one cuts by name — that one is destroyed. // 3 //

body.text:
karmamudrāprayogeṇa padmaṃ gṛhya yathāvidhi /
sphoṭayedyasya saṃkruddhaḥ sphuṭettasya tu jīvitam // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text: By the application of the activity-<s>mudrā</s>, having taken a lotus according to the rite, whoever's [lotus] one snaps with great anger — that one's life bursts open. Thus. // 4 //

children.translated_text: Therein, their heart[-mantra]s are:

children.text: oṃ mahāpadma ccheda māraya hoḥ phaṭ //
children.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>mahāpadma ccheda māraya</s> hoḥ phaṭ!'

body.text: oṃ samayapadma sphoṭa nāśaya raṭ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>samayapadma sphoṭa nāśaya</s> raṭ phaṭ!'

body.text: oṃ dharmapadma ccheda vināśaya dhṛṭ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>dharmapadma ccheda vināśaya</s> dhṛṭ phaṭ!'

body.text: oṃ karmapadma sphoṭa sphoṭaya jīvitamasya kṛṭ phaṭ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>karmapadma sphoṭa sphoṭaya jīvitam asya</s> kṛṭ phaṭ!'
<s>Mudrā</s>
Then the <s>dharma</s>-pledge secret <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge is as follows:

children.text: padmaṃ tu yoṣitāṃ cintya vajrantasyopari svayaṃ /
children.translated_text: Contemplating the lotus of women, and the <s>vajra</s> upon it oneself,
delighting [in the union of] the foremost <s>vajra</s>-lotus, one accomplishes through <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment). // 1 //

children.text: padmaṃ tu yoṣitāṃ cintya buddhantasyopari svayaṃ /
children.translated_text: Contemplating the lotus of women, and the <s>Buddha</s> upon it oneself,
delighting, meditating on the <s>Buddha</s>-crown, one accomplishes. // 2 //

children.text: padmaṃ tu yoṣitāṃ cintya padmaṃ tasyopari svayaṃ /
children.translated_text: Contemplating the lotus of women, and the lotus upon it oneself,
delighting in the foremost lotus-lotus, one attains pure accomplishment. // 3 //

body.text:
padmaṃ tu yoṣitāṃ cintya viśvantasyopari svayaṃ /
rāmayan viśvapadyāgrī viśvāṃ siddhimavāpnuyād // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text: Contemplating the lotus of women, and the <s>viśva</s> (universal) upon it oneself, delighting in the foremost <s>viśva</s>-lotus, one would attain universal accomplishment. Thus. // 4 //

children.translated_text: Therein, their heart[-mantra]s are:
'Oṃ <s>vajrapadma saṃyoga sādhaya</s> hrīḥ!'

body.translated_text: 'Oṃ <s>buddhamukuṭa saṃyoga sādhaya</s> śrīḥ!'
'Oṃ <s>padmapadma saṃyoga sādhaya</s> dhīḥ!'
'Oṃ <s>viśvapadma saṃyoga sādhaya</s> strīḥ!'
Then the proper lotus-family secret great <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge is as follows:

children.translated_text: The cupped salutation-hands at the tip, the pair of wrathful <s>vajra</s>-fingers,
the pair of tips as jewel, then the lotus, then the <s>vajra</s>-bond likewise. // 1 //
Having brought together the <s>vajra</s>-bond, the even middle sprout stands.
The index fingers not contracted — this is the firm <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Śākyamuni</s>. // 2 //
The <s>dharma</s>-<s>vajrā</s> stationed at the heart, reversed at the forehead,
the <s>samādhi</s>-yoga at the lap, reversed at the crown. // 3 //
Having bound <s>Vajradhātvīśvarī</s>, making a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) by the lotus-method,
joining with the middle [fingers] — this is proclaimed as the <s>Buddha</s>-lotus. // 4 //
That same with thumb-<s>vajra</s>, and the double-tip sword-hook likewise —
these are proclaimed as the secret <s>mudrā</s>s of the lotus-<s>vajra</s>-holder. // 5 //
That same with the thumb released, the index finger grasping the index,

children.text: valitā suratiḥ proktā sādhukāryā tathaiva ca // 6 //
children.translated_text: reversed — it is called 'delight' (<s>surati</s>), and likewise 'well done.' // 6 //
Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-bond, with even thumbs entered,
with curved tips stationed at the mouth — the middle lotus in the frown (<s>bhṛkuṭī</s>). // 7 //
That same at the heart — the displayer of the sun-disc.
With the banner-binding, that same, extended at the back of the head. // 8 //
Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-bond, with the form of curved tip-tips,
and likewise the lotus-sword, from the joining of the foremost lotus-method. // 9 //
Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-bond, by the entry of the left thumb,
the conch — the staff-tip thumb, the finger-tip last lotus. // 10 //
That same with all contracted, the little finger joined with the lotus,
the rosary-bead-tip counting, by the yoga of the right thumb. // 11 //
Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-bond, the little finger joined with the lotus,
the even-tip lotus-eye, reversed in dancing. // 12 //

body.text:
vajrabandhaṃ dṛḍhīkṛtya kaniṣṭhā padmasaṃyutā /
kuñcitā[gryaṃ pīḍayantu] dvayaṅguṣṭhakavacīkṛte- // ti // 13 //
body.translated_text: Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-bond, the little finger joined with the lotus, pressing the curved tips, armored by both thumbs. Thus. // 13 //

children.translated_text: That same with thumb-fangs, with even thumbs entered.
Hereafter I shall teach the unsurpassed foremost pledges. // 14 //
the thumbs in the binding cross-legged [position] — this is known as the secret <s>Viśveśvarī</s>. // 15 //

body.translated_text: Having made the <s>vajra</s>-bond at the base, the index finger joined with the lotus,

children.translated_text: Likewise with the <s>vajra</s>-bond, the little finger joined in the middle,
the <s>vajra</s> at the mouths of the thumbs — the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the center of the cloth. // 16 //
'Likewise in the <s>vajra</s>-bond, with the lotus joined by the thumbs,
raised from the face, stationed at the lap in <s>samādhi</s>.' (17)
'Likewise in the <s>vajra</s>-bond, evenly joined from the face,
all fingers made firm, the index fingers joined with the <s>vajra</s>.' (18)
'Likewise in the <s>vajra</s>-bond, the index fingers joined with the lotus,
the thumbs in the cross-legged bound position, with the middle [fingers] contracted in form.' (19)
'Likewise in the <s>vajra</s>-bond, the <s>vajra</s> joined by the thumbs,
the sword and hook with the tip-[fingers], the little fingers joined with the lotus.' (20)
'Likewise, having made it reversed, gathering the index finger and thumb,
one should firmly pull the raised left index finger.' (21)
