'That very one made even, through the yoga of the index finger and thumb,
the granter of approbation — of the great being <s>Padmatuṣṭi</s>.' (22)
'Likewise the <s>vajra</s>-bond, with all the tips joined at the face,
with the two thumb-tips pressing, with the tips assembled.' (23)

children.text: sā eva hṛdi sūryā tu mūrdhni padmadhvajīkṛtā /
children.translated_text: 'That very one at the heart is [<s>Padma</s>]-Sun; at the crown, made into a lotus-banner;

children.text: parivartya ca hāsā tu sthitā padmāṭṭahāsinī // 24 //
children.translated_text: reversed, the laughter — established as the lotus great-laugher.' (24)
'Having made the <s>vajra</s>-bond at the palm, through the yoga of the <s>dharma</s>-<s>vajra</s>-tip,

children.text: kaniṣṭhāṅga ṣṭhasandhī tu tārāyāḥ samayo hyayaṃ // 25 //
children.translated_text: with the little fingers and thumbs joined — this is the pledge of <s>Tārā</s>.' (25)
'Likewise in the <s>vajra</s>-bond, with the elder [fingers], the sword-lotus;
the palm-wheel likewise here, and likewise the recitation-giver.' (26)
'Likewise the <s>vajra</s>-bond, with the two bracelets released,
and again at the heart in binding — proclaimed as the secret protector.' (27)
'Likewise in the <s>vajra</s>-bond, the little fingers joined with the lotus,
the index fingers firmly contracted, with open thumb-fangs.' (28)
'That very one with the fist-yoga, with the two thumb-tips pressing —
the great fist of the lotus-secret, proclaimed as the foremost pledge.' (29)
'And of all the other [<s>mudrā</s>s] of those designated lotus-<s>lāsyā</s> and the rest,
having made the <s>vajra</s>-bond at the palm — the binding is just the same.' (30)

body.text:
tataḥ padmakulaguhyadharmamudrā bhavanti /
hrāḥ / grā / prā / hā / sra / sā / daḥ / haḥ /
gā / dhā / krā / vā / va / rā / ṣṭra / maḥ /
body.translated_text:
Then the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s of the lotus-family secret are:
<s>hrāḥ / grā / prā / hā / sra / sā / daḥ / haḥ /
gā / dhā / krā / vā / va / rā / ṣṭra / maḥ</s> /
'The action-<s>mudrā</s>s, in brief — the fist itself made twofold.'
The detailed procedure of the lotus-secret-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> from the Great King of Ritual Manuals of the <s>Dharma</s>-pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s is completed.
Chapter 17: Detailed Procedure of the Knowledge-<s>Maṇḍala</s> (<s>Jñānamaṇḍalavidhivistara</s>)

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatadharmasamayajñānasamayasaṃbhavādhiṣṭhānan padmannāma samādhiṃ samāpadmamāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ dharmasamādhijñānatathāgata hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the lotus of the empowerment born from the pledge of the knowledge-pledge of the <s>dharma</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: <s>oṃ dharmasamādhijñānatathāgata hūṃ</s>!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatva imaṃ svakuladharmasaṃbhavaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajradharma hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own, born from the <s>dharma</s> of his own family: <s>oṃ vajradharma hūṃ</s>!

body.text: atha vajragarbho bodhisatvo mahāsatva imaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ ratnadharma hūṃ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: <s>oṃ ratnadharma hūṃ</s>!

body.text: atha vajranetro bodhisatvo mahāsatva imaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ dharmadharma hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajranetra</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: <s>oṃ dharmadharma hūṃ</s>!

body.text: atha vajraviśvo bodhisatvo mahāsatva imaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ karmadharma hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajraviśva</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: <s>oṃ karmadharma hūṃ</s>!
Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>
Then the noble <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> spoke this <s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> of his own:

children.translated_text: 'Now, from here I shall teach the supreme knowledge-<s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>vajradhātu</s>, known as <s>Dharmajñāna</s> (Dharma-Knowledge).' (1)
'Through the method of the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should draw the threads of the entire <s>maṇḍala</s>;
in its center, one should draw the knowledge-<s>vajra</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>.' (2)

body.text:
tasya pārśveṣu sarveṣu mahāsatvā yathāvidhi /
viśveśvarādayo lekhyāḥ samāpannāḥ samāhitā // 3 // iti //
body.translated_text:
'On all his sides, the great beings, according to the proper method,
<s>Viśveśvara</s> and the rest should be drawn, having entered <s>samādhi</s>, concentrated.' (3)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>oṃ jñānabuddha hūṃ</s>! (1)

body.translated_text: <s>oṃ jñānaviśveśvara hūṃ</s>! (2)
<s>oṃ jñānabuddhamukuṭa hūṃ</s>! (3)
<s>oṃ jñānadharmeśvara hūṃ</s>! (4)
<s>oṃ jñānāmogheśvara hūṃ</s>! (5)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmabuddha hūṃ</s>! (6)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmarājadhara hūṃ</s>! (7)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmamāra hūṃ</s>! (8)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmatuṣṭi hūṃ</s>! (9)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmabhṛkuṭi hūṃ</s>! (10)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmasūrya hūṃ</s>! (11)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmacandra hūṃ</s>! (12)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmahāsa hūṃ</s>! (13)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmatāra hūṃ</s>! (14)

<s>oṃ jñānapadmamuṣṭi hūṃ</s>! (21)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmalāsye hūṃ</s>! (22)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmamāle hūṃ</s>! (23)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmagīte hūṃ</s>! (24)
<s>oṃ jñānapadmanṛtye hūṃ</s>! (25)
<s>oṃ padmajñānadhūpe hūṃ</s>! (26)
<s>oṃ padmajñānapuṣpe hūṃ</s>! (27)
<s>oṃ padmajñānadīpe hūṃ</s>! (28)
<s>oṃ padmajñānagandhe hūṃ</s>! (29)
<s>oṃ padmajñānāṅkuśa hūṃ</s>! (30)
<s>oṃ padmajñānāmoghapāśa hūṃ</s>! (31)
<s>oṃ padmajñānasphoṭa hūṃ</s>! (32)
<s>oṃ padmajñānāveśa hūṃ</s>! (33)
Initiation into the <s>maṇḍala</s>

body.text: athātra padmadharmamaṇḍale ākarṣaṇādividhivistaraṃkṛtvā, yathāvat praveśyaivaṃ vadet "na tvayānyasya vaktavyaṃ; mā te narakaṃ patanaṃ bhavet, duḥkhāni ve-" ti /
body.translated_text: Then, in this lotus-<s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, having performed the detailed procedure of attraction and the rest, having duly caused [the disciple] to enter, one should say thus: 'You must not tell anyone. Lest you fall into hell and [experience] suffering.'
Knowledge
Then one should generate knowledges for that one:

children.translated_text: 'Through the attainment of <s>Lokeśvara</s>, one should visualize a lotus at the heart;
having attained the lotus-<s>samādhi</s>, one swiftly rises up in an instant.' (1)
'Through the attainment of <s>Lokeśvara</s>, by the visualization of a lotus at the forehead,
having practiced, becoming firm, one becomes a sky-goer in an instant.' (2)
'Visualizing a lotus on the tongue, in the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>Lokeśvara</s>,
one becomes accomplished swiftly and travels through the sky.' (3)
'One should visualize a lotus at the crown, in the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>Lokeśvara</s>;
one becomes accomplished swiftly and rises upward in an instant.' (4)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>oṃ padmajñānahṛdayāviśa</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>oṃ padmajñānābhiṣekāviśa</s>!
<s>oṃ padmajñānavidyottamāviśa</s>!
<s>oṃ padmajñānoṣṇīṣāviśa</s>!

body.text: ākāśe vānyadeśe va padmabimbaṃ tu bhāvayet /
body.translated_text: 'In space or in another place, one should visualize a lotus-image;

body.text: anena vidhinā siddho adṛśyo bhavati kṣaṇāt // 1 //
body.translated_text: accomplished by this method, one becomes invisible in an instant.' (1)

children.text: ākāśe vānyadeśe vā padmabimbaṃ tu bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: 'In space or in another place, one should visualize a lotus-image;
mounted upon that, visualizing oneself — one becomes invisible.' (2)

children.text: ākāśe vānyadeśe vā padmabimbaṃ tu bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: 'In space or in another place, one should visualize a lotus-image;
when one sees [it], then one should seize [it] swiftly — one becomes invisible.' (3)

body.text:
ākāśe vānyadeśe vā padmabimbaṃ tu bhāvayet /
dṛṣṭvā tu bhukṣvā tatpadmamadṛśyo bhavati kṣaṇād // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
'In space or in another place, one should visualize a lotus-image;
having seen and eaten that lotus, one becomes invisible in an instant.' (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>oṃ padmākāśa</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>oṃ padmaratha</s>!
<s>oṃ padmajñāna gṛhṇa</s>!
<s>oṃ padmarasāyana</s>!

children.translated_text: 'A lotus-image of variegated color and form, with the hand
grasping [it] and binding the great <s>mudrā</s>, one becomes a bearer of all forms.' (1)
'A lotus-image of variegated color and form, one should draw;
meditating thereupon, one becomes a bearer of many forms.' (2)
'A lotus-image of variegated color and form, one should visualize
in space or in another place — one will become one whose form is sound.' (3)

body.text:
vicitravarṇasaṃsthānaṃ padmabimbaṃ ghaṭāpayet /
tatrārūḍhastu khegāmī kāmarūpī bhaveddhruvam // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
'A lotus-image of variegated color and form, one should construct;
mounted upon that, a sky-goer, one assuredly becomes one of desired form.' (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>oṃ padmadhara viśvarūpapravartakāviśa</s>!

body.translated_text: <s>oṃ viśvapadma pravartaya māṃ</s>!
<s>oṃ samādhiviśvapadmāviśa</s>!
<s>oṃ viśvapadmāsanotkṣipākāśaṃ viśvarūpamadhitiṣṭha māṃ</s>!

children.translated_text: 'Having properly bound the singular great <s>mudrā</s>, from <s>samādhi</s>,
one should give the lotus secretly — one assuredly becomes a subjugator.' (1)

body.translated_text: 'Having properly bound the singular <s>mudrā</s> designated as the pledge,

body.text: tayā gṛhya tu vai padmaṃ dadyād vaśyakaro bhavet // 2 //
body.translated_text: grasping with that the lotus and giving [it] — one becomes a subjugator.' (2)

children.translated_text: 'Having bound a certain <s>mudrā</s>, established in <s>samādhi</s>, auspicious,
to whomever one gives the knowledge-lotus — that one swiftly comes under control.' (3)

body.text:
badhvā caikatamāṃ mudrāṃ karmākhyāṃ samayānvitaḥ /
yasya dadyāt [sa suvaśīḥ] padmadānātkṣaṇād bhaved //iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
'Having bound a certain <s>mudrā</s> called the action[-<s>mudrā</s>], endowed with the pledge,
to whomever one gives [the lotus] — that one becomes well-controlled in an instant by the lotus-giving.' (4)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>oṃ mahāpadma hoḥ</s>!
<s>oṃ samayapadma hoḥ</s>!
<s>oṃ jñānapadma hoḥ</s>!
<s>oṃ karmapadma hoḥ</s>!
<s>Mudrā</s>
Then one should teach the great <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge of the knowledge-<s>maṇḍala</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Through the method of the <s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should accomplish the great <s>mudrā</s>s;
from here onward I shall teach — the foremost pledge should be accomplished.'
'Through the method of the <s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should establish the lotus-lotus;
the <s>dharma</s>-fist made twofold — the action-<s>mudrā</s> made twofold.'

body.translated_text: The detailed procedure of the knowledge-<s>maṇḍala</s> from the Great King of Ritual Manuals of the <s>Dharma</s>-pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s is completed.
Chapter 18a: Detailed Procedure of the Action-<s>Maṇḍala</s> (<s>Karmamaṇḍalavidhivistara</s>)

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatadharmakarmasamayasaṃbhavādhiṣṭhānapadmaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgatakarmāgra hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having again entered the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the lotus of the empowerment born from the pledge of the <s>dharma</s>-action-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: <s>oṃ sarvatathāgatakarmāgra hūṃ</s>!

body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own, born from the action of his own family: <s>oṃ hūṃ dhīḥ</s>!

body.text: atha vajragarbho bodhisatva imāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ ratnakarmasamaye hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: <s>oṃ ratnakarmasamaye hūṃ</s>!

body.text: atha vajranetro bodhisatva imāṃ svavidyottamāmabhāṣat oṃ padmakarmi hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajranetra</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: <s>oṃ padmakarmi hūṃ</s>!

body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajraviśva</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: <s>oṃ viśvakarmi hūṃ</s>!
Then the noble <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> spoke this action-<s>maṇḍala</s> of his own:

children.translated_text: 'Now, from here I shall teach the supreme action-<s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>vajradhātu</s>, known as <s>Padmakarma</s> (Lotus-Action).' (1)

body.text:
mahāmaṇḍalayogena sūtrayetsarvamaṇḍalaṃ /
buddhasya sarvataḥ sarvāḥ padmacinhadharā likhed // iti // 2 //
body.translated_text:
'Through the method of the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should draw the threads of the entire <s>maṇḍala</s>;
around the <s>Buddha</s> on all sides, one should draw all [goddesses] bearing lotus-emblems.' (2)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are the <s>vidyā</s> heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:
<s>oṃ padmabhūriṇī huṃ</s>! (1)

body.translated_text: <s>oṃ viśvakarmeśvari hūṃ</s>! (2)
<s>oṃ tathāgateśvaryābhiṣekakarmavidye hūṃ</s>! (3)
<s>oṃ dharmakarmeśvari jñānapūjāsamaye hūṃ</s>! (4)
<s>oṃ amoghakarmeśvari hūṃ</s>! (5)
<s>oṃ padmakarmabuddhe hūṃ</s>! (6)
<s>oṃ padmakarmavajriṇi hūṃ</s>! (7)
<s>oṃ padmakāmini māraṇapūjākarmasamaye hūṃ</s>! (8)
<s>oṃ padmakarmatuṣṭi hūṃ</s>! (9)
<s>oṃ padmakarmabhṛkuṭi hūṃ traḥ</s>! (10)
<s>oṃ padmakarmasūrye hūṃ</s>! (11)
<s>oṃ padmakarmadhvaje hūṃ</s>! (12)
<s>oṃ padmakarmahāse haḥ</s>! (13)
<s>oṃ padmakarmatāre hūṃ</s>! (14)
<s>oṃ padmakarmakumāri hūṃ</s>! (15)
<s>oṃ padmakarmanārāyaṇi hūṃ</s>! (16)
<s>oṃ padmakarmabrāhmi hūṃ</s>! (17)
<s>oṃ padmakarmanṛtyeśvari hūṃ</s>! (18)
<s>oṃ padmarakṣakarmasamaye hūṃ</s>! (19)
<s>oṃ mahāpracaṇḍi ghātani padmadaṃṣṭrākarmakari hūṃ</s>! (20)
<s>oṃ padmakarmamuṣṭi ghātaya hūṃ</s>! (21)
<s>oṃ ratipūje hūṃ jaḥ</s>! (22)

body.text:
CHAPTER 19 SARVARTHASIDDHI-MAHAMANDALA-VIDHI-VISTARA
Hymn of 108 names of the mahabodhisattva Akasagarbha
atha khalu sarvatathāgatāḥ punaḥ samājamāgamya, sarvatathāgatābhiṣekaratnaṃ tameva vajradharamāryākāśagarbha mahābodhisatvamanena nāmaṣṭaśatenādhyeṣitavantaḥ /

children.text: śuddha sarvārtha śuddhārtha dānacarya namo 'stu te // 6 //

children.translated_text: great consecration, world's purpose, purpose of joy, homage to you! (7)

children.text: dāna pradana dānāgrya tyāga tyāgāgrya dāyaka /
children.translated_text: Gift, supreme gift, foremost of giving, renunciation, foremost of renunciation, giver,
purpose of all beings, purpose of reality, purpose of great purpose, homage to you! (8)
Wish-fulfilling king, of great radiance, method of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>),
<s>Tathāgata</s>, great being, all <s>Buddha</s>s, homage to you! (9)
<s>Tathāgata</s> great jewel, <s>Tathāgata</s> great radiance,
<s>Tathāgata</s> great banner, great laughter, homage to you! (10)
Foremost of <s>Tathāgata</s>-consecrations, great consecration, great lord,
world-protector, foremost of the world, sun of the world, homage to you! (11)
Surpassing jewels and more, jewel-ornament, jewel-bearer,
jewel-light, great light, jewel-fame, homage to you! (12)
Jewel-heap, excellent jewel-arisen, gem, <s>vajra</s>-gem, virtue,
jewel-mine, of brightly shining limbs, all-jewel, homage to you! (13)
Great soul, staff, jewel-lord, fulfiller of all wishes,
attainer of all desires, jewel-mass, homage to you! (14)
Foremost, pervading, all-self, giver of boons, great boon,
splendor, all-prosperity, <s>Vajragarbha</s>, homage to you! (15)
Whoever maintains this auspicious one hundred and eight names,
that faultless one attains the consecration of all <s>Buddha</s>s in an instant! (16)

body.text:
adhyeṣayāmastvāṃ ratna bhāṣa svadhanasaṃcayaṃ /
sarvabuddhābhiṣekāgryamutpāda niyamakulam // 17 // iti //
body.translated_text:
We entreat you, O Jewel — proclaim the treasury of your own wealth!
Produce the supreme consecration of all <s>Buddha</s>s — the family-rule! (17)

body.text: athākāśagarbho bodhisatvaḥ idaṃ sarvatathāgatavacanamupaśrutya, sarvatathāgatābhiṣekasamayaṃ nāma svahṛdayamabhāṣat oṃ vajraratnaṃ hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha</s>, having heard these words of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, spoke this heart[-<s>mantra</s>] of his own called the Consecration-Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s: Oṃ — <s>Vajraratna</s>! Hūṃ!

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgata idaṃ sarvatathāgatamaṇisamayaṃ nāma vidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgatāśāparipūraṇamahāratna hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> called the Jewel-Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s: Oṃ — Great jewel of the fulfillment of all wishes of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! Hūṃ!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatva imaṃ svakulasaṃbhavaṃ vidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajra hūṃ traḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> born from his own family: Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>! Hūṃ Traḥ!

body.text: atha vajragarbho bodhisatva imaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ maṇi hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajragarbha</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — <s>Maṇi</s> (Gem)! Hūṃ!

body.text: atha vajranetro bodhisatva imaṃ svakulasaṃbhavaṃ vidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ padma hrīḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Vajranetra</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> born from his own family: Oṃ — <s>Padma</s> (Lotus)! Hrīḥ!

body.text: atha vajraviśvo bodhisatvo mahāsatva imaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ viśvaratna hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajraviśva</s> spoke this supreme <s>vidyā</s> of his own: Oṃ — Universal jewel (<s>Viśvaratna</s>)! Hūṃ!

body.text: athāryākāśagarbho bodhisa[tvo mahāsatvaḥ] sarvatathāgatābhiṣekaratnaṃnāma samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ; samanantarasamāpanne cātha tāvadeva sarvatathāgatahṛdayebhyo vajramaṇiratnaraśmayo niścaritāḥ / te sarvalokadhātavo 'vabhāsya sarvasatvān sarvatathāgatābhiṣekairabhiṣicya, punarapyekadhyībhūtvā, bhagavata ākāśagarbhasya mahābodhisatvasya hṛdaye 'nupraviṣṭā iti /
body.translated_text: Then the Noble <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha</s> entered the <s>samādhi</s> called the Consecration-Jewel of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s. And the very moment he entered that <s>samādhi</s>, <s>vajra</s>-gem-jewel-rays issued forth from the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Having illuminated all world-realms and consecrated all beings with the consecrations of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, they again became unified and entered the heart of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha</s>.

body.text: atha tat ākāśagarbhahṛdayātsa eva bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ samantaraśmijvālāgarbhā vicitravajramaṇiratnābhiṣekādyābharaṇālaṅkārālaṅkṛtakāyā mahavajramaṇiratnacinhamudrāvyagrakarā mahābodhisatvakāyā bhūtvā viniḥsṛtya, sarvalokadhātuṣu mahāratnavarṣādibhiḥ ratnotpattibhiḥ santoṣya, punarāgatya, bhagavato vairocanasya sarvato vajradhātumahāmaṇḍalayogena candramaṇḍalāśritā bhūtvedamudānamudānayiṃsuḥ /
body.translated_text: Then from the heart of <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, that very <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, with bodies adorned with ornaments and decorations of variegated <s>vajra</s>-gem-jewel consecrations and the rest, their essence a womb of garland-rays, with great <s>vajra</s>-gem-jewel symbol-<s>mudrā</s>s actively in their hands, having become great <s>Bodhisattva</s> forms, emerged. And having gratified [all beings] in all world-realms with great jewel-rains and other jewel-arisings, they returned, and in the arrangement of the <s>Vajradhātu</s> great <s>maṇḍala</s> of <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, stationed on moon-disks on all sides, uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: Oh! The complete assembly of all jewels of all <s>Buddha</s>s —
this <s>vajra</s>-jewel family has arisen for the world's purpose!

body.translated_text: Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>

body.text: athākāśagarbho bodhisatvo mahāsatva iti svakulamutpādya, sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ sarvāśāparipūrye niryātyedaṃ sarvārthasiddhinnāma mahāmaṇḍalamabhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha</s>, having thus generated his own family, having dedicated to all <s>Tathāgata</s>s for the fulfillment of all wishes, spoke this great <s>maṇḍala</s> called the Accomplishment of All Aims (<s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s>):

children.translated_text: Now I shall explain the supreme great <s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>Vajradhātu</s>, known as All-Accomplishment (<s>Sarvasiddhi</s>). (1)
Four-cornered, with four gates, adorned with four arched gateways,
furnished with four cords, decorated with silk banners and garlands. (2)
In all <s>maṇḍala</s> corners and at the junctions of the gate-projections,
studded with <s>vajra</s>-jewels — thus one should outline the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>. (3)
Within that, one should make the inner citadel, equal to the <s>vajra</s>-jewel;
there, with the device of eight pillar-tops, one should make the cord[-outline]. (4)
Adorned with five <s>maṇḍala</s>s, blazing with various jewel-mines,
there, surrounded by his own <s>mudrā</s>[-retinue], one should install the <s>Buddha</s>. (5)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Oṃ — <s>Buddha</s>-jewel! Hūṃ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-gem! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-jewel-sprout! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-jewel-lotus! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Jewel-lotus-rain! Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, [entering] the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the accomplishment of all wishes —
there one should draw <s>Vajragarbha</s>, the bestower of supreme jewels. (1)
On all his sides, joined with jewel-<s>mudrā</s>s,
the great beings should be drawn, duly and in order. (2)
Now these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Oṃ — Bestower of the accomplishment of all aims! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ vajramaṇicinhākāśagarbha bhagavan sidhya sidhya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — <s>Ākāśagarbha</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-gem-symbol, O <s>Bhagavān</s> — accomplish, accomplish! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ ratnāṅkuśākarṣaya sarvārthānānaya śīghraṃ sarvatathāgatasatyamanusmara hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Jewel-hook — attract! Bring all aims quickly! Remember the truth of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Gem-passion — subjugate! Bring all aims, <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Jewel-satisfaction! Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, [entering] the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the jewel-garland —
there in the center one should properly draw the supreme jewel-garland-bearer. (1)
On all his sides, duly and in order,
the great beings should be drawn, with gem-symbols foremost in their hands. (2)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Oṃ — Jewel-gaze! Traḥ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Jewel-garland of the consecration of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Gem-sun! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Wish-fulfilling jewel-banner, fulfiller of all wishes, <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ ratnāṭṭahāsa hasa ha ha hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Jewel-boisterous-laughter — laugh! Ha Ha! Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, [entering] the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the jewel-lotus —
there one should draw the powerful jewel-lotus-bearer. (1)
On all his sides, one should draw the great beings,
with gem-symbols, in brief, duly and in order. (2)

body.translated_text: Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Oṃ — Jewel-lotus! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Womb of the <s>samādhi</s>-knowledge of renunciation! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Supreme jewel-sheath! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Gem-wheel — set in motion! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Jewel-speech! Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, [entering] the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the jewel-rain —
there one should draw the great being raining down jewel-rain. (1)
On all his sides, the great beings, as prescribed,
endowed with jewel-symbols, with <s>mudrā</s>-hands, in brief. (2)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:

children.text: oṃ ratnavṛṣṭi varṣaya sarvārthasaṃpado bhagavan maṇihasta hūṃ //
children.translated_text: Oṃ — Jewel-rain — rain down! All purposes and prosperities, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, gem-handed! Hūṃ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Gem-offering pledge! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Gem-binding armor! Hūṃ!

body.text: oṃ maṇidaṃṣṭrākarāla mahāyakṣa hara hara sarvārthān bhīṣāpaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — Terrible with gem-fangs, great <s>yakṣa</s> — seize, seize all aims! Terrify! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Gem-jewel — bind! Pledge! Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, in all the corner sections —
the jewel-play goddesses and the rest should be drawn, duly and in order.
Therein, these are the <s>mudrā</s>s:
Oṃ — Jewel-delight! Hūṃ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Jewel-garland! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Jewel-song! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Jewel-dance! Hūṃ!

children.translated_text: Advancing with <s>vajra</s>-speed, [entering] the supreme outer <s>maṇḍala</s> —
in the corners of the outer <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should draw the incense-offering [goddesses] and the rest.
Therein, these are the <s>mudrā</s>s:
Oṃ — Incense-jewel!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Flower-gem!
Oṃ — Jewel-lamp!
Oṃ — Gem-perfume!

children.translated_text: The door-guardians should be made in the four gate-centers.
Hereafter I shall proclaim the detailed procedure in the <s>maṇḍala</s>.
Now here are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:

children.text: oṃ sarvaratnākarṣa āryāruṇa mahāsatva bhagavantaṃ ākāśagarbha codayākarṣaya śīghraṃ hoḥ jaḥ //
children.translated_text: Oṃ — Attract all jewels! Noble <s>Aruṇa</s>, great being — urge the <s>Bhagavān Ākāśagarbha</s> — attract quickly! Hoḥ Jaḥ!

body.text: oṃ sarvaratnapraveśasamaya praveśaya samayān mahāmaṇirājakulaṃ ratnapāśa hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — In the pledge of the entry of all jewels — cause the pledges to enter! Great gem-king family! Jewel-noose! Hūṃ!
Oṃ — Gem-binding! Hūṃ Vaṃ!
Oṃ — Gem-jewel-possession! Aḥ!
Initiation into the <s>maṇḍala</s>

body.text: athātra mahāmaṇḍale svayaṃ maṇiratnācāryo yathāvat praviśya, vidhivistaramātmanaḥ kṛtvā, tato ratnādhiṣṭhitakalaśodakena maṇiśiṣyānabhiṣicya, vajramaṇisamayamudrāṃ bandhayedanena hṛdayena oṃ vajramaṇi samaya vaṃ //
body.translated_text: Now here, in the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, the gem-jewel-master himself, having duly entered, having performed the detailed procedure for himself — then, having consecrated the gem-disciples with water from the jewel-empowered vase, one should bind the <s>vajra</s>-gem-pledge-<s>mudrā</s> with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-gem — pledge! Vaṃ!

body.text: tato yathāvarṇaprāptitayā vastramuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā, tādṛśenaivākṣiṇī badhvā, praveśayedanena hṛdayena oṃ hūṃ maṇirājakulaṃ //
body.translated_text: Then, having made a garment as upper-covering according to the attainment of the [appropriate] color, having bound the eyes with such [a cloth], one should lead [the disciple] in with this heart[-<s>mantra</s>]: Oṃ Hūṃ — Gem-king family!

body.text: tataḥ praveśya vaktavyaṃ "na tvayedaṃ kasyacid vaktavyaṃ; māte sarvajanmasu dāridryaduḥkhānmokṣe na bhaven, narakavāsaśca dṛḍho bhaved" ityuktvā, samayaṃ sphoṭayet; mahāyānābhisamayaṃ coccārayet /
body.translated_text: Then, having led [the disciple] in, one should say: 'You must not speak of this to anyone. Lest there be no liberation for you from the suffering of poverty in all your births, and your dwelling in hell become firm!' Having spoken thus, one should snap [the finger as] the pledge; and one should recite the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization.

body.text: tataḥ samāviṣṭasya vajravācā paripṛcchet / "kutra mahānidhirasti? / kathaṃ vā prāpyate /"
body.translated_text: Then, of the one who is possessed, one should inquire with the <s>vajra</s>-voice: 'Where is the great treasure? And how is it obtained?'

body.text: tato bhagavānākāśagarbho bodhisatvaḥ sarvaṃ jalpāpayatītya; uktamātre mukhabandhaṃ muktvā, mahāmaṇḍalaṃ darśayet, sarvatathāgatābhiṣekasamayaṃ codāharet, yāvad bhagavāṃstathāgatastu gata iti / tato yathāvibhavataḥ pūjān kṛtvā, sarvakāryāṇi sādhayediti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha</s>, causes [the possessed one] to speak everything — thus. The moment [this is] spoken, having removed the face-covering, one should show the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, and should proclaim the consecration-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, up to: 'the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, is thus-gone' — thus. Then, having made offerings according to one's means, one should accomplish all tasks.
<s>Mudrā</s>
Now here are the knowledge-<s>mudrā</s>s:

children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>Vajragarbha</s> great <s>mudrā</s>, perfectly concentrated,

children.text: nidhānaṃ khanate yatra nidhānaṃ tatra paśyati // 1 //
children.translated_text: wherever one digs for a treasure, one sees the treasure there. (1)

children.text: badhvā tu samayāgrīm vai nidhānaṃ yatra vidyate /
children.translated_text: Having bound the foremost pledge[-<s>mudrā</s>], wherever a treasure exists,

children.text: pīḍayet tatra tāṃ mudrāṃ svayamuttiṣṭhate tadā // 2 //
children.translated_text: one should press that <s>mudrā</s> there — [the treasure] then rises up by itself. (2)
Meditating with the <s>Vajragarbha</s> <s>samādhi</s>, perfectly concentrated,

children.text: manasā caiva jānāti nidhānaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati // 3 //
children.translated_text: one knows even with the mind where the treasure stands. (3)
Having bound the karma-<s>mudrā</s>, through the <s>Vajragarbha</s> <s>samādhi</s>,
wherever one enters with that <s>mudrā</s>, one should mark the treasure there. (4)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Oṃ — Great gem-jewel — enter! Hūṃ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — Gem — press — reveal!
Oṃ — Jewel-<s>samādhi</s> — speak!
Oṃ — Jewel-entry — reveal!

children.text: mahāmudrāṃ samādhāya yatra kāyaṃ tu veṣṭayet /
children.translated_text: Having established the great <s>mudrā</s>, wherever the body quivers,
one should know that there is a jewel-treasure — [this is for] those of the pledge-nature. (1)

children.text: badhvā tu samayāgrīm vai yatrāviśya parisphuṭet /
children.translated_text: Having bound the foremost pledge[-<s>mudrā</s>], wherever, having entered, it bursts open,
there one should know the treasure exists — it will be composed of great jewels. (2)

children.text: samādhimudrāṃ badhvā vai yadyāviśya svayaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>samādhi</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, if, having entered, one spontaneously
speaks where the treasure is — it will be composed of great jewels. (3)

body.text:
karmamudrāṃ tu badhvā vai yadāviśya paramparaṃ /
hastau bandhe tu samayānnidhintatra vinirdeśed // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Having bound the karma-<s>mudrā</s>, if, having entered in succession,
the hands [form] the binding of the pledge — one should point out the treasure there. (4)
Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Oṃ — Great jewel-body — reveal the jewel!

body.text: oṃ ākāśagarbha maṇiratna sphuṭa sphuṭa yatra nidhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ — <s>Ākāśagarbha</s> — gem-jewel — burst, burst — wherever the treasure is!
Oṃ — Gem-jewel-knowledge — speak spontaneously!
Oṃ — Again — pledge-binding — reveal yourself!

children.text: badhvā tu vai mahāmudrāṃ yatrāśaṅkā bhavettathā /
children.translated_text: Having bound the great <s>mudrā</s>, wherever suspicion arises,
one should know through knowledge that there is a treasure of jewel-origin. (1)
Wherever suspicion arises, there one should bind the foremost pledge[-<s>mudrā</s>];
when release occurs by itself, one should indicate the treasure there. (2)

children.text: samādhimudrāṃ badhvā vai śaṅkā yatra bhaveddhruvā /
children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>samādhi</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, wherever the suspicion is firm,
having generated knowledge, one should know — there the treasure exists eternally. (3)

children.text: yatra bhūyo bhavecchaṅkā karmamudrāṃ tu tatra vai /
badhnīyād vidhivattāṃ tu sphuṭejjñeyo nidhiḥ punaḥ // 4 //

body.text: oṃ sarvakarmāṇi sphoṭaya darśaya nidhi bandhotkṣipa //

children.text: badhvā samayāgrīn vai nidhiṃ tu parimārgayet /
badhvā karmamayīṃ mudrāṃ nidhiṃ tu parimārgayet /
yatrasthaḥ karmamudrāṃ tu bhrāmayet tatra nirdiśet // 4 //
badhvā tu samayāgrīn vai rāmayaṃstu striyantathā /

body.text:
badhvā tu karmamudrāṃ vai dvayendriyasamādhitaḥ /
sphuṭedyatra tu sā mudrā nidhintatra vinirdiśed // iti // 4 //

children.text: sā evāṅgu ṣṭhavajreṇa maṇiṃ dadyād hṛdi sthitaṃ // 2 //
kuḍmalāgryā maṇiṃ badhvā lokeśo dhanado bhavet /
sā eva vali[tāṃ kṛtvā] tarjanyā tarjanī grahā /
sā eva hāsasaṃsthā tu līlayā parivartitā // 17 //
sa tu sandhāya vācā vai svājñayā harate dhanaṃ /
madhyamā maṇiyogena tā eva tu vikalpitāḥ // 28 //

body.text: atha mahāmaṇikuladharmamudrājñānaṃ bhavanti, traḥ, graḥ, triḥ, hrīḥ, śrīḥ, iḥ, raḥ haḥ, dhrīḥ dhīḥ, kṛ, vā, ro, ḍhaḥ, ya, aḥ /
atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatābhiṣekadhāraṇīsamayasaṃbhavaratnādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemāṃ svamudrāmabhāṣat oṃ vajraratnastūpe hūṃ //
atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatva imāṃ svakulasaṃbhavāṃ mudrāmabhāṣat oṃ vajrābhiṣekamāle abhiṣiñca samaye hūṃ //
atha vajragarbho bodhisatvo mahāsatva imāṃ svamudrāmabhāṣat oṃ vajraratnābhiṣeke hūṃ //
atha vajranetro bodhisatvo mahāsatva imāṃ svamudrāmabhāṣat oṃ vajradharmābhiṣiñca māṃ //
atha vajraviśvo bodhisatvo mahāsatva imāṃ svamudrāmabhāṣat oṃ sarvābhiṣekapūjāsamaye hūṃ //
atha bhagavānāryākāśagarbho bodhisatvo mahāsatva idaṃ svakulasamayamudrāmaṇḍalamabhāṣat /

children.text: paryaṅkasthaṃ maṇiṃ pūrva vajradhātoḥ puro likhet /
oṃ sarvārthasiddhiprade mahāvajraratnasamaya maṇi sarvārthān me sādhaya dhāraṇī hū //

body.text: oṃ vajramaṇiratnanetrānaya vaśīkuru sarvārthasaṃpadaḥ śīghraṃ dṛṣṭyāṅkuśī hūṃ //
oṃ maṇiratnasūrye jvālaya sarva mahātejini hūṃ //
oṃ vajramaṇiratna draṃṣṭrākarāle hara hara hūṃ //

athātra maṇiguhyamaṇḍale yathāvatkarma kṛtvā, śiṣyāṃ praveya, brūyāt / "na tvayā kasyacidayaṃ nayo vaktavyaḥ / mā te mahādāri dyamakālakriyā narakapatanaṃ syād" , ityuktvā svamaṇisamayajñānānyutpādayet /
body.translated_text: Now here, having duly performed the action in the jewel-secret-<s>maṇḍala</s>, one should lead the disciples in and say: 'You must not speak this method to anyone — lest a great and terrible untimely death befall you, or a fall into hell.' Having said this, one should generate the self-jewel-pledge-<s>jñāna</s>s.
<s>Mudrā</s>

children.translated_text: Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-jewel in the sky, by the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-<s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: ātmanastu lalāṭe vai sthāpya rājā bhaveddhruvaṃ // 1 //
children.translated_text: and having placed it on one's own forehead — one certainly becomes a king. (1)
Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-jewel, one should bind the foremost pledge[-<s>mudrā</s>];
having placed it at the consecration-sites — kingship is certainly attained. (2)
Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-jewel, by the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-<s>samādhi</s>,
having installed that <s>jñāna</s>-jewel — one becomes a self-made king. (3)

body.text:
vajraratnaṃ nabhe likhya karmamudrāṃ tu bandhayet /
svasthāne tatpratiṣṭhāpya bhavedrājā svayaṃ kṛta // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-jewel in the sky, one should bind the activity-<s>mudrā</s>;
having installed it at one's own site — one becomes a self-made king. Thus ends [the section]. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Great <s>vajra</s>-jewel — consecrate me!

body.translated_text: Pledge-jewel — consecrate me!
<s>Dharma</s>-jewel — consecrate me!
Activity-jewel — consecrate me!

body.text: vajraratnaṃ tu hṛdaye mahāmudrāṃ tu bhāvayet /
body.translated_text: One should meditate on the <s>vajra</s>-jewel at the heart, [with] the great <s>mudrā</s>;
meditating thus, one attains the supremely wonderful consecration. (1)

children.translated_text: One should meditate on the <s>vajra</s>-jewel at the forehead, well-concentrated;

children.text: badhvā vai ratnavajrāntu bhavedrājā tu sarvataḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: having bound the jewel-<s>vajra</s>, one becomes king over all. (2)
The <s>vajra</s>-jewel at the tongue, by the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-<s>samādhi</s> —
meditating thus, one attains the consecration and the sovereignty of <s>Dharma</s>. (3)

body.text:
vajraratnaṃ svamuṣṇīṣe bhāvayaṃ susamāhitaḥ /
badhvā vai karmamudrāṃ tu bhavedrājā sukarmakṛd // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
One should meditate on the <s>vajra</s>-jewel at one's own <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance), well-concentrated;
having bound the activity-<s>mudrā</s> — one becomes a king, a doer of good deeds. Thus ends [the section]. (4)

children.translated_text: Now, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Oṃ — <s>vajra</s>-jewel-heart — consecrate! Hoḥ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — <s>vajra</s>-jewel-consecration! Traḥ!
Oṃ — <s>vajra</s>-jewel-<s>jñāna</s> — consecrate! Vaṃ!
Oṃ — <s>vajra</s>-jewel-<s>uṣṇīṣa</s> — empower me!

children.translated_text: Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-jewel on cloth and the like, by one's own self,
and meditating on the great <s>mudrā</s> — that one becomes a great king. (1)
Having drawn the [<s>vajra</s>-jewel] on cloth and the like — the unsurpassed,
and meditating on the <s>sattva</s>-<s>vajra</s> — one becomes the lord of pledges. (2)
Having drawn the <s>vajra</s>-jewel on cloth and the like, by one's own self,
and meditating on the <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>mudrā</s> — one certainly becomes the lord of <s>Dharma</s>. (3)

body.text:
paṭādiṣu samālikhya vajraratnamanuttaraṃ /
bhāvayetkarmamudrāṃ tu bhavetkarmādhipaḥ svayam // iti // // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Having drawn the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-jewel on cloth and the like,
and meditating on the activity-<s>mudrā</s> — one becomes the sovereign of all activities. Thus ends [the section]. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
<s>Vajra</s>-jewel[-image] — empower!

body.translated_text: <s>Vajra</s>-jewel-image — establish!
<s>Vajra</s>-jewel-image — enter!
<s>Vajra</s>-jewel-image — act!

children.text: sauvarṇa vātha raupyaṃ vajraratnaṃ tu bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: One should meditate on a golden or silver <s>vajra</s>-jewel,
or one made of other gems — meditating at the heart, one is consecrated. (1)
A golden [image] or one of other gems — the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-jewel —

children.text: sthāpya bhūyo lalāṭe tu bhavedrājā mahādhanaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: having placed it again on the forehead, one becomes a king of great wealth. (2)
A golden [image] or one of other gems — one should meditate on the <s>vajra</s>-jewel;

children.text: svamukhe caiva prakṣipya bhavedvācāṃ patistu saḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: having cast it into one's own mouth, that one becomes the lord of speech. (3)

body.text:
sauvarṇamanyaratnaṃ vā vajraratnantu bhāvayet /
uṣṇīṣe bhāvayaṃ bhūyo sarvakarmapatirbhaved // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
A golden [image] or one of other gems — one should meditate on the <s>vajra</s>-jewel;
meditating on the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> again — one becomes the lord of all activities. Thus ends [the section]. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Oṃ — <s>vajra</s>-jewel-heart-ornament! Hūṃ!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — <s>vajra</s>-jewel-consecration, granter of great aims!
Oṃ — <s>vajra</s>-jewel, lord of speech!
Oṃ — <s>vajra</s>-jewel, great lord of activities!
Then one should teach the jewel-family pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-secret-<s>jñāna</s>:

children.translated_text: Having bound the great <s>vajra</s>-jewel, that jewel likewise into the female organ,
inserting it and meditating on the great <s>mudrā</s> — one attains <s>siddhi</s>. (1)
Having bound the foremost pledge-jewel, into the female organ with the foremost pledge-
binding — there is <s>siddhi</s> in all consecrations. (2)
Having bound the great <s>vajra</s>-jewel and meditating on the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>,
inserting that jewel into the female organ — there is unsurpassed <s>siddhi</s>. (3)

body.text:
karmamudrāmaṇiṃ vidhvā strībhage karmamudrayā /
bandhayā tu bhavetsiddhiḥ sarvakarmasvanuttaram // iti // 4 //
body.translated_text:
Having inserted the activity-<s>mudrā</s>-jewel into the female organ with the activity-<s>mudrā</s>-
binding — there is <s>siddhi</s>, unsurpassed in all activities. Thus ends [the section]. (4)

children.translated_text: Therein, these are their heart[-<s>mantra</s>s]:
Oṃ — great <s>siddhi</s>!

body.translated_text: Oṃ — pledge-consecration-<s>siddhi</s>!
Oṃ — <s>dharma</s>-<s>siddhi</s>!
Oṃ — activity-<s>siddhi</s>!
Now here follows the great <s>mudrā</s>-binding for the <s>maṇḍala</s>:

children.translated_text: Having bound the jewel-<s>vajra</s>-sprout, the last finger of the middle ones
extended and joined — having placed it at the crown, it grants the foremost <s>siddhi</s>. (1)
Establishing the <s>vajra</s>-bind, the tips knotted and entwining,
the two thumbs and ring fingers forming a <s>vajra</s>, revolving — it grants consecration. (2)
By the method of the <s>vajra</s>-jewel, that same [<s>mudrā</s>] is revolved;
with the index-finger tips face-to-face, in conjunction — that one grants the consecration. (3)
That same [<s>mudrā</s>], with the thumbs and forefingers, by the method of <s>dharma</s>-<s>vajra</s>,
having bound it, placed at the forehead — grants the great <s>dharma</s>-consecration. (4)
Establishing the activity-<s>vajra</s>, revolving it at the forehead,
and placing the garland of all consecrations — one consecrates. (5)
The <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s> <s>mudrā</s>, the pledge-<s>mudrā</s> born of the <s>vajra</s>-realm,
having bound it as the jewel-installation — one is consecrated at the forehead. (6)
Thumbs in a cross-legged bind, the two index fingers joined,
with the jewel-tips brought together — one obtains the great <s>vajra</s>-jewel. (7)
Establishing the <s>vajra</s>-bind, one should extend the jewel-fist;
the jewel with the two middle fingers — grants the jewel-garland-consecration. (8)
Establishing the <s>vajra</s>-bind, the middle fingers joined with the jewel,
the two tips of the ring fingers unfolded — making a lotus, one attains <s>siddhi</s>. (9)
Having bound the jewel with the two middle fingers, all fingers raised upward,
meditating on jewels themselves — one becomes well-attended. (10)
Establishing the <s>vajra</s>-jewel, by the junction of [middle] fingers and thumbs,
the ring and little fingers alike — at the tongue in the mouth, it grants jewels. (11)

children.text: sā eva tarjanī vajrā tatsthā eva tathāṅku śī /
children.translated_text: That same [<s>mudrā</s>] with the <s>vajra</s>-index fingers standing in the same position, hook-shaped,
index finger drawing the index — it grants satisfaction. (12)
Having bound the jewel with the two middle fingers, standing with the tips contracted,
binding with the ring-finger tips, covered by the two thumbs — (13)

children.text: sā eva sūryāvartā tu mūrdhni bāhuprasāritā /
children.translated_text: that same [<s>mudrā</s>] as a sun-wheel, at the crown with arms extended,
the jewel as a banner-crest armlet — joined by the method of laughter. (14)

children.text: tābhiḥ padmaṃ tu saṃbhāvya madhyamāmyāṃ maṇīkṛtā // 15 // //
children.translated_text: with them forming a lotus — the jewel made by the two middle [fingers]. (15)

body.translated_text: Establishing the <s>vajra</s>-bind, with the elder and ring [fingers] raised tip-upward,

children.translated_text: That same [<s>mudrā</s>], with the last [fingers] offering, employed with the <s>vajra</s>-sheath,
and with the <s>vajra</s>-wheel method — that same [<s>mudrā</s>] drawn out from the mouth. (16)
Having bound the jewel-<s>vajra</s>-sprout, one should extend all fingers;

children.text: tāṃ tu mūrdhni pratiṣṭhāpya ratnavṛṣṭistu varṣayet // 17 //
children.translated_text: having installed it at the crown — it rains a jewel-shower. (17)

body.text:
sā eva cakrayogā tu hṛdi ratnadvidhīkṛtā /
maṇigrahāgradaṃṣṭrā tu muṣṭirmadhyamasandhite // ti // 18 //
body.translated_text:
That same [<s>mudrā</s>] with the wheel-method, the jewel at the heart split in two;
the jewel-grasping fang-tip, a fist joined at the middle. Thus ends [the section]. (18)
Then one should teach the pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>jñāna</s>:

children.translated_text: These very great <s>mudrā</s>s, having made them cupped (joined palm-to-palm), one should bind;
secret of secrets, in brief — they grant <s>siddhi</s> fourfold. Thus ends [the section].

children.text: yathāvad vajraguhye tu sarvakālaṃ na bandhayet /
children.translated_text: As prescribed in the <s>vajra</s>-secret, one should not bind [them] at all times;

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi dharbhamudrāḥ samāsata // iti //
children.translated_text: henceforth I shall teach the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s in brief. Thus ends [the section].

body.text:
traiḥ graiḥ haiḥ saiḥ gryaḥ kha dvyaiḥ haiḥ
dhraiḥ dhyaiḥ kraiḥ vaiḥ krayaiḥ rai yyaḥ maiḥ /
body.translated_text:
Traiḥ graiḥ haiḥ saiḥ gryaḥ kha dvyaiḥ haiḥ
dhraiḥ dhyaiḥ kraiḥ vaiḥ krayaiḥ rai yyaḥ maiḥ —
the secret-of-secrets foremost fist, split in two — accomplishes all activities. Thus ends [the section].
From the <s>Sarvatathāgatakarmasamaya</s>, the great ritual king, the detailed procedure of the jewel-secret-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> is completed.

body.text:
CHAPTER 21 JNANA-MANDALA-VIDHI-VISTARA
Emanation of deiteis from samadhi
body.translated_text:
Chapter 21: Detailed Procedure of the <s>Jñāna</s>-<s>Maṇḍala</s>
Emanation of deities from <s>samādhi</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi sarvatathāgatābhiṣekajñānasamayasaṃbhavādhiṣṭhānannāma samādhiṃ samāpadyemaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekajñānottama hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, once again entering the <s>samādhi</s> called 'the empowerment born from the consecration-<s>jñāna</s>-pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' uttered this, his own supreme <s>vidyā</s>: Oṃ — Supreme consecration-<s>jñāna</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s! Hūṃ!

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatva imaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ vajrajñānābhiṣekasamaya hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, uttered this, his own supreme <s>vidyā</s>: Oṃ — <s>Vajra</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-consecration-pledge! Hūṃ!

body.text: atha vajragarbho bodhisatvo mahāsatva imaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ maṇiratnābhiṣekajñāna hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajragarbha</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, uttered this, his own supreme <s>vidyā</s>: Oṃ — Jewel-gem-consecration-<s>jñāna</s>! Hūṃ!

body.text: atha vajranetro bodhisatvo mahāsatva imaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ dharmābhiṣekajñānaṃ hūṃ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajranetra</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, uttered this, his own supreme <s>vidyā</s>: Oṃ — <s>Dharma</s>-consecration-<s>jñāna</s>! Hūṃ!

body.text: atha vajraviśvo bodhisattvo mahāsatvaḥ imaṃ svavidyottamamabhāṣat oṃ sarvābhiṣekajñāna hūṃ //

Delineation of the <s>maṇḍala</s>
Then <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, uttered this, his own family-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>:

children.translated_text: Now henceforth I shall teach the supreme <s>jñāna</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>,
resembling the <s>vajra</s>-realm, called the jewel-<s>jñāna</s>. (1)

the signs at the heart should be drawn by the method of the <s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>. Thus ends [the section]. (2)

body.text: athātra maṇḍale yathāvad vidhivistaraṃ kṛtvā, śiṣyānevaṃ brūyāt / "na tvayā adṛṣṭadharmamaṇḍalasya vaktavyaṃ / mā te maraṇakālaḥ śīghramevāsiddhasya syād" , ityuktvā, maṇikuladharmajñānānyutpādayet /
body.translated_text: Now here, having duly performed the detailed procedure in the <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should say to the disciples: 'You must not speak of the unseen <s>dharma</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s> — lest the time of death come swiftly upon you, the unaccomplished.' Having said this, one should generate the jewel-family <s>dharma</s>-<s>jñāna</s>s.

Having drawn <s>Vajragarbha</s> on cloth and the like, in <s>samādhi</s>,

Having drawn <s>Vajragarbha</s> on cloth and the like, visualizing,

In the sky or in another place, meditating well-concentrated,

CHAPTER 22 KARMA-MANDALA-VIDHI-VISTARA
Emanation of deities from samadhi

body.translated_text: CHAPTER 23: THE DETAILED PROCEDURE OF ACCOMPLISHMENT THROUGH ALL RITUAL METHODS (<s>SARVA-KALPOPAYA-SIDDHI-VIDHI-VISTARA-TANTRA</s>)

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābrodhisatva idaṃ sarvatathāgatamahātatvavidhivistaratantramudājahāra / tatra prathamaṃ tāvat mahāmudrottamasiddhitantraṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, proclaimed this detailed tantra of the great reality-procedure of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, first of all, there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the great <s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Having bound the great <s>mudrā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in all the realms of space,
empowering <s>Buddha</s>-images, one should cause [them] to enter into one's own heart.' (1)
'If one desires the supreme and auspicious [attainment] in this very birth,

children.text: buddhatvaṃ tena kāmedaṃ na cet siddhiryathopari // 2 //
children.translated_text: one should desire <s>Buddha</s>hood through this; if not, [one obtains] accomplishment as described above.' (2)
'Having established the great <s>mudrā</s>, proclaiming the great reality,
one should contemplate everything, word by word, through union with beings.' (1)

children.text: ihaiva janmani padaṃ yadīcchet sauritvaṃ śubhaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'If one desires in this very birth the auspicious state of lordship,
one should desire it for oneself through this; if not, [one obtains] accomplishment as described above.' (2)

body.translated_text: Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the pledge <s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Contemplating "Just as <s>Vajradhara</s> is accomplished, so am I,"
one attains the lordship of a <s>Buddha</s>; if not, [one obtains] accomplishment as described above.'

body.translated_text: Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the <s>dharma</s> <s>mudrā</s>:

children.text: svabhāvaśuddhyā vācā vai sarvadharmā iti brūvan /
children.translated_text: 'Declaring by speech, "All <s>dharma</s>s are pure by nature,"
one attains the lordship of a <s>Buddha</s>; if not, [one obtains] accomplishment as described above.'
Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the action <s>mudrā</s>:
'Purifying all actions due to the universal purity of all,
one attains the lordship of a <s>Buddha</s>; if not, [one obtains] accomplishment as described above.'

body.translated_text: The supreme accomplishments of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> proclaimed the supreme accomplishment tantra of his own family:

children.translated_text: 'For the sake of all beings, by the Buddha's command, through the practice of all accomplishments,
accomplishing the great <s>mudrā</s> — [one attains] <s>Buddha</s>hood in this very birth.'

body.translated_text: Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the pledge [<s>mudrā</s>]:

children.translated_text: 'Contemplating "Just as <s>Vajradhara</s> is accomplished, so am I,"
through the practice of the great <s>mudrā</s>, one attains lordship in an instant.'
Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the <s>dharma</s> <s>mudrā</s>:

children.text: anakṣareṣu dharmeṣu prapañco na hi vidyate /
children.translated_text: 'In <s>dharma</s>s that are without syllables, conceptual elaboration does not exist;

children.text: imaṃ vadaṃstu dharmāgrīṃ bhāvayan sauritāṃ brajed // iti //
children.translated_text: speaking this foremost <s>dharma</s>, contemplating, one would attain lordship.'
Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the action <s>mudrā</s>:

children.text: yatkaroti hi karma vai śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubhaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever action one performs, whether virtuous or non-virtuous,
offering it to the Conquerors, one would attain lordship in an instant.'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ padmakulottamasiddhitantramudājahāra / tatra prathamantāvanmahāmudrottamasiddhitantraṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, proclaimed the supreme accomplishment tantra of the <s>Padma</s> (Lotus) family. Therein, first of all, there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the great <s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: '<s>Rāga</s> (passion) is pure by nature; it is rejected by the <s>tīrthika</s>s (non-Buddhist teachers);

children.text: tasyāvirāgo dharmo 'smiṃ mahāyāne tu sidhyatī- // ti //
children.translated_text: non-attachment to it is the <s>dharma</s> — in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, this [passion itself] is accomplished.'

body.translated_text: Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the pledge <s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Cultivating great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), through firm union in <s>samādhi</s>,
pervading [all beings] through the method of practice, one would attain lordship in an instant.'

body.translated_text: Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the <s>dharma</s> <s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: 'One should teach this doctrine: "Passion is pure by nature" —
having attained the perfection of passion (<s>rāga-pāramitā</s>), one would attain lordship in an instant.'

body.translated_text: Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the action <s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Through seeing and touching, through hearing and recollecting,
may I become for all beings the abode that ends all suffering.'

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvo maṇikulottamasiddhitantramudājahāra / tatra mahāmudrottamasiddhitantraṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, proclaimed the supreme accomplishment tantra of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Jewel) family. Therein, there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the great <s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: '"May I become the consecration of all <s>Buddha</s>s, like <s>Vajragarbha</s>" —
contemplating and visualizing thus, one attains lordship in an instant.'
Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the pledge <s>mudrā</s>:
'"May I become the fulfiller of all wishes of all beings,
equal to <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>" — one attains lordship in an instant.'
Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the <s>dharma</s> <s>mudrā</s>:
'Having abandoned one's own [possessions], joyfully giving wealth and gifts,
uttering the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s> — one attains lordship in this [very life].'
Then there is the supreme accomplishment tantra of the action <s>mudrā</s>:
'For the benefit of the destitute, devoted to the production of wealth,
through effort one attains lordship; if not, [one obtains] accomplishment as described above.'

body.translated_text: The detailed procedure for attaining supreme accomplishment of <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>bodhisattva</s>s through the <s>mudrā</s>s of all families.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ punarapi sarvatathāgata[samayasi]ddhitantramudājahāra / tatrāyaṃ sarvatathāgatasamayasiddhitantraṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, again proclaimed the accomplishment tantra of the pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the accomplishment tantra of the pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text: 'One whose attainment is through passion — one should purify that one through passion itself;
thus the great <s>mudrā</s> of the <s>Buddha</s> is declared as the pledge of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge).'

body.translated_text: Then there is the accomplishment tantra of the pledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Non-attachment to desires — this is the great pledge and doctrine;
purified in the <s>Tathāgata</s> family, not to be transgressed even by the Conquerors.'

body.translated_text: Then there is the accomplishment tantra of the pledge of the <s>Vajra</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'For one who is without anger, the display of great wrath for the sake of beings —
in the great <s>Vajra</s> family, this is the pledge difficult to transgress.'

body.translated_text: Then there is the accomplishment tantra of the pledge of the <s>Padma</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Through the knowledge of natural purity, one performs what must be done;
in the great <s>Padma</s> family, this is the pledge difficult to transgress.'

body.translated_text: Then there is the accomplishment tantra of the pledge of the <s>Ratna</s> (Jewel) family:

children.text: alpatve vā bahutve vā yathābhirucitaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whether in small measure or great, according to one's inclination,

children.text: avaśyo divasaḥ kāryo dānena samayo hyayam // iti //
children.translated_text: a day must necessarily be devoted to giving — for this is the pledge.'

body.translated_text: The detailed procedure tantra of the pledge of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, proclaimed the accomplishment tantra of the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment tantra of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.text: buddho dharma iti khyāta ityuktvā dharmatākṣaraṃ /
children.translated_text: '"The <s>Buddha</s> is the <s>Dharma</s>" — having declared this, [one utters] the syllable of <s>dharmatā</s> (reality);
this is the supreme doctrine of the knowledge of the great <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>.'
Therein, this is the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family:
'There is no <s>dharma</s> more faith-inspiring than passion, bestowing all happiness;
in the <s>Tathāgata</s> family too, this <s>dharma</s> is the supreme bestower of accomplishment.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Vajra</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of purifying by the <s>Buddha</s>'s command, or likewise for the purpose of protecting beings —
even one who is without anger, slaying the corrupted ones, attains purity.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Padma</s> family:

children.text: aliptaṃ salilaiḥ padmaṃ tathā rāgo na duṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'The lotus is unstained by water; likewise, passion does not corrupt;
thus speaking, performing prohibited actions, one is not stained by sins.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the accomplishment tantra of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Jewel) family:

children.text: dānātsamo na dharmo 'sti pratipattyā bravīti hi /
children.translated_text: 'There is no <s>dharma</s> equal to giving — this one declares through practice;
in the great <s>Maṇi</s> family, this <s>dharma</s>; if not, [one obtains] accomplishment as described above.'

body.translated_text: The detailed procedure tantra of the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment of all families.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, proclaimed the action-accomplishment tantra of all <s>Tathāgata</s> families. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> action-accomplishment tantra:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>Buddha</s>hood of all beings and indeed their <s>bodhisattva</s>hood —
disciplining each as appropriate, the action-<s>mudrā</s> is the supreme bestower of accomplishment.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the action-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Through the four kinds of worship, always in fourfold yoga,
through the practice of the four times, performing actions, one should accomplish [them].'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the action-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Vajra</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Whatever actions one performs for the destruction of wicked beings —
in the action-<s>Vajra</s> family, this bestows all accomplishments.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the action-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Padma</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Giving fearlessness to the frightened, disciplining each as appropriate —
this is the action in the <s>Padma</s> family, bestowing <s>Buddha</s>-accomplishment.'

body.translated_text: Then [there is] the action-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Jewel) family:

children.translated_text: 'Consecration and likewise giving, fulfilling all wishes —

children.text: buddhānāṃ dehināṃ caiva karma sarvārthasādhakam // iti //
children.translated_text: of <s>Buddha</s>s and embodied beings, this is the action that accomplishes all purposes.'

body.translated_text: The detailed procedure tantra of the action-accomplishment of all families.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, proclaimed the tantra of the <s>dharmatā</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-knowledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s> families.
Therein, this is the <s>dharmatā</s>-knowledge-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>samādhi</s> of <s>Vajrasattva</s> is declared as the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of the <s>Buddha</s>s;
this is the <s>Buddha</s>hood of the <s>Buddha</s> — a <s>Buddha</s> does not come to be from anything else.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>dharmatā</s>-knowledge-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Contemplating the great <s>mudrā</s>, one should accomplish all <s>siddhi</s>s;
in the <s>Tathāgata</s> family too, this <s>dharmatā</s> is the supreme bestower of accomplishment.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>dharmatā</s>-knowledge-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Vajra</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Through the supreme pledges that have been bound, one should accomplish all actions;
through the practice of the great <s>mudrā</s>, one would attain <s>vajra</s>-accomplishment.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>dharmatā</s>-knowledge-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Padma</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Through the practice of the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, one should set in motion the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s;
accomplishing <s>dharma</s>s through this, [they become] of the nature of <s>dharmatā</s>-<s>vajra</s>.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>dharmatā</s>-knowledge-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Jewel) family:

children.translated_text: 'Through the practice of the action-<s>mudrā</s>, [with] the action-<s>vajra</s> established in the heart,
contemplating, one attains this <s>dharmatā</s> — one attains one's own action-nature.'

body.translated_text: The <s>dharmatā</s>-knowledge-accomplishment tantra of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, proclaimed the knowledge-accomplishment tantra of all <s>Tathāgata</s> families. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> knowledge-accomplishment tantra:

children.translated_text: 'Abiding in the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>Vajrasattva</s>, through the practice of moon-and-<s>vajra</s>,

children.text: yathā varṇau tu tau vetti tathā lokaṃ tu vetti saḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: just as one perceives those two colors, so one perceives the world.' (1)

children.text: śuddhe śuddhamiti jñeyaṃ pāṇḍare tu prabhāsvaraṃ /
children.translated_text: 'In the pure [color], one should know purity; in the white, luminosity;
in the red, passion; within, anger — whatever color [appears], that is its nature.' (2)

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the knowledge-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Having established the great <s>mudrā</s>, radiant with the moon-disc,

children.text: svayaṃ kāyaṃ yathā vetti tathā vedyaṃ jaganmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: just as one perceives one's own body, so one knows the mind of the world.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the knowledge-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Vajra</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'In the sky or in another place, when wrathful, [one sees] <s>maṇḍala</s>s;
whatever kind one perceives — one should know that such is the mind.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the knowledge-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Padma</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Seeing subtle rows of syllables in the sky and on the earth,

children.text: yādṛgvarṇa samāsena vetti cittaṃ sa tādṛśaṃ //
children.translated_text: whatever color [they are], in summary — one knows the mind to be likewise.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the knowledge-accomplishment tantra of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Jewel) family:

children.text: sarvalokaṃ nirīkṣan vai pratibhāso hi yādṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Observing the entire world, whatever reflection [appears],

children.text: paśyate tādṛśaṃ caiva jagaccittaṃ tu lakṣayed // iti //
children.translated_text: one sees it as such — one should discern the mind of the world.'
'These very <s>samāpatti</s>s (meditative attainments), their comings and goings,
acting and wandering — as one sees [them], such is the tradition.' (1)

children.text: yasya yasya ca satvasya samāpattyā tu cintayet /
children.translated_text: 'Of whatever being one contemplates through <s>samāpatti</s>,

children.text: tasya tasya tathā caiva sarvacittāni budhyatī- // 2 //
children.translated_text: of that very being, likewise, one awakens to all [their] mental states.' (2)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One, <s>Vajradhara</s>.
The detailed procedure tantra of the knowledge of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>bodhisattva</s>, proclaimed the accomplishment-knowledge tantra of all <s>Tathāgata</s> families. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> accomplishment-knowledge tantra:

children.translated_text: 'Through the yoga of empowering beings, the contemplation of oneself as a <s>Buddha</s>-image —
through this yoga of knowledge, one would attain <s>Buddha</s>-accomplishment.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the accomplishment-knowledge tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'In the sky or in another place, [seeing] white and yellow-colored <s>maṇḍala</s>s,
one sees oneself directly as a being with one's own <s>mudrā</s>.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the accomplishment-knowledge tantra of the <s>Vajra</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'In those very images, a dark [form] extends in the center;
this is the supreme accomplishment of the <s>Vajra</s> family — it manifests swiftly if one desires.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the accomplishment-knowledge tantra of the <s>Padma</s> family:

children.translated_text: 'Those very [forms appearing as] sky-blue, one sees in lotus shapes;
in the great <s>Padma</s> family, <s>vidyā</s>-accomplishments arise.'

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the accomplishment-knowledge tantra of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Jewel) family:

children.translated_text: in the sky or in another place — those very ones, pure as space,
glittering with circles of rays, are seen — one would attain accomplishment. Thus.
<s>Vajrasattva</s> and the other beings, radiant with moon-discs,
first show themselves in their own forms at the time of accomplishment.

body.translated_text: The tantra of the elaboration of the procedure of the accomplishment-knowledge of all families.
Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> set forth the tantra of the <s>abhijñā</s> (direct knowledge) accomplishment-knowledge-<s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-families.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>abhijñā</s>-accomplishment-knowledge:

children.translated_text: Established in the <s>Vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, visualizing <s>Tathāgata</s>s in the entire body
and <s>bodhisattva</s>s — one would manifest [them] from the body likewise.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family <s>abhijñā</s>-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>Vajrasattva</s> great <s>mudrā</s>, well-concentrated,
the practitioner attains the five <s>abhijñā</s>s (direct knowledges) by this procedure.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the divine eye-knowledge:

children.translated_text: Having established the great <s>mudrā</s>, one should invoke the eye-consciousness.
By that, whatever one contemplates, one sees even from afar.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.

children.translated_text: Having established the great <s>mudrā</s>, one should invoke the ear-consciousness.
By that, whatever matter one contemplates, one hears even from far away.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.

children.translated_text: Having established the great <s>mudrā</s>, one should invoke the mind-consciousness.

children.text: tena ya satvamudvīkṣet cittaṃ jānāti tasya saḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: By that, whichever being one observes, one knows the mind of that one. // 1 //

children.text: mahāmudrāṃ samādhāya ātmano vā parasya vā /
children.translated_text: Having established the great <s>mudrā</s>, of oneself or of another,

children.text: manasā paśyate rūpaṃ yato janma sa āvahed // 2 //
children.translated_text: one sees the form mentally — one should discern from where the birth [came]. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>.
Now the accomplishment of the knowledge of the modes of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) is as follows:

children.translated_text: Having established the great <s>mudrā</s>, whatever supernatural power one desires,

children.text: yatra vā tatra vā tadvai saṃdarśayetsamādhine- //
children.translated_text: wherever — one would display that through <s>samādhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Mahābodhicitta</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>vajra</s>-family <s>abhijñā</s>-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having bound the foremost <s>Trilokavijaya</s> [<s>mudrā</s>], well-concentrated,
the practitioner attains the five <s>abhijñā</s>s by this procedure. // 1 //
Wrathful, [performing] all tasks in proper sequence,
through the yoga of the divine eye and the rest, one becomes omniscient in an instant. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the lotus-family <s>abhijñā</s>-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having joined the foremost <s>mudrā</s> of world-discipline, well-concentrated,
the practitioner attains the five <s>abhijñā</s>s by this procedure. // 1 //
Attached to passion, properly, in due sequence,
through the yoga of the divine eye and the rest, one will become omniscient. // 2 //

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Lokeśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the jewel-family <s>abhijñā</s>-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>mudrā</s> of the accomplishment of all purposes, well-concentrated,
the practitioner attains the five <s>abhijñā</s>s by this procedure. // 1 //
Performing <s>Buddha</s>-worship, in due sequence,
through the yoga of the divine eye and the rest, one sees the five <s>abhijñā</s>s.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Ākāśagarbha</s>.
The tantra of the elaboration of the procedure of the <s>abhijñā</s>-knowledge of all families.

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ sarvatathāgatakulasatyasiddhitantramudājahāra / tatra tathāgatasatyasiddhitantraṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> set forth the tantra of the truth-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-families. Therein, the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-truth-accomplishment is as follows:

children.translated_text: With speech that conforms to truth, the performance of oaths —
guarding the great truth, one would quickly attain <s>Buddha</s>hood.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family truth-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Oaths should be made as arising from the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family, in the pledge.
Guarding the <s>vajra</s>-truth, one attains the supreme accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>vajra</s>-family truth-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having made inviolable oaths regarding <s>vajra</s>-bearing,
one should guard this truth, if one desires the supreme accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the lotus-family truth-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having made oaths regarding the true <s>Dharma</s>, the supreme of the great lotus family,
one should guard the truth-pledge, if one desires the supreme accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradharma</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the jewel-family truth-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having made inviolable oaths regarding <s>Buddha</s>-worship,
one should guard the supreme truth — one will obtain consecration.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Buddhapūja</s>.
The tantra of the oath-accomplishment of all families.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> set forth the tantra of the reality-accomplishment of the pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the tantra of the reality-accomplishment of the pledge of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text: When 'I am the pledge' (<s>samayo 'ham</s>) is uttered, all <s>mudrā</s>s, even in [all] families,

children.text: svayaṃ badhvā dṛḍhaṃ yānti tataḥ paścādasādhitā //
children.translated_text: having bound themselves firmly, come — thereafter [they are] unaccomplished [no more].

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Mahāsamayasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family pledge-reality-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: When 'I am delight' (<s>suratas tvam</s>) is uttered, all <s>mudrā</s>s, [previously] unaccomplished,

children.text: svayaṃ badhvā tu sidhyante tatvacodān mahātmana //
children.translated_text: having bound themselves, are accomplished — urged by the reality, O great being.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Mahāsamayasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>vajra</s>-family pledge-reality-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: By a single 'hūṃ' utterance alone, all <s>mudrā</s>s in brief

children.text: svayaṃ bandhed vandhayedvāpi svayaṃ vāpi parasya ve- // ti //
children.translated_text: bind themselves or are bound — for oneself or for another. Thus.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the lotus-family pledge-reality-accomplishment:

children.text: sarvaśuddha iti prokte svato vāpi parasya vā /
children.translated_text: When 'all-pure' (<s>sarvaśuddha</s>) is uttered, of oneself or of another,

children.text: strīsaṅgādyāstu saṃyogā na mokṣaṃ yānti sarvaśa // iti //
children.translated_text: the unions beginning with the union with women do not go to release in any way. Thus.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the jewel-family pledge-reality-accomplishment:
By the <s>oṃkāra</s> alone, all <s>mudrā</s>s are accomplished in brief.
In all worlds, the foremost offerings of the Self-Existent Ones. Thus.
The tantra of the elaboration of the procedure of the reality-accomplishment-<s>mudrā</s> of the pledge of all families.

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ sarvatathāgatasiddhimudrātantramudājahāra / tatra sarvatathāgatasiddhitantraṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> set forth the tantra of the accomplishment-<s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, the tantra of the accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s is as follows:

children.translated_text: Having joined the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, recollecting the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
accomplishing — one is accomplished quickly; even <s>Buddha</s>-awakening is made firm.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>Vajrasattva</s> great <s>mudrā</s> and meditating,

children.text: purato vajrasatvaṃ ca siddhiḥ śīghratarā bhavet //
children.translated_text: on <s>Vajrasattva</s> before one — the accomplishment becomes exceedingly swift.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>vajra</s>-family accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having bound the foremost pledge with the <s>Vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: bhāvayan vajrasatvaṃ ca siddhistu dviguṇā bhavet //
children.translated_text: meditating on <s>Vajrasattva</s> — the accomplishment becomes doubled.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the lotus-family accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>dharma</s>-constituted <s>mudrā</s>, with the <s>Lokeśvara</s>-<s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: bhāvayan lokanāthaṃ ca siddhistu dviguṇā bhavet //
children.translated_text: meditating on the Lord of the World — the accomplishment becomes doubled.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the jewel-family accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having established the activity-<s>mudrā</s>, with the <s>Vajragarbha</s>-<s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: bhāvayan vajragarbhaṃ ca siddhistu dviguṇā bhavet //
children.translated_text: meditating on <s>Vajragarbha</s> — the accomplishment becomes doubled.

body.translated_text: The tantra of the elaboration of the accomplishment-procedure of all families.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> set forth the tantra of the accomplishment-practice of all accomplishments of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the tantra of the accomplishment-practice of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text: For oneself or for another, the practitioner of <s>Buddha</s>-recollection,

children.text: badhvā vai sarvamudrāstu tataḥ sidhyanti tatkṣaṇād //
children.translated_text: having bound all <s>mudrā</s>s — they are accomplished from that instant.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the accomplishment-practice of all accomplishments of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family and the rest:

children.translated_text: One should accomplish all <s>mudrā</s>s, meditating 'I am desire' (<s>kāmo 'ham</s>),
by the application of <s>vajra</s>-recitation — the foremost practice of all accomplishments.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the accomplishment-practice of all accomplishments of the <s>vajra</s>-family:

children.translated_text: Meditating on oneself as a <s>vajra</s>-image, well-concentrated,
one should bind all <s>mudrā</s>s — they go to accomplishment from that instant.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatavajra</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the accomplishment-practice of all accomplishments of the lotus-family:

children.translated_text: Meditating on oneself as a lotus-image, with oneself,
accomplishment consisting of all wisdom is remembered in the great lotus-family.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the accomplishment-practice of all accomplishments of the jewel-family:

children.translated_text: One should meditate on oneself as a blazing jewel-gem,
accomplishment consisting of all worship is remembered in the great jewel-family.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Ākāśagarbha</s>.
