The tantra of the elaboration of the procedure of the supreme accomplishment of all families.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> set forth the tantra of the empowerment-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-empowerment-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>Vajradhātvīśvarī</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, well-concentrated,
placing it at the heart, the <s>ūrṇā</s> (forehead-mark), the throat, and the crown — one is empowered by the <s>Buddha</s>s.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family empowerment-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having made firm the <s>Sattvavajrī</s>, with the <s>Vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>,
placing it at the heart, the <s>ūrṇā</s>, the throat, and the crown — one is empowered.
Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>vajra</s>-family empowerment-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>vajra</s>-huṃkāra-<s>mudrā</s>, well-concentrated,
stationed at the heart, the <s>ūrṇā</s>, the throat, and the crown — the empowerment[-stations] from that instant.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajranātha</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the lotus-family empowerment-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having made firm the <s>vajra</s>-lotus, with the <s>Lokeśvara</s>-<s>samādhi</s>,
stationed at the heart, the <s>ūrṇā</s>, the throat, and the crown — one should arrange for self-empowerment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the jewel-family empowerment-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having bound the great <s>vajra</s>-jewel, with the <s>Vajragarbha</s>-<s>samādhi</s>,
stationed at the heart, the <s>ūrṇā</s>, the throat, and the crown — one should arrange for self-empowerment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajragarbha</s>.
The tantra of the elaboration of the empowerment-procedure of all families.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> set forth the tantra of the consecration-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-consecration-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having established the <s>vajra</s>-jewel, placed at the forehead,
performing with both <s>vajra</s>-jewels — one becomes consecrated by the <s>Jina</s>s (Victors).

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family consecration-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Beginning with <s>Vajradhātvīśvarī</s> and the rest, with the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>mudrā</s>s in front,
proceeding on four sides with the garland — one is consecrated. Thus.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>vajra</s>-family consecration-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having joined the <s>vajra</s>-consecration-garland, placed at the forehead,
by that garland-consecration, one is consecrated by the <s>vajra</s>-holder. Thus.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the lotus-family consecration-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having established the <s>Dharmavajrī</s>, placed in front at the head,
consecrated by <s>Buddha</s>s thereby — one is consecrated in the sovereignty of <s>Lokeśvara</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the jewel-family consecration-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-sprout, placed at the forehead,
consecrated by <s>Buddha</s>s thereby — one is consecrated in the sovereignty of worship.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Ākāśagarbha</s>.
The tantra of the consecration-accomplishment of all families.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> set forth the tantra of the <s>samādhi</s>-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>samādhi</s>-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text: From the sustenance of all <s>Buddha</s>s, having bound the <s>mudrā</s>, concentrated,
reciting the <s>mantra</s>-<s>vidyā</s>s — one quickly attains accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family <s>samādhi</s>-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: <s>Samādhi</s> through <s>vajra</s>-<s>dharma</s>, by the yoga of being-empowerment,
the heart-<s>mudrā</s>, <s>mantra</s>, and <s>vidyā</s>s — they are quickly accomplished through recitation.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Buddhasamādhi</s>.

children.text: pūrvaṃ dhūpādibhiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā tu susamāhitaḥ /
krodhamuṣṭi prakurvan vai śīghraṃ sidhyet kulaṃ mame- //
sidhyate maṇikulaṃ sarvadadan dānāni vā sidhyatī- //
satvārthaṃ ca prakurvan vai buddhabodhyarthikaḥ svayaṃ /
kāmaṃ sevya sukhātmā tu suratastvamiti kurvan /
iyaṃ rakṣā tu mahatī śāśvatī siddhidā kṣaṇād //
abandhyo divasaḥ kāryo yathā śaktyā prayogataḥ /

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvo bhagavantametadavocat / "pratigṛhāṇa bhagavannidaṃ sarvatathāgatakulatantraṃ / yena sarvasatvāḥ sarvakalpaiśvaryatayādhigamaṃ kṛtvā, śīghramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyanta" iti //
atha bhagavān vajrapāṇaye bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya sādhukāramadāt / "sādhu sādhu vajrapāṇe subhāṣitaṃ, pratigṛhīto 'smābhiradhiṣṭhitaśce-" ti //
atha sarvatathāgatāḥ punaḥ samājamāgamya, vajrapāṇaye mahābodhisatvāya sādhukārāṇyadadan /

children.translated_text: Well done for <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Well done for <s>Vajraratna</s>!

children.text: vajradharmāya te sādhu sādhu te vajrakarmaṇe //
children.translated_text: Well done for <s>Vajradharma</s>! Well done for <s>Vajrakarma</s>!
This <s>sūtra</s> is well-spoken — the unsurpassed <s>Vajrayāna</s>,
the secret of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the compendium of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>!

body.translated_text: From the Compendium of the Reality of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the tantra of the detailed procedure of the accomplishment of skillful means for all rituals is completed.
CHAPTER 24: DETAILED PROCEDURE OF THE SECRET RITUAL OF ALL FAMILIES (<s>SARVAKULAKALPAGUHYAVIDHIVISTARATANTRA</s>)

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisatvaḥ sarvatathāgataguhyasiddhitantramudājahāra / tatrādita eva sarvatathāgatottamasiddhiguhyatantraṃ /
body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> brought forth the secret accomplishment-tantra of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, first of all, the secret tantra of the supreme accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text: Meditating on the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-awakening, perfectly concentrated,
'Awakening is obtained with ease' — thinking thus, one awakens.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, [representing] all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the supreme accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family:

children.text: satvavajrāṃ hṛdi badhvā bhāryā me tvamiti priyā /
children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>Sattvavajrā</s> at the heart, 'You are my consort, O beloved!'
Having spoken 'Be firm!' — one should accomplish all <s>mudrā</s>s. (1)
By this ritual-method, even one who has not accomplished [anything] through one's own actions,
having spoken 'She is [my] secret consort' — one surely attains accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Sattvavajra</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the supreme accomplishment of the <s>vajra</s>-family:

children.translated_text: However enraged, with the <s>vajra</s>-Hūṃ-syllable <s>mudrā</s>,
slaying even all <s>Buddha</s>s — from fear, accomplishment would be produced.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Hūṃkāra of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the supreme accomplishment of the lotus-family:

children.translated_text: Having joined the <s>samādhi</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, gazing with the <s>vajra</s>-gaze,
upon one's own wife or another's wife — one attains the beloved accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Padmarāga</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the supreme accomplishment of the jewel-family:

children.translated_text: Through the attainment of the two faculties, speaking 'This is supreme bliss,'
having offered one's own faculty to all <s>Buddha</s>s — one swiftly accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Maṇirāga</s>.
The secret tantra of the supreme accomplishment of all families.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> brought forth the secret tantra of the pledge-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the secret tantra of the pledge-accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s> [family]:

children.translated_text: Having spoken 'You are the pledge,' one should enamor all women;

children.text: ma virāgaya satvārthaṃ dhruvaṃ buddhāṃ sa rāgayed //
children.translated_text: do not become dispassionate — for the purpose of beings, one should surely enamor the <s>Buddha</s>s.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Mahāvairocana</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the pledge-accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family:

children.translated_text: Passion is not to be despised — one should enamor all women;
this is the secret pledge of the <s>vajra</s>-bearer — guarding it, one accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the pledge-accomplishment of the <s>vajra</s>-family:

children.translated_text: Slaying and slaying the world with the virtuous practices of body, speech, and action —
with Hūṃ-syllables, for the purpose of purification — the pledge is the giver of the accomplishment of aims.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Trailokyavijaya</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the pledge-accomplishment of the lotus-family:

children.translated_text: Passion is pure for those of pure nature, but impure for non-Buddhist yogins;
for those of pure nature, guarding the pledge, one attains accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the pledge-accomplishment of the jewel-family:

children.translated_text: Having first bound the <s>vajra</s>-gem, through the <s>Vajragarbha</s> <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: duṣṭānāṃ tu harannarthān samayaḥ siddhido bhaved //
children.translated_text: removing the misfortunes of the hostile — the pledge becomes the giver of accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajraratna</s>.
The detailed procedure of the secret tantra of the pledge-accomplishment of all families.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> brought forth the secret tantra of the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s> [family]:

children.translated_text: Meditating on the inherent purity of <s>dharma</s>s, perfectly concentrated,
while performing all activities — one attains awakening as accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhātu</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family:

children.translated_text: Enamoring all beings and non-detachment from sense-objects —
the purity of delighting and being delighted is the secret <s>dharma</s>, the excellent giver of accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajraguhya</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment of the <s>vajra</s>-family:

children.translated_text: Through the yoga of the nasal Hūṃ-syllable, slaying all the hostile,
established in the subtle <s>vajra</s> <s>samādhi</s> — one attains supreme accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Dharmahuṃkāra</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment of the lotus-family:

children.translated_text: Through the application of the subtle <s>vajra</s>, one should delight all women;
one attains <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment — through the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>Vajradharma</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment of the jewel-family:

body.text:
dvayendriyasamāpattyā sarvāśā paripūrayan /
yoṣitāṃ vā priyāṇāṃ vā siddhimāpnotyanuttarām /
body.translated_text:
Through the attainment of the two faculties, fulfilling all wishes —
of women or of dear ones — one attains unsurpassed accomplishment.
Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajraratna</s>.
The detailed procedure of the secret tantra of the <s>dharma</s>-accomplishment of all families.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> brought forth the secret tantra of the karma-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the secret tantra of the karma-accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s> [family]:

children.translated_text: Established in the <s>Vajrasattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, meditating on the recollection of <s>Buddha</s>s,
entering the body of a woman — one should mutually subjugate women.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the karma-accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family:

children.translated_text: Established in the <s>Vajrasattva</s> <s>samādhi</s>, entering likewise through the vulva,
one should properly pervade the body of the woman — one should enamor even one who is motionless.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrarāga</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the karma-accomplishment of the <s>vajra</s>-family:

children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>vajra</s>-Hūṃ-syllable-<s>mudrā</s>, perfectly concentrated,

children.text: praviśaṃstu bhage kruddhaḥ manasā sa tu pātayed //
children.translated_text: entering the vulva wrathfully — with the mind, one should cause her to fall.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasamaya</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the karma-accomplishment of the lotus-family:

children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>dharma</s>-karma-<s>mudrā</s>, through the lotus <s>samādhi</s>,
entering through the vulva — one should protect even all women.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrapadma</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the karma-accomplishment of the jewel-family:

children.translated_text: Having bound the karma-<s>vajra</s>-gem, through the <s>Vajraratna</s> <s>samādhi</s>,
entering through the vulva of women — in an instant, having possessed [them], one dances.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajraratna</s>.
The detailed procedure of the secret tantra of the karma-accomplishment of all families.

children.translated_text: One should make the secret <s>maṇḍala</s> in the form of a <s>dharmacakra</s>,
surrounded by <s>mudrā</s>-consorts; therein one should install the <s>Buddha</s>. (1)

body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> brought forth the secret tantra of the accomplishment of the purification of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the secret tantra of the accomplishment of the purification of the wheel of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text: Having entered that very secret [<s>maṇḍala</s>], one should say to the <s>Buddha</s> at that very instant,
'These consorts are yours, O Lord — give [them] to me always!' (2)

children.text: evaṃ brūvaṃstu sarveṣu kulamudrā nayeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Speaking thus in all the family-<s>mudrā</s> methods,
one attains the secret accomplishment of the <s>Buddha</s>s of incomparable splendor. (3)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the accomplishment of all <s>maṇḍala</s>s of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family:

children.translated_text: One should draw the <s>maṇḍala</s> resembling the <s>Vajradhātu</s>,
this supreme method of all <s>Tathāgata</s>-families.
One desiring accomplishment should quickly speak upon entering that very <s>maṇḍala</s>:
'In [sexual] union, you are the pledge — Hoḥ! O <s>Vajrasattva</s>, today accomplish me!' (2)
Reciting this heart[-<s>mantra</s>], one should accomplish — all accomplishments [will arise];
through the yoga of the urging of reality, he is pleased — and one swiftly accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the accomplishment of all <s>maṇḍala</s>s of the <s>vajra</s>-family:

children.translated_text: In the form of <s>Trailokyavijaya</s>, for the entire <s>vajra</s>-family,
the discerning one should draw the method of all <s>maṇḍala</s>s. (1)

children.text: taṃ praviṣṭvaiva śīghraṃ vai brūyātsiddhiṃ tu yācayan /
children.translated_text: Having entered that very [<s>maṇḍala</s>], one should quickly speak, requesting accomplishment:
'You are born from passion!' — speaking thus, one accomplishes in all [<s>maṇḍala</s>s]. (2)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrahuṃkāra</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the accomplishment of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the lotus-family:

children.translated_text: By the method of Disciplining the World, for all lotus-families,
the wise one should draw the <s>maṇḍala</s>s — having entered that very [<s>maṇḍala</s>], one should speak thus: (1)
'O <s>Dharma</s> of passion, great lotus — accomplish [it] swiftly for me, O Lord!'

children.text: evamuktvā tu sarveṣu maṇḍaleṣu sa sidhyatī- // 2 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, one accomplishes in all <s>maṇḍala</s>s. (2)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the accomplishment of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the jewel-family:

children.translated_text: By the method of the Accomplishment of All Aims, one should draw the <s>maṇḍala</s>s
of the great jewel-families — having entered that very [<s>maṇḍala</s>], one should speak thus: (1)
'Of all accomplishments of desires, the accomplishment of passion-wishes is supreme!
Accomplish, accomplish, O great being, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, for all accomplishments!' (2)
Speaking thus in all <s>maṇḍala</s>s upon entry,
one attains the great accomplishment — the unsurpassed secret of worship. (3)

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛti siddhātmā sādhayan siddhayaḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Thereafter, one whose self is accomplished, always accomplishing — the accomplishments [arise];

children.text: yadā na laghu siddhiḥ syāt sidhyante tatvacodanair // 4 //
children.translated_text: when accomplishment does not [come] swiftly, they are accomplished through the urgings of reality. (4)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
The detailed procedure of the secret tantra of the accomplishment of all family-<s>maṇḍala</s>s.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> brought forth the secret tantra of the accomplishment of all <s>mudrā</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the secret tantra of the <s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s> [family]:

children.translated_text: The great goddesses of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, beloved, bestowers of all happiness —

children.text: satyānuparivartinyā vāssatyaiḥ sāpi tā yanna sidhyata //
children.translated_text: with one who follows truth, or with truths — she too does not fail to accomplish.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the great <s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family:

children.translated_text: Having bound the great <s>mudrā</s> duly and in order,

children.text: idaṃ tatvaṃ rahasyaṃ ca vajravācā vadetvayaṃ // 1 //
children.translated_text: one should speak this reality and secret with the <s>vajra</s>-voice: (1)

children.text: vajrasatvaḥ svayamahaṃ tvamme bhāryā hṛdi sthitā /
children.translated_text: 'I myself am <s>Vajrasattva</s> — you, my consort, are established in my heart;
embracing the entire body, be raised up into the <s>vajra</s>-pride!' (2)
<s>Vajragarvā</s>, the great goddess, enamored by the urging of reality,
having become firm in the entire body, duly and swiftly accomplishes. (3)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān</s>, the lord of <s>Vajragarvā</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the pledge-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment of the <s>vajra</s>-family:

children.text: "sidhya sidhyādya samaye samayo 'haṃ tvaṃ priyā mama" /
children.translated_text: 'Accomplish, accomplish today, O pledge! I am the pledge, you are my beloved!'
Through this urging, swiftly, the enamored one accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment of the lotus-family:

children.translated_text: 'Awaken, awaken, O great female being! You are my most beloved consort!'
Through this urging, swiftly, the enamored one accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradharma</s>.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the karma-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment of the jewel-family:
'You are the consort who performs all actions — accomplish today, O <s>vajra</s>-bearer!'
Through this urging, swiftly, the enamored one accomplishes.
Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Ākāśagarbha</s>.
The detailed procedure of the secret tantra of the accomplishment of all <s>mudrā</s>s of all families.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> brought forth the secret tantra of the pledge-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the pledge-accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s> [family]:

children.translated_text: For the benefit of non-Buddhists, the consort of the <s>Buddha</s> is concealed;

children.text: lekhyā mudrā prayogeṇa iti vijñeya sidhyatī- //
children.translated_text: one should draw the <s>mudrā</s> by method — knowing thus, one accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Pledge of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the secret tantra of the pledge-accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family:

children.translated_text: Pervading the minds of all beings, bestowing happiness on all beings,
and being the father of all beings — desire is supreme among those of the supreme pledge.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
This is that supreme and most wondrous secret of all <s>Buddha</s>s;
one should know [it] with faith and purity — even what is difficult to accomplish is accomplished.
Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
Therein, this is the secret accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-family pledge:

children.translated_text: For the purification of passion, for those who are dispassionate and whose selves are formed by heretical views,
killing is the foremost pledge — this should be known as accomplishing. Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
Therein, this is the secret accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the <s>padma</s>-family pledge:

children.translated_text: Everything arises from the great elements — how then can it be called impure?
For the destruction of the heretics, one shall surely attain accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajranetra</s>.
Therein, this is the secret accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the <s>maṇi</s>-family pledge:

children.translated_text: When through association with women an accumulation of jewels is produced,
one should contemplate 'Women are the supreme jewel' — thus it is accomplished.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Ājñākara</s>.
The detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of secret accomplishment of all family pledges.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, brought forth the secret accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s> worship. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> worship secret accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Having become surrounded by women, the play of amusement is bliss;
offering this in the <s>Buddha</s>-worship, one attains the accomplishment of worship.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the secret accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family worship:

children.translated_text: Fatigued by the exertion of love-making, that bliss born of passion,
offering it in the worship of the four prostrations, one quickly accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
Therein, this is the secret accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-family worship:

children.translated_text: Having formed the <s>Huṃkāra</s>-pledge <s>mudrā</s> and embracing a woman,

children.text: tatpariṣvaṅgasaukhyaṃ tu niryātya hi sa sidhyatī- //
children.translated_text: offering that bliss of embrace, one thus accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrahuṃkāra</s>.
Therein, this is the secret accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the <s>padma</s>-family worship:

body.text:
lokeśvaramahaṃ bhāvya priyāvaktraṃ nirīkṣanvai /
tannirīkṣaṇasauravyaṃ tu niryātya hi sa sidhyatī- /
body.translated_text:
Having meditated on the great <s>Lokeśvara</s>, gazing upon the face of one's beloved,
offering that joy of gazing, one thus accomplishes.
Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Padmanetra</s>.
Therein, this is the secret accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the <s>maṇi</s>-family worship:

children.translated_text: Having become a bearer of the <s>karma-mudrā</s>, adorned with all ornaments,

children.text: striyaṃ pariṣvajya pūjāyāṃ vibhūtiṃ niryātya sidhyatī- //
children.translated_text: embracing a woman and offering it in worship, one attains splendor and accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajraratna</s>.
The detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of secret accomplishment of all family worship.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, brought forth the secret worship accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> secret worship accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Enjoying the wives of others such that no one perceives it,
meditating on oneself as <s>Buddha</s>, one attains accomplishment through worship.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family secret worship accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: One should establish <s>Vajralāsyā</s> (Vajra-coquetry) and form <s>Vajramālā</s> (Vajra-garland),
then having formed <s>Vajragītā</s> (Vajra-song), one should worship with <s>Vajranṛtyā</s> (Vajra-dance).
The supreme consecration of desire-passion — from the bliss of dance and song comes bliss;
there is nothing other than this — this is the unsurpassed secret worship.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family secret worship accomplishment <s>tantra</s>.

children.translated_text: According to the proper ritual method, one should worship with the secret worship;
meditating on <s>Trilokavijaya</s> (Conqueror of the Three Worlds), one attains the accomplishment of worship.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajraguhya</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>padma</s>-family secret worship accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: According to the proper secret method, worshipping well with the <s>dharma-mudrā</s>,
abiding in the <s>mudrā</s> of world-discipline, one attains the accomplishment of worship.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>maṇi</s>-family secret worship accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: According to the proper secret method, accomplishing well the <s>karma-mudrā</s>,
through the method of accomplishment of all aims, one attains the accomplishment of worship.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajragarbha</s>.
The detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of secret worship accomplishment of all families.

Then the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, brought forth the secret accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the opening of all <s>Tathāgata</s> families. Therein, this is the secret <s>tantra</s> of the accomplishment of the arising of <s>Tathāgata</s>-reality:

children.translated_text: Buddhahood, born from <s>samādhi</s>-<s>jñāna</s>, in brief,
is swiftly attained as the supreme through the method of passion-engagement with beings.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata</s>.
Therein, this is the great <s>Tathāgata</s>-family reality-opening accomplishment secret <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The being without beginning or end, whose characteristic is arising like space,
<s>Samantabhadra</s>, the self of all, desire, the lord of all worlds. (1)
That mind of all beings, because of its firmness, is called 'being' (<s>satva</s>);
through concentration it becomes like <s>vajra</s>; through certainties it attains <s>vajra</s>-nature. (2)
Through the method of empowerment of beings, one again becomes <s>Vajrasattva</s>;
that very <s>Bhagavān</s>, the being, is the <s>Tathāgata</s> with <s>vajra</s>-body. (3)
From the penetration of one's own mind comes <s>Buddha</s>-<s>bodhi</s> according to the proper method;
that very <s>Bhagavān</s> becomes the entire <s>Tathāgata</s> family.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the being without beginning or end.

children.translated_text: That very <s>Tathāgata</s> family is also known as the <s>vajra</s> family;
it is also the pure <s>padma</s> family, and it is also called the <s>maṇi</s>-being family.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatacakra</s>.
The detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of secret accomplishment of the arising of all families.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, brought forth the secret <s>tantra</s> of the accomplishment of the designation of <s>mudrā</s>-emblems of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.
Therein, this is the secret <s>tantra</s> of the accomplishment of the designation of <s>Tathāgata</s>-emblems:

children.text: sa eva bhagavān satvo vajrasatvo hṛdi sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: That very <s>Bhagavān</s>, the being, is <s>Vajrasattva</s> abiding in the heart;
through concentration he is <s>samādhi</s>, the accomplisher of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>bodhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family emblem-designation accomplishment secret <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The <s>vajra</s> is so called because of supreme penetration; the hook (<s>aṅkuśa</s>) because it releases from grasping;
the arrow (<s>vāṇa</s>) because of subtle piercing; the cry of approval (<s>sādhukāra</s>) because of satisfaction. (1)
The jewel (<s>ratna</s>) is so called because of arrangement; the sun (<s>sūrya</s>) because of the production of radiance;

children.text: ketuḥ samucchrayaḥ proktaḥ smito hāsastu kīrtitaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: the banner (<s>ketu</s>) is said to be because of elevation; the smile (<s>smita</s>) is declared to be because of laughter. (2)
The lotus (<s>padma</s>) because of the purification of passion; the sheath (<s>kośa</s>) because of cutting the affliction-enemy;
the wheel (<s>cakra</s>) because of the <s>maṇḍala</s> method; and from speech-lapse comes recitation. (3)
The all-<s>vajra</s> (<s>sarvavajra</s>) because of universality; the armor (<s>varma</s>) from the method of impenetrability;
the fang (<s>daṃṣṭrā</s>) because of the method of terrifying; the bond (<s>bandha</s>) because of the application of <s>mudrā</s>. (4)

children.text: yathā hi bhagavān śāśvo vajrasatvastu sarvagaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the eternal <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s> pervades all,

children.text: tathā vajrāṃ tu cihnādi bhāvayanniti sidhyatī- //
children.translated_text: so too, by meditating on the <s>vajra</s> emblems and the rest, one accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatacinha</s>.
The secret <s>tantra</s> of the accomplishment of emblem-designation of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, brought forth the secret <s>tantra</s> of the accomplishment of the arising of <s>mudrā</s>-bindings of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>mudrā</s>-binding-arising accomplishment secret <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Having formed the <s>vajra</s>-cross-legged posture, with both hands in the <s>vajra</s>-binding,
abiding in the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>Vajrasattva</s>, one swiftly attains Buddhahood.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family <s>mudrā</s>-binding-arising accomplishment secret <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Just as by means of their own seals, kings seal the royal decree,
so too, by means of their own <s>mudrā</s>s, the great beings seal people. (1)
Through the method of reflections of body-speech-mind <s>vajra</s>s,
the great <s>mudrā</s>s of the great beings — knowing this, one accomplishes. (2)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Mahāmudra</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family <s>mudrā</s>-binding-arising accomplishment secret <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Just as by means of fierce pledges, a certain person becomes bound,
inviolable — so too all <s>Tathāgatas</s> (1)
are bound by the supreme <s>vajra</s>-binding <s>mudrā</s>-pledge-bonds;
they do not transgress until death — knowing this, one accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrasamaya</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>dharma</s>-family <s>mudrā</s>-binding-arising accomplishment secret <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The <s>vajra</s>-speech is indeed inviolable by the <s>Jinas</s> in every way;

children.text: ayaṃ bandha iti jñātvā dharmamasya prasidhyatī- //
children.translated_text: knowing 'this is the bond,' the <s>Dharma</s> of this one is accomplished.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradharma</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>karma</s>-family <s>mudrā</s>-binding-arising accomplishment secret <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The <s>vajra</s>-command is indeed inviolable, and <s>karma</s> is abundant;
knowing the <s>karma</s> of one who is obedient to the command, one quickly accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajra</s>.
The detailed secret <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of accomplishment of <s>mudrā</s>-binding-arising of all families.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān vajrapāṇiṃ mahābodhisatvamevamāha / "idamapi mayā bhagavan parigṛhītamadhiṣṭhitaṃ ce-" ti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke thus to <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>: 'This too, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, has been accepted and empowered by me.'

body.text: atha sarvatathāgatāḥ punaḥ samājamāgamya vajrapāṇaye sarvatathāgatadhipataye sādhukārāṇyadaduḥ //
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having again assembled, gave cries of approval to <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the lord of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>:

children.text: sādhu te vajrasatvāya vajraratnāya sādhu te /
children.translated_text: Well done to you, O <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Well done to you, O <s>Vajraratna</s>!

children.text: vajradharmāya te sādhu sādhu te vajrakarmaṇe //
children.translated_text: Well done to you, O <s>Vajradharma</s>! Well done to you, O <s>Vajrakarman</s>!
This <s>sūtra</s> is well spoken — the unsurpassed <s>Vajrayāna</s>,
the secret of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the compendium of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Thus.

body.translated_text: From the <s>Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha</s>, the detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of the secret of the ritual of all families is completed.
CHAPTER 25: SARVA-KALPA-GUHYOTTARA-TANTRA-VIDHI-VISTARA (The Detailed Procedure of the Supreme Secret <s>Tantra</s> of All Rituals)

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, brought forth the supreme <s>Dharma</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> supreme <s>Dharma</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Meditating on the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>, well-concentrated,
through the method of recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>, one attains the supreme accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family supreme <s>Dharma</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Abiding in the <s>samādhi</s> of all beings, meditating well-concentrated,
through the method of recollection of passion, one attains the supreme accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatasamādhi</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family supreme <s>Dharma</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Meditating on the form of <s>Trilokavijaya</s> (Conqueror of the Three Worlds) before oneself,
becoming endowed with the power of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, one becomes the conqueror of the three worlds.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>padma</s>-family supreme <s>Dharma</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

body.text:
jagadvinayadharmaṃ tu bhāvayan puratasta[thā /]
sarvākāravaropetaṃ vinayaṃ prakaroti sa //
body.translated_text:
Meditating on the <s>Dharma</s> of world-discipline before oneself,
endowed with excellence of all forms, one performs the discipline of the world.
Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradharma</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>maṇi</s>-family supreme <s>Dharma</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Meditating on the form of <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> (Accomplishment of All Aims) before oneself,
endowed with excellence of all forms, one will obtain the wealth of all aims.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>.
The detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of supreme <s>Dharma</s> accomplishment of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, brought forth the <s>Dharma</s>-pledge accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dharma</s>-pledge accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.text: buddhā[nusmṛ]timāṃ bhūtvā vajra vajra iti brūvan /
children.translated_text: Having become one who possesses <s>Buddha</s>-recollection, reciting '<s>vajra</s>, <s>vajra</s>,'
through the method of the subtle <s>vajra</s>, one attains <s>Buddha</s>-accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family <s>Dharma</s>-pledge accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Meditating on the <s>samādhi</s> of <s>Vajrasattva</s> through the subtle <s>vajra</s>,
one attains <s>Vajrasattva</s>-hood, uttering '<s>Vajrasattva</s>.'

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family <s>Dharma</s>-pledge accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Recollecting the form of <s>Trilokavijaya</s> before oneself,

children.text: huṃ huṃ huṃ humiti procya siddhimāpnotyanuttarām //
children.translated_text: reciting 'Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ,' one attains the unsurpassed accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrahuṃkāra</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>padma</s>-family <s>Dharma</s>-pledge accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Meditating on the form of world-discipline through the subtle <s>vajra</s>,

children.text: śudhya śudhya iti procya uttamāṃ siddhimāpnute- //
children.translated_text: reciting 'Purify, purify!' one attains the supreme accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradharma</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>maṇi</s>-family <s>Dharma</s>-pledge accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Meditating on the form of <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> through the subtle <s>vajra</s>,

children.text: sidhya sidhya iti procya arthasiddhiḥ parā bhaved //
children.translated_text: reciting 'Accomplish, accomplish!' the supreme accomplishment of aims comes to be.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, <s>Maṇidharma</s> (Jewel-<s>Dharma</s>).
The detailed ritual <s>tantra</s> of the true-<s>dharma</s>-pledge-<s>siddhi</s> of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, brought forth the true-<s>dharma</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the true-<s>dharma</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s:

children.translated_text: The true <s>Dharma</s> is without syllables, born from <s>samādhi</s>-<s>jñāna</s>;
by the syllable 'a,' the non-arising of all <s>dharma</s>s is proclaimed. (1)
By this <s>mudrā</s>-method, meditating with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
the <s>jñāna</s> consisting of all syllables — the <s>Sugata</s>'s [wisdom] — is accomplished in an instant. (2)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the noble <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, [who is] all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family true-<s>dharma</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: One who has faith in this <s>sūtra</s>, which is the <s>tattva</s> (reality) of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,
who holds it, recites it, a faithful one — attains unsurpassed <s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family true-<s>dharma</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: For the benefit of sinful beings, and for carrying out the <s>Buddha</s>'s command,
for the purpose of disciplining the wicked — through killing, <s>siddhi</s> is accomplished.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s> of the <s>vajra</s>-family.
Therein, this is the lotus-family true-<s>dharma</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Having arrived at natural purity, it is proclaimed as the ultimate reality;
meditating on this primordial [truth] — through <s>Dharma</s>, one quickly accomplishes <s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the jewel-family true-<s>dharma</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The giving of aims to all beings, for the fulfillment of all wishes —
meditating on this <s>Dharma</s> in the jewel-family, one quickly accomplishes <s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Dharmaratna</s> (Dharma-Jewel).
The detailed ritual <s>tantra</s> of the true-<s>dharma</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s> of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, brought forth the <s>samādhi</s>-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>samādhi</s>-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The <s>samādhi</s>-activity of the <s>Buddha</s>s, which brings about <s>Buddha</s>-awakening —
one who meditates on this attains the supreme <s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the [<s>Tathāgata</s>]-family <s>samādhi</s>-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The supreme and manifold activity of the <s>samādhi</s>s of <s>Vajrasattva</s>,
the universal maker of all beings — through this meditation, <s>siddhi</s> is accomplished.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajra</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family <s>samādhi</s>-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: For the purpose of purifying sin, [this is] the destroyer of all sin;
the killing of all beings — through faith, <s>siddhi</s> is accomplished.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrī</s>.
Therein, this is the lotus-family <s>samādhi</s>-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: One whose self is purified of all sin, by means of universal purity, he performs
all tasks — this is the activity; through this meditation, <s>siddhi</s> is accomplished.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Padma</s>.
Therein, this is the jewel-family <s>samādhi</s>-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Fulfilling all the wishes of all the hopeful and destitute,
the accomplishment of all aims, the universal self — <s>siddhi</s> is accomplished; in this there is no doubt.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Ratnadhvaja</s> (Jewel-Banner).
The detailed ritual <s>tantra</s> of the <s>samādhi</s>-activity-<s>siddhi</s> of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, brought forth the subtle-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> subtle-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: One who constantly applies the subtle <s>vajra</s>-method with all [types of] meditation,
endowed with all modes of excellence — attains the five <s>abhijñā</s>s (super-knowledges).

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the all-<s>Tathāgata</s>-family subtle-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Neither before another master, nor before anyone else, nor before a non-disciple or a son —
should one reveal the <s>mudrā</s>s; their <s>siddhi</s> lies in utmost secrecy.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family subtle-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: By the subtle <s>vajra</s>-method, through the application of <s>hūṃ</s>-sound at the nose,
abiding in the <s>vajra</s>-wrath-<s>samādhi</s> — one should accomplish all tasks.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajra</s>.
Therein, this is the lotus-family subtle-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Having fixed the <s>vajra</s>-gaze, by the subtle <s>vajra</s>-method,
abiding in the great lotus-<s>samādhi</s> — one attains the <s>siddhi</s> of passion.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Padmarāga</s> (Lotus-Passion).
Therein, this is the jewel-family subtle-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: With blazing gaze, most subtle, by the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-<s>samādhi</s>,
by the subtle <s>vajra</s>-method — one becomes the attractor of all aims.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>.
The subtle-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s> of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, brought forth the eye-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> eye-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: When a <s>mudrā</s> or <s>samādhi</s> is employed for accomplishment,

children.text: tadā khe dhātavaḥ śubhrāstārakākārāḥ sa paśyati // 1 //
children.translated_text: then one sees in the sky luminous elements in the form of stars. (1)
Then, O wise one, know: 'This is my <s>Buddha</s>-eye';
from then on, one should accomplish all the ritual procedures of the <s>Buddha</s>s. (2)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family eye-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Whatever entities exist, both stationary and moving,
one sees their reflections rushing through the sky. (1)
Coming and going — the purity of the <s>vajra</s>-eye;
knowing this, through worship one attains unsurpassed <s>siddhi</s>. (2)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family eye-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: From those revolving clockwise and counter-clockwise, one sees with the eye in the sky
the space-elements swiftly whirling, resembling clouds. (1)

children.text: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā na hi bibhyeta mudrāstā vajrasaṃbhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing that, one should not be afraid — those <s>mudrā</s>s are born of <s>vajra</s>;
by grasping them, the <s>mudrā</s>s are accomplished through the <s>mudrā</s>-eye. (2)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajra</s>.
Therein, this is the lotus-family eye-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.text: śvetāṃ raktāṃ sitāṃ pitāṃ yadā paśyanti maṇḍalān /
children.translated_text: When one sees white, red, pale, and yellow <s>maṇḍala</s>s,
then one's intentions are realized — accomplished through the <s>vajra</s>-eye. (2)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the jewel-family eye-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

body.text:
ākāśe ratnasaṃkāśā hiraṇyādiṣu sādṛśāḥ /
yadā tu paśyate khe tu khacakṣuḥ sidhyate sade- /
body.translated_text:
When one sees in the sky [visions] resembling gems, similar to gold and the like,
then in the sky — the sky-eye is accomplished well.
Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajragarbha</s>.
The detailed ritual <s>tantra</s> of the eye-<s>jñāna</s>-<s>siddhi</s> of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, brought forth the supreme-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> supreme-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: By the method of the activity-<s>maṇḍala</s>, worshiping all the leaders,
for the sake of the fruition of the bliss of passion — one attains <s>Buddha</s>-<s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family supreme-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Performing the secret worship, meditating 'I am passion,'
one attains the supreme <s>siddhi</s>, equal in splendor to <s>Vajrarāga</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Kāma</s> (Desire).
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family supreme-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Performing the secret worship, meditating 'I am wrath,'
one attains the supreme <s>siddhi</s>, comparable to <s>Trailokyavijaya</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>.
Therein, this is the lotus-family supreme-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: With an inward mind, meditating on the purity of desire,
worshiping the <s>Buddha</s>s with tones and <s>bindu</s>s (drops) — one attains <s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the jewel-family supreme-activity-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Having established <s>vajra</s>-pride, with bows shaken by devotion,
one devoted to prostration always attains the consecrations.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrābhiṣekaratna</s> (Vajra-Consecration-Jewel).
The detailed ritual <s>tantra</s> of the supreme-activity-<s>siddhi</s> of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, brought forth the activity-pledge-secret-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> activity-pledge-secret-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.text: kāmādyāḥ sarvasaukhyā me sadaiva hṛdaye sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Desire and all other pleasures ever abide in my heart;
Ah, how wonderful — non-attachment to the aims of beings is taught therein! (1)
This indeed is the activity-pledge; through <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>samādhi</s>,
meditating and worshiping the <s>Buddha</s>s — one attains the supreme <s>siddhi</s>. (2)

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family activity-pledge-secret-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Samantabhadra</s>, I am desire, the giver of happiness to all beings;
abiding in <s>Vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, worshiping — one attains <s>siddhi</s>.'

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Kāma</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family activity-pledge-secret-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Samantabhadra</s>, I am wrath, the benefactor of all beings;
through the <s>vajra</s>-<s>hūṃkāra</s>-method, worshiping — one attains <s>siddhi</s>.'

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>.
Therein, this is the lotus-family activity-pledge-secret-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Samantabhadra</s>, I am passion, the giver of all bliss;
abiding in the form of world-discipline, worshiping — one attains <s>siddhi</s>.'

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Padmarāga</s>.
Therein, this is the jewel-family activity-pledge-secret-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Samantabhadra</s>, I am the king, the great giver of aims to all beings;
in the form of the accomplishment of all aims, worshiping — one attains <s>siddhi</s>.'

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Sarvārthasiddhi</s> (Accomplishment of All Aims).
The detailed ritual <s>tantra</s> of the activity-pledge-secret-<s>siddhi</s> of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, brought forth the activity-<s>dharmatā</s>-supreme-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> activity-<s>dharmatā</s>-supreme-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Facing the foremost [direction, namely] the south, one should bind an armor with one's own <s>samādhi</s>;
established at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> — it will become an ultimate protection.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Buddha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family activity-<s>dharma</s>-supreme-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.text: saṃlikhya tu bhagākāraṃ kuḍye meḍhraṃ samucchritaṃ /
children.translated_text: Having drawn the form of a vulva on a wall, with an erect phallus,

children.text: yāṃ striyaṃ cintayan mṛduṃ kuryātsāsya vaśībhaved //
children.translated_text: whichever woman one thinks of gently — she will come under one's power.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the noble <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family activity-<s>dharma</s>-supreme-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.text: bhūmau yakṣamukhaṃ likhya tasyāgryāṅgu lito nakhaṃ /
children.translated_text: Having drawn a <s>yakṣa</s>-face on the ground, and from the tip of its foremost finger, a nail —
having struck at the eye-region — one attracts excellent women.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the lotus-family activity-<s>dharma</s>-supreme-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.text: padmaṃ gṛhya karābhyāṃ tu nirīkṣya rāgaśuddhitāṃ /
children.translated_text: Taking a lotus in both hands and gazing upon the purity of passion,
with the <s>vajra</s>-gaze, one arouses passion in women from all sides.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
Therein, this is the jewel-family activity-<s>dharma</s>-supreme-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Abiding in <s>vajra</s>-jewel-<s>samādhi</s>, grasping a jewel with both hands,
by the jewel-<s>hūṃkāra</s>-method — one overpowers all women.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrahūṃkāra</s>.
The detailed ritual <s>tantra</s> of the activity-<s>dharma</s>-supreme-<s>siddhi</s> of all families.

Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, brought forth the activity-task-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s> activity-task-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.text: pūjākarmavidhiṃ yojya yadyat kāryaṃ tu cintayet /
children.translated_text: Having applied the worship-activity-procedure, whatever task one contemplates,

children.text: tattad vijñāpya mudrāṃ tu sādhayeta vicakṣaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: having announced that and [bound] the <s>mudrā</s> — the wise one should accomplish it.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhātu</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family activity-task-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Having applied the secret worship procedure, in <s>Vajrasattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>,
whatever task one declares — one quickly attains <s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family activity-task-<s>siddhi</s>-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Having performed the great worship of the family-secret, in the wrath-<s>samādhi</s>,
whatever the wise one contemplates — that one will quickly attain <s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrakrodha</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the lotus-family activity-task-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having performed mental worship with the <s>Lokeśvara</s>-<s>samādhi</s>,
whatever task the wise one contemplates — all of that one would quickly attain.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Padmadhara</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the jewel-family activity-task-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Having performed worship with incense and the rest, with the <s>Vajragarbha</s>-<s>samādhi</s>,
whatever task the wise one contemplates — all of that is accomplished in an instant.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajragarbha</s>.
The tantra of the elaboration of the procedure of the activity-task-accomplishment of all families.

Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> set forth the tantra of the <s>mudrā</s>-visualization-empowerment-yoga-accomplishment of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-empowerment-yoga-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Through the application of the subtle <s>vajra</s>, concentrated in the <s>Buddha</s>-yoga,
one would attain the supreme accomplishment — the accomplisher of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>mudrā</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi Tathāgata</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family being-empowerment-yoga-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: The being (<s>sattva</s>) is indeed the self-nature of all — established even in the body, in oneself.
Empowering thus, 'I am the being' — meditating with the I-notion (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>),

body.translated_text: one is accomplished. Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>, [the one who revealed] the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the tantra of the <s>vajra</s>-family <s>vajra</s>-empowerment-yoga-accomplishment:

children.text: yathā satvastathā mudrā yathā mudrāstathā hyahaṃ /
children.translated_text: As the being, so the <s>mudrā</s>; as the <s>mudrā</s>, so am I.
By this meditation-yoga, one should well accomplish all <s>mudrā</s>s.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
Therein, this is the tantra of the lotus-family <s>dharma</s>-empowerment-yoga-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: Through the application of the <s>dharma</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, meditation with the subtle <s>vajra</s>,
all of that is the <s>samādhi</s> of the great being regarding speech-<s>mudrā</s>s.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Āryāvalokiteśvara</s>. Therein, this is the tantra of the jewel-family activity-empowerment-yoga-accomplishment:

children.translated_text: All <s>Buddha</s>-consecrations, the accomplishments of the worship-pledge,
meditating '<s>Bhagavān</s>' — one should accomplish the <s>vajra</s>-activities.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrakarma</s>.
The tantra of the <s>mudrā</s>-visualization-accomplishment of all families.

body.text: atha] bhagavan[sarvatathāgatāḥ] punaḥ samājamāgamya, bhagavate sarvatathāgatacakravartine vajrapāṇaye mahābodhisatvāya sādhukārāṇyadaduḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having again come together in assembly, gave exclamations of 'well done!' to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>cakravartin</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s>.

children.translated_text: Well done to you, O <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Well done to you, O <s>Vajraratna</s>!
Well done to you, O <s>Vajradharma</s>! Well done to you, O <s>Vajrakarma</s>!

body.text:
subhāṣitamidaṃ sūtraṃ vajrayānamanuttaraṃ /
sarvatathāgataṃ guhyaṃ mahāyānābhisaṃ[graham // iti //]
body.translated_text: This <s>sūtra</s> is well spoken — the unsurpassed <s>Vajrayāna</s>, the secret of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the compendium of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Thus.
The elaboration of the procedure of the supreme secret tantra of all <s>kalpa</s>s, from the <s>Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha</s>, is fully completed.
CHAPTER 26a: <s>SARVA-KALPĀNUTTARA-TANTRA</s>
Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> uttered this inspired utterance:

children.translated_text: This secret is not suitable for those of wrong views, for the dispassionate.
For the benefit of all beings, I shall teach the procedures. Thus.

body.translated_text: Then the great <s>Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi</s> spoke the elaboration of the procedure of service to the families of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the tantra of the elaboration of the procedure of service to the families of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.

body.text: tatrāyaṃ hṛdayopacāravidhi[vistaratantro bhavati] / mahāmaṇḍalaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhūpapuṣpadīpagandhapūjāmudrābhir kṛtvā, tato vajra[vācā jāpamārabhyati /]
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the tantra of the elaboration of the procedure of heart-service. Having seen the great <s>maṇḍala</s>, having performed worship with the <s>mudrā</s>s of incense, flowers, lamps, and perfume, then one begins recitation with the <s>vajra</s>-voice.

body.text: tatrāyaṃ jāpavidhirbhavati / yathā sthānasthitaścaturmāsaṃ catuḥsandhyaṃ dhūpādibhiryathāvatpūjāṃ kṛtvā, sarvatathāgatamahāyānābhisamayanāmāṣṭaśatena sarvatathāgatānabhiṣṭutya, caturmudrāpraṇāmayogena praṇamannātmaniryātanapūjā kāryanena mantracatuṣṭayena /
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the procedure of recitation: remaining in one's place for four months, at the four junctures [of the day], having performed worship properly with incense and the rest, having praised all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with the one hundred and eight [names] called 'the <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,' bowing with the yoga of the four <s>mudrā</s>-prostrations, one should perform the self-offering worship with these four <s>mantra</s>s:
'Oṃ! For the worship-attendance of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I offer myself. O <s>Vajrasattva</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, empower me!'
'Oṃ! For the worship-consecration of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I offer myself. O <s>Vajraratna</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, consecrate me!'

body.text: oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāpravartanāyātmānaṃ niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajradharma pravartaya māṃ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ! For the setting in motion of the worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I offer myself. O <s>Vajradharma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, set me in motion!'

body.text: oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjākarmaṇe ātmānaṃ niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajrakarma kuru māṃ //
body.translated_text: 'Oṃ! For the worship-activity of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, I offer myself. O <s>Vajrakarma</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, perform [your activity] upon me!'

body.text: "tato 'viraktaḥ sarvakāmaguṇeṣu sarvāhāraḥ sarvakāmopabhogīhṛdayārthaḥ svamātmānaṃ buddhabimbaṃ purato vāṅmātreṇāpi bhāvayan yathākāmakaraṇīyatayā, aṣṭaśataṃ vajravācā japannāśu prasidhyatī-" tyāha bhagavān vajrasatvaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s> said: 'Then, unattached to all objects of desire, partaking of all food, enjoying all desires, [understanding] the meaning of the heart[-<s>mantra</s>], meditating on oneself or on a <s>Buddha</s>-image before one, even with speech alone, according to one's wish, reciting the one hundred and eight with the <s>vajra</s>-voice — one is quickly accomplished.'

body.text: "athottamasiddhimicchettataḥ paṭe bhagavantaṃ tathāgataṃ madhye lekhayet / tasya caturmahāsatvamaṇḍalayogena yathābhirucitavarṇābharaṇā mahāsatvāścandramaṇḍalapratiṣṭhitā lekhyāḥ koṇabhāgeṣu kuladevya iti / tataḥ paṭasyodārāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā yathāvajjapayogena tāvajjapet yāvanmāsacatuṣṭayaṃ, tataḥ sakalāṃ rātriṃ japet / tataḥ prabhāte sarvatathāgatatatvādīnuttamasiddhīnavāpnotī-" tyāha bhagavān vajradharaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s> said: 'Now, if one desires the supreme accomplishment, then one should have the <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata</s> painted in the center of a cloth. By the yoga of the four great being-<s>maṇḍala</s>s, the great beings with colors and ornaments as preferred, established on moon-discs, should be painted; the family goddesses in the corner sections. Then, having performed elaborate worship of the cloth, one should recite by the method of recitation for as long as four months. Then one should recite for the entire night. Then, at dawn, one attains the supreme accomplishments of the reality of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the rest.'

body.text: "athamudrāsādhanamicchettena sarvatathāgatasatvavajrimudrāṃ badhvā paṭasyāgrato vajravācāṃ śatasahasraṃ yathākāmakaraṇīyatayā yathāvad bandhan muñcaṃśca japet / tato 'nte sakalāṃ rātriṃ, aviśramato kiñcitkālaṃ muñcan, yathāvacca bandhan japet / tato mudrā jvalatyāviśatyuttiṣṭhati vācaṃ muñcatīti / tato mudrābandhanenotpatati kāmarūpī bhavati antardhāti sarvakarmāṇi ca karoti / sarvamudrāśca bandhamātrā yathāvatsarvakarmāṇi kurvantī-"tyāha bhagavān vajradharaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s> said: 'Now, if one desires the <s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment, having bound the <s>Sattvavajrī</s>-<s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, one should recite one hundred thousand [times] before the cloth with the <s>vajra</s>-voice, according to one's wish, properly binding and releasing. Then, at the end, for the entire night, without rest, releasing for a little while, and properly binding, one should recite. Then the <s>mudrā</s> blazes, enters, rises up, and releases speech. Then, by binding the <s>mudrā</s>, it flies up, takes on any desired form, disappears, and performs all activities. And all <s>mudrā</s>s, merely by binding, properly perform all activities.'

body.text: "atha samādhayo iṣyet tena sūkṣmavajrādārabdhavya samādhimabhirocet taṃ hṛdayayogato 'bhyaset, tāvadyāvac caturmāsaṃ / tato 'nte sakalāṃ [rātriṃ paryaṅkāvikṣaptasamāpannena tiṣṭhet / tataḥ prabhāte sarvatathāgatādyāḥ] sarvasiddhaya āmukhībhavanti / tato yādṛśī abhirucistādṛ[śīmavāpnotī-"tyāha bhagavān vajrasatvaḥ //]
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s> said: 'Now, if one desires the <s>samādhi</s>s, one should begin with the subtle <s>vajra</s>, and whatever <s>samādhi</s> one favors, one should practice that through the heart-yoga, for as long as four months. Then, at the end, one should sit for the entire night, having entered the cross-legged posture without distraction. Then, at dawn, all accomplishments beginning with [those of] all <s>Tathāgata</s>s become manifest. Then one attains whatever kind of accomplishment one desires.'

body.text: atha karmasādhanaṃ bhavati / tathaiva japanmāsamekaṃ sādhayet / tato 'nte sakalāṃ rātriṃ ja[pet / tataḥ sarvakarmāṇi sidhyantī-"tyāha bhagavān vajradha]raḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s> said: 'Now the activity-accomplishment is as follows: reciting in the same manner, one should accomplish for one month. Then, at the end, one should recite for the entire night. Then all activities are accomplished.'

body.text: "atha karmāṇi bhavanti / sakṛduccāritenātmaparagrāmanagararakṣa bhavati // kavacaba[ndhādināveśamapi kṛtvā candanagandhena grahāgraha]spṛṣṭavajrāṅku śaśarahastaratnasūryadhvajadantapaṅktipadmakhaḍgacakrajivhāsarvavajrakavacadaṃṣṭrāmuṣṭimudrādinisarvabhāvānāviśayati sakṛjjaptena // māyākarma ca mayūrapatrapiñcchake vajraṃ cidhvā bandhayet / tatastaṃ mayūrāṅgapiñcchakaṃ satvavajri mudra[yā badhyāt tā]vajjapedyāvat sarvatathāgatamudrā āviśati / tataśca piñcchakān nānādyāni rūpāṇi paśyati / tataḥ prabhṛti tena piñcchakena sarvarūpāṇi vidhivad darśayati / tenaiva piñcchakena sakṛjjapte bhrāmitenātmanaḥ sarvarūpāṇi darśayati / tenaiva piñcchakena laukikāni māyākarmāṇi darśayati / buddhabodhisatvabimbānyapi darśayati / daśasu dikṣu sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu tathāgatāḥ saparṣanmaṇḍalāḥ samārasenādharṣaṇādibuddharddhivikurvitāni kurvanto darśayati / yāvatsarvākāravaropetaṃ buddharūpamātmānaṃ bhavatī-"ti //
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s> said: 'Now the activities are as follows: by a single utterance, the protection of one's own and others' villages and cities is effected. By the armor-binding and other means of entry, and with sandalwood-perfume, one enters into all states through the <s>mudrā</s>s of the <s>vajra</s>-hook, arrow, hand-jewel, sun, banner, row of teeth, lotus, sword, wheel, tongue, all-<s>vajra</s>, armor, fang, and fist — [all this] by a single recitation, and through those who are touched by the planetary seizers. And the illusion-activity [is as follows]: one should draw a <s>vajra</s> on a peacock feather-plume and bind it. Then one should bind that peacock-body plume with the <s>Sattvavajrī</s>-<s>mudrā</s> and recite until the <s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s enters. Then from the plumes, one sees manifold forms. Thenceforth, with that plume one properly displays all forms. With that very plume, recited once and whirled, one displays all forms of oneself. With that very plume one displays worldly illusion-activities. One displays even the images of <s>Buddha</s>s and <s>bodhisattva</s>s. One displays <s>Tathāgata</s>s in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the ten directions, with their retinue-assemblies, performing the miraculous activities of <s>Buddha</s>s such as the defeat of <s>Māra</s> and so forth. Up to [the point where] one becomes a <s>Buddha</s>-form oneself, endowed with all excellent aspects.'

body.text: "vaśīkaraṇaṃ kartukāmaḥ sarvatathāgatasatvamudrāṃ badhvā tāvajjaped yāvatsā mudrāṃ jvalati / tataḥ prabhṛti mudrābandhena sarvatathāgatānabhyārāgayati vaśīkaroti / kiṃ punaranyāṃ satvān? //
body.translated_text: 'One who desires to perform subjugation (<s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>), having bound the being-<s>mudrā</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, should recite until that <s>mudrā</s> blazes. Thenceforth, by binding the <s>mudrā</s>, one enamors and subjugates all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. How much more so other beings?'

body.text: "atha laukikottamasiddhayaḥ sādhayitukāmena tenādita eva tathaiva japatā māsamekamaṣṭasāhasrikeṇa japtavyaḥ / tato 'nte mudrāṃ badhvā tathaiva sakalāṃ rātriṃ japet, yāvanmudrā jvalati / tataḥ prabhṛti mudrābandhena laukikasiddhividyādharasiddhīnāmekataro bhavatī-"tyāha bhagavāṃ vajradharaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s> said: 'Now, one who desires to accomplish the supreme worldly accomplishments should first, reciting in the same manner for one month, recite with eight thousand [repetitions]. Then, at the end, having bound the <s>mudrā</s>, one should recite in the same manner for the entire night until the <s>mudrā</s> blazes. Thenceforth, by binding the <s>mudrā</s>, one becomes one [who has attained] either the worldly accomplishment or the <s>vidyādhara</s>-accomplishment.'
The elaboration of the procedure of service to the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family is fully completed.
Now the elaboration of the procedure of service to the <s>vajra</s>-family is as follows:

body.text: "tatrādita eva pūrvamevaṃ kuryāt / tathaiva yathākāmakaraṇīyatayā, akṣaralakṣaṃ japet / asya sakalāṃ rātriṃ japet / tataḥ prabhṛti sarvasatvanigrahānugrahakṣamo bhavatī-"tyāha bhagavāṃ vajradharaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s> said: 'Therein, first one should do as before. In the same manner, according to one's wish, one should recite one hundred thousand syllables. One should recite for the entire night. Thenceforth one becomes capable of restraining and favoring all beings.'

body.text: atha sādhayitumicchet tena yathāvatpaṭaṃ citrāpayitavyaḥ / tatastathaiva pūjāṃ kṛtvā māsamekaṃ sarvakāmabhojī yathākāmakaraṇīyatayā, aṣṭasāhasrikeṇa jāpena catuḥsandhya vajravācā japet, tāvadyāvanmāsānte paṭasyodārāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā vajra-huṃkāramahāmudrāṃ badhvā tāvajjapedyāvattasmāt mudrāṃ bandhāt, huṃkāraśabdo viniḥsṛtaḥ / tataḥ prabhāte maheśvarādayo devādhipatayaḥ sagaṇaparivārāḥ puraḥsthitvājñāṃ mārgayanti / tato vidyādhareṇaivaṃ vaktavyaṃ "yadāhaṃ brūyāmāgacchatedaṃ kuruta tadā bhavadbhirāgatya mamājñā kārye-"ti / tataḥ prabhṛti sakalatrilokādhipatirbhavati / yathecchayā ca muhūrtamātreṇa sakalaṃ tribhuvanamājñāpayan bhramati / punarapyeti ca, nigrahānugrahaṃ kurvaṃ, divyāni ca trilokabhogāni copabhuñjan yathākāmakaraṇīyatayā, sarvasurādhipatiyoṣitādyāḥ sarvayoṣitā ārāgayitvopabhuñjati / na ca tasya kaścit kiṃcicchaknoti kartuṃ, huṃkāreṇa ca sarvaduṣṭade[vādīn pramarditvā tatastāvatkalpaśatasahasrān jīvatī-"tyāha bhagavān vajradharaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Now, if one desires to accomplish, one should have a cloth painted properly. Then, having performed worship in the same manner, for one month, partaking of all desired enjoyments, according to one's wish, one should recite at the four junctures with the <s>vajra</s>-voice, with eight thousand recitations, until at the month's end, having performed elaborate worship of the cloth, having bound the <s>vajra</s>-huṃkāra great <s>mudrā</s>, one should recite until from that <s>mudrā</s>-binding the sound of the huṃkāra issues forth. Then, at dawn, <s>Maheśvara</s> and other lords of gods, together with their retinue-hosts, standing before one, seek instruction. Then the <s>vidyādhara</s> should say thus: "When I say 'come and do this,' then you should come and carry out my command." Thenceforth one becomes the sovereign of the entire three worlds. And at one's wish, in a mere moment, commanding the entire triple world, one wanders about. And one returns again, performing restraint and favor, enjoying the divine enjoyments of the three worlds according to one's wish, enamoring and enjoying the consorts of all the lords of the gods and all women. And no one is able to do anything to him, and crushing all wicked gods and the rest with the huṃkāra, one lives for a hundred thousand <s>kalpa</s>s.'

body.text: "atha mudrāsādhanamicched] yathāvajjapaṃ kṛtvā māsānte vajra-huṃ-kārasamayamudrāṃ badhvā sakalāṃ rātriṃ japet / tataḥ prabhāte mudrāḥ siddhā bhavanti / tato yathāvan mudrābandhena huṃkāraprayuktena ākāśagamanaviśvasaṃdarśanāntardhānamāyāsandarśanasarvāveśanākarṣaṇavaśīkaraṇasarvatuṣṭisaṃjananasarvaratnābhiharaṇamahātejojvālāsandarśanaratnavṛṣṭisandarśanamahāṭṭahāsapramuñcanasarvasatvasaṃśodhanacchindanabhindanaṛtucakraparivartanayathāvattatvollāpanasarvakarmapravartanarakṣajaṃbhanastaṃbhanatrāsanamāraṇasarvasatvamudraṇakāmaratikriyāpravartanābhiṣekasarvabhāvagāyāpananṛtyāpanāhvāyanapraveśanasphoṭanāveśanādīni sarvakarmāṇi karotī-"tyāha bhagavān vajradharaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s> said: 'Now, if one desires the <s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment, having performed recitation properly, at the month's end, having bound the <s>vajra</s>-hūṃkāra pledge-<s>mudrā</s>, one should recite for the entire night. Then, at dawn, the <s>mudrā</s>s become accomplished. Then, properly, by the <s>mudrā</s>-binding employed with the huṃkāra, one performs all activities — sky-going, display of all forms, disappearance, display of illusions, entering into all [beings], attracting, subjugating, generating satisfaction in all, bringing all jewels, display of great blazing splendor, display of jewel-rain, releasing great terrifying laughter, purification of all beings, cutting, splitting, turning the wheel of seasons, proper utterance of reality, setting all activities in motion, protection, paralyzing, immobilizing, terrifying, slaying, sealing all beings, performing the activity of desire and delight, consecrating, causing singing of all states, causing dancing, summoning, causing entry, snapping, causing possession, and the rest.'

body.text: "atha sūkṣmajñānasādhanamicchet tena vajra-huṃ-kārasamādhimabhyasatā tathaiva jāpayogena māsaṃ sādhayitavyaṃ / tato 'nte 'nenaiva samādhinā sakalāṃ rātriṃ japet / tāvad yāvat prabhāte pañcābhijñā bhūtvā sarvasatvānugrahanigrahakṣamo bhavatī-"tyāha bhagavān vajradharaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Now, if one desires the accomplishment of subtle knowledge, then having practiced the <s>vajra</s>-huṃ-kāra-<s>samādhi</s>, one should accomplish [it] through the yoga of recitation for one month in the same manner. At the end [of the month], through that very <s>samādhi</s>, one should recite throughout the entire night. Then, at dawn, having obtained the five superknowledges (<s>pañcābhijñā</s>), one becomes capable of both favoring and subduing all beings" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.

body.text: "atha karmasādhanamicchet tena tathaiva japatā māsamekaṃ sādhayitavyaṃ / tato 'nte sakalāṃ rātriṃ japet / tataḥ sarvakarmāṇi sidhyantī"tyāha bhagavān vajradharaḥ // tataḥ karmāṇi bhavanti sakṛduccāritena manīṣitayā rakṣādīni sarvakarmāṇi karoti //
body.translated_text: "Now, if one desires the accomplishment of action, then reciting in the same manner, one should practice for one month. At the end [of the month], one should recite throughout the entire night. Then all actions are accomplished" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>. Thereupon, actions arise: by a single utterance, with one's intention, one performs all actions such as protection and the rest.
The detailed procedure of the ancillary accomplishment of the <s>Vajra</s> family is completed.
Now there is the detailed procedure of the ancillary [practices] of the <s>Padma</s> family.

body.text: "tatrādita eva tāvacchatasahasraṃ japet, pūrvamevākṛtā bha[vati]tataḥ sādhanaṃ bhavati / paṭe bhagavān sarvajagadvinayādyāḥ kartavyāstasya sarvapārśveṣu caturmaṇḍalayogena mahāsatvacatuṣṭayaḥ kāryaḥ ante ca devyaḥ / tataḥ sa eva jāpavidhivistaro māsānte sakalāṃ rātriṃ japet / tataḥ sarvajagadvinayo bhagavānāgacchati, yathākālaṃ vareṇābhipracārayatī-"ti āha bhagavān vajradharaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Therein, first of all, one should recite one hundred thousand [times]; once the preliminary [practice] has been completed, then the accomplishment [practice] begins. On a cloth, one should depict the Blessed One <s>Sarvajagadvinaya</s> and the others; on all his sides, through the yoga of the four <s>maṇḍala</s>s, one should create the four <s>mahāsattva</s>s, and at the periphery, the goddesses. Then, [following] the same detailed procedure of recitation, at the end of the month one should recite throughout the entire night. Then the Blessed One <s>Sarvajagadvinaya</s> comes, and at the appropriate time bestows the boon" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.

body.text: "atha mudrāsādhanamicchet tena tathaiva padmavajrimudrābandhaṃ kṛtvā yathāvan mucyāṣṭasāhasrikeṇa jāpena catuḥsandhyaṃ japet / tataḥ sakalāṃ rātriṃ mudrābandhena japet / prabhāte siddhirbhavati / tato mudrābandhena yathāvat sarvajagadvinayaṃ karotī-"tyāha bhagavānavalokiteśvaraḥ //
body.translated_text: "Now, if one desires the accomplishment of <s>mudrā</s>, then in the same manner, having bound the <s>padmavajrī</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, properly releasing [it], one should recite with eight thousand recitations at the four junctures [of the day].
