Then one should recite throughout the entire night with the <s>mudrā</s> bound. At dawn, accomplishment arises. Then through the <s>mudrā</s>-binding, one properly performs the subjugation of the entire world (<s>sarvajagadvinaya</s>)" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.

body.text: "atha samādhinayasādhanamamicchet tena tathaiva māsānte sakalāṃ rātriṃ yathābhirucitena samādhinā jāpo dātavyaḥ / tataḥ prabhāte sarvasamādhaya āmukhībhavantī-"tyāha bhagavān vajradharmaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Now, if one desires the accomplishment of the <s>samādhi</s>-method, then in the same manner, at the end of the month, throughout the entire night, recitation should be performed with whichever <s>samādhi</s> one prefers. Then at dawn, all <s>samādhi</s>s become accessible" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradharma</s>.

body.text: atha karmasādhanamicchet tathaiva japanmāsānte sakalāṃ rātriṃ japet / tataḥ sarvakarmakṣayo bhavatī-"tyāha bhagavāṃ vajradharaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Now, if one desires the accomplishment of action, reciting in the same manner, at the end of the month one should recite throughout the entire night. Then the exhaustion of all <s>karma</s> occurs" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
The detailed procedure of the ancillary [practices] of the <s>Padma</s> family is completed.
Now there is the detailed procedure of the ancillary [practices] of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Jewel) family.

body.text: "tatrādita eva sarvatathāgatapraṇāmacatuṣṭayaṃ kṛtvā śatasahasraṃ japet / tatastathaiva paṭe bhagavāṃ sarvārthasiddhiṃ caturmudrāmaṇḍalayogena likhet / tatastathaiva pūjāṃ kṛtvā tathaiva sādhayet / māsānte sakalāṃ rātriṃ japet / tataḥ prabhāte bhagavāṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekaratnaḥ ākāśagarbho bodhisatva āgatyābhiṣekaṃ dadāti / tenābhiṣekeṇa trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau vidyādharacakravartī bhavatī-"tyāha bhagavān vajradharaḥ /
body.translated_text: "Therein, first of all, having performed the fourfold prostration to all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, one should recite one hundred thousand [times]. Then, in the same manner, on a cloth one should depict the Blessed One <s>Sarvārthasiddhi</s> through the yoga of the four-<s>mudrā</s>-<s>maṇḍala</s>. Then, having performed worship in the same manner, one should practice likewise. At the end of the month, one should recite throughout the entire night. Then at dawn, the Blessed One, the Jewel of the Consecration of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s, [and] the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, having come, bestow the consecration. Through that consecration, one becomes a <s>vidyādhara</s>-<s>cakravartin</s> (sovereign wielder of knowledge) in the tri-thousand great-thousand world-system" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.

body.text: "atha mudrāsādhanamicchet tena tathaiva dharmavajriprayogeṇa vajraratnamudrā yathāvatsādhyā sarvāśākarmakarī bhavatī //
body.translated_text: "Now, if one desires the accomplishment of <s>mudrā</s>, then in the same manner, through the practice of the <s>dharmavajrī</s>, the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-<s>mudrā</s> should be properly accomplished — it becomes the performer of all wish-fulfilling actions.

body.text: "atha maṇijñānamicchet sādhayituṃ tena tathaiva vajraratnodbhavasamādhiryathānukramato bhāvayitavyaḥ / niḥsvabhāvādākāśātkathaṃ ratnasaṃbhava iti, ratnācca kathaṃ bodhisatvakāyasaṃbhava iti / imaṃ samādhiṃ catuḥsaṃdhyaṃ bhāvya japed, yathopari tato māsānte tenaiva samādhinā [sakalāṃ rā]triṃ japet / tataḥ prabhāte sarvatathāgatairāgatya yathābhirucito 'bhiṣicyata"ityāha bhagavanākāśagarbhaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Now, if one desires to accomplish jewel-knowledge, then in the same manner, the <s>samādhi</s> arisen from the <s>vajra</s>-jewel should be cultivated in sequence: 'How does a jewel arise from space, which is without inherent nature?' and 'How does a <s>bodhisattva</s>-body arise from the jewel?' Having contemplated this <s>samādhi</s> at the four junctures [of the day] and recited, as described above, at the end of the month one should recite throughout the entire night with that very <s>samādhi</s>. Then at dawn, all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having come, consecrate [the practitioner] as one prefers" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Ākāśagarbha</s>.

body.text: "atha kāmasādhana[micchet] tathaiva japatā māsānte sakalāṃ rātriṃ japet / tataḥ prabhāte bhagavānākāśagarbhaḥ sarvārthasādhako bhavatīti / tataḥ sarvakarmāṇi kuryād" ityāha bhagavānāryavajradharaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Now, if one desires the accomplishment of desires, reciting in the same manner, at the end of the month one should recite throughout the entire night. Then at dawn, <s>Bhagavān Ākāśagarbha</s> becomes the accomplisher of all purposes. Thereupon, one should perform all actions" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Āryavajradhara</s>.
The detailed procedure of the ancillary [practices] of the <s>Maṇi</s> (Jewel) family is completed.
Now there is the detailed common procedure of the ancillary [practices] of all families.
Therein, first of all, the detailed ancillary [practice] of all heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s:

body.text: "hṛdayamanīṣitāni sarvatathāgatānāṃ sidhyantām" ityuccārya hṛdayaṃ yathābhirucito japya sādhanavidhiḥ kartavya iti //
body.translated_text: "Having uttered, 'May the intentions of the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s be accomplished,' one should recite whichever heart[-<s>mantra</s>] one prefers and perform the accomplishment procedure."

body.text: tatrāyaṃ mudropacāravidhiḥ / "sarvamudrā me bhogyā bhavantī-" tyuktvā samayamudrāṃ badhvā yathābhirucito yathāśaktyā japet / tato yathāvatsiddhiriti //
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the procedure for the ancillary [practice] of <s>mudrā</s>: "Having said, 'May all <s>mudrā</s>s become enjoyable to me,' one should bind the pledge-<s>mudrā</s> and recite whichever [<s>mantra</s>] one prefers according to one's ability. Then accomplishment [comes] as appropriate."

body.text: tatrāyaṃ sarvamantropacāravidhiḥ / "niḥprapañcā vāksiddhirbhavatu, sarvatathāgatasamādhayo me ājāyantām" ityuktvā mantraṃ yathābhirucito japet, eṣā siddhiriti //
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the procedure for the ancillary [practice] of all <s>mantra</s>s: "Having said, 'May the accomplishment of speech free from conceptual elaboration arise, may the <s>samādhi</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s arise in me,' one should recite whichever <s>mantra</s> one prefers — this is the accomplishment."

body.text: tatrāyaṃ vidyopacāravidhiḥ / "avidyāndhā ca te me satvāḥ sarvatathāgatāśca vidyādhigamasaṃvarabhūtā" ityuktvā vidyāṃ yathābhirucito japya sādhanamāvahed" ityāha bhagavānāryavajradharaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the procedure for the ancillary [practice] of <s>vidyā</s>: "Having said, 'Those beings of mine are blinded by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), and all <s>Tathāgata</s>s are the embodiment of the vow of attaining knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>),' one should recite whichever <s>vidyā</s> one prefers and bring about the accomplishment" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Āryavajradhara</s>.

body.text: "atha sarvahṛdayamudrāmantravidyānāṃ yathākāmakaraṇīyatayā vajrajāpavidhivistaro bhavati / yasya satvasya hṛnmudrāṃ mantraṃ vidyāṃ tu sādhayet / jāpārthatastamātmānaṃ satvaṃ vā sādhya sidhyatī-" tyāha bhagavān vajrasatvaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Now there is the detailed procedure of <s>vajra</s>-recitation for performing at will all heart[-<s>mantra</s>]s, <s>mudrā</s>s, <s>mantra</s>s, and <s>vidyā</s>s: 'Of whatever being one would accomplish the heart[-<s>mantra</s>], <s>mudrā</s>, <s>mantra</s>, or <s>vidyā</s> — by accomplishing that very being or oneself for the purpose of recitation, accomplishment is achieved'" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
The detailed common recitation procedure of all families is completed.
Now there is the detailed common accomplishment procedure of all families.

body.text: tatrādita eva tathāgatakulasiddhayaḥ / tadyathārthaniṣpattisiddhiḥ ṛddhisiddhirvidyādharatvaṃ mahāsiddhiśceti //
body.translated_text: Therein, first of all, the accomplishments of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family, namely: the accomplishment of material attainment (<s>arthaniṣpatti</s>), the accomplishment of supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>), <s>vidyādhara</s>-hood, and the great accomplishment (<s>mahāsiddhi</s>).

body.text: "tatrārthaniṣpattirbhavati / yatrā nidhiśaṅkā bhavet tatra mudrāṃ badhvā svasamādhinā tannidhisthānaṃ vajradṛṣṭyā nirīkṣayet / yadi vajrākāramuttiṣṭhatvaṃ paśyati tathā jñātavyaṃ nidhiratrāstīti / tato vajrasphoṭasamayamudrāṃ badhvotkhanya yathākāmakaraṇīyatayā gṛṇhīyādacirāt prāpnotī-" tyāha bhagavān vajrasatvaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Therein, the material attainment arises thus: wherever one suspects a treasure, there, having bound the <s>mudrā</s>, in one's own <s>samādhi</s>, one should examine that treasure-location with the <s>vajra</s>-gaze. If one sees a <s>vajra</s>-form arising, then one should know: 'A treasure is here.' Then, having bound the <s>vajra</s>-bursting-pledge-<s>mudrā</s>, digging it up, one should take [it] to use at will — one obtains [it] before long" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.

body.text:
"tatra ṛddhisiddhiniṣpattirbhavati / yāṃ mudrāṃ sādhayed "vajrasiddhir / "ityuktvā ṛddhisiddhiścaturvidhā bhava[nti tadyathā] jalasyoparicaṃkramaṇaniṣīdatādikaṃ tathāgatādisarvarūpasaṃdarśanaṃ yāvadabhirucistāvad adreṣyatvaṃ / ākāśagāmī ca yojanasahasramūrdhvamutpatyadhastācca gacchati / sarvādiśaśca yojanasahasrād yathābhirucitavegaḥ paribhramyāgacchati / yojanasahasrādarśena sarvasatvamanīṣitāni jñānāti / sarvabhāvāni ca cakṣuṣā paśyati śrotreṇa śṛṇoti / sarvadikṣu sa yojanasahasrādarśena mano 'bhirucitāḥ sarvastriyo 'ṅge samutkṣipyānayati / sarvahiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktādayaśca sarvārthānapaharati, na cāsya kaścit kiṃcit chaknoti kartuṃ / yad vajreṇāpyadṛśyo bhavati /
kiṃ punaranyaiḥ? / daśapuruṣasahasrabalī nityārogyavān nityaṃ sarvakāmopabhojī sadāyauvano divyarūpī sarvatathāgatān savajrasatvāṃ paśyan pūjayaṃścānuttaravajrasiddhiścatvārivarṣasahasrāṇi jīvatī-" tyāha bhagavān sarvatathāgatavajraṛddhiḥ //
body.translated_text:
"Therein, the accomplishment of supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>-<s>siddhi</s>) arises thus: whichever <s>mudrā</s> one would accomplish — having said '<s>vajra</s>-accomplishment!' — the fourfold supernatural accomplishment arises, namely: walking on water, sitting upon it, and so forth; displaying all forms such as <s>Tathāgata</s> and others, as far as one desires; invisibility; and sky-going — flying upward one thousand <s>yojana</s>s and descending below; and traversing one thousand <s>yojana</s>s in all directions at whatever speed one desires, then returning. One knows the intentions of all beings within a thousand <s>yojana</s>s by sight. One sees all things with the eye and hears with the ear. In all directions within a thousand <s>yojana</s>s by sight, one lifts upon one's body and brings all women [one] desires. One carries away all gold, silver, jewels, pearls, and all valuables, and no one is able to do anything to one — for one becomes invisible even to the <s>vajra</s>.
How much more so to others? One possesses the strength of ten thousand men, is always free from illness, always enjoys all pleasures, is perpetually youthful, of divine form, seeing and worshipping all <s>Tathāgata</s>s together with <s>Vajrasattva</s>, and with the unsurpassed <s>vajra</s>-accomplishment, lives for four thousand years" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatavajraṛddhi</s>.

body.text: tatrāyaṃ vajravidyādharasiddhiniṣpattirbhavati / mudrān sādhayaṃ "vajravidyādhara" iti kuryāt, siddhayā vajravidyādharacakravartī bhavati / sarvakāmopabhogī sahasrabuddhakṣetramekakṣaṇena paribhramyāgacchati / sarvasukhāni paribhuṃkte / dviraṣṭavarṣavayuḥ ākuñcitakuṇḍalakeśadhārī mahāvajravidyādharaḥ sarvatathāgatān savajrasatvān paśyan mahākalpasthāyī bhavatī-" tyāha bhagavān sarvatathāgatavidyādharaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the accomplishment of <s>vajra</s>-<s>vidyādhara</s>-hood: accomplishing the <s>mudrā</s>, one should declare '<s>vajra</s>-<s>vidyādhara</s>!' Through that accomplishment, one becomes a <s>vajra</s>-<s>vidyādhara</s>-<s>cakravartin</s> (sovereign wielder of <s>vajra</s>-knowledge). One enjoys all pleasures and traverses a thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields in a single instant, then returns. One experiences all joys. Appearing as a youth of sixteen years, bearing curled and coiled hair, a great <s>vajra</s>-<s>vidyādhara</s>, seeing all <s>Tathāgata</s>s together with <s>Vajrasattva</s>, one endures for a great <s>kalpa</s>" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatavidyādhara</s>.

body.text: tatra mahāsiddhiniṣpattirbhavati / svamudrāṃ hṛdayārthataḥ sādhayan / svamudrā satvarūpī bhavatya, ekakṣaṇena daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu viśvarūpī viśvakriyāpravartakaḥ, sarvatathāgatān savajrasatvāṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvākāravaropetābhiḥ sarvatathāgatapūjābhiḥ saṃpūjyāśeṣānavaśeṣasatvārthaṃ ca kṛtvā punarapyāyāti / sarvalokadhātusarvakāmasarvasukhasaumanasyāni sarvākāravaropetānyupabhuñjan, vajrasatvasamo mahābodhisatvaḥ aśeṣānavaśeṣamahākalpāyurbhavatī-" tyāha bhagavān sarvatathāgatasiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, the great accomplishment (<s>mahāsiddhi</s>) arises thus: accomplishing one's own <s>mudrā</s> with the intention of the heart — one's own <s>mudrā</s> assumes the form of a being; in a single instant, in all world-systems in the ten directions, manifesting in all forms, setting in motion all activities, seeing all <s>Tathāgata</s>s together with <s>Vajrasattva</s>, worshipping [them] with all manner of excellent <s>Tathāgata</s>-offerings, and having performed the welfare of all beings without remainder, one returns again. Enjoying all the pleasures, joys, and mental delights of all world-systems, endowed with all excellent qualities — a great <s>bodhisattva</s> equal to <s>Vajrasattva</s>, one lives for immeasurable great <s>kalpa</s>s without remainder" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatasiddhi</s>.

body.text: tatraitā vajrakulasiddhayaḥ / tadyathā trilokavijayasiddhiḥ sarvābhiṣekasiddhiḥ sarvasukhasaumanasyasiddhiḥ uttamasiddhiriti //
body.translated_text: Therein, these are the accomplishments of the <s>Vajra</s> family, namely: the accomplishment of the Conquest of the Three Worlds (<s>Trilokavijaya</s>), the accomplishment of all consecrations, the accomplishment of all happiness and mental delight, and the supreme accomplishment.

body.text: "tatra trilokavijayasiddhirbhavati / trilokavijayamudrāṃ badhvā maheśvaraṃ [vāmapa]denākramya sādhayet / tataḥ sā pratimā nādaṃ muñcati / tato huṃkāraḥ prayoktavyaḥ / huṃkāre prayuktemātre maheśvarādayaḥ sarvatrailokyādhipatayaḥ saparivārā; sādhakasya purata āgatvā ājñāvaśyavidheyā bhavanti / tataḥ prabhṛti sarvatrilokādhipatirvajradharo bhavati / ākāśena gacchati sakalatrilokacakraṃ parikramyāgacchati, duṣṭadevādayaśca sarvasatvān huṃkāreṇa damayati / sarvatathāgatavajrahuṃkārarūpī sakalatrilokamājñayā vartayan sarvatathāgatān savajrasatvān paśyannārāgayaṃśca varṣahasrān jīvatī-" tyāha bhagavān vajrahuṃkāraḥ //
body.translated_text: "Therein, the accomplishment of the Conquest of the Three Worlds arises thus: having bound the <s>Trilokavijaya</s>-<s>mudrā</s>, treading upon <s>Maheśvara</s> with the left foot, one should practice. Then that image emits a sound. Then the <s>huṃkāra</s> should be employed. The very moment the <s>huṃkāra</s> is employed, <s>Maheśvara</s> and all the lords of the three worlds with their retinues, having come before the practitioner, become obedient to one's command. From then on, one becomes the <s>vajra</s>-bearing sovereign of all three worlds. One goes through the sky, traverses the entire wheel of the three worlds and returns, and subdues wicked <s>deva</s>s and all beings with the <s>huṃkāra</s>. Assuming the form of the <s>vajra</s>-<s>huṃkāra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, governing the entire three worlds by command, seeing all <s>Tathāgata</s>s together with <s>Vajrasattva</s> and delighting [in them], one lives for a thousand years" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajrahuṃkāra</s>.

body.text:
"tatrāyaṃ sarvābhiṣekasiddhimudrāṃ sādhayan / sarvatathāgatābhiṣekaratnamudrayā pūrvamātmānamabhiṣicya sādhayet / tatastasya siddhasya caturvidhamabhiṣeko bhavati /
vajrābhiṣeko ratnābhiṣeko dharmābhiṣekaḥ karmābhiṣekaśceti / tatra vajrābhiṣeke labdhe sarvatathāgatānāṃ vajradharo bhavati / ratnābhiṣeke sarvaratnādhipatirbhavati /
dharmābhiṣeke dharmarājā bhavati / karmābhiṣeke laukikarokottarasarvakarmasiddhimavāpnotī-" tyāha bhagavāṃ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekaḥ //
body.translated_text:
"Therein, accomplishing the <s>mudrā</s> of the accomplishment of all consecrations — first having consecrated oneself with the jewel-<s>mudrā</s> of the consecration of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, one should practice. Then for the accomplished one, the fourfold consecration arises:
the <s>vajra</s>-consecration, the jewel-consecration, the <s>dharma</s>-consecration, and the action-consecration. Therein, having obtained the <s>vajra</s>-consecration, one becomes the <s>vajra</s>-bearer of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s. [With] the jewel-consecration, one becomes the lord of all jewels.
[With] the <s>dharma</s>-consecration, one becomes a <s>Dharma</s>-king. [With] the action-consecration, one attains the accomplishment of all worldly and supramundane actions" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatābhiṣeka</s>.

body.text: "tatreyaṃ sarvasukhasaumanasyasiddhir, yaduta guhyapūjābhirnityaṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāṃ kurvan, sarvatathāgatasarvasukhasaumanasyasiddhimavāpnotī-" tyāha bhagavāṃ sarvatathāgatasarvasukhasaumanasyaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Therein, this is the accomplishment of all happiness and mental delight: namely, always performing the worship of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s with secret offerings, one attains the accomplishment of all happiness and mental delight of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatasarvasukhasaumanasya</s>.
"Therein, this is the supreme accomplishment: namely, 'I am equal to <s>Vajradhara</s>'" — thus spoke <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.

Therein, these are the accomplishments of the <s>Padma</s> family, namely: the accomplishment of attraction (<s>anurāgaṇa</s>), subjugation (<s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>), protection (<s>rakṣa</s>), and lotus-<s>siddhi</s>.

children.translated_text: "Therein, the accomplishment of attraction arises thus: through the contemplation of lotus-passion as appropriate, one becomes capable of attracting all beings beginning with all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Through the recollection of one's own <s>Lokeśvara</s>, one likewise becomes capable of subjugating all beings.
Through the <s>samādhi</s> of pervading loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), one becomes capable of protecting, shielding, and guarding the entire world.

children.text: svaṃ padmasamādhinā padmaṃ hastena gṛhya sādhayaṃ lokeśvararūpī sarvākāravaropetaścaturvarṣahasraṃ jīvatī-" tyāha bhagavān sarvatathāgatapadmaḥ //
children.translated_text: by one's own <s>padma</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, grasping a lotus in hand and accomplishing, in the form of <s>Lokeśvara</s>, endowed with excellence of all forms, one lives for four thousand years.' Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatapadma</s>.

body.text: tatraitā maṇikulasiddhayaḥ / tadyathā sarvakulābhiṣekasiddhiḥ, mahātejastvaṃ, sarvāśāprapūraṇaṃ, ratnasiddhiśceti //
body.translated_text: Therein, these are the accomplishments of the <s>maṇi</s>-family, namely: the accomplishment of consecration of all families, great radiance, fulfillment of all wishes, and jewel-accomplishment.

body.text: "tatra sarvatathāgatābhiṣekasiddhiḥ / yaduta svābhiṣekaniryātanā pradīpadānaṃ dānapāramitāpāripūriḥ, yathāśakyaratnasādhanaṃ catvābhiḥ siddhibhiḥ sarvatathāgatāṃ pūjayannacirāt sidhyatī-" tyāha bhagavāṃ sarvatathāgataratnaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Therein, the accomplishment of the consecration of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>: namely, offering one's own consecration, the giving of lamps, the fulfillment of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), and the accumulation of jewels as far as one is able — worshipping all <s>Tathāgatas</s> with these four accomplishments, one quickly accomplishes.' Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgataratna</s>.
The detailed procedure of the accomplishments common to all families is completed.
'Now I shall explain the accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the methods of all rituals.' Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the being without beginning or end.
Therein, first of all, the accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the heart-method:

children.text: yathā vinayo loko hi tādṛśī siddhiriṣyate /
children.translated_text: As the world is to be disciplined, such is the accomplishment that is desired;
the method therein is the <s>mudrā</s>, the great bestower of all accomplishments.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>mudrā</s>-method accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The world is disciplined through dispassion, yet <s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment is born from passion;
the method therein is meditation — the supreme producer of all accomplishments.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>mantra</s>-method accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: This world has fallen from truth; <s>mantra</s>-accomplishment is not desired [by it];
the method is freedom from conceptual elaboration — the supreme producer of all accomplishments.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>vidyā</s>-method accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: This [world] is attached to ignorance; <s>vidyā</s>-accomplishment is not desired [by it];
the method therein is the exalted one — the supreme bestower of all accomplishments. Thus.

body.translated_text: The accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of the methods of all rituals.
'Now I shall explain the merit-accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of all rituals.' Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgata</s>.
Therein, first of all, the merit-accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of one's own heart:

children.translated_text: Having performed the fourfold worship, one attains great merit;

children.text: buddhapūjāgrapuṇyā hi sidhyate nātraṃ saṃśaya // iti //
children.translated_text: the merit of <s>Buddha</s>-worship is foremost — it is accomplished; there is no doubt herein. Thus.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>mudrā</s>-merit accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Guarding the secret pledge, one attains great merit;

children.text: apuṇyo 'pi hi sidhyeya śīghraṃ samayarakṣaṇād // iti //
children.translated_text: even one without merit can quickly accomplish through guarding the pledge. Thus.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>mantra</s>-merit accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Through the primordial words of the <s>Buddhas</s>, one attains great merit;
through the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, even one without merit quickly attains accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>vidyā</s>-merit accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Giving is the foremost of merits — by giving, one attains merit;
one who is complete in the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) quickly attains Buddhahood. Thus.

body.translated_text: The merit-accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of all rituals.
'Now I shall explain the wisdom-accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of all rituals.
Therein, first of all, the heart-wisdom accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

body.text:
a-akṣarapraveśena sarvākṣaravijānanā /
svavaktraparavaktraṃ tu bhāvayaṃ siddhimāpnuyād /
body.translated_text:
Through entering the syllable 'A,' there is knowledge of all syllables;
meditating on one's own face as the face of another, one attains accomplishment.
Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>mudrā</s>-wisdom accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The <s>prajñā</s> called 'penetrating' is proclaimed as <s>samādhi</s>;

children.text: tayā tu mudrāḥ sidhyante bhāvayaṃ sidhyati kṣaṇād //
children.translated_text: through it, <s>mudrā</s>s are accomplished — meditating, one accomplishes in an instant.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Prajñāgrya</s> (Foremost in Wisdom).
Therein, this is the <s>mantra</s>-wisdom accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The one called 'following the sound of <s>prajñā</s>,' through being <s>samādhi</s>, through elaboration —
through cultivating it, one quickly attains <s>mantra</s>-accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrabuddhi</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>vidyā</s>-wisdom accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Between <s>vidyā</s> and special <s>mantra</s>s, there is no distinction;
meditating thus with <s>prajñā</s>, accomplishment will surely come swiftly.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgataprajñājñāna</s> (Wisdom-Knowledge of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>).
The detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of wisdom-accomplishment of all rituals.
'Now I shall explain the accumulation-accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of rituals.' Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>.
Therein, first of all, the accumulation-accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of all hearts:

children.translated_text: Performing all worship, the accumulation indeed increases;

children.text: kuśalānāṃ tu dharmāṇāṃ tataḥ sidhyati saṃbhṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: then, having accumulated wholesome <s>dharma</s>s, one accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>mudrā</s>-accumulation accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Through entering many <s>cakra</s>s and through the creation of many <s>maṇḍala</s>s,
through the worship-<s>mudrā</s>s of accumulation, great accomplishment proceeds.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>mantra</s>-accumulation accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Through the method of rejoicing and through reciting the true <s>Dharma</s>,
and through the bestowing of many recitations, <s>mantra</s>-accomplishment will surely come. Thus.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>vidyā</s>-accumulation accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Through the thorough abandonment of ignorance and through the path of the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>),
one whose accumulation is complete quickly attains accomplishment. Thus.

body.translated_text: The accumulation-accomplishment <s>tantra</s> of all rituals.
The detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of all rituals is completed.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, brought forth the <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the origin of emblems of all families. Therein, how does the <s>vajra</s> originate?

children.text: sa eva bhagavāṃ satvaḥ sarvacittaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: That very <s>Bhagavān</s>, the being, the mind of all, the self-sovereign lord,
is the <s>vajra</s> of body, speech, and mind — the firm being, self-born.
The supreme being among beings, through <s>vajra</s>-meditation in the heart,

children.text: vajrasatva iti khyātastu tasmiṃ vajro pratiṣṭhitaḥ //
children.translated_text: is known as <s>Vajrasattva</s> — in him the <s>vajra</s> is established.
That very one, through the method of <s>jñāna</s>, of the <s>Buddhas</s> of incomparable splendor,
emerging from the heart, becomes universal, assuming all forms.

children.text: sarvadhāturajaḥsaṃkhyāḥ sa eva tu jino bhavet /
children.translated_text: Equal in number to the dust-particles of all realms, that very one becomes the <s>Jina</s>;
from those <s>vajra</s>-bodies, <s>Vajrasattva</s> arises.
From that very primordial being arise all the emblems;
from the emblems arise the great beings — from them all this is guided. Thus.
Whoever hears this, has faith, and holds it in the heart,
and meditates, always contented — one will quickly attain accomplishment.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
The detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of the knowledge of the origin of the reality of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, spoke the detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of the knowledge of the origin of all rituals.
Therein, first of all, this is the <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the ritual-origin of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>:

children.translated_text: The <s>jñāna</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> is non-conceptual and eternal;
from that non-conceptual <s>jñāna</s>, through conceptualization, a ritual (<s>kalpa</s>) is called so.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the ritual-origin of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family:

children.translated_text: Where the non-conceptual one, whose essence is ritual, is conceived as arising from conceptualization —
<s>Vajrasattva</s>, the great being — by that it is called a ritual.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the ritual-origin of the <s>vajra</s> family:

children.text: yathā likhya hi kalpayante vidhayaḥ kalpasiddhidāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as by writing, procedures granting ritual-accomplishment are conceived —
therefore it is called a ritual, by those whose nature is free from conceptualization.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the ritual-origin of the <s>padma</s> family:

children.text: rāgo vikalpasaṃbhūtaḥ sa ca padme pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Passion arises from conceptualization, and it is established in the lotus;
therefore, accomplishments that abide in ritual indeed arise.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the ritual-origin of the <s>maṇi</s> family:

children.translated_text: Gems are indeed non-conceptual, elevated with their powers;
thus divine accomplishments arise, free from conceptualization.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
The <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the ritual-origin of all families.
Now, the <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the heart-origin of all rituals:

children.translated_text: Through the procedures of intention, what is intended is accomplished;
the accomplisher through <s>samādhi</s>, abiding in the heart — therefore it is called 'heart.'

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the origin of all <s>mudrā</s>s:

children.translated_text: Just as a king's supreme decree-seal is difficult to transgress and inviolable,
so too the universal emblem of the great being — thus it is proclaimed as '<s>mudrā</s>.'

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the origin of <s>mantra</s>:

children.text: anatikrama[ṇo ca] hi durbhedyo guhya eva ca /
children.translated_text: Indeed inviolable and impenetrable and secret,
the secret accomplishment is counseled — therefore it is called '<s>mantra</s>.'

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the origin of <s>vidyā</s>:

children.translated_text: For the destruction of ignorance, for the accomplishment of the supreme <s>vidyā</s> of speech,
the accomplishment of knowing is found — therefore it is proclaimed as '<s>vidyā</s>.'

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhara</s>.
The <s>tantra</s> of the knowledge of the origin of heart and the rest of all rituals.
Now, the <s>tantra</s> of the arising of knowledge of all rituals.
Therein, first of all, this is the <s>tantra</s> of the arising of heart-knowledge:

children.text: hṛdayaṃ japya vijñeyamātmano vā parasya vā /
children.translated_text: Having recited the heart[-<s>mantra</s>], one should know what is to be known — of oneself or of another,

children.text: bhavyaṃ bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati śṛṇoti ca //
children.translated_text: what is to come, what has been, and what will be — one who sees and hears all.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>tantra</s> of the arising of <s>mudrā</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: Having formed one or another <s>mudrā</s> according to the proper procedure, with the mind

children.text: kṛtvā nirīkṣellokaṃ tu sarvaṃ jñeyaṃ yathoparī- // ti //
children.translated_text: directed, gazing upon the world — all that is to be known becomes known as described above. Thus.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the <s>tantra</s> of the arising of <s>mantra</s>-knowledge:

children.translated_text: One who utters a <s>mantra</s> once and speaks with one's own tongue —

children.text: bhavyaṃ bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca tatsarvaṃ satyamāvahed //
children.translated_text: what is to come, what has been, and what will be — all that becomes truth.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>tantra</s> of the arising of <s>vidyā</s>-knowledge:

children.text: sakṛduccārya vidyāṃ tu vedayenmanasā sa tu /
children.translated_text: Having uttered the <s>vidyā</s> once, one should perceive with the mind;

children.text: bhavya bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ [ca vajravākśāsa]naṃ yathe- // ti //
children.translated_text: what is to come, what has been, and what will be — like the decree of <s>vajra</s>-speech. Thus.

body.translated_text: The detailed <s>tantra</s> of the procedure of the arising of knowledge of all rituals is completed.
Now, the <s>tantra</s> of the accomplishment of the secret body-speech-mind <s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s> common to all families.
Therein, this is the accomplishment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family secret body-<s>mudrā</s>:

children.text: yathā tathā niṣaṇṇastu paryaṅkena tu sādhayet /
children.translated_text: However one is seated, one should accomplish through the cross-legged posture;
following the depiction, the great being accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the accomplishment of the <s>vajra</s>-family secret body-<s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: In the well-established warrior's stance (<s>pratyālīḍha</s>), following the depiction,
one should accomplish in great fury — accomplishment herein is without doubt.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrahuṃkāra</s>.
Therein, this is the accomplishment of the <s>padma</s>-family secret body-<s>mudrā</s>:

children.translated_text: Established in the <s>vajra</s>-cross-legged posture, with both hands in <s>vajra</s>-binding,
having become a body in <s>samādhi</s>, one should accomplish that which arises from the lotus.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Padmasattva</s>.
Therein, this is the accomplishment of the <s>maṇi</s>-family secret body-<s>mudrā</s>:

children.text: utthito vā niṣaṇṇo vā caṅkraman vā yathā tathā /
children.translated_text: Whether standing, sitting, walking, or in whatever posture,
through the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-consecration, accomplishment herein is without doubt.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajragarbha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family secret speech-<s>mudrā</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: With the tongue-tip not overly flowing, joined with the two sets of teeth and lips,
one should accomplish all rituals, free from the tone of <s>vajra</s>-speech.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajravāc</s> (Vajra-Speech).
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family secret speech-<s>mudrā</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: With the thundering '<s>Hūṃ</s>' sound like clouds, firm in deep wrathful speech,
bursting forth in wrath — the great <s>vajra</s>, the accomplishment of <s>vajra</s>-wrath-speech.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Vajrahuṃkāra</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>padma</s>-family secret speech-<s>mudrā</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Without exhalation, with subtle breath, with subtle speech clearly articulated,
all recitations are accomplished, for the <s>samādhi</s>-<s>jñāna</s>-womb.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Sarvatathāgatasamādhijñānagarbha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>maṇi</s>-family secret speech-<s>mudrā</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: With well-articulated speech, always devoted to prostration,
reciting with disciplines also — everything quickly accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Sarvatathāgatapūjāvidhivisarakarmā</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family secret mind-<s>mudrā</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: 'Desire is indeed the eternal <s>Bhagavān</s>, the giver of happiness to all beings;
one is <s>Vajrasattva</s> oneself' — meditating thus, one quickly accomplishes.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Kāma</s> (Desire).
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family secret mind-<s>mudrā</s> accomplishment <s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: For the benefit of all beings, for the discipline of the wicked,
For the sake of protecting the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching, wrath is the supreme accomplisher of <s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>vajra</s>-<s>hūṃkāra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the lotus-family secret-mind-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Just as a lotus, though defiled, is [yet] endowed with great beauty despite the faults of its dwelling,

children.text: tathā me rāgadoṣaistu bhavedrāgaḥ sa sidhyatī- //
children.translated_text: so too, despite the faults of my passion — that passion itself is accomplished as <s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Padmarāga</s>.
Therein, this is the jewel-family secret-mind-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment-<s>tantra</s>:

body.text:
kadā nu sarvasatvānāṃ sarvakāryārthasiddhaye /
ratnavarṣāṇi varṣeyaṃ siddhaḥ sarvāśu sidhyatī- /
body.translated_text:
When will I rain jewel-showers for the accomplishment of all the aims and tasks of all beings?
The accomplished one attains <s>siddhi</s> in all [aims].
Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the noble <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>.
Therein, this is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-family secret-<s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment-<s>tantra</s>:

children.text: utthito vā niṣaṇṇo vā [caṅkramanvā] yathā tathā /
children.translated_text: Whether standing, sitting, or walking, in whatever manner,
with the left hand in the secret <s>mudrā</s> — performing all [actions], one accomplishes <s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the secret <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the <s>vajra</s>-family secret-<s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment-<s>tantra</s>:

children.text: yathā tathā sthitaścaiva kurvan cāpi yathā tathā /
children.translated_text: Abiding in whatever manner, and performing in whatever way,
having bound the crooked wrath-finger, concealed by cloth — <s>siddhi</s> is accomplished.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the great wrathful king of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
Therein, this is the lotus-family secret-<s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: The lotus-fist with the left hand, covered [by cloth],
having bound it — one quickly attains lotus-<s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Avalokiteśvara</s>.
Therein, this is the jewel-family secret-<s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment-<s>tantra</s>:

children.translated_text: Having bound the jewel-fist, with the left [hand] covered, with reverence,

children.text: yathā tathā kriyate vai ratnasiddhimavāpnu] yād //
children.translated_text: performing in whatever manner — one attains jewel-<s>siddhi</s>.

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān Ākāśagarbha</s>.
Therein, this is the all-families secret common <s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment-<s>tantra</s>:

By the method of the great <s>mudrā</s>, in the <s>samādhi</s> of one's own being,
through <s>vajra</s>-speech and <s>vajra</s>-gaze — before long, the supreme <s>siddhi</s> [is attained].
Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Vajrasattva</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.
The secret body-speech-mind-<s>vajra</s>-<s>mudrā</s>-accomplishment-<s>tantra</s> of all families is completed.

body.text: atha bhagavān vajrapāṇiḥ sarvatathāgatanāhūyaivamāha / "pratipadyata bhagavantastathā[gatā idaṃ kalpamadhitiṣṭhanti prativedayanti /"
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān Vajrapāṇi</s>, having summoned all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, said thus: 'Proceed, O <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata</s>s — empower and declare this ritual procedure!'

body.text: atha sa]rvatathāgatāḥ punaḥ samājamāgamya, punarapi sādhukārāṇyadaduḥ /
body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having come again to the assembly, gave their acclamations once more:

children.text: sādhu te vajrasatvāya vajraratnā[ya sādhu te /
children.translated_text: Well done to <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Well done to <s>Vajraratna</s>!

children.text: vajradharmāya te sādhu sādhu te] vajrakarmaṇe //
children.translated_text: Well done to <s>Vajradharma</s>! Well done to <s>Vajrakarma</s>!
This <s>sūtra</s> is well spoken — the unsurpassed <s>Vajrayāna</s>,
the secret of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the compendium of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Thus ends [the section].

body.translated_text: From the <s>Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha</s>, the unsurpassed <s>tantra</s> of all ritual procedures is fully completed.
Chapter 26b: Epilogue of the <s>Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha</s>
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having risen from his seat, praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with this hymn of one hundred and eight names:

children.translated_text: O <s>Vajradhātu</s>, great being, fulfiller of all aims, [you who are] the supreme meaning,
O king of the <s>Śākya</s>s, of great <s>jñāna</s>, whose self is <s>vajra</s> — homage to you! (1)

body.translated_text: O one born of beings, whose meaning is reality (<s>tattva</s>), cause of beings, great method,
O great purposer of beings' aims, fulfiller of tasks, being of beings — homage to you! (2)

children.translated_text: O <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>, great <s>dharma</s>, turner of the <s>dharma</s>-wheel,
O great utterance, foremost of <s>vidyā</s>s, great being — homage to you! (3)
O great activity, great protector, accomplisher of all activities,
O great self, foremost in the conduct of beings, cause of beings — homage to you! (4)
O one who has attained all <s>pāramitā</s>s, knower of omniscient <s>jñāna</s>,
O great skillful means for all beings, great <s>prajñā</s> — homage to you! (5)
O foremost of the foremost in great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), whose nature is compassion, whose self is compassion,
O giver of all gifts, great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), maker of all — homage to you! (6)
O Lion of the <s>Śākya</s>s, great <s>Śākya</s>, <s>Śākya</s> of <s>Śākya</s>s, great sage,
O all-pervading one, great discipliner, guide of the guidable, foremost in discipline — homage to you! (7)
O one who has equally attained the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s> of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,
O <s>Vajra</s>-lord, great lord, mass of beings — homage to you! (8)
O great radiance, great light, great vigor, great power,

children.text: ma[hāvīra suvīrāgrya śambhu vīra namo 'stu te] // 9 //
children.translated_text: O great hero, foremost of excellent heroes, auspicious hero — homage to you! (9)
O <s>Brahman</s>, self-born one, <s>Bhagavān</s>, hero of the <s>Śākya</s>s, great sage,

children.text: sarvātmaka mune śuddha dharmarāja namo 'stu te // 10 //
children.translated_text: O universal self, pure sage, <s>Dharma</s>-king — homage to you! (10)
O one whose body is space, foremost of bodies, contemplator of the three bodies beyond body,
O all-body, great body, <s>vajra</s>-body — homage to you! (11)
O speechless speech, foremost of speeches, revealer of three speeches beyond speech,
O all-speech, supremely great speech, <s>vajra</s>-speech — homage to you! (12)
O mindless mind, foremost of minds, revealer of three minds beyond mind,
O all-mind, great mind, <s>vajra</s>-mind — homage to you! (13)
O non-<s>vajra</s> <s>vajra</s>, foremost of <s>vajra</s>s, purifier of three <s>vajra</s>s beyond <s>vajra</s>,
O all-<s>vajra</s>, great <s>vajra</s>, <s>vajra</s> of <s>vajra</s>s — homage to you! (14)
O all-pervading one, foremost of the foremost of existences, victorious lord of the <s>Sugata</s>s,
O great king of the three realms, <s>Vairocana</s> — homage to you! (15)
And whoever hears this hymn of one hundred and eight names even once,
or recites it or meditates upon it — every [such person] attains <s>Buddha</s>-hood. (16)

body.text:
adhyeṣayā]mi tvānnātha sarvasatvahitārthataḥ /
mahākāruṇyamutpādya dharmacakraṃ pravartaye- // 17 // ti //
body.translated_text:
I entreat you, O lord, for the benefit of all beings —
having generated great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), turn the <s>dharma</s>-wheel! (17) Thus ends [the section].

Then the <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, having heard the command of the lord of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, summoned all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and said thus: 'Proceed, O <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata</s>s, to enter the assembly!'

body.text: jñāvacanamupaśrutya, sarvatathāgatānāhūyaivamāha / "pratipadyata bhagavantaḥ tathāgatāḥ samā[jamāpantum" iti //

body.translated_text: Then all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having entered the assembly, uttered this verse:

body.text:
sarvasatvahitārthāya sarvalokeṣu sarvataḥ /
[yathā vinayato viśvaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartyatām // iti //]
body.translated_text:
For the benefit of all beings, everywhere in all worlds,
according to [their] discipline, let the universal <s>dharma</s>-wheel be turned! Thus ends [the section].

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu sarvasatvānāṃ purataḥ spharya yāvatsarva[paramāṇurajomaṇḍaleṣu bhagavān śākyamuni]stathāgato dharmacakraṃ pravartayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: And the moment this was spoken, pervading before all beings in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, in all world-realms, as far as all the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of atoms and particles — the <s>Bhagavān Śākyamuni Tathāgata</s> turned the <s>dharma</s>-wheel.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, again uttered this verse:

children.translated_text: For the benefit of all beings, everywhere in all worlds,

children.text: yathā vinayato viśvaṃ vajracakraṃ pravartyatām // iti //
children.translated_text: according to [their] discipline, let the universal <s>vajra</s>-wheel be turned! Thus ends [the section].

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre tathaiva sarvabuddhakṣe[treṣu yāvat sarvaparamāṇurajomaṇḍaleṣu bha]gavān vajradhātustathāgato vajradhātvādīn sarvavajracakrāṇi pravartayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: And the moment this was spoken, likewise in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, as far as all the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of atoms and particles — the <s>Bhagavān Vajradhātu Tathāgata</s> turned all <s>vajra</s>-wheels beginning with the <s>vajradhātu</s>.
Then <s>Trailokyavijaya</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, uttered this verse:

children.translated_text: For the benefit of all beings, everywhere in all worlds,
according to [their] discipline, let the universal wrath-wheel be turned! Thus ends [the section].

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre tathaiva] sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu yāvat sarvaparamāṇurajomaṇḍaleṣu bhagavāṃstrilokavijayī tathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatakro[dhacakraṃ pravartayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: And the moment this was spoken, likewise in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, as far as all the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of atoms and particles — the <s>Bhagavān Trailokyavijayī Tathāgata</s> turned the all-<s>Tathāgata</s> wrath-wheel.
Then the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, uttered this verse:

body.text:
sarvasatvahitārthāya sarvalokeṣu sarvataḥ /
yathā vi[nayato viśvaṃ padmacakraṃ pravartyatām // iti //]
body.translated_text:
For the benefit of all beings, everywhere in all worlds,
according to [their] discipline, let the universal lotus-wheel be turned! Thus ends [the section].

body.text: athāsmin bhāṣitamātre tathaiva sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu yāvat sarvaparamāṇurajomaṇḍaleṣu bhagavāṃ dharmarājā tathāgataḥ padmacakraṃ pravartayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: And the moment this was spoken, likewise in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, as far as all the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of atoms and particles — the <s>Bhagavān Dharmarāja Tathāgata</s> turned the lotus-wheel.
Then the noble <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, uttered this verse:

children.translated_text: For the benefit of all beings, everywhere in all worlds,

children.text: yathā vinayato viśvaṃ maṇicakraṃ pravartyatām // iti //
children.translated_text: according to [their] discipline, let the universal jewel-wheel be turned! Thus ends [the section].

body.text: athāsmin[bhāṣitamātre sarvabuddhakṣetrāntargata]sarvasatvāḥ sūkṣmā vā sthūlā vā te sarve sarvatathāgataṃ sumerugirimūrdhni vajramaṇiratnaśikharakūṭāgāre sarvatathā[gatasiṃhāsane sthitvā vajradhātvādīn sarva]cakrāṇi pravartayantaṃ sarvato 'drākṣuriti //
body.translated_text: And the moment this was spoken, all beings within all <s>Buddha</s>-fields — whether subtle or gross — all of them saw the one seated on the all-<s>Tathāgata</s> lion-throne in the <s>vajra</s>-jewel-peak pinnacle-mansion on the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, turning all wheels beginning with the <s>vajradhātu</s>, from all sides.
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, at that time uttered this verse:

children.translated_text: For the benefit of all beings — act according to the task!
The supreme descent into human [birth] — let the <s>vajra</s>-wheel be turned! Thus ends [the section].

body.text: atha punarapi bhagavān sarvata[thāgatānāhūyaivamāha / "pratipadyata bha]gavantastathāgatāḥ punaḥ samājamāpantum" iti //
body.translated_text: Then again the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having summoned all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, said thus: 'Proceed, O <s>Bhagavān Tathāgata</s>s, to enter the assembly again!'

body.text: atha bhagavantaḥ sarvatathāgatāḥ punaḥ samājamā[padya, vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭā]iti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>s, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having entered the assembly again, entered into the heart of <s>Vairocana</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgataḥ sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajramātmānamavabudhya, va[jrapāṇimevamāha / "praviśakulapu]tra tvamapi mama hṛdaye; sarvatathāgatasarvavajrakulasarvamaṇḍalāḥ sarvatathāgatahṛdayeṣu samanupra[viṣṭāḥ" /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān Vairocana Tathāgata</s>, having realized himself as the body-speech-mind-<s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, said to <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> thus: 'Enter, O son of the family, you too into my heart; all the <s>vajra</s>-families and all the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s have entered into the hearts of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s.'
Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, authorized by all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, uttered this verse:

children.translated_text: For the benefit of all beings, I proceed in all ways —
to enter the body, speech, and mind <s>vajra</s> of all <s>Buddha</s>s! Thus ends [the section].

body.text: athāsmin bhā]ṣitamātre yāvantastathāgatāḥ sarvalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsameṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu tiṣṭhanti te tathā[gatā ekaikena sarvaloka]dhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāḥ spharaṇakāyāḥ bhagavato vairocanasya hṛdaye praviṣṭāḥ /
body.translated_text: And the moment this was spoken, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s who abide in all the world-realms equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms — those <s>Tathāgata</s>s, each with emanation-bodies equal in number to the atoms and particles of all world-realms, entered into the heart of the <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇirmahābodhisa[tvaḥ sarvatathāgateṣu] bhagavataśca vairocanasya sarvakāyeṣu sarvavākpravartanasthāneṣu sarvacittasantatipravāheṣu sarvavajranayeṣu sarvā[ṅgapratyaṅgeṣu sarvasthāneṣu] sarvalakṣaṇeṣu sarvānuvyañjaneṣu sarvaromakūpeṣu sarvaparamāṇurajomaṇḍaleṣu ca hṛdayeṣu praviṣṭvā sthitā iti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having entered into all <s>Tathāgata</s>s and into all the bodies of the <s>Bhagavān Vairocana</s>, into all the sites of speech-operation, into all streams of mind-continuity, into all <s>vajra</s>-methods, into all limbs and sub-limbs, into all sites, into all marks, into all secondary marks, into all pore-openings, and into the hearts of all the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of atoms and particles — having entered, he abided.

Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the recently fully awakened one, the body-speech-mind-<s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, having realized himself as the body of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, proceeded from that summit of <s>Sumeru</s> to the <s>Bodhi</s>-site (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>); having arrived, beneath the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, in conformity with the world, he again took up grass and uttered this inspired utterance:

body.text: saṃbuddhaḥ sarvatathāgatakāyavākcittavajraḥ sarvatathāgatakāyamātmānamavabudhya, tasmāt sumerugirimūrdhādyena [bodhimaṇḍaṃ tenopajagā]mopetya, bhagavato bodhivṛkṣasyādhastāt lokānuvartanatayā, punastṛṇāni gṛhyedamudānamudānayāmāsa /

children.translated_text: Ah, how wonderful — the supreme aim of the self is the aim of beings, for the teachers of beings;
that the steadfast ones, in accordance with [the needs of] those to be disciplined, abide in the appearance of a heretical view!
For the unteachable world, blinded by wrong views on all sides,
for the sake of purification through the light of <s>jñāna</s> — one should attain <s>Buddha</s>-awakening! Thus ends [the section].

body.text: atha kāmāvacarā devā bhagavatastatvamajānanto brūvan / "kiṃ bho śramaṇa evaṃ tīvrāṇyevaṃ raudrāṇi bo[dhyārthāya] duḥkhānyutsahasī-" ti /
body.translated_text: Then the gods of the desire-realm, not knowing the reality (<s>tattva</s>) of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said: 'Why, O ascetic, do you endure such fierce, such terrible sufferings for the sake of awakening?'

body.text: atha bhagavāṃstāni tṛṇānyāstaryopaviṣṭvā tāṃ devānevamāha / "pratipadyata mārṣā mama bodhiṃ [prāptum" iti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having spread that grass and sat down, said to those gods: 'Proceed, sirs, to attain my awakening!'

body.text: atha kāmāva]carā devā bhagavato bhāṣitasyārthamajānanto yena śakro devānāmindraḥ tenopajagāmopetya, śakraṃ devānāmindrami[daṃ vṛttāntamārocayā]māsa /
body.translated_text: Then the gods of the desire-realm, not understanding the meaning of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, went to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and reported this matter to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods.

body.text: atha śakro devānāmindraḥ sarvakāmāvacaradevasaṅghaparivāro rūpāvacarādhipatiṃ mahābrahmāṇamidaṃ [vṛttāntamārocayā]māsa /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, accompanied by the entire host of desire-realm gods, reported this matter to <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, the overlord of the form-realm.
Then <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, together with all the desire-realm and form-realm gods, reported that matter to <s>Īśvara</s>, the overlord of the three worlds.

body.text: atha mahe]śvarastrilokādhipatirnārāyaṇādīn sarvadevādhipatīnevamāha / "pratipadyata mārṣāstathāgato 'rhaṃ samyaksaṃbuddho [lokānuvartanatayā pu]naranuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ darśayiṣyati / māmantryā evaṃ vidyen na tathāgato mānuṣo bhavati, devā eva [tathāgatā bhavanti], manuṣe ghaṭayeyuḥ, na tathāgatatva iti / tatsādhu pratipadyata tatra pūjanāya gantu" miti /
body.translated_text: Then <s>Maheśvara</s>, the lord of the three worlds, spoke thus to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and all the other lords of gods: "Understand, sirs — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Awakened One, will again demonstrate the unsurpassed perfect awakening in conformity with the world. Having consulted me, know it thus: the <s>Tathāgata</s> is not a human being; the <s>Tathāgata</s>s are indeed gods. They may exert themselves among humans, but that is not [true] <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood. Therefore, understand well; let us go there to worship."

body.text: atha maheśva[rādidevādhipatayaḥ sthitvā] bodhimaṇḍe, yena ca bhagavān bodhimaṇḍaniṣaṇṇaḥ tenopajagāmopetya ca bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya, bhagavantamevamāhuḥ / ["pratipadya bha]gavannasmākamanukampāmupādāya, asmāt tṛṇasaṃstarādutthāya, divyeṣvāsaneṣu niṣadyānuttarāṃ samayaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhu" //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Maheśvara</s> and the other lords of gods, having stationed themselves at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), approached the Blessed One who was seated at the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>, and having saluted the feet of the Blessed One with their heads, spoke thus to the Blessed One: "Understand, Blessed One — out of compassion for us, rising from this grass-seat, sitting upon divine seats, please awaken to the unsurpassed perfect awakening."

body.text: atha [bhagavān de]vādhipatīnevamāha / "pratipadyata mārṣā mamānuttarāṃ samayaksaṃbodhi dātu" miti / atha te evamāhur / "na vayaṃ bhagavaṃ samarthā bodhiṃ da[ātuṃ] / yadi vayaṃ samarthā bhavemastadātmanaivābhisaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyemahī-" ti //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One spoke thus to the lords of gods: "Understand, sirs — [you must] give me the unsurpassed perfect awakening." Then they spoke thus: "We are not capable, Blessed One, of giving awakening. If we were capable, we would awaken to the perfect awakening by ourselves."

body.text: atha bhagavānidamevārthamuddīpayaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā i[māṃ gāthā]mabhāṣat /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, illuminating this very meaning to an even greater degree, spoke this verse:

children.text: na sā rūpi na cārūpi na satyaṃ na mṛṣāśuci /
children.translated_text: "It is neither with form nor without form, neither true nor false-impure;
this <s>Buddha</s>-awakening is knowledge — having realized [it], one becomes a Conqueror."

body.text: atha te devādhipa[tiyo mu]hūrtaṃ tūṣṇīmbhāvena tasthuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then those lords of gods stood in silence for a moment.

body.text: atha bhagavāṃstatastṛṇāsanādutthāya, tāṃ devānevamāha / "pratipadyata mārṣā īdṛśaṃ jñānamavaboddhuṃ /" [ta e]vamāhur / "na śaktamo bhagavan" //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having risen from that grass-seat, spoke thus to those gods: "Understand, sirs — [you should] realize such knowledge." They spoke thus: "We are not able, Blessed One."
Then the Blessed One, having sat down on that very seat, spoke this verse:

children.translated_text: "Through the realization of the mind, make firm the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening);
having made firm the <s>vajra</s> in the being, contemplate oneself as <s>Buddha</s>."

body.text: atha ta evamāhur / "evamastv" iti kṛtvā sarve prakrāntāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then they spoke thus: "So be it" — and all departed.

body.text: atha bhagavān rātrau prabhātāyāṃ [lokānu]vartanatayā mārāṃ jitvānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya, aśeṣānavaśeṣa[satvadhātuṣu sarvasatvahitārthāya, svahṛda]yāvasthitamāryavajrapāṇinamanena nāmāṣṭaśatenābhistauti /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at the break of night, in conformity with the world, having conquered <s>Māra</s> and awakened to the unsurpassed perfect awakening, for the welfare of all beings in all realms of beings without remainder, praised the noble <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> established in his own heart with this eulogy of one hundred and eight names:

children.translated_text: "O <s>Vajrasattva</s>, great being, <s>Mahāyāna</s>, great-souled one,
great splendor, great purity, great protector — homage to you! (1)
O <s>Vajrarāja</s>, great <s>vajra</s>, O <s>vajra</s> of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s,
great being, great valor, great skillful means — homage to you! (2)
O <s>Vajrarāga</s>, greatly pure, all-bliss, great happiness,
supreme of joys, beginningless and endless, great desire — homage to you! (3)
O <s>Vajrasādhu</s>, great satisfaction, well-done, joy-giver,
great delight, great rejoicing, exultation — homage to you! (4)
O <s>Vajraratna</s>, great king, self-consecrated, greatly wise,
all-jewel, great splendor, ornament — homage to you! (5)
O <s>Vajrateja</s>, great radiance, <s>vajra</s>-light, great brilliance,
Conqueror-light, great flame, <s>Buddha</s>-light — homage to you! (6)
O <s>Vajraketu</s>, great banner, great standard, wealth-giver,
sky-banner, great staff, renunciation-banner — homage to you! (7)
O <s>Vajrahāsa</s>, great laughter, great joy, delight-giver,
force of delight, lover of delight, <s>dharma</s>-delight — homage to you! (8)
O <s>Vajradharma</s>, great <s>dharma</s>, purifier of all <s>dharma</s>s,
<s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>, supreme good <s>dharma</s>, passion-<s>dharma</s> — homage to you! (9)
O <s>Vajratīkṣṇa</s>, great sheath, <s>prajñā</s>-knowledge, greatly wise,
sin-cutter, great sword, <s>Buddha</s>-weapon — homage to you! (10)
O <s>Vajrahetu</s>, great wheel, <s>Buddha</s>-wheel, great treasury,
all-<s>maṇḍala</s>, foremost of <s>dharma</s>s, <s>dharma</s>-wheel — homage to you! (11)
O <s>Vajrabhāṣa</s>, great speech, free from elaboration, great syllable,
without syllable, great recitation, <s>Buddha</s>-voice — homage to you! (12)
O <s>Vajrakarma</s>, supreme good action, great action, doer of good deeds,
secret worship, great worship, <s>Buddha</s>-worship — homage to you! (13)
O <s>Vajrarakṣa</s>, great armor, supreme shield, greatly firm,
great protection, great essence, <s>Buddha</s>-power — homage to you! (14)
O <s>Vajrayakṣa</s>, great wrath, terrifier of all the wicked,
great skillful means of all <s>Buddha</s>s, supreme <s>yakṣa</s> — homage to you! (15)
Great union, great <s>mudrā</s>, great pledge-binder,
great fist, supreme of oceans, <s>vajra</s>-fist — homage to you! (16)
You are to be venerated, honored, and worshipped, to be revered by the <s>Tathāgata</s>s,
since you are called the <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening), beginningless and endless. (17)
Having attained you, all the Conquerors and the valorous <s>bodhisattva</s>s
have arisen and will arise — as the foremost causes of <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. (18)

children.text: namaste vajrasattvāya vajraratnāya ca te namaḥ /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, <s>Vajrasattva</s>! And homage to you, <s>Vajraratna</s>!
Homage to you, <s>Vajradharma</s>! Homage to you, <s>Vajrakarma</s>! (19)
Having praised you with these supreme names and bowed with devotion,
by that merit, may everyone indeed attain <s>Buddha</s>-awakening. (20)
Whoever would correctly recite this supreme eulogy of one hundred and eight names,
even once, abiding in good devotion, would attain complete <s>Buddha</s>hood."

body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One, the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇiṃ mahābodhisatvaṃ te sarvatathāgatā [ekakaṣṭhe]na sādhukārāṇyanuprādān //
body.translated_text: Then all those <s>Tathāgata</s>s bestowed acclamations upon the great <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> in unison:

children.text: sādhu te vajrasatvāya vajraratnāya sādhu te /
children.translated_text: "Well done to you, <s>Vajrasattva</s>! Well done to you, <s>Vajraratna</s>!

children.text: vajradharmāya te sādhu sādhu te vajrakarmaṇe //
children.translated_text: Well done to you, <s>Vajradharma</s>! Well done to you, <s>Vajrakarma</s>!
Well spoken is this <s>sūtra</s>, the unsurpassed <s>Vajrayāna</s>,
the secret of all <s>Tathāgata</s>s, the compendium of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>."

body.text: idam [avocadbhagavānāttamanāḥ satathāratāryabodhisatvaśca sarvaḥ svahṛdaye praviśya bhagavataśca vajrasatvasya ca] bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. Overjoyed, all the <s>Tathāgata</s>s and the noble <s>bodhisattva</s>s, having entered their own hearts, rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One and of <s>Vajrasattva</s>.
The <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s> called the Compendium of the Reality of All <s>Tathāgata</s>s (<s>Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha</s>) is completed.
<s>Oṃ</s> — Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!
